title: Implement process global shim — env, cwd, platform, exit, stdout, pid
description:
# Goal
Implement the global process object that nearly every Node.js extension expects. This is the SINGLE MOST CRITICAL shim — 315 uses of process.env, 139 of process.cwd(), 70 of process.exit(), 62 of process.platform across the conformance corpus.

# Background (DATA-DRIVEN)
Analysis of 200+ extensions in tests/ext_conformance/artifacts/ shows process.* is used more than ANY other Node.js API:
  process.env          315 occurrences (config, API keys, feature flags)
  process.cwd          139 occurrences (resolve relative paths)
  process.exit          70 occurrences (fatal error handling)
  process.platform      62 occurrences (platform detection)
  process.stdout        44 occurrences (output streaming)
  process.pid           33 occurrences (process identification)
  process.argv          23 occurrences (CLI argument parsing)
  process.kill          17 occurrences (signal sending)
  process.stdin         15 occurrences (input reading)
  process.on            13 occurrences (event handlers)
  process.execPath      12 occurrences (binary path)
  process.arch           3 occurrences (architecture detection)

Without this shim, the MAJORITY of extensions fail on the very first line that reads process.env.

# API Surface (prioritized by usage)

## Tier 1 — Must Have (blocks 80%+ of extensions)
- process.env → Proxy object that reads from Rust env vars via hostcall
  - CRITICAL: Must support process.env.HOME, process.env.PATH, etc.
  - Must be a Proxy so dynamic property access works (not just pre-defined keys)
  - Security: filtered by extension policy (some env vars blocked)
- process.cwd() → string (current working directory via hostcall)
- process.platform → "linux" | "darwin" | "win32" (compile-time constant)
- process.exit(code?) → void (requests extension shutdown with code)
- process.pid → number (QuickJS thread ID or synthetic)
- process.argv → string[] (["pi", extension_name])

## Tier 2 — Should Have (blocks 20-40% of extensions)
- process.stdout → writable stream stub { write(data) }
  - Route to console.log internally
  - Needed by extensions that pipe output
- process.stderr → writable stream stub { write(data) }
- process.on("exit", callback) → register cleanup handler
- process.on("uncaughtException", callback) → error handler
- process.kill(pid, signal) → hostcall to Rust (capability-gated)
- process.execPath → "/usr/bin/pi" (path to Pi binary)
- process.arch → "x64" | "arm64" (compile-time)
- process.version → "v20.0.0" (synthetic Node.js version for compat)
- process.versions → { node: "20.0.0", v8: "n/a", ... }

# Implementation Strategy
- process is a GLOBAL object, not a module import — register it in QuickJS global scope at runtime init
- process.env: Use ES6 Proxy to intercept property access → hostcall to Rust std::env::var()
  - Cache env vars for the lifetime of the extension (snapshot at load time)
  - Writes to process.env: store locally, dont mutate real env
- process.cwd(): Single hostcall at init, cache result
- process.exit(): Request extension shutdown via runtime signal (dont call std::process::exit!)
- process.stdout/stderr: Lightweight writable stream that calls console.log/console.error

# Security Considerations
- process.env MUST filter sensitive vars (API keys, secrets) based on extension policy
- process.kill MUST be capability-gated (deny by default)
- process.exit should NOT kill the Pi process — only the extension context

# Files to Modify
- src/extensions_js.rs: Register process global at QuickJS context creation
- src/extension_dispatcher.rs: Add env-read hostcall handler

# Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] process.env.HOME returns home directory
- [ ] process.env.PATH returns PATH
- [ ] process.env.NONEXISTENT returns undefined
- [ ] process.cwd() returns current working directory
- [ ] process.platform returns correct platform string
- [ ] process.exit(0) cleanly terminates extension without crashing Pi
- [ ] process.stdout.write("hello") outputs to console
- [ ] process.env write doesnt mutate real environment
- [ ] Sensitive env vars filtered by policy
- [ ] 15+ unit tests covering all Tier 1 + Tier 2 APIs

title: [DEADLOCK-AUDIT] P0: await-holding-lock pattern in src/rpc.rs (4 sites)
description:
Concurrency audit of src/rpc.rs found 4 instances of the await-holding-lock anti-pattern, which is a classic deadlock hazard in async code — tasks that need the same lock can deadlock while this task is suspended at .await.

**Affected sites:**
- src/rpc.rs:1317 [P0]: guard.persist_session().await held while outer session lock active (set_session_name handler)
- src/rpc.rs:1433 [P0]: guard.persist_session().await held while outer session lock active (bash execution handler)
- src/rpc.rs:4678 [P0]: apply_thinking_level calls guard.persist_session().await while guard reference still borrowed + outer lock held
- src/rpc.rs:1117 [P1]: apply_thinking_level().await called while session lock held (set_thinking_level handler)

**Why this matters:**
When an async task holds a Mutex guard across an .await point, the task is suspended with the lock held. If the awaited future ends up needing the same Mutex (even indirectly, e.g., through callbacks or other task spawns), the system deadlocks.

**Fix pattern:**
For each site: scope the guard drop before the .await. Either:
1. `let data = { let guard = mutex.lock().await; data_from(guard) };  do_async(data).await;`  — drop guard before await
2. If the awaited value truly needs the lock: redesign to take a snapshot, release lock, do async work, reacquire lock briefly to apply result
3. If persist_session() is the guilty awaited op: persist outside the lock with a copy of what needs persisting

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Each of the 4 sites rewritten so no lock is held across .await
- [ ] `cargo clippy -- -W clippy::await_holding_lock` passes without warnings on rpc.rs
- [ ] Integration test that exercises concurrent set_session_name + bash call + set_thinking_level does not deadlock under contention (e.g., 100 parallel requests)

Discovery: orchestrator-run deadlock-finder subagent, tick 27.
close_reason: Fixed 4 await-holding-lock sites in src/rpc.rs — commit 4c6498c79; verified with targeted RPC tests

title: FUZZ-P1.6: Message Types — Proptest serde(untagged) enum deserialization for Message/ContentBlock
close_reason: Completed: 5 proptests verified passing (256 cases each), stack overflow fixed by reducing strategy nesting depth.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## FUZZ-P1.6: Message Types Proptest

### Background
src/model.rs (~44KB) defines the core message and content types used throughout the system. These are deserialized from both API responses (untrusted) and session files (user-editable). The use of #[serde(untagged)] enums makes deserialization particularly tricky and fragile.

### Key Types to Fuzz

1. **Message enum**:
```rust
pub enum Message {
    User(UserMessage),
    Assistant(AssistantMessage),
    ToolResult(ToolResultMessage),
    Custom(CustomMessage),
}
```
Risk: #[serde(untagged)] means serde tries each variant in order. Ambiguous JSON could match the wrong variant.

2. **UserContent enum**:
```rust
pub enum UserContent {
    Text(String),
    Blocks(Vec<ContentBlock>),
}
```
Risk: Also #[serde(untagged)]. A JSON string matches Text, a JSON array matches Blocks. But what about: JSON number? JSON null? JSON object? Empty array?

3. **ContentBlock enum**:
```rust
pub enum ContentBlock {
    Text(TextContent),      // has text_signature: Option<String>
    Thinking(ThinkingContent),
    Image(ImageContent),
    ToolCall(ToolCall),
}
```
Risk: Tagged by 'type' field. What if type is missing? What if type is an unexpected value?

4. **ImageContent**: base64 data field — no validation that it's valid base64 or valid image data
5. **ToolCall**: arguments field is serde_json::Value — unbounded
6. **AssistantMessage**: Has content, api, provider, model, usage, stop_reason, error_message, timestamp — many optional fields

### Specific Risks
1. **Untagged enum ambiguity**: UserContent::Text("[]") vs UserContent::Blocks(vec\![]) — edge case where a string looks like an array
2. **Missing discriminator fields**: ContentBlock without 'type' field → deserialization error, but verify no panic
3. **Invalid base64 in ImageContent**: data: "not-base64\!\!\!" → should be accepted by deserializer (it's just a String), but downstream consumers must handle
4. **Negative token counts in Usage**: input_tokens: -1, output_tokens: -999 → overflow in cost calculations
5. **Very large content arrays**: 100K ContentBlocks in one message → memory
6. **Conflicting role + content type**: role: "user" but content matches AssistantMessage format
7. **text_signature field on TextContent**: Easily forgotten field (known gotcha) — verify it deserializes correctly when present/absent/null

### Implementation Approach
Create strategies:
- `arbitrary_message_json()`: Random valid-ish Message JSON
- `content_block_strategy()`: Generates each ContentBlock variant + edge cases
- `ambiguous_user_content()`: Specifically targets untagged enum edge cases
- `chaos_message()`: Fully random JSON

### Invariants to Assert
- No panic on any JSON input for Message deserialization
- Valid Message JSON round-trips: deserialize → serialize → deserialize produces identical structure
- UserContent::Text always gets plain strings, Blocks always gets arrays (no misclassification)
- Empty content array → valid Message with no content (not error)
- Missing optional fields → None (not error)
- Unknown fields in JSON → ignored (not error)

### Files to Modify
- src/model.rs (add proptest module to existing tests)

### Acceptance Criteria
- At least 4 proptest functions covering Message, UserContent, ContentBlock, and round-trip
- Minimum 256 cases per property
- Explicit test for untagged enum ambiguity
- Any misclassification bugs found are documented and fixed

comments.text: Claimed by NavyBridge (claude-opus-4-6). Starting implementation of Message/ContentBlock/UserContent proptest coverage in src/model.rs.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone

Fixed stack overflow: reduced strategy nesting depth (bounded_json_value → scalar_json_value in tool_call/tool_result/custom message strategies, vec sizes 0..6 → 0..3). All 5 tests pass reliably without RUST_MIN_STACK override.

title: Implement mock layer for Rust QuickJS runtime
description:
# Implement mock layer for Rust QuickJS runtime

## Context
The Rust runtime executes extensions in QuickJS. The hostcall bridge (src/extensions.rs dispatch_hostcall_events/dispatch_hostcall_session) handles JS->Rust calls. For conformance testing, we need to intercept these and return mock responses from the shared mock spec.

## Architecture
In Rust, hostcalls flow:
1. JS calls pi.session(op, payload) or pi.events(op, payload)
2. QuickJS calls back to Rust via registered hostcall functions
3. Rust dispatch_hostcall_events() / dispatch_hostcall_session() routes to real implementations
4. For mocking: we need TestSession / TestDispatcher that reads mock spec

## What Already Exists
- NullSession in extension_dispatcher.rs: returns empty/default for all session calls
- TestSession in extension_dispatcher.rs: similar but for tests
- These are close to what we need but lack mock spec integration

## What To Do
1. Create ConformanceMockSession that implements ExtensionSession trait
2. ConformanceMockSession reads mock_spec.json and returns configured responses
3. Create ConformanceMockDispatcher for non-session hostcalls (exec, http, etc.)
4. Create a test function: load extension + run with mocks + capture output as JSON
5. Output format must EXACTLY match the TS harness output format

## Key Implementation Details
- JsExtensionSnapshot already captures registrations (tools, slash_commands, shortcuts, flags, event_hooks, providers)
- We need to also capture hostcall invocations during load
- The mock layer goes between the extension and the real dispatch

## Acceptance Criteria
- ConformanceMockSession passes compilation
- Load hello.ts extension with mock session, capture registrations
- Output JSON matches TS harness format
close_reason: Created tests/conformance_mock.rs with 11 tests implementing the conformance mock layer: ConformanceMockSpec (JSON-loadable spec), ConformanceMockSession (implements ExtensionSession with capture logging), HostcallCaptureLog (records all hostcall invocations), ConformanceOutput/ConformanceRegistrations (structured output format for diff-based conformance testing). Tests cover: mock session compilation + default spec, configured state returns, mutation capture (set_name/set_model/set_thinking_level/set_label), spec JSON deserialization, capture log serialization, hello.ts loading with mock session, tool registration capture, session-calling extension loading, multi-registration type capture (commands+shortcuts+flags+providers+models), and JSON round-trip. All tests pass, clippy clean (lib error is pre-existing in interactive.rs), fmt clean.

title: Implement TUI snapshot testing infrastructure
description:
# Implement TUI snapshot testing infrastructure

## Goal
Create infrastructure for testing the interactive TUI by capturing terminal output
and comparing against golden snapshots, with detailed logging.

## Background
src/interactive.rs is 2842 lines with only 2 trivial tests (<0.1% coverage).
This is the most user-visible code and needs comprehensive testing.

## Approach: Snapshot Testing

### Why Snapshots?
- TUI output is complex (ANSI codes, layout)
- Pixel-perfect testing impractical
- Snapshots capture "expected output" simply
- Easy to update when intentional changes made

### Snapshot Format
```
// tests/snapshots/tui_initial_state.snap
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Pi - AI Coding Agent                │
├─────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                     │
│ > [cursor]                          │
│                                     │
├─────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Model: claude-sonnet-4   Tokens: 0  │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Logging Requirements
- Use TestLogger (bd-3ml) for each snapshot test.
- Log view size, theme name, state flags, and snapshot name.
- On mismatch, dump the rendered view (ANSI-stripped) + diff context.

## Determinism Requirements
- Force terminal size (80x24) and disable time-based animations/spinners in test mode.
- Strip ANSI codes for snapshots.
- Use a fixed default theme and locale.

## Implementation

### Snapshot Library
Use insta crate for Rust snapshot testing:
```toml
[dev-dependencies]
insta = { version = "1", features = ["filters"] }
```

### Test Structure

Strip ANSI codes for deterministic snapshots:
```rust
fn strip_ansi(s: &str) -> String {
    let re = regex::Regex::new(r"\x1b\[[0-9;]*[a-zA-Z]").unwrap();
    re.replace_all(s, "").to_string()
}
```

title: Validate Rust QuickJS runtime can load extensions and capture registrations
description:
# Validate Rust QuickJS runtime can load extensions and capture registrations

## Context
The Rust extension runtime uses:
- src/extensions_js.rs: JsExtensionLoadSpec, swc TypeScript compilation, QuickJS execution
- src/extensions.rs: CompatibilityScanner (pattern detection), load_all_extensions(), ExtensionManager
- src/extension_dispatcher.rs: hostcall dispatch

Extensions are loaded via JsExtensionLoadSpec -> swc transpiles TS to JS -> QuickJS executes -> snapshot_extensions() captures JsExtensionSnapshot (tools, slash_commands, shortcuts, flags, event_hooks, providers).

## What To Do
1. Write a minimal Rust test that creates a JsExtensionLoadSpec for hello.ts
2. Load it through the extension pipeline
3. Capture the resulting JsExtensionSnapshot
4. Verify the snapshot contains expected registrations
5. Serialize the snapshot as JSON for comparison

- src/extensions_js.rs (JsExtensionLoadSpec, load flow)
- src/extensions.rs (CompatibilityScanner, ExtensionManager)
- tests/e2e_extension_registration.rs (existing test patterns)

## Acceptance Criteria
- hello.ts loads without panics
- JsExtensionSnapshot captures expected registrations
- Snapshot can be serialized to JSON
close_reason: Rust QuickJS runtime validated: hello.ts and all 60 official extensions load successfully. JsExtensionSnapshot captures registrations (tools, commands, flags, shortcuts, handlers). comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
QuickJS embedder obligations + hardening (key references)

- Microtasks/job queue: QuickJS requires the embedder to drain pending jobs (Promises/queueMicrotask) via JS_ExecutePendingJob. This is the foundation of the PiJS deterministic tick model.
  Ref: https://cs.opensource.google/fuchsia/fuchsia/+/master:third_party/quickjs/quickjs.h

- Module resolution: embedder can install a custom module loader (JS_SetModuleLoaderFunc) to control how import/module names resolve (critical for node:* shims and virtual modules).
  Ref: https://cs.opensource.google/fuchsia/fuchsia/+/master:third_party/quickjs/quickjs.h

- Resource limits: QuickJS supports a memory cap (JS_SetMemoryLimit) and an interrupt hook (JS_SetInterruptHandler) suitable for CPU/time budgets (terminate runaway extensions deterministically).
  Ref: https://cs.opensource.google/fuchsia/fuchsia/+/master:third_party/quickjs/quickjs.h
  Ref (overview + timeout mention): https://quickjs-ng.github.io/quickjs-ng/developer-guide/intro.html

- rquickjs maps these controls into Rust-level APIs (Runtime::set_memory_limit, set_max_stack_size, set_gc_threshold, etc.).
  Ref: https://docs.rs/rquickjs/latest/rquickjs/struct.Runtime.html

Acceptance reminder for bd-1f5: these embedder controls must be exercised in unit tests (budget exceed => deterministic host_result error; cancellation must not silently drop).

title: Implement pi.sendMessage() and pi.sendUserMessage() for message injection
description:
Allow extensions to inject messages into the conversation.

## API Spec (from legacy)
```typescript
// Custom message (not for LLM, optional display)
pi.sendMessage({
  customType: string,
  content: string,
  display?: boolean,
  details?: unknown
}, {
  triggerTurn?: boolean,
  deliverAs?: 'steer' | 'followUp' | 'nextTurn'
});

// User message (triggers LLM turn)
pi.sendUserMessage(content, {
  deliverAs?: 'steer' | 'followUp'
});
```

## Delivery Modes
- **steer**: Interrupt after current tool, skip remaining tool calls
- **followUp**: Queue after agent finishes current turn
- **nextTurn**: Default, processed as next user input

## Implementation Requirements
1. Hostcall handlers for 'sendMessage' and 'sendUserMessage'
2. Integration with agent message queues (steering_queue, follow_up_queue)
3. Custom message type in session entries
4. Display logic in TUI for custom messages

## Data Flow
1. Extension calls pi.sendMessage({customType: 'bookmark', content: 'Saved\!'})
2. Hostcall creates CustomMessage entry
3. If display=true, shows in TUI
4. If triggerTurn=true, queues for processing

## Test Plan
- Unit test: sendMessage creates correct entry type
- Unit test: sendUserMessage triggers agent turn
- Integration test: steer mode interrupts current processing
- Integration test: followUp mode queues correctly

## Files to Modify
- src/extensions.rs (hostcall handlers)
- src/extensions_js.rs (bridge to Rust)
- src/agent.rs (message queue integration)
- src/interactive.rs (display custom messages)
close_reason: pi.sendMessage() and pi.sendUserMessage() both fully implemented as hostcalls in src/extensions.rs (line ~5531 and ~5606). ExtensionHostActions trait defines both methods. Hostcall handles validation, permission checks, and message delivery.

title: Implement pi.registerShortcut() for extension keyboard bindings
description:
Allow extensions to register custom keyboard shortcuts.

## API Spec (from legacy)
```typescript
pi.registerShortcut(key, {
  description: string,
  handler: (ctx) => Promise<void>
});
```

Key format: 'ctrl+u', 'alt+shift+x', 'f1', etc.

## Implementation Requirements
1. ShortcutRegistry in extension runtime
2. Hostcall handler for 'registerShortcut'
3. Integration with keybindings system (src/keybindings.rs)
4. Validation that key isn't reserved (interrupt, clear, exit, suspend)
5. Shortcut execution via extension runtime

## Reserved Keys (cannot be overridden)
- ctrl+c (interrupt)
- ctrl+d (exit)
- ctrl+l (clear)
- ctrl+z (suspend)

## Data Flow
1. Extension calls pi.registerShortcut('ctrl+u', {...})
2. Hostcall validates key not reserved, stores in registry
3. KeyMsg in bubbletea checked against extension shortcuts
4. If match, invoke JS handler with ExtensionContext

## Test Plan
- Unit test: registerShortcut stores shortcut
- Unit test: reserved keys rejected
- Integration test: registered shortcut triggers handler

title: Workstream: Interactive Editor UX Parity (autocomplete, multiline, bang, images)
description:
# Goal
Bring the **interactive editor experience** to parity with legacy pi-mono, focusing on:
- Autocomplete (commands, templates, skills, file references, path completion)
- Multi-line editing behavior (Shift+Enter inserts newline, Enter submits)
- Bash shortcuts (`!` and `!!`)
- Clipboard image paste + drag/drop attachments

# Legacy Behavior (Source-of-Truth)
From `legacy_pi_mono_code/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/README.md` → “Editor”:
- File reference: type `@` to fuzzy-search project files
- Path completion: Tab to complete paths
- Multi-line: Shift+Enter (Ctrl+Enter on Windows Terminal)
- Images: Ctrl+V to paste, or drag onto terminal
- Bash commands: `!command` runs and sends output to LLM, `!!command` runs without sending

Legacy implementation details:
- Autocomplete is provided by `CombinedAutocompleteProvider` (slash commands, prompt templates, extension commands, skill commands, file path completion using `fd`).
- Image paste writes clipboard image to a temp file and inserts the file path into the editor.

# Current Rust State (Gap)
- `src/interactive.rs` reserves Tab for future autocomplete but has no autocomplete UI.
- No `@` file fuzzy search.
- No Shift+Enter newline semantics (current behavior differs).
- No `!` / `!!` bash shortcuts.
- No clipboard image paste handler.

# Scope / Deliverables
## 1) Autocomplete engine
- Provide suggestions for:
  - Slash commands (built-in)
  - Prompt templates (`/<template>`)
  - Skill commands (`/skill:name`) when enabled
  - File references after typing `@` (fuzzy search project files)
  - Path completion when cursor is inside a path token

## 2) Autocomplete UI
- Render a dropdown/list with:
  - configurable max visible items (`autocomplete_max_visible`)
  - keyboard navigation
  - selection/accept behavior

## 3) Multi-line input semantics
- Shift+Enter inserts newline; Enter submits.
- Windows Terminal: Ctrl+Enter inserts newline.

## 4) Bash shortcuts
- `!cmd`: run and include output in LLM context.
- `!!cmd`: run but do not include output in LLM context.

## 5) Clipboard image paste and drag/drop
- Ctrl+V attempts to read clipboard image:
  - if an image exists, write it to a temp file and insert the file path at cursor.
  - do nothing (silent) if clipboard has no image or access denied.
- Drag/drop: terminals usually paste a file path; ensure we handle file paths cleanly.

# Testing
- Unit tests for autocomplete matching and insertion.
- State tests for key interactions (Tab, Shift+Enter, Ctrl+V).
- Integration tests for `!` / `!!` behavior (using deterministic command runner where possible).

# Dependencies
- Keybinding routing (`bd-3ip`) for Tab / Shift+Enter / Ctrl+V behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
[ ] Autocomplete exists (commands/templates/skills/files/paths)
[ ] Tab path completion works
[ ] @ fuzzy file reference works
[ ] Shift+Enter inserts newline; Enter submits
[ ] ! and !! bash shortcuts implemented
[ ] Ctrl+V image paste + drag/drop attachment supported
[ ] Editor settings are wired (padding, max visible)

title: Implement mock layer for pi-mono TS runtime
description:
# Implement mock layer for pi-mono TS runtime

## Context
The TS runtime uses real implementations for hostcalls during normal operation. For conformance testing, we need to intercept these and return mock responses from the shared mock spec.

## Architecture
pi-mono loader.ts creates an ExtensionAPI with:
- Registration methods: on(), registerTool(), registerCommand(), etc. -- these WRITE to the Extension object
- Action methods: sendMessage(), exec(), setModel(), etc. -- these delegate to ExtensionRuntime

For registration methods: no mocking needed -- they naturally capture what extensions register.
For action methods: we replace the runtime with mock implementations that read from the mock spec.

## What To Do
1. Create a Bun script: tests/ext_conformance/ts_harness/run_extension.ts
2. Import loadExtensions from pi-mono
3. Before loading, create a custom ExtensionRuntime that:
   a. Reads mock_spec.json for session state, exec responses, etc.
   b. Captures all calls to action methods
   c. Returns deterministic responses
4. After loading, serialize the Extension object (handlers, tools, commands, flags, shortcuts)
5. Output structured JSON to stdout

## Key Implementation Details
- The ExtensionRuntime is created by createExtensionRuntime() in loader.ts
- We can replace it with our mock runtime BEFORE calling loadExtensions()
- EventBus (pi.events) needs mock: capture all emitted events
- exec() calls need mock: return from mock spec
- HTTP calls (if extension uses fetch directly) need mock: use Bun test mocks or intercept

## Acceptance Criteria
- run_extension.ts loads an extension and outputs JSON
- JSON includes: registrations (tools, commands, flags, shortcuts, handlers), captured_calls, load_time_ms
- Output is deterministic (same extension + same mock spec = same output)
close_reason: TS oracle harness implemented and working. All 60 official extensions load successfully via Bun + load_extension.ts. Deterministic JSON output enables differential conformance testing.

title: [PERF-8] Criterion benchmark suite for TUI rendering performance
description:
## Problem

No benchmarks exist for TUI rendering performance. Cannot track regressions or verify optimization impact. Need baselines BEFORE optimizations AND verification AFTER.

## Solution: Criterion Benchmark Suite

### CRITICAL: Benchmarks Must Be Independent of Optimizations

Previous version had dependencies on PERF-1 and PERF-3. This was WRONG — benchmarks should be created FIRST to establish baselines, then run again after optimizations to verify improvement.

**Phase 1 (this bead): Create benchmark scaffolding and record baselines**
- No dependency on any PERF optimization beads
- Benchmarks measure the CURRENT (unoptimized) code
- Baselines establish the "before" numbers

**Phase 2 (after optimizations): Re-run benchmarks**
- After PERF-1 through PERF-7 are implemented, re-run benchmarks
- Compare against baselines to verify improvement
- This is done as part of PERF-9 (CI regression gate)

### Benchmarks

1. **build_conversation_content**
   - 10 messages (typical short conversation)
   - 100 messages (medium conversation)
   - 1000 messages (long session)

2. **view() full render cycle**
   - Empty conversation
   - 50 messages + active streaming
   - 200 messages + scrolled to top

3. **Viewport operations**
   - page_up/page_down with 10000 lines
   - set_content with 5000 lines
   - goto_bottom performance

4. **Markdown rendering**
   - Short message (100 chars)
   - Long message (10KB with code blocks)
   - Message with tables and lists

5. **String allocation counting** (optional, if allocator instrumentation is feasible)
   - Count allocations per frame via custom allocator wrapper
   - Compare before/after PERF-7

### Setup

```rust
// benches/tui_perf.rs
use criterion::{criterion_group, criterion_main, Criterion, BenchmarkId};

fn bench_build_conversation_content(c: &mut Criterion) {
    let mut group = c.benchmark_group("build_conversation_content");
    for n_messages in [10, 100, 1000] {
        group.bench_with_input(
            BenchmarkId::new("messages", n_messages),
            &n_messages,
            |b, &n| {
                let mut app = create_test_app_with_messages(n);
                b.iter(|| {
                    app.build_conversation_content()
                });
            },
        );
    }
    group.finish();
}
```

### Baseline Recording
- Run benchmarks on CI reference machine  
- Store baseline in `benches/baselines/` for comparison
- criterion generates HTML reports automatically

### Helper Functions Needed
- `create_test_app_with_messages(n: usize)` — creates a PiApp with n realistic messages
- Messages should include: user text, assistant markdown, tool calls, tool results, thinking blocks
- This helper is also useful for PERF-TEST (bd-172np)

## Files to Create
- benches/tui_perf.rs (new benchmark file)

## Dependencies
- **NONE** — benchmarks measure existing code to establish baselines
- (Previously depended on PERF-1 and PERF-3, which was wrong — you need baselines before optimization)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Criterion benchmark for build_conversation_content at 3 conversation sizes
- [ ] Criterion benchmark for view() at 3 scenarios
- [ ] Criterion benchmark for viewport operations  
- [ ] Criterion benchmark for markdown rendering
- [ ] Helper function create_test_app_with_messages() for realistic test data
- [ ] Baseline recorded and checked in (benches/baselines/)
- [ ] cargo bench runs successfully
- [ ] HTML report shows p50/p95/p99 and regression detection

close_reason: Completed: expanded SSE proptests + RCH validations

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## FUZZ-P1.1: SSE Parser Proptest Expansion

### Background
The SSE parser (src/sse.rs, 902 lines) already has ONE proptest: `sse_chunking_invariant` (line 883) with 64 cases that validates parsing is chunk-boundary-independent. This is good but only scratches the surface.

### Current Code Under Test
- `process_line()` (line 52-86): Parses individual SSE field lines via `split_once(':')`
- `feed_into()` (line 89-162): Processes stream data, handles CRLF/LF/CR line endings
- `flush()` (line 179-201): Handles incomplete streams
- `SseStream` UTF-8 handling (lines 238-300): Handles incomplete multibyte sequences across chunks

### Specific Risks to Fuzz
1. **UTF-8 edge cases**: Incomplete multibyte sequences split across chunks (lines 254-271). The code accumulates bytes in a leftover buffer and tries to decode — fuzz the boundary between valid/invalid UTF-8.
2. **BOM handling**: BOM stripping at position 0 is explicit (lines 98-102). Test BOM at non-zero positions, multiple BOMs, BOM split across chunks.
3. **Bare CR handling**: Lines 126-132 handle bare CR (\r without \n). The parser must not confuse bare CR with CRLF.
4. **Oversized data fields**: Lines 62-63 append to `current_data` without bounds. Generate events with multi-megabyte data: fields to test memory behavior.
5. **Null bytes in id field**: Already rejected at line 67 — verify this with proptest.
6. **Empty field names**: What happens with `:\n` (colon at start of line)?
7. **Retry field**: The `retry:` field should parse as integer (line 73-78). Fuzz with non-numeric, negative, overflow values.
8. **Duplicate fields**: Multiple `data:` or `event:` fields in one event.

### Implementation Approach
Add new proptest strategies to the existing test module at line 381+:
- `utf8_edge_strategy()`: Generates strings with multibyte chars at chunk boundaries
- `bom_strategy()`: Tests BOM placement variations
- `line_ending_strategy()`: All combinations of \r, \n, \r\n, missing terminators
- `oversized_data_strategy()`: Data fields from 1KB to 10MB
- `retry_field_strategy()`: Non-numeric, negative, overflow retry values

### Invariants to Assert
- Parsing a complete stream in one chunk vs. arbitrary chunk boundaries MUST produce identical events (existing test)
- No panic on any valid or invalid SSE input
- BOM at position 0 is stripped; BOM elsewhere is preserved
- Null bytes in id: field are rejected (event has no id)
- UTF-8 replacement characters appear for invalid byte sequences, never panic

### Files to Modify
- src/sse.rs (add proptest strategies and new test functions to existing test module)

### Acceptance Criteria
- At least 5 new proptest functions targeting the risks above
- Minimum 256 cases per property (up from 64)
- All tests pass with `cargo test sse::tests` on nightly
- Any bugs found are fixed inline

title: Phase 3: Differential Test Runner (compare TS vs Rust output)
description:
# Phase 3: Differential Test Runner (compare TS vs Rust output)

## Purpose
This is the CORE of the conformance system. The differential test runner:
1. Takes an extension path and a mock spec
2. Runs it through the TS runtime (via Bun subprocess)
3. Runs it through the Rust runtime (via library call)
4. Compares the outputs
5. Reports PASS (identical) or FAIL (with diff)

## Why A Runner (Not Just Tests)
Individual test functions are fine for small numbers of extensions. But we have 200+ extensions to test. The runner automates:
- Extension discovery from the validated manifest
- Mock spec selection (per-extension or default)
- Parallel execution (both runtimes concurrently)
- Structured output comparison
- Report generation

## Runner Architecture

```
ConformanceRunner
  |
  +-- for each extension in manifest:
  |     |
  |     +-- Run TS harness (Bun subprocess) -> ts_output.json
  |     +-- Run Rust harness (library call) -> rust_output.json
  |     +-- Compare(ts_output, rust_output) -> diff_result
  |     +-- Record result
  |
  +-- Generate report: {total, passed, failed, skipped, diffs: [...]}
```

## Comparison Strategy
Not just byte-equality. Semantic comparison that:
- Ignores key ordering in JSON objects
- Handles numeric precision differences (f64 vs TS number)
- Normalizes string whitespace where appropriate
- Groups differences by category (registration, event, hostcall)
- Provides human-readable diff output

## Output
- Per-extension: PASS/FAIL with detailed diff
- Aggregate: summary report with pass rate per tier
- Machine-readable: JSON report for CI
- Human-readable: markdown report for review
close_reason: Differential test runner implemented in tests/ext_conformance_diff.rs. Runner: discovers extensions from VALIDATED_MANIFEST.json, runs TS oracle (Bun + load_extension.ts), runs Rust runtime (QuickJS), compares outputs with diff_snapshots(). All 60 official extensions pass.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
DESIGN DECISION: Why Rust integration test (not standalone binary)?

1. CARGO TEST INTEGRATION: Each extension as a #[test] function = automatic parallelism, filtering, and CI integration.
2. LIBRARY ACCESS: Can call Rust extension runtime directly without subprocess overhead.
3. EXISTING PATTERN: conformance_fixtures.rs already uses this pattern with fixture_test! macro.
4. REPORTING: cargo test --format json gives structured output for CI.

The TS side runs as a Bun subprocess because we cannot embed the TS runtime in Rust. This is fine -- the subprocess produces JSON on stdout, which is trivial to parse. The overhead is ~50ms per subprocess spawn, acceptable for 200 extensions.

title: Set up VCR-style test infrastructure for provider streaming
description:
# Set up VCR-style test infrastructure for provider streaming

## Goal
Create infrastructure to record and replay real API responses for provider testing.

## Background
VCR (Video Cassette Recorder) testing pattern:
1. First run: Make real API call, record response to file
2. Subsequent runs: Replay recorded response, no network

This gives us:
- Real response format testing (not simplified mocks)
- Deterministic CI (no flaky network tests)
- Real error response testing (rate limits, auth failures)

## Implementation

### Recording Mode
```rust
// tests/vcr/mod.rs

pub struct VcrRecorder {
    cassette_path: PathBuf,
    mode: VcrMode,
}

pub enum VcrMode {
    Record,    // Make real calls, save to cassette
    Playback,  // Replay from cassette, fail if not found
    Auto,      // Playback if exists, else record
}

impl VcrRecorder {
    pub fn new(test_name: &str) -> Self { ... }

    pub async fn request(&self, req: Request) -> Response {
        match self.mode {
            VcrMode::Record => self.record_and_return(req).await,
            VcrMode::Playback => self.playback(req),
            VcrMode::Auto => ...
        }
    }
}
```

### Cassette Format
```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "test_name": "anthropic_streaming_text",
  "recorded_at": "2026-02-02T...",
  "interactions": [
    {
      "request": {
        "method": "POST",
        "url": "https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages",
        "headers": { ... },
        "body": { ... }
      },
      "response": {
        "status": 200,
        "headers": { ... },
        "body_chunks": [
          "event: message_start\ndata: {...}\n\n",
          "event: content_block_delta\ndata: {...}\n\n",
          ...
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

### SSE Streaming Support
For streaming responses, store individual chunks:
- Each SSE event as separate chunk
- Preserve timing information (optional replay delay)
- Support partial responses (stream interruption)

### Sensitive Data Redaction
```rust
pub fn redact_cassette(cassette: &mut Cassette) {
    // Replace API keys with placeholder
    cassette.redact_header("x-api-key", "[REDACTED]");
    cassette.redact_header("authorization", "[REDACTED]");

    // Replace sensitive response data
    cassette.redact_body_field("api_key", "[REDACTED]");
}
```

## Logging Requirements
- Use TestLogger (bd-3ml) to log record/playback actions.
- Log cassette path, mode, request summary (method/url), and redaction summary.
- On playback mismatch, log expected vs actual interaction keys + diff hints.

## Files to Create
- tests/vcr/mod.rs - VCR infrastructure
- tests/vcr/cassette.rs - Cassette format/loading
- tests/vcr/recorder.rs - Recording logic
- tests/vcr/playback.rs - Playback logic
- tests/fixtures/vcr/ - Directory for cassette files

## Testing the VCR System
- Unit test: Load cassette from JSON
- Unit test: Match request to interaction
- Unit test: Redaction works
- Integration: Record + playback cycle

## Environment Variables
- VCR_MODE=record|playback|auto
- VCR_CASSETTE_DIR=path/to/cassettes

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Recording mode saves cassettes
- [ ] Playback mode replays cassettes
- [ ] SSE streaming supported
- [ ] Sensitive data redacted
- [ ] Record/playback actions logged with detail
- [ ] CI uses playback mode only

title: [gh167] DECISION NEEDED: before_provider_request rewrite hook
description: Most sensitive: exposes fully-built provider body + auth headers to JS per provider on the hot path, needs validated re-ingest of mutated JSON. Event does not exist today (ExtensionEventName list extensions.rs:9712-9741). Blocked on raw-item passthrough for usefulness.
notes:
DECIDED + IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-16). Decision record:
- Event `before_provider_request` added as a KNOWN, actionable (non-informational, 5s budget) ExtensionEventName (ALL=30; drift-guard ordinals updated).
- Exposure: fully-built provider request body + provider/api/model/baseUrl identifiers. AUTH HEADERS ARE DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from the event — consistent with bd-j8sxn's wontfix-by-design (no live creds to sandboxed JS); pi-better-compaction only consumes event.payload.
- Plumbing: StreamOptions.before_provider_request (BeforeProviderRequestHook in provider.rs); agent.rs builds the hook per stream when extensions are active and normalizes handler responses (accepts the rewritten payload object directly per upstream pi, or { payload } wrapped; null/non-object => no rewrite; dispatch failures fail open).
- Firing site: OpenAI Responses provider (incl. Codex mode) — the API surface the blocking consumer (pi-better-compaction native-replay, unblocked by the raw-item passthrough) targets. Other providers can adopt by reading options.before_provider_request the same way (follow-up if a consumer needs it).
- Validated re-ingest: typed round-trip impossible (&'static str fields), so structural validation — rewrite must be an object with non-empty string `model` + `input` array; `stream: true` re-imposed (SSE reader invariant); extension-added fields survive because the validated JSON is sent verbatim; invalid rewrites are logged and the ORIGINAL body is sent (fail-open).
- Conformance: pi-better-compaction fixture summaries + focused-test docs updated (event no longer 'unknown on this host'); scenario suite passes with --features ext-conformance.
Verification (Linux worker, HEAD): 3 new unit tests + openai_responses/extensions-core/agent-integration (186) + extensions_js (199, bridge hashes unaffected) + focused conformance scenario all pass; cargo fmt clean; clippy errors on the -D warnings run are all in untouched files (models.rs/ast_tools.rs/app.rs/interactive-commands baseline owned by concurrent agents).
close_reason: before_provider_request hook implemented: known actionable event, body-only exposure (no auth headers), StreamOptions interceptor wired from agent, fired by OpenAI Responses provider with validated fail-open re-ingest

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: DECISION (2026-08-16, maintainer-delegated): implement before_provider_request with REDACT-AND-REAPPLY. The hook sees the request body (messages/input/params) but auth/credential headers are STRIPPED from what JS sees; JS may rewrite the body (the plugin's real use is replaying the compacted window); the host VALIDATES the returned body and RE-APPLIES the real credentials AFTER the hook, so JS can neither read, strip, nor redirect credentials. Fail-open: hook error/timeout/invalid-payload -> original request proceeds unchanged. Depends on bd-50tx7 (done) for the body to carry replayable items.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: VERIFIED + status (2026-08-16): before_provider_request is implemented and matches the decided redact-and-reapply posture. Security properties independently verified: (1) BeforeProviderRequestEvent (provider.rs:128) exposes provider/api/model/baseUrl/PAYLOAD only — NO headers field, so JS structurally cannot read auth headers; (2) the hook rewrites the JSON BODY only, credentials live in headers attached separately by the provider, so a JS body-rewrite cannot strip/redirect credentials; (3) base_url exposure is safe — gemini keeps the key in a header not the URL (tests assert !url.contains('key=')); (4) validated re-ingest of the rewrite (openai_responses.rs:1487) + fail-open on serialize/reject/handler-error (agent.rs:1962 build hook, normalize at :98). COVERAGE: wired into the openai-responses route only (the plugin's target, where raw-item replay lives); the other 10 providers are fail-open-by-omission (hook simply not invoked). Hook is attached whenever extensions exist and no-ops when no extension registered the event. Test before_provider_request passes. REMAINING (optional, not needed by pi-better-compaction): extend hook invocation to anthropic/openai/gemini/etc. Leaving in_progress for that broader coverage.

title: [TUI-1] Verify and fix Ctrl+P model cycling with scoped-models (bd-21gp)
description:
## Problem

/scoped-models sets model patterns and persists them. Ctrl+P is supposed to cycle through only the scoped models when a scope is active. This may not be fully working (tracked as bd-21gp).

## INVESTIGATION RESULT: cycle_model() Already Works

After reading the codebase, **cycle_model() at line ~8843 already respects model scope**:

```rust
let scope_configured = self.config.enabled_models
    .as_ref()
    .is_some_and(|patterns| !patterns.is_empty());
let use_scope = scope_configured || !self.model_scope.is_empty();
let mut candidates = if use_scope {
    self.model_scope.clone()
} else {
    self.available_models.clone()
};
```

The function:
- Checks both `config.enabled_models` and `self.model_scope`
- If either is non-empty, cycles only through scoped models
- If candidates are empty, shows "No models in scope" message
- Sorts and deduplicates candidates before cycling

### What This Bead Reduces To

Since the core cycling logic already works, this bead focuses on:

1. **Verification**: Run manual testing to confirm Ctrl+P respects scope end-to-end
2. **Edge case review**: Check that scope is correctly populated from /scoped-models patterns
3. **Test coverage**: Add unit tests that lock in the current correct behavior

### Potential Issue to Investigate
- How does `self.model_scope` get populated from `/scoped-models` patterns?
- Does `/scoped-models gpt-4*` correctly filter `self.available_models` into `self.model_scope`?
- Are the glob patterns matched correctly (case sensitivity, wildcard behavior)?
- What happens when available_models changes (e.g., extension adds a new model) -- is scope re-evaluated?

## Files to Verify
- src/interactive.rs: cycle_model() function (line ~8843), /scoped-models handler (lines 9702-9773)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Verify cycle_model() respects model_scope when non-empty (reading confirms: YES)
- [ ] Verify /scoped-models correctly populates model_scope from glob patterns
- [ ] Verify edge case: scope matches nothing -> falls back to all models with warning

title: Design capability prompt UX spec — information architecture and interaction model
description:
# Goal
Design the complete UX specification for capability prompts — what the user sees, what information is displayed, what actions are available, and how decisions flow through the system.

# Background
When an extension requests a sensitive capability (e.g., filesystem write, shell exec, HTTP request), the runtime needs to ask the user for permission. This task designs WHAT that interaction looks like before any code is written. Getting the UX right is critical because:
- Too much information overwhelms (users click "allow all" and defeat the purpose)
- Too little information prevents informed consent
- The prompt frequency matters — showing a dialog for every fs.readFile call is unusable

# Deliverables
1. Prompt content specification:
   - Extension identity: name, version, publisher
   - Capability requested: human-readable description (not raw enum)
   - Scope: what specifically (file path, URL, command)
   - Risk level: visual indicator (green/yellow/red)
   - Decision options: Allow Once / Allow Always / Deny / Deny Always

2. Grouping/batching rules:
   - Batch multiple requests from same capability class (e.g., 5 file reads → single prompt)
   - Never batch across risk levels (dont mix filesystem with shell exec)
   - Allow "Allow all for this session" as a convenience option

3. Decision persistence model:
   - Keyed by (extension_id, capability_type, scope_pattern)
   - Example: ("auto-commit-extension", "exec", "git *") → AllowAlways
   - Scope patterns support globs for paths and commands

4. RPC mode equivalent:
   - JSON-RPC notification format for prompts
   - Response format for decisions
   - Timeout behavior (deny after 30s with no response)

5. Mockup/wireframe for TUI widget (ASCII art acceptable)

# Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Written spec document in docs/capability-prompts.md
- [ ] Covers all 5 hostcall types: tool, exec, http, session, ui
- [ ] Includes risk classification rubric
- [ ] Includes batching algorithm pseudocode
- [ ] Includes RPC JSON schema
- [ ] Reviewed against EXTENSIONS.md spec for consistency
close_reason: Completed spec doc in docs/capability-prompts.md

comments.author: IvoryIsland
comments.text: Drafted full UX spec in docs/capability-prompts.md (risk rubric, batching rules + pseudocode, TUI wireframe, RPC event/command schemas) aligned with EXTENSIONS.md capability taxonomy/policy.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
DESIGN REFINEMENT (from review):

The original spec has 4 decision options: Allow Once / Allow Always / Deny / Deny Always.
After review, we need a 5th: "Allow for this session" — a middle ground between "once" and "always".

Rationale: Users commonly want to approve an extension for the current session without persisting the decision permanently. "Allow Once" is too narrow (re-prompts on every call), "Allow Always" is too broad (persists forever). "Allow for session" is the sweet spot for exploratory use.

Updated decision options:
  [Allow Once] [Allow Session] [Allow Always] [Deny] [Deny Always]

"Allow Session" decisions are stored in-memory only (cleared when session ends).

Make sure the UX spec includes this 5th option with clear visual distinction from the persistent options.

## Gap Analysis (from FEATURE_PARITY.md)

1. **Hostcall ABI** — ACTUALLY COMPLETE (stale doc). dispatch_host_call_shared() routes all 7 capabilities.
2. **Extension UI bridge** — ACTUALLY COMPLETE (stale doc). request_ui/respond_ui cycle wired end-to-end.

title: Impl: WebAssembly bridge for PiJS (QuickJS has no wasm)
description:
# Assumption / Constraint
Assume **QuickJS does not provide WebAssembly** (`globalThis.WebAssembly` absent). We still must run the full pinned sample set, including extensions that ship Emscripten-style JS+WASM bundles.

# Goal
Provide a **PiWasm bridge** so JS-tier extensions can use a **WebAssembly-compatible API** even though the JS engine lacks wasm.

# Genericity constraint (non-negotiable)
- **No per-extension exceptions**: the bridge must not branch on extension id/name.
- Behavior is determined only by: wasm bytes, import object shape, policy/capabilities, and deterministic runtime configuration.
- Sample set is only used to define the **minimum required semantics**, not to justify one-off hacks.

# Strategy (hybrid)
- Use **wasmtime** (same engine as Tier A WASM host) to execute wasm.
- Expose a minimal `globalThis.WebAssembly` polyfill (or equivalent injected module) that is **generically compatible** with common JS+WASM glue patterns.
- All imports that represent side effects must route through **connector hostcalls** and therefore capabilities/logging.

# Scope / Deliverables
## WebAssembly JS surface (subset)
- `WebAssembly.instantiate(bytes, imports)`
- `WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(resp, imports)` (if needed; otherwise extc rewrite to non-streaming)
- `WebAssembly.compile(bytes)` / `WebAssembly.Module`
- `WebAssembly.Instance` exports behavior used by typical glue code
- `WebAssembly.Memory` with `.buffer` semantics compatible with standard glue patterns
- Traps/errors mapped to actionable Pi errors + structured logs

## Import object handling
- Support JS functions as wasm imports with deterministic call ordering.
- Restrict / gate imports that imply OS access.

## Caching + perf
- Cache compiled wasm modules keyed by sha256(bytes + wasmtime_version + policy_version).
- Minimize cross-boundary copies; measure and optimize boundary overhead.

# Security constraints
- Enforce memory/table limits per extension policy.
- Ensure wasm cannot access host OS except via explicit connector imports.
- Structured logs: every instantiate/compile includes extension_id + artifact_id + elapsed + limits.

# Acceptance (hard)
- Any **wasm-using JS-tier artifact** in the pinned sample set runs end-to-end **without manual source edits** using this bridge (or Tier A when appropriate).
- The E2E harness passes **16/16** sample extensions.
- The implementation remains **generic** (no extension-id special-casing), enforced by tests/review.

# Tests (required)
- Unit tests: wasm compile/instantiate, memory growth boundaries, import call routing, trap mapping.
- Conformance fixtures for wasm-in-js scenarios with deterministic traces.
- Security tests: denied connector imports, exceeded limits, malicious wasm.

# Dependencies
- Must compose with unified capability model (bd-2hr) and dispatcher enforcement (bd-h04).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Scope in description implemented fully with no feature loss
- [ ] Unit tests cover core success/failure + edge cases for this bead
- [ ] Integration/E2E script exercises the end-to-end path (or explicitly marks N/A with rationale) and emits detailed JSONL logs + artifacts per bd-4u9

- [ ] Docs/fixtures updated if behavior or UX changes

title: Workstream: /share + /copy Parity (gist + clipboard)
description:
# Goal
Match legacy `/copy` and `/share` behaviors in interactive mode.

# Legacy Behavior
## `/copy`
- Copies the last assistant message to clipboard.
- If nothing to copy: show an error.

## `/share`
Legacy implementation (`legacy .../interactive-mode.ts`):
1) Ensure `gh` is installed and logged in (`gh auth status`).
2) Export session to a temp HTML file.
3) Show a cancellable loader UI while creating a **secret gist**:
   - `gh gist create --public=false <tmpFile>`
4) Parse gist URL from stdout and extract gist ID.
5) Compute viewer URL via `PI_SHARE_VIEWER_URL` (default `https://buildwithpi.ai/session/`) and show:
   - `Share URL: <viewer>#<gistId>`
   - `Gist: <gistUrl>`

# Current Rust State (Gap)
- `/copy` is feature-gated and currently just reports “clipboard not enabled”.
- `/share` only writes an HTML file to temp and prints the path; no gist.

# Scope / Deliverables
- Implement cross-platform clipboard copy for `/copy` with actionable error messages.
- Implement gist-based `/share` with:
  - `gh` presence/auth checks
  - cancellable UI/loader
  - robust gist ID parsing
  - env var `PI_SHARE_VIEWER_URL` support
  - cleanup of temp files

# Testing
- Add tests that validate:
  - gist ID parsing
  - error messaging when `gh` missing or not logged in
  - `/copy` behavior with and without clipboard support (mocking where needed)

# Dependencies
- Keybinding layer is helpful for cancellation UX but not required.

## Acceptance Criteria
[ ] /copy copies last assistant message to clipboard
[ ] /share creates private gist via gh and prints viewer URL
[ ] PI_SHARE_VIEWER_URL supported
[ ] Share operation is cancellable and cleans up temp files

title: FUZZ-V2: Phase 2 Validation Suite — Build all harnesses, 60s smoke run each, structured pass/fail report

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## FUZZ-V2: Phase 2 Validation Suite

### Purpose
After all P2 harnesses and seed corpora are built, this validation suite:
1. Builds ALL fuzz harnesses (cargo fuzz build)
2. Runs each for 60 seconds (smoke test)
3. Generates a structured pass/fail report with detailed logging

### What This Produces

A script that:
```bash
#\!/bin/bash
# scripts/validate_fuzz_p2.sh
set -euo pipefail

TARGETS=$(cargo fuzz list 2>/dev/null)
REPORT_FILE="fuzz/reports/p2_validation_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).json"
RESULTS=()

echo "Building all fuzz targets..."
cargo fuzz build 2>&1 | tee fuzz/reports/build.log
BUILD_STATUS=$?

for target in $TARGETS; do
    echo "Running $target for 60s..."
    START=$(date +%s%N)
    cargo fuzz run "$target" -- -max_total_time=60 2>&1 | tee "fuzz/reports/${target}.log"
    EXIT=$?
    END=$(date +%s%N)
    ELAPSED_MS=$(( (END - START) / 1000000 ))
    
    # Count corpus growth
    CORPUS_COUNT=$(ls fuzz/corpus/$target/ 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
    
    RESULTS+=('{"target":"$target","exit_code":$EXIT,"time_ms":$ELAPSED_MS,"corpus_count":$CORPUS_COUNT}')
done

# Generate JSON report...
```

### Report Format
```json
{
  "phase": "P2",
  "timestamp": "2026-02-15T...",
  "build_status": "pass",
  "targets": [
    {
      "name": "fuzz_sse_parser",
      "status": "pass",
      "exit_code": 0,
      "time_ms": 62341,
      "corpus_size": 847,
      "new_corpus_entries": 234,
      "seed_corpus_size": 15,
      "crashes_found": 0,
      "log_file": "fuzz/reports/fuzz_sse_parser.log"
    }
  ],
  "summary": {
    "total_targets": 14,
    "passed": 14,
    "failed": 0,
    "total_corpus_growth": 1234,
    "total_time_ms": 873000
  }
}
```

### Logging Requirements
- Per-target: name, build status, run status, timing, corpus growth, crash count
- Build log: full cargo fuzz build output captured
- Run log: full libfuzzer output per target (includes coverage stats, new units found)
- Summary: total targets, pass/fail counts, total time, any crashes
- All logs persisted in fuzz/reports/ directory

### Crash Handling
If a target crashes during the 60s smoke run:
1. The crash input is saved to fuzz/artifacts/<target>/
2. The report marks that target as 'crashed'
3. The script continues to the next target (don't stop on first crash)
4. Final exit code is non-zero if any target crashed

### Acceptance Criteria
- Script builds all fuzz targets successfully
- Each target runs for at least 60 seconds without hanging
- JSON report is generated with per-target results
- All logs are persisted in fuzz/reports/
- Exit code reflects overall pass/fail
- Script handles crashes gracefully (continues to next target)
- Documented in fuzz/README.md

- PiWasm (WASM component model)
- Protocol messages (`ExtensionMessage` `host_call` -> `host_result`) for future Tier-C / harness use

# Current State (Observed in Code)
- Hostcall ABI types + schema validation exist in `src/extensions.rs`:
  - `ExtensionMessage` / `ExtensionBody::{HostCall, HostResult}`
  - `validate_host_call()` and `validate_host_result()`
  - `required_capability_for_host_call()` (capability derivation)
- A **shared hostcall dispatcher already exists**: `dispatch_host_call_shared()` in `src/extensions.rs`.
  - It does validation, capability derivation, policy (incl. prompt cache), timeouts, and structured logging.
  - It is **not yet wired into the actual runtime entrypoints** (JS pump + WASM hostcall + protocol message routing).
- PiJS runtime today uses an internal queue (`HostcallRequest` from `src/extensions_js.rs`) and a separate dispatch path in `src/extensions.rs` (`pump_js_runtime_once` -> `dispatch_hostcall_*`).
- PiWasm runtime today dispatches hostcalls inside `src/extensions.rs` under `mod wasm_host` (`HostState::call`) with its own flow.

# Concrete Gaps (What’s Still Missing)
1. **Adoption**: JS + WASM runtime paths must both call `dispatch_host_call_shared()` (single enforcement point).
2. **Protocol adapter**: no runtime/library adapter currently accepts an `ExtensionMessage(type=host_call)` and emits `host_result`.
3. **Strict taxonomy everywhere**: any non-taxonomy JS/WASM codes (e.g., `tool_error`, `SHUTDOWN`, `CANCELLED`) must be eliminated or deterministically mapped to:
   - `timeout | denied | io | invalid_request | internal`
4. **Canonical params shape**: JS + WASM must hash *the same* canonical `{method, params}` for equivalent calls. In practice this means aligning the session/ui/events params shape (flattened `op + args` vs wrapped `{op,args}`) so parity tests can be meaningful.
5. **Spec compliance**: `host_result.output` must always be an object (use `{}` on error), and `error` must be present iff `is_error=true`.

# Why This Matters
- **Security**: capability decisions must not diverge by runtime; one enforcement point prevents "JS allows what WASM denies" classes of bugs.
- **Compatibility**: extensions will only “just work” if hostcalls behave consistently.
- **Conformance**: the harness needs a stable ABI surface (payload/result + logs) to diff and diagnose deterministically.

# Deliverables (This Workstream)
- Wire JS runtime hostcalls through `dispatch_host_call_shared()`.
- Wire WASM `host.call()` through `dispatch_host_call_shared()`.
- Implement a protocol adapter `ExtensionMessage host_call -> host_result` that uses the shared dispatcher.
- Add parity tests ensuring JS/WASM/protocol are behavior-identical for canonical hostcalls.
- Contain or eliminate duplicate hostcall ABI type definitions to prevent drift.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] JS, WASM, and protocol adapter all enforce capability derivation + policy + timeout in the same place.
- [ ] Only taxonomy codes are observable at the ABI boundary.
- [ ] `HostResultPayload` is schema-valid: `output` is always an object; `error` iff `is_error`.
- [ ] Deterministic logs are emitted (`host_call.start/end`, `policy.decision`) with `params_hash` only (no raw params).
- [ ] Table-driven parity tests fail on any JS/WASM drift.

title: Hostcall ABI: Implement Shared Dispatcher (HostCallPayload -> HostResultPayload)
description:
# Goal
Make `dispatch_host_call_shared()` (in `src/extensions.rs`) the **single source of truth** for hostcall execution, and harden it so it is:
- **Spec compliant** (schema-valid `host_result`)
- **Strict taxonomy** only (`timeout|denied|io|invalid_request|internal`)
- **Deterministic** (params hashing + logs)
- **Safe** (capability derivation is core-defined; mismatch => `invalid_request`)

This bead is the foundation that unblocks wiring the shared dispatcher into:
- JS runtime (`bd-1uy.1.3`)
- WASM runtime (`bd-nom.1`)
- Protocol adapter (`bd-1uy.1.2`)

# Current State (Observed)
- `dispatch_host_call_shared()` exists and already does:
  - `validate_host_call()`
  - `required_capability_for_host_call()` derivation
  - policy evaluation + prompt-cache integration
  - timeout wrapping via `asupersync::time::timeout`
  - structured logs: `host_call.start`, `policy.decision`, `host_call.end`
- BUT there are correctness/spec gaps that must be fixed *before* it can be the canonical ABI:

## Gap A: `host_result.output` must be an object
- `validate_host_result()` requires `output` is an object.
- The shared helpers currently return `output: Value::Null` on errors.
- Spec (`EXTENSIONS.md` §3.2) explicitly says output is an object and may be empty on error.

### Fix
- Change shared error constructors to always use `json!({})` as output.
- Add regression tests ensuring shared dispatcher results always pass `validate_host_result()`.

## Gap B: Non-taxonomy internal codes must map deterministically
- Internal dispatchers can currently emit non-taxonomy `HostcallOutcome::Error.code` values like:
  - `tool_error`
  - `SHUTDOWN`
  - `CANCELLED`
- Shared dispatcher must map these to taxonomy in a principled way.

### Proposed mapping (v1)
- `tool_error` -> `io` (default), unless there is a clear `invalid_request` signal
- `SHUTDOWN`/`shutdown` -> `internal` (host lifecycle), not `denied`
- `CANCELLED` -> `timeout` (closest user-facing semantics) OR `internal` (if we want to reserve `timeout` strictly for wall deadlines). Choose once, document, test.

## Gap C: Canonical `params` shape for session/ui/events
- Cross-runtime parity requires that the canonical `{method, params}` is identical between JS and WASM for the same logical call.
- WASM hostcalls treat params as a **flattened** object: `{ op: "set_model", provider: "...", modelId: "..." }`.
- JS hostcalls today are split:
  - dispatch uses `payload` (args only)
  - hashing uses `{ op, args }`

### Fix
- Define and enforce the canonical params shape in the shared dispatcher contract:
  - `tool`: `{ name, input }`
  - `exec`: `{ cmd, args?, options? }`
  - `http`: `{ url, method, headers?, body?, body_bytes?, timeout_ms? }`
  - `session/ui/events`: `{ op, ...args_fields }` (flattened)
- The wiring beads (`bd-1uy.1.3`, `bd-nom.1`) must convert their runtime-native requests into this canonical shape before calling `dispatch_host_call_shared()`.

# Tests (Must-Have)
## Unit tests (table-driven)
- Validation:
  - empty call_id -> `invalid_request`
  - unknown method -> `invalid_request`
  - capability mismatch -> `invalid_request`
- Policy:
  - strict deny -> `denied`
  - permissive allow -> success
- Timeouts:
  - timeout_ms triggers `timeout` and sets `error.retryable=true`
- Method coverage (happy-path + one failure each):
  - tool
  - exec
  - http
  - session
  - ui
  - events
  - env
  - log

## Logging assertions
- Emits `host_call.start` and `host_call.end`
- Includes `runtime`, `call_id`, `extension_id`, `capability`, `method`, `params_hash`, and `duration_ms`
- Never logs raw params (hash only)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All `dispatch_host_call_shared()` outputs pass `validate_host_result()`.
- [ ] All error codes are mapped into the fixed taxonomy.
- [ ] Canonical params shape is documented (in-bead) and enforced by tests.
- [ ] Shared dispatcher is ready to be called by JS/WASM/protocol wiring beads without bespoke policy/timeout/logging.

title: Hostcall ABI dispatcher: Canonical params shape + params_hash parity contract
description:
# Goal
Define and enforce the **canonical hostcall params shape** used for:
- capability derivation (`required_capability_for_host_call`)
- `params_hash` computation
- cross-runtime parity tests (JS/WASM/protocol)

This eliminates a class of “same logical call, different hash/logs” drift.

# Current State / Drift
- WASM hostcalls already treat params for `session/ui/events` as *flattened*:
  - `{ op: "set_model", provider: "...", modelId: "..." }`
- JS hostcalls currently have split representations:
  - dispatch uses args-only payload
  - hashing uses `{ op, args }`

Shared dispatcher expects `HostCallPayload.params` to be the canonical representation.

# Canonical Params Shapes (v1)
- `tool`: `{ name: <tool_name>, input: <tool_input_object> }`
- `exec`: `{ cmd: <string>, args?: <array>, options?: <object>, ... }`
  - accept legacy `command` alias for cmd (normalize)
- `http`: `{ url, method?, headers?, body?, body_bytes?, timeout_ms? }`
- `fs`: `{ op: <read|write|list|stat|mkdir|delete>, path: <string>, ... }`
- `env`: `{ name?: <string>, names?: <string[]> }`
- `session/ui/events`: `{ op: <string>, ...args_fields }` (flattened)
- `log`: `{ level?: <string>, message?: <string>, data?: <any> }`

# Implementation Scope
- Add a helper that can build canonical params for session/ui/events from `(op, args)`:
  - flatten object args into top-level keys
  - preserve non-object args by storing under a reserved key (e.g. `payload`) if needed
- Update/ensure `shared_params_hash()` hashes `{method, params}` using canonicalized JSON (sorted object keys, stable arrays).
- Document the contract in-code near the dispatcher and in-bead so future changes are deliberate.

# Tests
- Table-driven tests verifying that:
  - canonicalization produces stable JSON for equivalent inputs
  - params_hash matches between JS and WASM for the same logical call
  - validate_host_call still succeeds for canonical payloads

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Canonical params shapes are implemented and documented.
- [ ] JS/WASM parity tests can rely on identical params_hash for canonical calls.

title: Hostcall ABI dispatcher: Eliminate non-taxonomy error codes (tool_error/SHUTDOWN/CANCELLED)
description:
# Goal
Ensure the shared hostcall dispatcher is the **single enforcement point** for the fixed v1 error taxonomy:
- `timeout`
- `denied`
- `io`
- `invalid_request`
- `internal`

No other error codes may escape at the ABI boundary (JS, WASM, protocol).

# Current State
- Lower-level JS/WASM dispatch helpers can emit non-taxonomy strings in `HostcallOutcome::Error.code`:
  - `tool_error`
  - `SHUTDOWN`
  - `CANCELLED`
- `outcome_to_host_result()` currently maps unknown codes to `internal`, and maps `shutdown` to `denied`.

# Scope
1. Define the canonical mapping for legacy/internal codes:
   - `tool_error` -> `io` (default)
   - `shutdown`/`SHUTDOWN` -> `internal` (host lifecycle)
   - `cancelled`/`CANCELLED` -> `timeout` or `internal` (choose once; document)
2. Update `outcome_to_host_result()` accordingly.
3. Where practical, remove the sources of these codes in the underlying dispatchers:
   - tool execution errors should directly choose taxonomy codes
   - manager shutdown should return a deterministic taxonomy code

# Tests
- Unit tests:
  - force each legacy code path and assert mapped `HostCallErrorCode` is as expected.
  - assert no code outside taxonomy appears in emitted `HostResultPayload.error.code`.
- Parity tests (`bd-1uy.1.4`) must fail if any runtime emits a non-taxonomy code.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Shared dispatcher maps all known legacy codes into taxonomy deterministically.
- [ ] Unknown codes are treated as `internal` and logged (optional warning) so drift is visible.

title: Hostcall ABI: Wire ExtensionMessage host_call -> host_result (Protocol Adapter)
description:
# Goal
Make the protocol types in `src/extensions.rs` actionable by implementing a runtime/library **protocol adapter** that:

1. Accepts `ExtensionMessage(type=host_call)`
2. Dispatches via `dispatch_host_call_shared()`
3. Emits `ExtensionMessage(type=host_result)`

This turns `host_call`/`host_result` into a real ABI surface that can be used for:
- harness testing (treat hostcall ABI as an artifact)
- future Tier-C process IPC runtimes
- debugging/replay tooling (log-driven reproduction)

# Current State
- `ExtensionMessage::parse_and_validate()` exists.
- Hostcall validation exists (`validate_host_call`, `validate_host_result`).
- Shared dispatcher exists (`dispatch_host_call_shared`) but is not exposed through protocol message routing.

# Scope
- Provide a small, decoupled API surface (library function), not necessarily a user-facing CLI:
  - `async fn handle_extension_message(ctx: HostCallContext<'_>, msg: ExtensionMessage) -> Vec<ExtensionMessage>`
- v1 supported message types:
  - `host_call` -> `host_result`
- For other message types:
  - either return a single `error` message, OR
  - return a `host_result` with `invalid_request` (pick one and document)

# Required Semantics
- Must preserve `call_id` exactly.
- Must emit schema-valid `HostResultPayload`:
  - `output` is always an object (`{}` on error)
  - `error` present iff `is_error=true`
- Error codes must be taxonomy-only.
- Message `id` rules:
  - Do not reuse incoming message id for the response.
  - Generate a deterministic response id format (e.g. `"host_result:<call_id>"` or `"msg-<uuid>"` depending on determinism needs).
  - Include `context`/correlation only in logs, not in protocol payload unless spec requires.

# Streaming-Ready Design (Future-Proof)
- Return `Vec<ExtensionMessage>` so we can later emit multiple `host_result` chunks (`chunk.index`, `chunk.is_last`).
- Initial implementation emits exactly 1 message with `chunk=None`.

# Tests
- Unit tests:
  - parse+validate `host_call` JSON -> adapter -> `host_result` validates (including `validate_host_result`).
  - capability mismatch -> `invalid_request`.
  - denied-by-policy -> `denied`.
  - timeout -> `timeout` with retryable flag.
- Harness test:
  - use protocol adapter to simulate an external runtime calling hostcalls and compare logs/outputs to JS/WASM parity test suite (`bd-1uy.1.4`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `ExtensionMessage(type=host_call)` round-trips through adapter to a valid `host_result`.
- [ ] No bespoke policy/timeout/logging exists in the adapter; it is a thin wrapper around the shared dispatcher.
- [ ] Adapter can be used by future process-based extension runners without rewriting hostcall semantics.

title: Hostcall ABI: JS Runtime Uses Shared Dispatcher + Taxonomy
description:
# Goal
Refactor PiJS hostcalls so **all JS-origin hostcalls** execute through the shared hostcall dispatcher:

`HostcallRequest (PiJS)` -> canonical `HostCallPayload` -> `dispatch_host_call_shared()` -> `HostResultPayload` -> Promise completion

This removes JS/WASM drift and enforces the fixed taxonomy.

# Current State (Observed)
- PiJS enqueues `HostcallRequest` from `src/extensions_js.rs`.
- The runtime pump (`pump_js_runtime_once` in `src/extensions.rs`) drains the queue and currently dispatches via `dispatch_hostcall()` / `dispatch_hostcall_allowed()` which:
  - returns `HostcallOutcome`
  - may emit non-taxonomy error codes (`tool_error`, `SHUTDOWN`, `CANCELLED`)
  - logs separately from the shared dispatcher
- Shared dispatcher exists: `dispatch_host_call_shared()`.

# Scope
1. **Canonical payload conversion** (JS request -> HostCallPayload)
   - Set `call_id` from request.
   - Set `method` from request kind:
     - Tool -> `"tool"`
     - Exec -> `"exec"`
     - Http -> `"http"`
     - Session -> `"session"`
     - Ui -> `"ui"`
     - Events -> `"events"`
   - Set `capability` to the derived capability (core-defined):
     - tool name mapping per `required_capability_for_host_call()`
     - other methods use method name (`exec/http/session/ui/events/...`)
   - Set `timeout_ms` from existing JS hostcall timeout extraction (`js_hostcall_timeout_ms`).

2. **Canonical `params` shape alignment** (critical for parity)
   - `tool`: `{ "name": <tool>, "input": <payload> }`
   - `exec`: `{ "cmd": <cmd>, ...payload_fields }` (ensure `args/options` propagate)
   - `http`: params is the request object (existing)
   - `session/ui/events`: flatten op + args into a single object:
     - `{ "op": <op>, ...args_fields }`
     - This matches the WASM hostcall params convention used by `HostState::call()` today.

3. **Dispatch + completion**
   - Build `HostCallContext` with:
     - `runtime = "js"`
     - `extension_id = request.extension_id`
     - `policy`, `tools`, `http`, `manager` (for prompt cache + session/ui/events)
     - `fs/env_allowlist` (only if JS runtime should expose them; otherwise None)
   - Call `dispatch_host_call_shared()`.
   - Convert `HostResultPayload` -> `HostcallOutcome` for Promise completion:
     - success: `HostcallOutcome::Success(result.output)`
     - error: `HostcallOutcome::Error { code: taxonomy_code, message }`

4. **Eliminate old paths**
   - Remove or quarantine the older `dispatch_hostcall*` codepaths that bypass shared dispatcher.
   - Keep test interceptors (if needed) as a deliberate hook *around* the shared dispatcher rather than a parallel implementation.

# Required Semantics
- Preserve deterministic scheduler invariants (no synchronous reentrancy): completions must still be delivered as macrotasks.
- JS-visible error codes must be taxonomy-only.
- Logs must remain deterministic and must not include raw params (hash-only).

# Tests
- Unit tests:
  - tool failure maps to taxonomy (no `tool_error`)
  - manager shutdown path maps to taxonomy (no `SHUTDOWN`)
  - unknown tool name -> `invalid_request`
  - denied-by-policy -> `denied`
  - session/setModel input validation -> `invalid_request`
- Determinism tests:
  - confirm that params_hash matches WASM for identical logical calls (requires canonical params shape)
- Conformance harness smoke:
  - run a JS extension that exercises session/ui/events and assert logs + outcomes match fixtures.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] PiJS hostcalls do not bypass `dispatch_host_call_shared()`.
- [ ] JS Promise rejection codes are taxonomy-only.
- [ ] `params_hash` parity holds for canonical calls vs WASM/protocol.
- [ ] Existing PiJS scheduler/event-loop conformance tests remain green.

In src/extensions.rs, eliminated non-taxonomy JS hostcall error codes in runtime path: SHUTDOWN -> denied (session/ui/events when manager unavailable), tool_error -> io (tool execution failure), cancelled -> timeout (stream cancellation). In src/extension_dispatcher.rs, added protocol host_call->host_result adapter with taxonomy mapping and object-output normalization. title: Hostcall ABI: Cross-Runtime Parity Tests (JS/WASM/Protocol)
description:
# Goal
Add tests that prove the **hostcall ABI is stable and identical** across:
- PiJS hostcalls (JS)
- PiWasm hostcalls (WASM)
- protocol adapter (`ExtensionMessage host_call -> host_result`)

# Why
Without parity tests, JS/WASM drift can regress silently and break:
- security claims (policy enforcement)
- compatibility claims (extensions “just work”)
- conformance harness reliability (logs/ABI change without detection)

# Scope
Create a canonical set of `HostCallPayload` examples and assert:
1. **Outputs** match across all 3 paths:
   - same `is_error`
   - same taxonomy error code (if error)
   - same method-specific output shape on success
2. **Schema validity**:
   - every produced `HostResultPayload` passes `validate_host_result()`
   - `output` is always an object (`{}` on error)
   - `error` present iff `is_error=true`
3. **Logs** (structured evidence ledger):
   - `host_call.start` and `host_call.end` exist
   - include `runtime`, `capability`, `method`, `params_hash`, `duration_ms`
   - never include raw params (hash only)
4. **Params hash parity**:
   - for each canonical call, JS and WASM compute the same `params_hash`
   - this requires enforcing the canonical params shapes (flattened session/ui/events)

# Canonical Cases (Minimum)
- `tool`:
  - grep success (read)
  - unknown tool invalid_request
  - tool error mapping (ensure taxonomy)
- `exec`:
  - invalid args shape -> invalid_request
  - timeout path -> timeout
- `http`:

title: Hostcall ABI: Consolidate Duplicate HostCallPayload/HostResultPayload Types
description:
# Goal
Eliminate (or strictly contain) duplicated hostcall ABI type definitions so the ABI cannot drift:
- `crate::extensions::{HostCallPayload, HostResultPayload, HostStreamChunk, ...}`
- `crate::connectors::{HostCallPayload, HostResultPayload, HostStreamChunk, ...}`

# Why This Is Not Cosmetic
Right now, the two type graphs are **not identical** (real drift already exists):
- `extensions::HostStreamChunk` includes `backpressure` fields; `connectors::HostStreamChunk` does not.
- error helpers in `connectors` produce `output: null` on errors, while protocol validation requires `output` is an object.

If we keep two competing definitions, we will eventually ship a protocol/schema mismatch.

# Scope
1. Choose a single canonical home for the ABI structs/enums.
   - Recommended: make `extensions::*` canonical, since it is tied directly to `ExtensionMessage` protocol/schema.

2. Make the non-canonical module:
   - re-export the canonical types, OR
   - become a thin newtype wrapper with explicit conversions.

3. Fix helper constructors to be spec-compliant everywhere:
   - `host_result_err*` must set `output: {}` (object), not `null`.
   - Ensure `error` presence matches `is_error`.

4. Update `HttpConnector` and any other connector code to use canonical types.

# Tests
- Compile-time:
  - ensure only one canonical type is used across modules (no parallel structs).
- Runtime:
  - round-trip serialize/deserialize between connector boundary and protocol boundary.
  - assert that any `HostResultPayload` produced by helpers passes `validate_host_result()`.
- Drift sentinel:
  - a unit test that asserts the JSON Schema (`docs/schema/extension_protocol.json`) matches the Rust type serialization shape (including backpressure fields).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] There is exactly one source-of-truth for hostcall ABI structs/enums.
- [ ] All helper constructors return schema-valid payloads.
- [ ] All call sites compile and tests pass.
- [ ] A drift sentinel test would fail if future fields are added to one side but not the other.
