title: Extension registry protocol spec and local index schema
description:
# Goal
Design the extension registry protocol — how extension metadata is fetched from remote sources (GitHub, npm), stored locally, and queried for search/browse operations.

# Background
The package manager (src/package_manager.rs) already knows how to install from npm and GitHub. But there is no structured index of AVAILABLE extensions. Users must know exact package names. This task designs the metadata layer that enables discovery.

# Deliverables

1. Remote data sources:
   - GitHub: Search GitHub repos with topic "pi-extension" via GitHub API
   - npm: Search npm registry for packages with "pi-extension" keyword
   - Curated list: static JSON manifest in a Pi-maintained repo (for quality-vetted extensions)

2. Local index schema (SQLite or JSON):
   {
     "version": 1,
     "last_refreshed": "2026-01-15T10:30:00Z",
     "extensions": [
       {
         "id": "auto-commit-on-exit",
         "name": "Auto Commit on Exit",
         "description": "Automatically commits changes when Pi session ends",
         "version": "1.2.0",
         "source": { "type": "npm", "package": "@user/pi-auto-commit" },
         "author": "username",
         "license": "MIT",
         "tags": ["git", "automation", "lifecycle"],
         "conformance_tier": 1,
         "pi_version_range": ">=0.5.0",
         "downloads_30d": 1500,
         "last_updated": "2026-01-10T00:00:00Z",
         "readme_url": "https://...",
         "repository_url": "https://..."
       }
     ]
   }

3. Refresh strategy:
   - On first "pi search": fetch and cache index
   - Auto-refresh if cache older than 24 hours
   - Manual refresh: "pi update-index"
   - Incremental: only fetch new/updated since last refresh

4. Search algorithm:
   - Fuzzy text match on name + description + tags
   - Weighted scoring: name match (3x) > tag match (2x) > description match (1x)
   - Sort by relevance * quality_signal (conformance tier, downloads)

# Files to Create/Modify
- New: src/extension_index.rs (index management, search, refresh)
- src/package_manager.rs: Wire index into install flow
- src/config.rs: Add index cache path

# Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Schema documented in docs/extension-registry.md
- [ ] Index refresh from GitHub + npm sources works
- [ ] Fuzzy search returns relevant results
- [ ] Cache invalidation after 24h
- [ ] Index stored in ~/.pi/agent/extension-index.json
close_reason: Completed

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
DESIGN REFINEMENT (from review):

The registry spec MUST be offline-first:
1. Ship a bundled seed index with the Pi binary (embedded at compile time)
2. First search uses seed index if no network (no "please wait" on first run)
3. Background refresh when network becomes available
4. Stale cache warning ("Index is 7 days old, run pi update-index to refresh")
5. Never fail on network error — always fall back to cached/seed index

This matters because:
- New users running pi search for the first time shouldnt wait for a network fetch
- Users on restricted networks (corp firewalls, planes) should still discover extensions
- The seed index can be updated with each Pi release (60+ known extensions)

title: pi search CLI command — search available extensions by keyword
description:
# Goal
Implement the "pi search <query>" CLI command that searches the extension index and displays results in a rich terminal table.

# Background
This is the primary user-facing discovery command. It queries the local extension index (built by the registry protocol spec task) and presents results in a scannable format.

# Usage
  pi search git          # Search for git-related extensions
  pi search "auto commit" # Phrase search
  pi search --tag provider # Filter by tag
  pi search --sort downloads # Sort by popularity
  pi search --limit 20     # Limit results

# Output Format (rich_rust table)
  Name              Version  Description                        Downloads  Tier
  auto-commit       1.2.0    Auto commit on session exit         1,500     T1
  git-branch-hook   0.5.0    Switch branches via /git command      890     T2
  git-stats         2.0.1    Show git statistics in session        650     T1

  3 extensions found. Install with: pi install <name>

# Implementation Plan
1. Add "search" subcommand to clap CLI (src/cli.rs)
2. In main.rs, route to search handler
3. Search handler:
   a. Load or refresh extension index
   b. Apply fuzzy search with query
   c. Apply filters (--tag, --tier, --source)
   d. Sort results (--sort: relevance (default), downloads, name, updated)
   e. Render rich_rust table with columns: Name, Version, Description, Downloads, Tier
   f. Print install hint at bottom

4. Auto-refresh:
   - If index doesnt exist or is >24h old, refresh before searching
   - Show "Refreshing extension index..." message during refresh
   - Cache refreshed index for subsequent searches

# Files to Modify
- src/cli.rs: Add search subcommand with args
- src/main.rs: Route search subcommand
- New: src/extension_search.rs or add to extension_index.rs

# Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] "pi search git" returns relevant results
- [ ] Results sorted by relevance by default
- [ ] --tag filter works
- [ ] --sort flag works (relevance, downloads, name, updated)
- [ ] Rich table output with colors

title: Quality signals computation and display for extension discovery
description:
# Goal
Compute and display quality signals for extensions in search results and info views, helping users assess extension reliability before installing.

# Background
Not all extensions are equal. Some are well-tested (conformance tier 1), actively maintained, and widely used. Others are experimental, abandoned, or incompatible. Quality signals help users make informed decisions — like star ratings on app stores or crate download counts on crates.io.

# Quality Signals

1. Conformance Tier (from Pi conformance test suite):
   - T1: Fully tested, all assertions pass
   - T2: Mostly tested, minor issues
   - T3: Partially tested, some features fail
   - Untested: No conformance data

2. Maintenance Status:
   - Active: Updated within 90 days
   - Maintained: Updated within 1 year
   - Stale: Not updated in 1+ year
   - Abandoned: Not updated in 2+ years, no response to issues

3. Compatibility Score (from compat scanner):
   - Green: 100% compatible, no Node.js dependencies
   - Yellow: 90%+ compatible, minor shim gaps
   - Red: <90% compatible, significant issues

4. Popularity Metrics:
   - npm downloads (30d) if from npm
   - GitHub stars if from GitHub
   - Install count from Pi telemetry (future)

5. Composite Quality Score (0-100):
   - 40% conformance tier
   - 25% maintenance status
   - 20% compatibility score
   - 15% popularity metrics

# Display Format
In search results table: colored badge (green/yellow/red) + numeric score
In info view: detailed breakdown of each signal

# Implementation Plan
1. Compute signals at index refresh time
2. Store in extension index entry
3. Sort by composite score in search results (default)
4. Display badge in search table column
5. Detailed breakdown in pi info output

# Files to Modify
- Extension index module: Add quality computation
- Search/info display code: Add quality columns/sections

# Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All 5 signal types computed for indexed extensions
- [ ] Composite score calculated with documented weights
- [ ] Quality badge visible in search results
- [ ] Detailed breakdown in pi info
- [ ] Score updates on index refresh

description:
# Goal
End-to-end test suite for the extension discovery system, validating search, info display, index management, and edge cases like offline mode and stale caches.

# Test Categories

## 1. Index Management Tests (8+ tests)
- First-run: index created from scratch (mock GitHub + npm responses via VCR)
- Index refresh: stale index (>24h) triggers auto-refresh
- Incremental update: only new/modified extensions fetched
- Cache corruption: graceful recovery from malformed index file
- Offline mode: search works on cached index when network unavailable
- Manual refresh: pi update-index forces full refresh
- Index versioning: migration from v1 to v2 schema
- Concurrent access: two pi instances dont corrupt index

## 2. Search Tests (10+ tests)
- Exact name match: pi search "auto-commit" → returns exact match first
- Fuzzy match: pi search "git comit" → returns git commit extensions
- Tag filter: pi search --tag provider → only provider extensions
- Category filter: pi search --category automation
- Sort by downloads: pi search --sort downloads → descending order
- Sort by name: pi search --sort name → alphabetical
- Limit: pi search --limit 5 → exactly 5 results
- Empty results: pi search "xyznonexistent" → helpful message
- Special characters: pi search "c++" → handles special chars
- Long query: pi search "an extension that helps with git management" → reasonable results

## 3. Info Display Tests (6+ tests)
- Basic info: pi info auto-commit → shows metadata panel
- README rendering: README markdown rendered as terminal output
- Missing README: graceful fallback message
- Capabilities section: shows required permissions
- Install hint: correct install command shown

## 4. Quality Signals Tests (5+ tests)
- Conformance tier displayed correctly (T1/T2/T3)
- Maintenance status computed from last-updated date
- Composite score calculated with correct weights
- Badge colors match risk level (green/yellow/red)
- Score updates on index refresh

## 5. CLI Integration Tests (5+ tests)
- pi search output is valid table (parseable columns)
- pi info output fits terminal width
- pi collections lists available collections
- pi search from within interactive TUI (/search command)
- Error messages include help text

- Terminal width simulation for output tests

title: [AUTH-2] /login google|gemini API-key auth flow (no hardcoded OAuth client)
description:
## Problem

`/login` does not provide a dedicated Google/Gemini auth UX. Earlier assumptions about shipping built-in Google OAuth constants/client credentials are not aligned with current Google docs.

## Verified Constraint (from bd-2gdoo)

Gemini docs position API keys as the primary/easiest auth path. OAuth is possible but requires user/project setup in Google Cloud (OAuth consent + desktop client credentials / ADC flow), so a single hardcoded shared client_id/secret is not a safe default.

## Solution

Implement API-key-first `/login google` and `/login gemini` flow:

1. `/login google` and `/login gemini` both route to Google/Gemini API-key login UX.
2. Prompt for Gemini/Google API key and store in `auth.json` under `google` credential.
3. Provide clear guidance for key creation and secure handling.
4. Optional follow-up guidance can reference advanced OAuth/ADC paths, but this task does not hardcode Google OAuth client credentials.
5. `/logout google` and `/logout gemini` clear stored credentials.
acceptance_criteria: 1) `/login google` and `/login gemini` store API-key credentials in `auth.json` and provider resolution uses them. 2) `/logout google|gemini` removes stored credentials cleanly. 3) UX explicitly documents API-key-first behavior and avoids misleading built-in OAuth claims. 4) Unit tests cover alias handling (`google`/`gemini`), storage behavior, and auth resolution precedence.
notes: Implemented google/gemini API-key-first login flow in src/interactive.rs using canonical provider normalization and alias-safe credential persistence/removal helpers. /login google|gemini now prompts API-key guidance (no hardcoded OAuth claim), stores under canonical provider google, and /logout google|gemini clears both canonical+alias entries. Added unit tests for alias normalization, prompt coverage, canonical persistence, and alias removal behavior. Verification: cargo check --all-targets and cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings reached green during run; cargo fmt --check remains noisy due concurrent unrelated file edits in other active workstreams.
close_reason: Completed: API-key-first google/gemini login/logout flow verified with focused auth+tui tests

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE PROJECT:

1. RELIABILITY: The most impactful items are the fake version strings. When providers deprecate the impersonated versions, Pi users will get unexplained auth failures, degraded service, or API rejections — and Pi's own logs won't help debug the issue because the sent identity is wrong.

2. DROP-IN CLAIM INTEGRITY: The README positions Pi as a reliable, production-quality tool with 'materially stronger security model'. Sending false platform information (darwin/arm64 on Linux, claiming to be Node.js) undermines this claim. Per AGENTS.md's drop-in messaging guardrail, we should not claim production quality while actively sending false identifiers.

3. OPERATIONAL RESILIENCE: Hard-coded OAuth credentials with no overrides create a single point of failure. If ANY provider rotates their client ID, ALL existing Pi binaries break for that provider's OAuth flow with no workaround short of a new release.

4. CORRECTNESS PRINCIPLE: The project forbids unsafe code and has strict clippy lints because correctness matters. Sending 'darwin/arm64' on linux/x86_64 is a correctness bug at the same level — it's provably wrong output.

5. FUTURE-PROOFING: Every date-tagged string (2023-06-01, 2024-02-15-preview, 2025-04-01, etc.) is a ticking time bomb. Each one will eventually need updating. Env-var overrides let users self-serve while waiting for a release.

title: AUDIT-CRIT: Fake/stale version strings in provider User-Agent headers
description: Sub-epic for Critical severity findings. Six provider files send hard-coded version strings that impersonate specific versions of VS Code, GitHub Copilot, Node.js, Google Antigravity, and Google Cloud SDK. These are actively wrong (not just stale) — they send false platform/version information to upstream APIs on every request. Risk: API rejections when providers enforce minimum versions or deprecate old API versions; incorrect telemetry; potential TOS violations for impersonating other software.

title: Fix Copilot provider: stale VS Code + Copilot version strings
description:
FILE: src/providers/copilot.rs:30-33

PROBLEM:
Two const strings impersonate specific outdated software versions:
  - Line 30: EDITOR_VERSION = 'vscode/1.96.2' (VS Code is now well past 1.96)
  - Line 33: COPILOT_USER_AGENT = 'GitHubCopilotChat/0.26.7' (Copilot extension updates frequently)

These are sent as HTTP headers to the GitHub Copilot API on every request. GitHub can use these for version gating, telemetry, or deprecation enforcement.

WHY THIS MATTERS:
- GitHub has historically blocked or degraded service for old Copilot client versions
- When GitHub deprecates the 0.26.x line, Pi users will get unexplained failures
- Pi should identify itself honestly rather than impersonating VS Code

RECOMMENDED FIX:
Option A (preferred): Send Pi's own identity: 'pi_agent_rust/{CARGO_PKG_VERSION}' as User-Agent, and 'pi_agent_rust/{CARGO_PKG_VERSION}' as editor-version. This is honest but may cause rejection if Copilot API checks for known clients.
Option B (pragmatic): Add env var overrides PI_COPILOT_EDITOR_VERSION and PI_COPILOT_USER_AGENT that default to the current const values, so users can update without rebuilding. Document the env vars.
Option C (best of both): Try Pi's own identity first; if 403/forbidden, fall back to the compat strings and log a warning.

CONSIDERATIONS:
- The Copilot API may reject requests from unrecognized User-Agent strings. Test with a real Copilot token before shipping Option A.
- The GITHUB_API_VERSION on line 36 ('2025-04-01') is a different concern — that's an API version header, not a client version. It's currently fine but should also get an env override for future-proofing.
- Look at how pi-mono handles this — it may have a dynamic version strategy we should match.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTATION NOTES:
- The Copilot API is documented at https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/building-copilot-extensions
- GitHub uses the editor-version and User-Agent to determine client capability
- Pi-mono likely sends the current system's VS Code version if launched from VS Code, or a fallback string otherwise. Check legacy_pi_mono_code/pi-mono for the pattern.
- If choosing Option B (env overrides), the env vars should be:
  PI_COPILOT_EDITOR_VERSION (default: vscode/1.96.2)
  PI_COPILOT_USER_AGENT (default: GitHubCopilotChat/0.26.7)
- If choosing Option A (honest identity), test thoroughly — Copilot API may gate on recognized editor strings
- Consider reading the actual VS Code version from the environment if Pi is launched from VS Code (VS Code sets VSCODE_PID and other env vars that could be used to detect the host editor)

title: Fix Copilot provider: add env override for GitHub API version
description:
FILE: src/providers/copilot.rs:36

PROBLEM:
GITHUB_API_VERSION = '2025-04-01' is hard-coded. GitHub API versions are date-based and older versions eventually get sunset. While this isn't immediately broken (the version is recent), there's no way to update it without rebuilding.

RECOMMENDED FIX:
Add PI_GITHUB_API_VERSION env var override, defaulting to the current const. Pattern:
  let api_version = std::env::var('PI_GITHUB_API_VERSION').unwrap_or_else(|_| GITHUB_API_VERSION.to_string());

DEPENDENCY: Can be done independently but should be reviewed alongside bd-2vbks.1.1 since they touch the same file.

title: Fix Gemini provider: wrong OS/arch in antigravity User-Agent
description:
FILE: src/providers/gemini.rs:330

PROBLEM:
Hard-coded: request.header('User-Agent', 'antigravity/1.15.8 darwin/arm64')
This sends 'darwin/arm64' (macOS on Apple Silicon) to Google's API REGARDLESS of the actual OS and architecture. On Linux x86_64 (which is the primary deployment target for Pi), this is actively lying about the platform.

The version '1.15.8' is also frozen and will go stale as the real Antigravity tool updates.

WHY THIS IS CRITICAL:
- Google may use OS/arch for feature gating, routing, or analytics
- Sending wrong platform info could cause subtle behavior differences
- If Google starts enforcing User-Agent validation, all non-macOS users break silently
- This is the single most obviously wrong hard-coded value in the codebase

RECOMMENDED FIX:
1. Build the OS/arch string dynamically:
   let os = std::env::consts::OS;  // 'linux', 'macos', 'windows'
   let arch = std::env::consts::ARCH;  // 'x86_64', 'aarch64'
   // Map to Google's expected format if needed (darwin vs macos, arm64 vs aarch64)
   let ua = format!('antigravity/{version} {os}/{arch}');

2. For the version, add an env var override PI_ANTIGRAVITY_VERSION (note: there's already ANTIGRAVITY_VERSION_ENV = 'PI_AI_ANTIGRAVITY_VERSION' in http/client.rs — check if that's already intended for this purpose and unify).

3. Test with a real Google Gemini CLI OAuth token to confirm the API accepts the new User-Agent.

CONSIDERATIONS:
- Google's API may expect 'darwin' not 'macos' — need a mapping function
- Google's API may expect 'arm64' not 'aarch64' — need a mapping function  
- The non-antigravity path (line 333) has the same issue: 'google-cloud-sdk vscode_cloudshelleditor/0.1' also lies about the client identity
- Check if PI_AI_ANTIGRAVITY_VERSION env var in http/client.rs was intended to feed into this — there may be an incomplete wiring

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTATION NOTES:
- This task, bd-2vbks.1.4, bd-2vbks.1.5, and bd-2vbks.2.1 all modify the same function in gemini.rs (the streaming request builder around lines 310-350). They should be implemented together in a single PR to avoid merge conflicts.
- The platform-info utility (bd-2vbks.2.2) must be created first as it provides the OS/arch mapping functions.
- Testing is critical: Google APIs have been known to reject requests with unrecognized User-Agent strings. Before merging, test with:
  1. A real Google Gemini API key (standard path)
  2. A real Gemini CLI OAuth token (google_cli_mode path)
  3. A real Antigravity OAuth token (antigravity path)
- If any Google path rejects the honest User-Agent, document the rejection and fall back to impersonation with a logged warning.
- The std::env::consts::OS values need mapping: 'macos' -> 'darwin', 'linux' -> 'linux', 'windows' -> 'windows'. For ARCH: 'aarch64' -> 'arm64', 'x86_64' -> 'amd64' or 'x86_64' (check what Google expects).

title: Fix Gemini provider: stale google-cloud-sdk User-Agent string
description:
FILE: src/providers/gemini.rs:333

PROBLEM:
Hard-coded: request.header('User-Agent', 'google-cloud-sdk vscode_cloudshelleditor/0.1')
This impersonates the VS Code Cloud Shell Editor extension version 0.1. Pi is neither VS Code nor Cloud Shell Editor.

This is the non-antigravity Gemini CLI code path. Same class of issue as the antigravity path (bd-2vbks.1.3) but different string.

RECOMMENDED FIX:
- Use Pi's own identity or at minimum a configurable string
- Pattern: env var PI_GEMINI_CLI_USER_AGENT with a sensible default like 'pi_agent_rust/{CARGO_PKG_VERSION}'
- If Google's API rejects unknown User-Agents, document the compat requirement and keep the impersonation string as a documented fallback

DEPENDENCY: Should be done together with bd-2vbks.1.3 since they're in the same function and share the same pattern.

title: Fix Gemini provider: false x-goog-api-client Node.js claim
description:
FILE: src/providers/gemini.rs:323

PROBLEM:
Hard-coded: .header('x-goog-api-client', 'gl-node/22.17.0')
This tells Google that the client is Node.js version 22.17.0. Pi is a Rust binary — this is categorically false.

The 'gl-' prefix is Google's convention for client library identification:
  gl-node = Google client library for Node.js
  gl-python = Google client library for Python
  gl-go = Google client library for Go

There is no 'gl-rust' convention, which is probably why the original port copied the Node.js string from pi-mono (which IS Node.js).

WHY THIS MATTERS:
- Google uses x-goog-api-client for usage analytics and client support prioritization
- Sending false data pollutes their analytics
- If Google ever ties API behavior to client library version (e.g., deprecation warnings), Pi users would get Node.js-specific messages

RECOMMENDED FIX:
- Send an honest identifier: 'gl-rust/{CARGO_PKG_VERSION}' or 'pi-agent-rust/{CARGO_PKG_VERSION}'
- If Google requires a known 'gl-' prefix, use 'gl-rust/0.1.0' or similar
- Add PI_GOOG_API_CLIENT env var override for flexibility
- Test with real Google API credentials to confirm acceptance

DEPENDENCY: Should be done together with bd-2vbks.1.3 and bd-2vbks.1.4 since all three touch the same streaming_url/request-building code path in gemini.rs.

title: Fix Azure provider: stale preview API version default
description:
FILE: src/providers/azure.rs:28

PROBLEM:
DEFAULT_API_VERSION = '2024-02-15-preview' — this is a preview version from February 2024. Azure has since released stable GA versions (e.g., 2024-06-01, 2024-10-21). Using a preview API version in production means:
- Potential deprecation without notice (preview versions have shorter lifecycles)
- Missing features available in newer stable versions
- Azure may eventually return errors for sunset preview versions

CONTEXT:
Azure OpenAI API versioning is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/openai/reference. The version is sent as a query parameter: ?api-version=2024-02-15-preview

Tests in providers/mod.rs already show other versions being used (2024-10-21, 2024-06-01) when parsed from user-provided URLs, so the URL-parsing path works. The issue is the DEFAULT when no version is specified.

RECOMMENDED FIX:
1. Update DEFAULT_API_VERSION to the latest stable GA version (check Azure docs for current)
2. Add PI_AZURE_API_VERSION env var override
3. Update the test on line 950 that asserts the old default
4. Consider logging a warning when using the default version, suggesting users specify explicitly

CONSIDERATIONS:
- Some Azure deployments may be pinned to older API versions — the env override handles this
- The preview version may actually be required for some features (e.g., assistants API) — document this in the env var docs

title: Fix Anthropic provider: date-tagged beta flags may be stale
description:
FILE: src/providers/anthropic.rs:32

PROBLEM:
ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_BETA_FLAGS = 'claude-code-20250219,oauth-2025-04-20'
These anthropic-beta header flags contain specific dates (2025-02-19 and 2025-04-20). Beta flags in the Anthropic API are used to opt into pre-GA features. They have specific lifecycles:
- They may graduate to GA (at which point sending them is harmless but unnecessary)
- They may be replaced by newer beta flag identifiers
- They may be removed entirely (which could cause warnings or errors)

ALSO:
Line 498: 'prompt-caching-2024-07-31' — another date-tagged beta flag for prompt caching.

WHY THIS MATTERS:
- If Anthropic removes or renames these beta flags, the API may reject requests or log warnings
- There's no way to update beta flags without rebuilding the binary

RECOMMENDED FIX:
1. Add PI_ANTHROPIC_BETA_FLAGS env var override that APPENDS to (or replaces) the default flags
2. Check Anthropic's current API docs to see if any of these flags have graduated to stable
3. If prompt-caching is now GA, remove that beta flag entirely
4. Consider a periodic reminder (log at startup?) when using date-tagged beta flags older than N months

CONSIDERATIONS:
- The beta flags are conditionally added (oauth flags only when using oauth token, caching only when caching enabled) — the env override should respect this conditional logic
- pi-mono may have already updated these — check upstream

title: AUDIT-HIGH: Hard-coded platform identifiers sent to Google APIs
description: Sub-epic for High severity findings. The Gemini provider sends 'PLATFORM_UNSPECIFIED' and 'IDE_UNSPECIFIED' in client-metadata instead of actual values. This loses useful telemetry for Google and may affect routing or feature gating.

title: Fix Gemini client-metadata: report actual platform and IDE type
description:
FILE: src/providers/gemini.rs:326

PROBLEM:
Hard-coded JSON in client-metadata header:
  {"ideType":"IDE_UNSPECIFIED","platform":"PLATFORM_UNSPECIFIED","pluginType":"GEMINI"}

Both ideType and platform are set to 'UNSPECIFIED' when Pi could report accurate values.

For ideType: Pi is a CLI tool, not an IDE. The correct value depends on what Google's API expects. Options:
- 'CLI' if Google supports it
- 'IDE_UNSPECIFIED' might actually be correct for a non-IDE tool (investigate Google's enum)
- 'TERMINAL' or 'AGENT' if those are valid values

For platform: Should report the actual OS. Google likely expects values like:
- 'LINUX', 'MACOS', 'WINDOWS' (need to check their enum)
- Could map from std::env::consts::OS

RECOMMENDED FIX:
1. Research Google's client-metadata schema (check pi-mono, Gemini CLI source, or API docs)
2. Set platform dynamically based on actual OS
3. Set ideType to the most appropriate value for a CLI agent
4. Keep pluginType as 'GEMINI' (this identifies the API surface being used, not the client)
5. Add PI_GEMINI_CLIENT_METADATA env var override for the full JSON string as an escape hatch

ALSO IN: src/auth.rs:2477-2478 and 2527-2528 — the same UNSPECIFIED values appear in OAuth token exchange payloads. Fix those too.

DEPENDENCY: Related to bd-2vbks.1.3 (same Gemini request-building code), should be done in same PR.

title: Create shared platform-info utility for OS/arch/client identity strings
description:
PROBLEM:
Multiple provider files need OS, architecture, and client identity strings:
- gemini.rs needs OS/arch for User-Agent (bd-2vbks.1.3)
- gemini.rs needs platform for client-metadata (bd-2vbks.2.1)
- copilot.rs needs editor/client version (bd-2vbks.1.1)
- auth.rs needs platform for OAuth metadata
- http/client.rs already has a DEFAULT_USER_AGENT with CARGO_PKG_VERSION

Instead of each provider building its own strings, create a small shared utility that provides:
1. pi_user_agent() -> 'pi_agent_rust/{version}'
2. os_name() -> maps std::env::consts::OS to provider-expected names ('darwin'/'linux'/'windows')
3. arch_name() -> maps std::env::consts::ARCH to provider-expected names ('arm64'/'amd64'/'x86_64')
4. platform_string() -> '{os}/{arch}'

LOCATION: src/platform.rs (new file) or add to existing src/app.rs or src/http/client.rs

CONSIDERATIONS:
- Google expects 'darwin' not 'macos', 'arm64' not 'aarch64' — the mapping must handle this
- Some providers may need different formats — the utility should provide building blocks, not one-size-fits-all
- The version should use env!('CARGO_PKG_VERSION') which is already used elsewhere
- http/client.rs already has DEFAULT_USER_AGENT — this utility should supersede/unify with it

THIS IS A PREREQUISITE for bd-2vbks.1.3, bd-2vbks.1.4, bd-2vbks.1.5, bd-2vbks.2.1.

title: AUDIT-MED: OAuth credentials frozen in binary without env-var overrides

title: Add env-var overrides for Google Gemini CLI OAuth credentials

AUDIT-MED: Compaction default assumes 200K context window
description: ResolvedCompactionSettings::default() in src/compaction.rs:69-81 hard-codes context_window_tokens=200_000. While main.rs:230 overrides this dynamically from ModelEntry.context_window, ANY code path that uses the Default impl without overriding gets Anthropic's 200K window. This is wrong for OpenAI (128K), smaller Gemini models (32K), DeepSeek (64K), etc. The Default should either require an explicit context window (no Default impl) or use a more conservative fallback.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
ANALYSIS: The Default impl for ResolvedCompactionSettings (src/compaction.rs:69-81) uses context_window_tokens=200_000 which is Anthropic-specific. Code paths that call this:

1. main.rs:1221-1226 — GOOD: Overrides with context_window_tokens_for_entry() which reads from ModelEntry
2. sdk.rs:1666 — NEEDS CHECK: Creates ResolvedCompactionSettings with explicit values but may use defaults
3. interactive/perf.rs:489 — NEEDS CHECK: Uses settings from agent, which should already be model-specific
4. Tests — Many tests use Default or explicit 200K, which is fine for tests

The real risk is any NEW code path that calls ResolvedCompactionSettings::default() without overriding context_window_tokens. 

RECOMMENDED APPROACH: Instead of removing Default, change the default to a conservative value like 32_768 (smallest common context window) and add a log warning when the default is used. This way, if someone forgets to override, compaction triggers too early (safe) rather than too late (unsafe — could exceed context window).

Alternative: Remove the Default impl entirely and require all callers to provide explicit values. This is the safest but most disruptive approach.

title: AUDIT-LOW: Provider metadata duplicates/approximates context windows
description: In src/provider_metadata.rs, nearly all non-Anthropic providers hard-code context_window: 128_000 as a routing default. Many models have different actual context windows (Gemini 1M+, DeepSeek 64K, etc.). These should ideally come from the model registry or models.json rather than provider-level defaults. Lower priority because the per-model context_window in ModelEntry should take precedence at runtime.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
ANALYSIS: src/provider_metadata.rs has ~80 providers, nearly all with context_window: 128_000. This is a routing default only — the actual per-model context window comes from ModelEntry (populated from models.json or the built-in catalog with 11,712 lines). The provider_metadata context_window is used as a FALLBACK when no model-specific value is available.

The concern is that 128K is wrong for many providers:
- Gemini: models range from 32K to 2M
- DeepSeek: 64K context
- Mistral: varies by model (32K-128K)  
- Cohere: varies by model

However, since the model registry should always have the correct value, this is a low-impact issue. The fix would be to either:
1. Set provider-level context_window to the MINIMUM of that provider's models (conservative, safe)
2. Remove context_window from ProviderRoutingDefaults and require it to always come from the model entry
3. Leave as-is but document that this is a fallback only, not the source of truth

Option 2 is cleanest but most disruptive. Option 1 is safest. Option 3 is pragmatic.

title: Wrap extension lifecycle in Cx::region() for structured concurrency
description:
Use asupersync structured concurrency to guarantee cleanup of extension resources.

## Current State
- Extensions use basic Cx but not region() for lifecycle management
- Potential for orphaned extension tasks or leaked event handlers
- No guaranteed quiescence on extension unload

## Background (asupersync)
Cx::region() provides:
- Guaranteed child task completion on scope exit
- No orphaned tasks (enforced by type system)
- Bounded cleanup with cancellation budgets

## Implementation
1. Wrap ExtensionManager lifetime in Cx::region()
2. All extension event dispatch spawns tasks owned by the region
3. On shutdown, region guarantees all handlers complete or cancel
4. Add cancellation budget for extension cleanup (e.g., 5s max)

## Test Plan
- Unit test: extension with slow cleanup completes within budget
- Unit test: region exit waits for in-flight event handlers
- Integration test: Ctrl+C during extension execution cleans up properly

- src/extensions.rs (wrap in region)
- src/extensions_js.rs (spawn tasks via region)
- src/agent.rs (ensure extension region lifecycle)

This should be done after basic extension runtime works.

title: [PERF-1] Implement MessageRenderCache for conversation content memoization
description:
## Problem

`build_conversation_content()` is called every frame and re-renders ALL messages including full markdown rendering. For a conversation with 100 messages, this means 100 markdown renders per frame x 60 frames/second = 6000 markdown renders/second. This is the single biggest performance bottleneck in the TUI.

## Solution: MessageRenderCache

Implement a per-message render cache that stores the rendered output for each ConversationMessage. Cache key is a lightweight tuple. Only re-render when content changes or global invalidation occurs.

### Design

```rust
struct MessageCacheKey {
    content_hash: u64,      // DefaultHasher (SipHash) of message.content + message.thinking
    collapsed: bool,        // whether message is collapsed (for tool messages)
    role: MessageRole,      // different roles have different rendering
}

struct MessageRenderCache {
    entries: Vec<Option<(MessageCacheKey, String)>>,
    /// Bumped on global invalidation: terminal resize, theme change, toggle-thinking.
    /// Cache entries from a previous generation are considered stale.
    generation: u64,
    current_generation: u64,
}
```

### Simplified Cache Key (No terminal_width)

Previous design included `terminal_width` in the per-message cache key. This is REDUNDANT with the generation mechanism:
- When the terminal is resized, bump `generation` -- all entries become stale in one operation
- Same for theme change and thinking toggle
- This keeps the per-message key small (content_hash + collapsed + role) and avoids storing width in every entry

### Hash Implementation

Use `std::hash::DefaultHasher` (SipHash) rather than adding an FxHash dependency:
```rust
fn compute_content_hash(content: &str, thinking: Option<&str>) -> u64 {
    use std::hash::{Hash, Hasher};
    let mut hasher = std::hash::DefaultHasher::new();
    content.hash(&mut hasher);
    if let Some(thinking) = thinking {
        thinking.hash(&mut hasher);
    }
    hasher.finish()
}
```
The hash is computed once per cache miss (not per frame for cache hits), so SipHash's slightly higher cost vs FxHash is irrelevant.

### Cache Key by Message Type
- **User messages**: content_hash covers text content
- **Assistant messages**: content_hash covers text + thinking (if thinking_visible)
- **Tool call/result messages**: content_hash covers tool name + output. The `collapsed` field is critical because TOOL_AUTO_COLLAPSE_THRESHOLD (20 lines) affects what renders -- when collapsed, only TOOL_COLLAPSE_PREVIEW_LINES (5) lines show.
- **System messages**: content_hash covers content

### Cache Invalidation Rules
1. **Per-message**: When message content changes (streaming delta -- cache miss on content_hash)
2. **Per-message (tool)**: When tool message collapse state toggles (collapsed field differs)
3. **Global (generation bump)**: On terminal resize, theme change, toggle-thinking -- bump generation, all entries miss
4. **Full clear**: On ConversationReset, /clear -- clear entries vec entirely

### Implementation in build_conversation_content()
- Before rendering each message, compute cache key
- Check cache[i]: if key matches and generation matches, use cached String
- If miss: render markdown, store (key, rendered_string) in cache, return rendered String
- For streaming (current_response): ALWAYS render fresh (content changes every frame)
- After AgentDone: cache the finalized message (now immutable)

### Performance Guarantee
- Scrolling through 1000 messages: O(visible_messages) per frame (only visible messages need cache lookup)
- During streaming: O(1) re-render (only current message re-rendered, all others cache hits)
- Theme change: O(N) for one frame (all misses), then O(visible_messages) again

## Files to Modify
- src/interactive.rs: Add MessageRenderCache field to PiApp, modify build_conversation_content()

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] MessageRenderCache struct with DefaultHasher-based cache keys
- [ ] Cache key: (content_hash, collapsed, role) -- NO terminal_width (use generation for that)
- [ ] Generation bump on resize, theme change, toggle-thinking
- [ ] build_conversation_content() uses cache for finalized messages
- [ ] Tool messages cached with collapse state in key
- [ ] Streaming messages bypass cache
- [ ] All 263+ tui_state tests pass
- [ ] Clippy clean

## Unit Tests (specified here, implemented in PERF-TEST)
- cache hit for unchanged message returns same content
- cache miss after content change returns new content
- tool message cache miss when collapse state toggles
- generation bump forces full re-render (simulates resize)
- streaming message (current_response non-empty) bypasses cache
- benchmark: build_conversation_content() with 100 cached messages vs uncached

All 3304 lib tests pass, clippy clean.

title: PARITY-UX.5: Global blockImages filter — apply image blocking at agent loop level, not just ReadTool

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## PARITY-UX.5: Global blockImages Filter

### The Gap
pi-mono applies blockImages as defense-in-depth at the agent session level (src/core/sdk.ts:243-277). Before sending messages to the LLM, it filters out ALL image content blocks if blockImages is enabled.

Our Rust port only applies blockImages in the ReadTool (src/tools.rs:1087). This means images from other sources (user paste, extension-provided, session replay) could still reach the LLM.

### Why This Matters
blockImages is a cost-control and privacy feature. Users who enable it expect NO images to be sent to the LLM, regardless of source. Currently, only read-tool images are blocked.

### Implementation Plan
1. In the agent loop (src/agent.rs), before sending messages to the provider:
   - If config.images.block_images is true
   - Filter out all ContentBlock::Image variants from the message list
   - Also filter ImageContent from UserContent::Blocks
2. This should happen at the to_llm_messages() conversion point (or just before)
3. Log when images are filtered (debug level)

### Pi-Mono Reference
- Filter logic: legacy_pi_mono_code/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/src/core/sdk.ts:243-277
- wraps convertToLlm with image filtering

### Acceptance Criteria
- blockImages=true filters ALL image content, not just read-tool images
- Filtering happens before messages reach the provider
- Test with user-provided image content + blockImages=true → no images sent
- ReadTool filtering still works (defense in depth)
- Debug log when images are filtered

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Testing Requirements

### Unit Tests (tests/block_images_global.rs)
1. **Filter at agent loop level**: blockImages=true, message contains ImageContent → image stripped before sending to provider
2. **Multiple image sources**: User-pasted image, read-tool image, extension-provided image → ALL stripped
3. **Filter preserves non-image content**: Text + Image message → only text sent to provider
4. **No filter when disabled**: blockImages=false → images pass through normally
5. **Defense in depth**: blockImages=true → ReadTool ALSO strips images (existing behavior preserved)
6. **Empty message after filter**: Message that is ALL images → empty content sent or message skipped (decide behavior)

### Integration Tests (VCR)
7. **Full pipeline**: VCR cassette test, send user message with embedded image, blockImages=true, verify API request body has no image content blocks
8. **Debug logging**: blockImages=true + image present → debug log "Filtered N image(s) from message"

title: PARITY-SDK.2: Implement create_agent_session() — programmatic session creation for embedding
close_reason: Completed: create_agent_session + SessionOptions + AgentSessionHandle APIs landed in src/sdk.rs with unit coverage for defaults, model switching, no-session, and path resolution; follow-on SDK parity work tracked in dependent beads.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## PARITY-SDK.2: Implement create_agent_session()

### The Gap
pi-mono provides createAgentSession() (src/core/sdk.ts:162-295) — a factory function that creates a fully configured agent session for programmatic use. It handles:
- Loading config from settings.json
- Setting up provider with model selection
- Configuring tools (with optional custom working directory)
- Loading extensions
- Setting up system prompt
- Returning an AgentSession object with prompt()/subscribe()/model/thinking/compact APIs

Our Rust code has no equivalent. Session creation is intertwined with main.rs CLI flow.

### What pi-mono createAgentSession Provides
```typescript
const session = await createAgentSession({
  provider: "anthropic",
  model: "claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
  systemPrompt: "You are a helpful assistant.",
  tools: [createReadTool(), createBashTool()],
  workingDirectory: "/path/to/project",
  onEvent: (event) => { /* handle events */ },
});

const response = await session.prompt("Hello!");
```

### Implementation Plan
1. Extract session creation logic from main.rs into a standalone function in src/sdk.rs
2. Define SessionOptions struct matching pi-mono CreateAgentSessionOptions:
   ```rust
   pub struct SessionOptions {
       pub provider: Option<String>,
       pub model: Option<String>,
       pub system_prompt: Option<String>,
       pub tools: Option<Vec<ToolDefinition>>,
       pub working_directory: Option<PathBuf>,
       pub thinking: Option<ThinkingLevel>,
       pub on_event: Option<Box<dyn Fn(AgentEvent) + Send>>,
       pub extensions: Option<Vec<PathBuf>>,
       pub session_path: Option<PathBuf>,
       pub no_session: bool,
   }
   ```
3. create_agent_session(options) returns an AgentSessionHandle with:
   - prompt(message) -> AgentResult (runs one turn)
   - subscribe(callback) -> unsubscribe handle
   - model() / set_model()
   - thinking() / set_thinking()
   - compact()
   - abort()
   - get_messages()
   - get_state()

### Key Challenge: Async Runtime
pi-mono runs on Node event loop. Our Rust version runs on asupersync.
The SDK function must work both:
- From within an asupersync runtime (library use)
- By creating its own runtime if needed (standalone binary use)

### Acceptance Criteria
- create_agent_session(options) compiles and works
- Can run a simple prompt → response cycle programmatically
- Event callback receives all AgentEvent variants
- Works with Anthropic provider at minimum
- Integration test demonstrates basic usage

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:

title: FUZZ-P3.2: Crash corpus management — storage, minimization, regression test generation

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## FUZZ-P3.2: Crash Corpus Management

### What This Task Does
When a fuzzer finds a crash, it saves the crashing input to fuzz/artifacts/<target>/. This task establishes a workflow for:
1. Minimizing crash inputs (removing unnecessary bytes)
2. Categorizing and deduplicating crashes
3. Storing crash inputs for regression testing
4. Tracking crash resolution status

### Crash Minimization Workflow
```bash
# When a crash is found:
cargo fuzz tmin <target> fuzz/artifacts/<target>/crash-<hash>

# This produces a minimized input that triggers the same crash
# but with fewer bytes — easier to understand and debug
```

### Crash Storage Structure
```
fuzz/
├── artifacts/           # Raw crash inputs (gitignored, transient)
│   └── <target>/
│       └── crash-<hash>
├── crashes/             # Minimized, categorized crashes (committed)
│   └── <target>/
│       ├── oom-001.bin          # Out-of-memory
│       ├── panic-unwrap-001.bin # Unwrap panic
│       ├── index-oob-001.bin   # Index out of bounds
│       └── README.md           # Crash catalog with descriptions
└── regression/          # Regression test inputs (committed)
    └── <target>/
        └── *.bin        # Inputs that previously crashed, now fixed
```

### Crash Categorization
Crashes should be categorized by root cause:
- **OOM**: Memory exhaustion from unbounded allocation
- **Stack overflow**: Deep recursion without limit
- **Panic (unwrap)**: .unwrap() on None/Err
- **Panic (index)**: Array index out of bounds
- **Panic (assertion)**: assert! or debug_assert! failure
- **Timeout**: Infinite loop or catastrophic backtracking
- **Logic error**: Incorrect behavior without crash (found by assertion in harness)

### Integration with P3.4 (Regression Tests)
Each fixed crash should become a regression test:
1. Minimize the crash input
2. Move to fuzz/regression/<target>/
3. P3.4 generates a #[test] function that loads and runs the input
4. This prevents the same bug from reappearing

### Files to Create
- fuzz/crashes/ directory structure
- fuzz/regression/ directory structure
- Documentation: fuzz/README.md (crash management workflow)

### Acceptance Criteria
- Clear process for crash triage: find → minimize → categorize → fix → regress
- At least one example crash walked through the full workflow (even if synthetic)
- fuzz/crashes/ directory structure is in place
- README.md documents the workflow

title: Build semantic JSON comparator (not just byte equality)
description:
# Build semantic JSON comparator (not just byte equality)

## Context
Raw byte-equality comparison would produce false failures due to:
- JSON key ordering differences
- Numeric precision (Rust f64 vs JS number)
- Whitespace normalization
- Array ordering when order does not matter (e.g., set of tools)

We need a semantic comparator that understands the structure.

## Comparison Rules

### Registration Comparison
- Tools: compare by name, ignore ordering. For each tool, compare: name, description, parameters schema
- Commands: compare by name, ignore ordering. Compare: name, description, userFacing
- Flags: compare by name, ignore ordering. Compare: name, type, default, description
- Shortcuts: compare by key, ignore ordering. Compare: key, description
- Event handlers: compare by event name. Compare: set of subscribed events

### Event Response Comparison
- For each event type + payload: compare handler return values
- Allow for: undefined vs null equivalence, missing vs empty array equivalence

### Hostcall Comparison
- Compare captured hostcall sequences (order matters here)
- For each hostcall: compare type, method, arguments, return value

### Numeric Tolerance
- Allow +/- 1e-10 for floating point values
- Timestamps should be identical (both mocked to same value)

## Implementation
File: tests/ext_conformance/comparator.rs (or in the runner module)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Comparator correctly identifies: identical outputs, registration diffs, event diffs, hostcall diffs
- False positive rate: 0% (identical outputs never flagged as different)
- Human-readable diff output for failures
close_reason: Created tests/conformance_comparator.rs with 18 tests implementing the semantic JSON comparator for extension conformance testing. Features: canonicalization (key ordering), numeric precision tolerance (1e-9), null/missing field equivalence, empty array/null equivalence, set-based array comparison for registrations (commands by name, shortcuts by key_id, flags by name, providers by id, tool_defs by name, models by id), event hooks set comparison, ordered hostcall sequence comparison, CompareResult/DiffEntry structures with JSON serialization, human-readable diff report formatting. Tests cover: identical outputs (pass), key ordering independence, null vs missing, numeric tolerance, significant numeric diffs, set-based registration ordering, missing/extra items detection, field diffs, hostcall ordering, hostcall length mismatches, event hook set comparison/diffs, JSON round-trip, format report readability, full complex comparison, empty array vs null. All 18 tests pass.

description:
# Record VCR cassettes for Anthropic provider scenarios

## Goal
Create recorded cassettes for all Anthropic provider test scenarios.

## Scenarios to Record

### Happy Path Scenarios
1. **Simple text response** - Single text block, stop reason "stop"
2. **Multi-paragraph response** - Multiple text deltas
3. **Extended thinking** - thinking_start/delta/end + text response
4. **Tool call single** - Single tool_call in response
5. **Tool call multiple** - Multiple tool_calls in single response
6. **Tool result processing** - tool_result message handling

### Error Scenarios
7. **Rate limit (429)** - With retry-after header
8. **Auth failure (401)** - Invalid API key
9. **Forbidden (403)** - Resource access denied
10. **Bad request (400)** - Malformed request
11. **Server error (500)** - Internal server error
12. **Overloaded (529)** - Anthropic overloaded

### Edge Cases
13. **Empty response** - No content blocks
14. **Very long response** - Hits max_tokens
15. **Unicode content** - Emoji, CJK, RTL text
16. **Large tool call args** - Big JSON in arguments
17. **Stream interruption** - Partial response simulation

### Extended Thinking Variants
18. **Thinking only** - No final text, just thinking
19. **Thinking with tool calls** - Thinking then tool use
20. **Thinking budget exceeded** - Hits thinking token limit

## Recording Process
```bash
# Set API key (not committed)
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...

# Record mode
VCR_MODE=record cargo test provider_streaming::anthropic

# Verify cassettes created
ls tests/fixtures/vcr/anthropic_*.json
```

## Logging Requirements
- Use TestLogger (bd-3ml) during recording runs.
- Log cassette name/path, model, prompt summary hash, and redaction summary.
- Capture command line + env (redacted) used to record each cassette.

## Determinism + Redaction
- Keep prompts/tool schemas identical across recordings; store prompt hashes in a manifest.
- Ensure API keys and any sensitive fields are redacted.
- Record with fixed model versions + params (temperature, max_tokens, thinking level).

## Files Created
- tests/fixtures/vcr/anthropic_simple_text.json
- tests/fixtures/vcr/anthropic_extended_thinking.json
- tests/fixtures/vcr/anthropic_tool_call.json
- tests/fixtures/vcr/anthropic_rate_limit.json
- ... (20 cassettes total)
- tests/fixtures/vcr/anthropic_manifest.json (scenario → prompt hash + params)

## Dependencies
- bd-1pf (VCR infrastructure must exist)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] 20 cassettes recorded
- [ ] All scenarios covered
- [ ] Sensitive data redacted
- [ ] Cassettes valid JSON
- [ ] Manifest includes prompt hashes + params
- [ ] Playback matches recording
- [ ] Recording logs captured with redacted env
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] Scope in description implemented fully with no feature loss
[ ] Unit tests cover core success/failure + edge cases for this bead
[ ] Integration/E2E script exercises the end-to-end path (or explicitly marks N/A with rationale in notes) and emits detailed JSONL logs + artifacts per bd-4u9
[ ] Logs include inputs, outputs, timing, and redaction summary; artifacts list is deterministic
[ ] Quality gates pass: cargo fmt --check, cargo check --all-targets, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test
[ ] Docs/fixtures updated if behavior or UX changes

title: Epic: Extensions Runtime Integration (100% Parity)
description:
# Epic: Extensions Runtime Integration

## Executive Summary

This epic tracks all work required to achieve 100% feature parity for the Pi Agent extensions runtime. The Rust port has ~70-80% of the extensions infrastructure implemented (QuickJS runtime, Promise bridge, capability policy, protocol validation) but is missing the critical agent integration layer that wires everything together.

## Background & Context

The TypeScript Pi Agent supports a powerful extensions system that allows:
- Custom tool registration (pi.registerTool)
- Slash command registration (pi.registerCommand)
- Event hook interception (pi.on for lifecycle events)
- UI interactions (dialogs, notifications, status updates)
- Session access (messages, state, entries)

The Rust port has implemented the JavaScript runtime (PiJS using QuickJS) with:
- Full Promise bridge architecture (native Rust → JS Promise → completion)
- All 6 hostcall types defined (tool, exec, http, session, ui, events)
- Deterministic event loop with timer management
- TypeScript transpilation via SWC
- Virtual module shims for Node.js compatibility
- Capability manifest and policy enforcement

## What's Missing (The Integration Layer)

The gap is the "glue" between the agent loop and the extension runtime:

1. **Hostcall Dispatcher**: Extensions call pi.tool(), pi.http(), etc. These enqueue HostcallRequest objects, but nothing processes them.

2. **Tool Execution Bridge**: Extensions can register tools, but the agent can't execute them.

3. **Event Hook Dispatch**: Extensions register hooks via pi.on(), but the agent doesn't fire events at lifecycle points.

4. **Slash Command Handler**: Extensions register commands, but /command invocations don't reach the JS runtime.

5. **Session Context Binding**: The ExtensionSession trait is defined but not bound to actual session state.

6. **UI Marshaling**: Extension UI requests need to flow to TUI or RPC layer.

## Success Criteria

- All extension fixture tests pass
- Extensions can register and execute tools
- Extensions can intercept and modify tool results via events
- Slash commands registered by extensions are executable
- Event hooks fire at all documented lifecycle points
- UI dialogs work in both TUI and RPC modes
- Benchmark targets met for hostcall dispatch (<100µs)

## References

- src/extensions.rs (protocol, policy, connectors)
- src/extensions_js.rs (QuickJS runtime, Promise bridge)
- EXISTING_PI_STRUCTURE.md Section 12 (Extensions API spec)
close_reason: All parent-child children closed (bd-1yo9, bd-10vp, bd-37qz). Core integration layer complete: hostcall dispatcher routes all 6 kinds, tool execution bridge works, event hook dispatch fires at all lifecycle points, session/UI handlers implemented.

title: Extension session connector integration (interactive + RPC)
description:
# Background
Extensions rely on session operations to:
- read the current session state (model/thinking/streaming flags, session id/name/file)
- enumerate messages/entries/branch
- mutate session metadata and content (set_name, append_message, append_entry, set_model, set_thinking_level, set_label)

In the Hostcall ABI these should be routed as `host_call` with `method = session` and a connector-specific `params` shape.

`src/extensions.rs` defines the `ExtensionSession` trait and `dispatch_hostcall_session()` already supports a rich set of ops + aliases.

# Gap (Concrete, Observed)
We currently have **two** `ExtensionSession` implementations with **different semantics**:
- Interactive: `InteractiveExtensionSession` (`src/interactive.rs`)
- Non-interactive / agent session handle: `SessionHandle` (`src/session.rs`)

Mismatch examples (these are the real parity risks):
- `get_state`:
  - interactive returns a rich object (e.g. `model`, `thinkingLevel`, `isStreaming`, `isCompacting`, `sessionId`, `sessionFile`, `sessionName`, `autoCompactionEnabled`, `messageCount`, ...)
  - `SessionHandle` returns only `{sessionFile, sessionName}`
- `get_messages`:
  - interactive filters to message entries on the current path + specific message types
  - `SessionHandle` returns all `SessionEntry::Message` across the entire session, not branch-scoped
- `get_entries` / `get_branch`:
  - interactive returns entries for the current path; branch is treated as current path
  - `SessionHandle` returns all entries for `get_entries`, but branch is only current path
- Persistence:
  - interactive saves immediately when `save_enabled`
  - `SessionHandle` mutates in-memory but does not save

Net: extensions can observe different state shapes + ordering depending on mode, which breaks compatibility and makes conformance/E2E flaky.

# Goal
Implement the session connector surface used by extensions and wire it end-to-end with **identical semantics** in:
- interactive TUI mode
- RPC mode (`pi --mode rpc`)

# Deliverables
1) **Contract (spec-first)**
- Define exact op names + params + return shapes (including allowed aliases).
- Pin field names + defaults to legacy expectations.

2) **Shared semantics**
- Unify the "extension-visible session state" builder so interactive + RPC produce the same shape.
- Enforce deterministic ordering for enumeration APIs.
- Define persistence rules (when session mutations must be saved) so extensions do not observe "worked but not persisted" behavior.

3) **Hostcall ABI wiring**
- Route `session.*` through the shared hostcall dispatcher (bd-1uy.1.1) so:
  - capability derivation + policy are consistent
  - timeouts/cancellation are enforced
  - error mapping uses taxonomy-only codes (`timeout|denied|io|invalid_request|internal`)

4) **Tests + E2E**
- Unit tests for each op (success + invalid_request + denied + timeout/cancel where applicable).
- Cross-mode parity tests (interactive vs RPC vs protocol adapter where applicable).
- E2E scenarios with JSONL logs + deterministic artifacts per bd-4u9.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Sample extensions that rely on session APIs run unmodified.
- Behavior is deterministic under harness control.
- Hostcall error codes are taxonomy-only.

[ ] Scope in description implemented fully with no feature loss
[ ] Unit tests cover core success/failure + edge cases for this bead

[ ] Logs include inputs, outputs, timing, and redaction summary; artifacts list is deterministic
[ ] Quality gates pass: cargo fmt --check, cargo check --all-targets, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test

title: Spec: Extension session API contract (ops, params, outputs, determinism)
description:
# Goal
Define the **authoritative Extension Session connector contract** used by JS + WASM extensions.

This spec must be precise enough that we can implement it once and then:
- run conformance fixtures
- run cross-mode parity tests (interactive vs RPC)
- never re-open legacy code to resolve ambiguity

# Inputs (Where the truth lives)
- Legacy Pi (TypeScript): `legacy_pi_mono_code/` (search for `pi.session(`)
- Current Rust impl candidates:
  - `src/extensions.rs` (`dispatch_hostcall_session()`)
  - `src/interactive.rs` (`InteractiveExtensionSession`)
  - `src/session.rs` (`SessionHandle`)
  - `src/extension_dispatcher.rs` (table-driven tests + op coverage examples)

# Contract Surface
Pi extensions call `pi.session(op, args)`.

## Ops (must be specified)
Read-only:
- `get_state` (and accepted aliases)
- `get_messages`
- `get_entries`
- `get_branch`
- `get_model`
- `get_thinking_level`

Write:
- `set_name`
- `append_message`
- `append_entry` (custom entry)
- `set_model`
- `set_thinking_level`
- `set_label`

Convenience aliases (must be pinned):
- `get_file` (derived from state)
- `get_name` (derived from state)

## For each op, specify EXACTLY
- Allowed op spellings/aliases (case/underscore/camelCase tolerance)
- Params schema:
  - required keys
  - accepted alternate key spellings (e.g. `modelId` vs `model_id`)
  - defaults (if missing)
  - validation rules (empty string vs null vs missing)
- Output schema:
  - exact JSON shape (object keys + types)
  - nullability rules
  - ordering guarantees for lists
- Error mapping:
  - `invalid_request` for validation
  - `denied` when session handle is absent/unavailable
  - `io` for persistence failures
  - `internal` for unexpected failures
  - `timeout` only where the op is explicitly allowed to time out

# Canonical Output Shapes (must be stable)
## `get_state`
Pin the canonical state object.

Today interactive returns a rich object (model/thinking/streaming/session id/name/file/counts) while `SessionHandle` returns only `{sessionFile, sessionName}`.

This spec must choose the **canonical superset** and define default values for non-interactive/RPC mode so shape is identical across modes.

## Enumeration APIs
- Define whether `get_messages`/`get_entries` enumerate the **current branch/path** only (legacy-like) vs the entire session file.
- Define filtering rules for message types (which SessionMessage variants are included).

# Determinism Requirements
- For any list return value: define a stable ordering key (typically session order within the current path).
- Define whether IDs and timestamps are returned and if they need normalization in tests.

# Persistence Rules
Define when session mutations must be persisted:
- In interactive mode, persistence should occur immediately when `save_enabled`.
- In RPC mode, define whether persistence must be immediate or end-of-turn, and ensure it is identical to interactive in observable behavior.

# Hostcall ABI Integration Requirements
- Session ops must be expressible as canonical `HostCallPayload { capability: "session", method: "session", params: ... }`.
- The params shape must be compatible with `params_hash` parity across JS/WASM/protocol (bd-1uy.1.1.2).

# Deliverables
- A written spec section (likely in the bead description or referenced doc) listing:
  - op table with params/output/errors
  - canonical `get_state` schema
  - determinism + persistence rules
  - mapping into Hostcall ABI canonical params

## Acceptance Criteria
- Spec is detailed enough that two engineers can independently implement it and produce identical behavior.
- Spec explicitly calls out any deviations from legacy (ideally none).
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] Op/params/output/error table complete for all session ops (including aliases)
[ ] Canonical `get_state` schema pinned with explicit defaults for non-interactive/RPC mode
[ ] Determinism rules explicit (ordering + filtering for messages/entries)
[ ] Persistence rules explicit (when and how session mutations are saved)
[ ] Canonical Hostcall ABI params shape pinned (enables `params_hash` parity)
[ ] Test plan enumerated: unit + parity + E2E (bd-1gl.1, bd-kh2.2)
close_reason: Spec complete (see comment)

comments.author: RosePrairie
comments.text:
# Extension Session API Contract (v1)

This is the **authoritative spec** for the extension session connector:

- Extension JS/WASM calls: `pi.session(op, args)`
- Hostcall ABI: `HostCallPayload { capability: "session", method: "session", params: { op, ... } }`
- Implementations MUST be **identical across modes** (interactive vs RPC/non-interactive), with explicit defaults where a mode lacks data.

Primary goals:
- Pin exact op names + aliases
- Pin params + output schemas (including ordering guarantees)
- Pin taxonomy-only error mapping
- Pin determinism + persistence rules
- Pin canonical ABI params shapes to enable `params_hash` parity

---

## 1) Canonical Hostcall Params Shape (Normative)

All session hostcalls use:

```json
{ "op": "get_state", "...": "..." }
```

Rules:
- `op` is required and MUST be a string.
- Host normalizes op by:
  - trimming
  - ASCII lowercasing
  - accepting both snake_case and camelCase spellings (see per-op alias lists).
- For `params_hash` parity, the **canonical** `op` value is the snake_case form listed below.
- Canonical argument keys are **camelCase** (e.g. `modelId`, `targetId`, `customType`).
  - Host MUST accept snake_case aliases.

---

## 2) Canonical `get_state` Schema (Normative)

`get_state` MUST return the legacy-compatible superset (matches pi-mono RPC `RpcSessionState`).

```jsonc
{
  // model may be omitted/null if not known
  "model": {
    "provider": "anthropic",
    "id": "claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
    "name": "Claude Sonnet 4",
    "api": "anthropic-messages",
    "baseUrl": "https://api.anthropic.com",
    "reasoning": true,
    "contextWindow": 200000,
    "maxTokens": 16384,
    "apiKeyPresent": true
  },

  "thinkingLevel": "off",          // string; default "off"
  "isStreaming": false,             // bool
  "isCompacting": false,            // bool
  "steeringMode": "one-at-a-time", // "all" | "one-at-a-time"
  "followUpMode": "one-at-a-time", // "all" | "one-at-a-time"

  "sessionFile": "/abs/path/session.jsonl", // string|null
  "sessionId": "<uuid>",                    // string (required)
  "sessionName": "my session",              // string|null

  "autoCompactionEnabled": false, // bool
  "messageCount": 0,              // int >= 0 (count on current branch)
  "pendingMessageCount": 0        // int >= 0
}
```

Defaults when the mode cannot supply a field:
- `model`: `null`
- `thinkingLevel`: `"off"`
- `isStreaming`: `false`
- `isCompacting`: `false`
- `steeringMode`: `"one-at-a-time"`
- `followUpMode`: `"one-at-a-time"`
- `sessionFile`: `null`
- `sessionId`: `""` only if session is unavailable (otherwise MUST be non-empty)
- `sessionName`: `null`
- `autoCompactionEnabled`: `false`
- `messageCount`: `0`
- `pendingMessageCount`: `0`

Notes:
- `messageCount` counts **SessionEntry::Message** entries on the **current branch**.
- `pendingMessageCount` is about queued steering/follow-up messages, not session file length.

---

## 3) Enumeration Semantics (Determinism)

### 3.1 `get_entries`
- Returns **all session entries** (entire session file), excluding the session header.
- Ordering: stable **append/file order** (oldest first).
- Includes all entry types: message, model_change, thinking_level_change, compaction, branch_summary, label, session_info, custom.

### 3.2 `get_branch`
- Returns the **current path** from root to current leaf (pi-mono `SessionManager.getBranch()` semantics).
- Ordering: stable path order (root → leaf).
- Includes all entry types in the path.

### 3.3 `get_messages`
- Returns message payloads for the **current branch only**.
- Include only `SessionEntry::Message` payloads whose `role` is one of:
  - `user`, `assistant`, `toolResult`, `custom`, `bashExecution`
- Exclude message roles `branchSummary` / `compactionSummary` (those are top-level entries).
- Ordering: branch order (root → leaf).

---

## 4) Op Table (Normative)

### Read ops

#### `get_state`
- Aliases accepted: `get_state`, `getState`, `getstate`
- Params: none
- Output: canonical `RpcSessionState` object (see §2)
- Errors:
  - `denied`: session handle unavailable

#### `get_entries`
- Aliases: `get_entries`, `getEntries`, `getentries`
- Output: `SessionEntry[]` (full file, append order)
- Errors:
  - `denied`: session handle unavailable

#### `get_branch`
- Aliases: `get_branch`, `getBranch`, `getbranch`
- Output: `SessionEntry[]` (current path)
- Errors:
  - `denied`: session handle unavailable

#### `get_messages`
- Aliases: `get_messages`, `getMessages`, `getmessages`
- Output: `SessionMessage[]` (current branch only; see §3.3)
- Errors:
  - `denied`: session handle unavailable

#### `get_model`
- Aliases: `get_model`, `getModel`, `getmodel`
- Output:
```json
{ "provider": "anthropic", "modelId": "claude-sonnet-4-20250514" }
```
- Nullability: either field may be `null`.
- Errors:
  - `denied`: session handle unavailable

#### `get_thinking_level`
- Aliases: `get_thinking_level`, `getThinkingLevel`, `getthinkinglevel`
- Output: string or `null`
- Errors:
  - `denied`: session handle unavailable

#### `get_file`
- Aliases: `get_file`, `getFile`, `getfile`
- Output: same as `get_state.sessionFile` (string|null)
- Errors:
  - `denied`: session handle unavailable

#### `get_name`
- Aliases: `get_name`, `getName`, `getname`
- Output: same as `get_state.sessionName` (string|null)
- Errors:
  - `denied`: session handle unavailable

---

### Write ops (append-only semantics)

Write ops MUST:
- append exactly one entry (except where explicitly defined otherwise)
- advance the session leaf pointer to the new entry
- persist immediately when persistence is enabled (see §5)
- return the new entry id as a string

#### `set_name`
- Aliases: `set_name`, `setName`, `setname`
- Canonical params:
```json
{ "name": "My Session" }
```
- Validation:
  - `name` required; if null/missing => `invalid_request`
  - empty/whitespace name => clear (store `null` name)
- Output: new entry id string (session_info entry)
- Errors:
  - `invalid_request`
  - `denied`
  - `io` (persistence failure)

#### `append_message`
- Aliases: `append_message`, `appendMessage`, `appendmessage`
- Canonical params:
```json
{ "message": { "role": "user", "content": "hi", "timestamp": 123 } }
```
- Compatibility:
  - If `message` field is missing, host MAY treat the entire params object as the message.
- Output: new entry id string (message entry)
- Errors:
  - `invalid_request` (message parse/validation)
  - `denied`
  - `io`

#### `append_entry`
- Aliases: `append_entry`, `appendEntry`, `appendentry`
- Canonical params:
```json
{ "customType": "my_ext.state", "data": {"k": "v"} }
```
- Validation:
  - `customType` required and non-empty
- Output: new entry id string (custom entry)
- Errors:
  - `invalid_request`
  - `denied`
  - `io`

#### `set_model`
- Aliases: `set_model`, `setModel`, `setmodel`
- Canonical params:
```json
{ "provider": "anthropic", "modelId": "claude-sonnet-4-20250514" }
```
- Validation: provider/modelId required non-empty
- Output: new entry id string (model_change entry)
- Side effects: update session header provider/modelId
- Errors: `invalid_request` | `denied` | `io`

#### `set_thinking_level`
- Aliases: `set_thinking_level`, `setThinkingLevel`, `setthinkinglevel`
- Canonical params:
```json
{ "thinkingLevel": "high" }
```
- Accepted aliases: `level`, `thinking_level`
- Validation: required non-empty
- Output: new entry id string (thinking_level_change entry)
- Side effects: update session header thinkingLevel
- Errors: `invalid_request` | `denied` | `io`

#### `set_label`
- Aliases: `set_label`, `setLabel`, `setlabel`
- Canonical params:
```json
{ "targetId": "abcd1234", "label": "review" }
```
- Accepted aliases:
  - `target_id`, `entryId`, `entry_id`
- Semantics:
  - `label` missing/null/empty => clear label for target
- Validation:
  - `targetId` required non-empty
  - targetId MUST exist in the session; otherwise `invalid_request`
- Output: new entry id string (label entry)
- Errors: `invalid_request` | `denied` | `io`

---

## 5) Persistence Rules (Normative)

- If the session is backed by a persistent store and saving is enabled:
  - every write op MUST call `save()` before returning success
  - failures surface as taxonomy `io`
- If saving is disabled (ephemeral sessions):
  - write ops mutate in-memory only and MUST NOT return `io` due to persistence

---

## 6) Error Taxonomy Mapping (Normative)

- `invalid_request`: bad `op`, missing/invalid params, parse failures, target missing
- `denied`: session handle not configured/unavailable
- `io`: persistence failure (save/index) or backing store I/O failures
- `internal`: invariant violations

Timeout:
- Session ops are expected to be fast; `timeout` should only arise from the outer hostcall deadline.

---

## 7) Known Rust Divergences to Fix (follow-up beads)

Current mismatches observed in Rust code (to be resolved in bd-321a.2/.3/.4):
- `SessionHandle.get_state()` currently returns only `{sessionFile, sessionName}`; must return the canonical superset (§2).
- `InteractiveExtensionSession.get_entries()` currently returns current path; must return full file entries (§3.1).
- `SessionHandle.get_messages()` currently iterates all entries; must be branch-only (§3.3).
- Write ops in `SessionHandle` currently do not persist immediately; must follow §5.
- `set_label` currently does not error when `targetId` does not exist; must be `invalid_request`.
- `append_entry` currently allows empty `customType`; must be `invalid_request`.

title: Impl: Align SessionHandle (RPC/non-interactive) extension session semantics to spec
description:
# Goal
Make the non-interactive / RPC-mode session connector semantics match the session spec (bd-321a.1) exactly.

This work is primarily about the `SessionHandle` implementation in `src/session.rs`.

# Background (Observed)
`SessionHandle` currently diverges from interactive semantics:
- `get_state` returns only `{sessionFile, sessionName}`
- `get_messages` enumerates all `SessionEntry::Message` across the entire session (not branch-scoped)
- `get_entries` returns all entries (not branch-scoped)
- mutating ops do not persist (`save_enabled` not consulted)

# Scope
1) **Canonical state builder**
- Introduce a shared helper (module/function) that constructs the canonical `get_state` payload from:
  - Session header (provider/model/thinking)
  - Session entries for current path (messageCount)
  - Known runtime flags (streaming/compacting/pending message counts)
- The helper should be reusable by interactive and non-interactive implementations so drift becomes mechanically harder.

2) **Branch scoping + filtering**
- Update `get_messages` to follow the spec:
  - enumerate entries for current path
  - include exactly the allowed message variants
  - preserve stable order
- Update `get_entries` and `get_branch` semantics to match spec (likely both current-path scoped, unless spec chooses otherwise).

3) **Persistence semantics**
- Mutating ops must persist in the same cases as interactive.
- If the runtime has `save_enabled=false`, define the observable behavior and ensure it matches spec.

4) **Error mapping**
- Ensure any errors raised from session locking / save failures map onto the fixed hostcall taxonomy (no ad-hoc codes).

# Tests
- Unit tests for `SessionHandle` op semantics:
  - `get_state` schema keys + defaults
  - `get_messages` filtering and ordering
  - `get_entries`/`get_branch` scoping
  - persistence: verify session file changes when `save_enabled=true`

## Acceptance Criteria
- Running the same extension in interactive and RPC mode yields identical session API observable outputs (modulo explicitly-specified fields).
- No new behavior is introduced outside the spec.
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] Scope in description implemented fully with no feature loss
[ ] `SessionHandle` behavior matches the spec (bd-321a.1) for all implemented ops
[ ] Unit tests cover success/failure + edge cases for all touched ops

title: Hostcall ABI: Session method routing uses shared dispatcher + taxonomy
description:
# Goal
Route all extension session operations through the **shared hostcall dispatcher** (bd-1uy.1.1) so behavior is:
- consistent across JS / WASM / protocol adapter
- capability-enforced in one place
- taxonomy-correct (`timeout|denied|io|invalid_request|internal` only)
- conformance-testable with stable `params_hash` parity

# Background (Observed)
Session ops currently have logic in `dispatch_hostcall_session()` (`src/extensions.rs`) and differ between interactive and non-interactive `ExtensionSession` implementations.

The Hostcall ABI workstream requires:
- canonical params shape
- strict error taxonomy
- shared enforcement point

# Scope
1) **Canonical params shape**
- Implement the spec-chosen canonical `HostCallPayload` params for `method="session"` (bd-321a.1).
- Ensure JS/WASM/protocol compute identical `params_hash` for equivalent calls.

2) **Dispatcher wiring**
- Ensure the runtime path that handles session hostcalls calls `dispatch_host_call_shared()` (bd-1uy.1.1).
- Any existing direct dispatch must be removed or made a thin adapter.

3) **Taxonomy-only errors**
- Eliminate any ad-hoc error codes observable at the ABI boundary.
- Ensure "no session configured" is `denied` (not `invalid_request`).

4) **Parity tests integration**
- Extend (or satisfy) bd-1uy.1.4 canonical cases for session:
  - `get_state` success
  - `set_model` invalid_request (missing provider/modelId)
  - `set_label` invalid_request (missing targetId)
  - denied when session handle missing

# Tests
- Table-driven unit tests for the dispatcher session route.
- Parity test coverage via bd-1uy.1.4.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Session hostcalls behave identically across JS/WASM/protocol adapter and emit taxonomy-only errors.
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] Session hostcalls route through the shared dispatcher (bd-1uy.1.1)
[ ] Canonical params shape implemented and `params_hash` parity holds across runtimes
[ ] Only taxonomy error codes are observable at the ABI boundary
[ ] Parity test suite (bd-1uy.1.4) includes session cases and passes
[ ] Unit tests cover success + error paths for session routing
[ ] Quality gates pass: cargo fmt --check, cargo check --all-targets, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test
