TESTING + LOGGING REQUIREMENTS

Code-search is the highest-signal discovery method, but it is easy to get wrong (false positives/negatives). Make it testable.

Unit tests
- Fixture-based tests that validate:
  - signature matching rules (imports + export default + registration calls)
  - false-positive suppression (repos that mention Pi but do not implement ExtensionAPI)
  - stable extraction of (repo, path-to-entrypoint, snippet/anchor)

E2E script
- Offline E2E that replays fixture search results and outputs a normalized list of entrypoints.

Logging
- JSONL logs should record:
  - exact search queries executed
  - hit counts per query
  - per-hit classification decision + reason
  - any rate-limit/backoff events

Quality gate
- A “known corpus” regression test: ensure we can rediscover a fixed set of known entrypoints from our vendored artifacts (sanity check the matcher).

title: Implement pi.registerFlag() for extension CLI flags
description:
Allow extensions to register custom CLI flags.

## API Spec (from legacy)
```typescript
pi.registerFlag(name, {
  description: string,
  type: 'boolean' | 'string',
  default?: boolean | string
});

// Later retrieval:
const value = pi.getFlag('my-flag');
```

## Implementation Requirements
1. FlagRegistry in extension runtime
2. Two-phase CLI parsing (like legacy):
   - First pass: parse extension/skill/prompt/theme flags, load resources
   - Second pass: parse with extension-registered flags
3. Hostcall handlers for 'registerFlag' and 'getFlag'
4. Integration with clap argument parsing

## Challenges
- Flags must be registered before CLI parsing completes
- Extension loading happens early in startup
- Need to re-parse args after extensions register flags

## Data Flow
1. Extensions loaded early (from settings + CLI flags)
2. Extension calls pi.registerFlag('my-flag', {...})
3. CLI re-parses with registered flags
4. Extension can call pi.getFlag('my-flag') to get value

## Test Plan
- Unit test: registerFlag stores flag definition
- Unit test: getFlag returns correct value
- Integration test: --my-flag value parsed correctly
- E2E test: pi --my-flag value runs with extension seeing value

## Files to Modify
- src/extensions.rs (FlagRegistry)
- src/extensions_js.rs (hostcall handlers)
- src/cli.rs (two-phase parsing)
- src/main.rs (wire up flag registration timing)

title: Implement pi.events for inter-extension communication
description:
Allow extensions to communicate via a shared event bus.

## API Spec (from legacy)
```typescript
const eventBus = pi.events;

// Emit custom event
eventBus.emit(eventName: string, data: unknown): void

// Listen for events
const unsubscribe = eventBus.on(eventName: string, handler: (data) => void): () => void
```

## Use Cases
- Extension coordination (one extension signals another)
- Workflow automation (chain of extensions)
- State sharing between extensions

## Implementation Requirements
1. SharedEventBus in extension runtime
2. Hostcall handlers for 'events.emit' and 'events.on'
3. Handler registration with unsubscribe support
4. Event dispatch to all registered handlers

## Concurrency Notes
- Multiple handlers may fire concurrently
- Handlers execute in JS runtime context
- Errors in one handler shouldn't affect others

## Test Plan
- Unit test: emit triggers registered handlers
- Unit test: unsubscribe stops handler calls
- Unit test: multiple handlers receive same event
- Integration test: two extensions communicate

## Files to Modify
- src/extensions.rs (SharedEventBus)
- src/extensions_js.rs (hostcall handlers)

title: [MOCK-CODE-FINDER] Implement real node:crypto cipher/keypair APIs or narrow exported surface
description:
# Finding
A production mock-code-finder pass found exported node:crypto APIs in src/crypto_shim.rs that are still wired to unsupportedCryptoApi instead of real behavior: createCipheriv, createDecipheriv, generateKeyPairSync, publicEncrypt, and privateDecrypt. docs/extension-compatibility-matrix.md also records symmetric encryption as Missing, and tests/node_crypto_shim.rs currently asserts that createCipheriv/createDecipheriv throw. br search found no existing open or closed bead for createCipheriv, node:crypto, cipher, generateKeyPair, publicEncrypt, or privateDecrypt.

# Why this matters
Extensions that depend on common Node crypto primitives can load successfully but fail at runtime on a missing API. Because the functions are exported from the virtual node:crypto module, this is more actionable than an unsupported provider route: it is a partially exposed compatibility surface.

# Desired outcome
Choose the truth-preserving implementation path and complete it end to end:
- Prefer implementing real Node-compatible behavior for a bounded, high-value subset first, such as createCipheriv/createDecipheriv for aes-128-gcm/aes-192-gcm/aes-256-gcm with update/final/getAuthTag/setAuthTag semantics, strict key/iv/tag validation, Buffer-compatible outputs, and fail-closed unsupported algorithms.
- If keypair/RSA APIs remain out of scope, either implement a similarly bounded RSA/keypair subset or narrow/document/export-gate them so the compatibility matrix and tests no longer imply accidental runtime support.
- Update docs/extension-compatibility-matrix.md and any parity/runtime matrix artifacts only after executable behavior exists.

# Test obligations
Add or update tests/node_crypto_shim.rs with positive encrypt/decrypt round trips against Node-compatible vectors, negative controls for bad key/iv/tag lengths, unsupported algorithms, double-finalization, and auth-tag failures. Add extension conformance or runtime API matrix checks if those artifacts classify node:crypto support.

# Validation
Use rch for any cargo-heavy work. Minimum expected proof: cargo fmt --check, focused rch test for node_crypto_shim, cargo check --all-targets and clippy via rch if Rust dependency/API shape changes, staged UBS or staged-delta gate, and ./scripts/reconcile_beads_ledger.sh.

# Claim boundary
Do not claim full Node crypto parity unless the matrix and tests cover it. Partial support must be explicitly named and fail closed for everything else.
close_reason: Completed: added bounded AES-128-GCM/AES-256-GCM createCipheriv/createDecipheriv support with strict key/IV/tag validation, AAD, auth failure handling, updated node_crypto_shim tests and compatibility matrix, and passed focused/full validation gates.

title: Implement verbose test logging infrastructure
description:
# Implement verbose test logging infrastructure

## Goal
Create shared infrastructure for detailed logging in all integration tests,
enabling easy debugging when tests fail.

## Background
E2E and integration tests need detailed logging to debug failures:
- Every test action should be logged
- Timestamps for timing analysis
- Context (file paths, values) for reproduction
- Logs dumped automatically on test failure

## Implementation

### Log Infrastructure
```rust
// tests/common/logging.rs

use std::sync::Mutex;
use std::time::Instant;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct LogEntry {
    pub timestamp: Instant,
    pub level: LogLevel,
    pub category: &'static str,
    pub message: String,
    pub context: Vec<(String, String)>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub enum LogLevel {
    Debug,
    Info,
    Warn,
    Error,
}

pub struct TestLogger {
    entries: Mutex<Vec<LogEntry>>,
    start: Instant,
}
```

### Redaction + Artifacts
- Add helpers to redact sensitive values in env/header/context keys (API keys, auth headers).
- Add a simple artifact registry: `record_artifact(name, path)` so tests can attach outputs.
- On panic, dump logs + artifact list (paths) to stderr.

### Test Harness Integration
```rust
// tests/common/harness.rs

pub struct TestHarness {
    pub logger: TestLogger,
    pub temp_dir: TempDir,
}

impl Drop for TestHarness {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if std::thread::panicking() {
            eprintln!("\n=== TEST LOGS ===\n{}", self.logger.dump());
            eprintln!("=== ARTIFACTS ===\n{}", self.logger.dump_artifacts());
        }
    }
}
```

### Optional File Output
- If `TEST_LOG_PATH` is set, write logs to that path in addition to stderr.

## Files
- tests/common/mod.rs
- tests/common/logging.rs
- tests/common/harness.rs

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] TestLogger captures all levels
- [ ] Context key-values supported
- [ ] Timestamps included
- [ ] Redaction helpers present
- [ ] Artifact registry present
- [ ] Auto-dump on test failure
- [ ] Optional file output works
- [ ] All integration tests use harness
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] Scope in description implemented fully with no feature loss
[ ] Unit tests cover core success/failure + edge cases for this bead (add regression coverage if applicable)

[ ] Quality gates pass: cargo fmt --check, cargo check --all-targets, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test
[ ] Docs/fixtures updated if behavior or UX changes

title: Define publishing order + versioning policy across sibling crates
description:
# Goal
Write down the concrete publish plan so we can execute it deterministically across repos.

# Decisions Required
- Versioning scheme:
  - charmed_rust and sqlmodel_rust use `version.workspace = true` today. Decide whether we keep a unified workspace version (recommended) or split.
  - Decide tag format: `vX.Y.Z` (recommended) and whether crates share the same tag.
- Publish order:
  - Identify all internal path/workspace deps that must be published first (macros crates, conformance crates, harmonica, etc.).
- Release workflow standard:
  - Minimal build/test job + publish job gated on tags and `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`.

# Deliverables
- A single checklist (in this issue) that lists:
  - the exact crate publish order
  - the exact commands (`cargo publish -p <crate> --all-features`, etc.)
  - what to verify (`cargo publish --dry-run`, included files, CI status)

# Acceptance
- The publish order is complete (no missing internal deps).
- Plan includes at least: asupersync workspace crates, charmed workspace crates needed by Pi, sqlmodel workspace crates, rich_rust.
close_reason: Completed

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
Publish plan draft for bd-3mmy (dependency derived from cargo metadata in /data/projects/asupersync, /data/projects/charmed_rust, /data/projects/sqlmodel_rust, /data/projects/rich_rust).

Decisions
- Versioning: keep unified workspace version for charmed_rust and sqlmodel_rust using [workspace.package].version.
- Tag format: vX.Y.Z per repository; publish only from signed or protected tag pipelines.
- Scope for this migration: publish all crates required to remove pi_agent_rust path deps, plus strict dependency prerequisites.

Exact publish order (minimum set required by pi_agent_rust)
1. asupersync-macros
2. asupersync-conformance
3. asupersync
4. charmed-lipgloss
5. charmed-bubbletea-macros
6. charmed-bubbletea
7. charmed-harmonica
8. charmed-bubbles
9. charmed-glamour
10. sqlmodel-core
11. sqlmodel-macros
12. sqlmodel-schema
13. sqlmodel-console
14. sqlmodel-sqlite
15. rich_rust

Rationale by workspace
- asupersync depends on path crates asupersync-macros and asupersync-conformance.
- pi depends on charmed-bubbletea, charmed-lipgloss, charmed-bubbles, charmed-glamour; transitive requirements are bubbletea-macros and harmonica.
- pi depends on sqlmodel-core and sqlmodel-sqlite; sqlmodel-sqlite depends on sqlmodel-console -> sqlmodel-schema -> sqlmodel-macros -> sqlmodel-core.
- rich_rust has no internal path deps.

Command checklist (run in each source repo)
- Preflight:
  - cargo fmt --all -- --check
  - cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
  - cargo test --workspace
- Package + dry run each crate before publish:
  - cargo package -p <crate> --locked
  - cargo publish -p <crate> --dry-run --locked
- Publish in listed order with retry/backoff for crates.io index delay:
  - cargo publish -p <crate> --locked
  - sleep 30

Release workflow standard (all sibling repos)
- Trigger: refs/tags/v* plus manual dispatch fallback.
- Job 1 validate: fmt + clippy -D warnings + tests.
- Job 2 publish: verify Cargo.toml version matches tag, then publish crates in dependency order if CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN is set.
- Job 3 summary/release: write publish status to GitHub step summary and create release notes artifact.

Verification checklist
- crates.io shows new versions for all crates in order.
- cargo publish --dry-run passes on a clean checkout at the release tag.
- ci publish logs show no unresolved path dependencies.
- pi_agent_rust compiles after replacing path deps with versions.

pi_agent_rust migration steps after publishes
1. Replace path deps in Cargo.toml with version-only entries for all published crates.
2. Add local-dev override guidance via [patch.crates-io] in developer docs (optional local workflow, not committed for release branches).
3. Run: cargo update && cargo check --all-targets && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test.
4. Cut pi_agent_rust tag only after green CI on version-only dependency graph.

Notes
- charmed_rust and sqlmodel_rust already use workspace versioning patterns, so unified tag per repo is the least error prone path.
- Existing release workflows already approximate this; standardization mainly needs consistency on dependency order and retry behavior.

title: Phase 3: OAuth support for extension providers
description:
Add OAuth authentication support for extension-registered providers.

## Background
Phase 1 (bd-1oj9): Basic provider registration
Phase 2 (bd-39q8): Custom streaming
This phase adds OAuth for providers requiring browser-based auth.

## API Addition
```typescript
pi.registerProvider(name, {
  // ... base config
  oauth?: {
    authUrl: string,
    tokenUrl: string,
    clientId: string,
    scopes: string[],
    redirectUri?: string
  }
});
```

## Implementation Requirements
1. OAuth flow initiation from CLI
2. Local callback server for redirect
3. Token storage and refresh
4. Integration with provider requests

## OAuth Flow
1. Extension registers provider with oauth config
2. User selects provider requiring auth
3. Pi opens browser to authUrl
4. User authenticates, redirected to local server
5. Token exchanged and stored
6. Provider uses token for requests

## Test Plan
- Unit test: OAuth config stored correctly
- Integration test: OAuth flow completes (mocked browser)
- Test: Token refresh works

## Files to Modify
- src/extensions.rs (OAuth config)
- src/oauth.rs (new - OAuth flow)
- src/provider.rs (use OAuth tokens)

title: Epic: Differential Extension Conformance Testing (TS-Rust Oracle)
description:
# Epic: Differential Extension Conformance Testing (TS-Rust Oracle)

## The Core Principle

Every extension that works in pi-mono TypeScript runtime MUST produce IDENTICAL behavior in our Rust QuickJS runtime, with ZERO source code modifications. This is not a theoretical goal -- it is a hard requirement for production readiness.

## Why Differential Testing (Not Fixture Replay)

Previous approach: capture TS outputs once, save as fixtures, replay in Rust.
Problem: fixtures are stale, hard to maintain, don't catch edge cases.

New approach: Run the SAME unmodified extension code through BOTH runtimes simultaneously, with the SAME inputs/mocks, and compare outputs directly. The TypeScript pi-mono runtime IS the oracle. This is differential/oracle testing.

Benefits:
- No fixture staleness -- always testing against live TS behavior
- Catches subtle differences in event ordering, error messages, type coercion
- Can test with ANY extension, not just ones we have written fixtures for
- Easy to add new extensions to the corpus -- just drop them in

## Architecture

Extension Source (.ts file) -> BOTH pi-mono (TS via Bun/jiti) AND Rust (swc+QuickJS) -> Compare outputs (registrations, event responses, hostcall results) -> PASS or FAIL

## Corpus (collected)

1,167+ TypeScript files across 5 tiers:
- 60 official pi-mono example extensions
- 58 community extensions
- 63 npm registry extensions
- 23 third-party GitHub extensions
- 7 agent collection extensions

## Key Technical Details

- pi-mono location: legacy_pi_mono_code/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/
- Extension loader (TS): src/core/extensions/loader.ts -- uses jiti for TS loading
- Extension types (TS): src/core/extensions/types.ts -- ExtensionAPI, Extension, events
- Extension runner (TS): src/core/extensions/runner.ts -- lifecycle management
- Rust runtime: src/extensions.rs + src/extensions_js.rs -- QuickJS-based
- Bun 1.3.8: Available at /home/ubuntu/.bun/bin/bun
- Artifacts: tests/ext_conformance/artifacts/

## Success Criteria

- 100% of official pi-mono extensions (60) produce identical output in both runtimes
- 90%+ of community extensions produce identical output
- Performance within 2x of TypeScript for load time, 1.5x for event dispatch
- Zero crashes, zero panics, zero undefined behavior
- CI pipeline runs full suite on every PR
- Machine-readable conformance report generated per run

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
SUPERSEDES EXISTING BEADS: This epic replaces the previous fragmented conformance testing beads (bd-6vcm, bd-2jlj, bd-c6xq, bd-2bis) with a unified DIFFERENTIAL TESTING approach. Key change: instead of capturing TS fixtures once and replaying in Rust, we run BOTH runtimes on every test and compare directly. The TS pi-mono runtime IS the oracle.

RELATED EXISTING BEADS: bd-6vcm (Feature: Extension Conformance Testing), bd-2jlj (Epic: Full Pi Extension Conformance), bd-c6xq (Reference capture harness), bd-2bis (Fixture-based conformance tests), bd-382l (Phase 1: Research & Source Acquisition), bd-2vrw (Phase 2: Test Infrastructure). These should be considered superseded by this epic's phases.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
CORPUS INVENTORY: As of 2026-02-05, we have 1,167 TypeScript files across 5 tiers in tests/ext_conformance/artifacts/:
- 60 official pi-mono example extensions (gold standard): hello, pirate, ssh, tools, plan-mode, doom-overlay, etc.
- 58 community extensions: mitsuhiko(10), hjanuschka(14), tmustier(12), nicobailon(6), qualisero(7), prateekmedia(6), others(3)
- 63 npm registry extensions: aliou-pi-*, pi-annotate, pi-brave-search, pi-mermaid, vaayne-*, walterra-*, etc.
- 23 third-party GitHub repos: aliou-pi-extensions(59 sub-exts), w-winter-dot314(40 sub-exts), etc.
- 7 agent collection directories

Multi-extension collections (aliou=59, w-winter=40) inflate individual entry count to 280+ extensions. After validation, expect 200-300 genuine loadable extensions.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
TECHNICAL ARCHITECTURE NOTES:

TS RUNTIME (pi-mono):
- loader.ts uses jiti (JIT TS loader by unjs)
- Extension factory: export default function(pi: ExtensionAPI) { ... }
- Registration methods write to Extension object: handlers, tools, commands, flags, shortcuts, messageRenderers
- Action methods delegate to shared ExtensionRuntime: sendMessage, exec, setModel, etc.
- Action methods throw during load (by design -- only registration happens at load time)
- Bun 1.3.8 available at /home/ubuntu/.bun/bin/bun
- pi-mono source at legacy_pi_mono_code/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/

RUST RUNTIME:
- extensions_js.rs: JsExtensionLoadSpec, swc TS compilation, QuickJS execution
- extensions.rs: CompatibilityScanner (line 127-414), ExtensionManager, dispatch
- JsExtensionSnapshot captures: tools, slash_commands, shortcuts, flags, event_hooks, providers
- Hostcall bridge: JS pi.events(op,payload) -> Rust dispatch_hostcall_events()
- Session bridge: JS pi.session(op,payload) -> Rust dispatch_hostcall_session()
- ExtensionSession trait: get_state, get_messages, set_name, set_model, set_label

SHARED CONCERNS:
- Both runtimes must use identical mock specs for deterministic comparison
- Timestamps, random values, file paths must all be deterministic
- Event payloads must be identical in shape and content

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone

title: Gap: QuickJS resolver lacks native npm module support (node-pty, chokidar, jsdom, etc.)
description:
# Problem
8 extensions from seed-42 random trials fail because they import npm packages that require native Node.js bindings or complex dependency trees not available in the QuickJS sandbox.

# Failing Extensions
| Extension | Missing Module |
|---|---|
| npm/pi-mermaid | beautiful-mermaid |
| npm/pi-interactive-shell | node-pty |
| npm/aliou-pi-guardrails | @aliou/pi-utils-settings |
| npm/pi-brave-search | @mozilla/readability |
| community/nicobailon-interactive-shell | node-pty |
| third-party/marckrenn-pi-sub | @marckrenn/pi-sub-shared |
| npm/pi-watch | chokidar |
| npm/vaayne-pi-web-tools | jsdom |

# Analysis
These fall into two sub-categories:
1. **Native bindings** (node-pty): Cannot run in QuickJS at all — need a stub or "not supported" error
2. **Complex JS deps** (chokidar, jsdom, @mozilla/readability, beautiful-mermaid): Pure JS but huge dependency trees

# Possible approaches
- Virtual module stubs that throw helpful "not available in sandbox" errors
- For pure-JS deps: bundle with esbuild into the extension at install time
- Accept these as permanent N/A (native binding requirement)

# Evidence
- `tests/ext_conformance/reports/random_trials/RANDOM_TRIALS_REPORT.md`
- `target/ext_conformance/logs/random_trials/trial_seed_42.jsonl`

title: [PROVIDER-OPENROUTER-DYNAMIC-MODELS] Handle OpenRouter dynamic model registry
description:
## Problem

OpenRouter is fundamentally different from the other 4 new providers (Groq, Cerebras, Kimi, Qwen). It is a **proxy/aggregator** that routes to upstream providers. Its model registry is:
- **Dynamic**: Models are added/removed as upstream providers change
- **Large**: Potentially thousands of models across all upstream providers
- **Heterogeneous**: Models have different capabilities, pricing, and context windows
- **Namespaced**: Model IDs use `provider/model-name` format (e.g., `anthropic/claude-3-opus`)

The current pi_agent architecture assumes a static model registry defined at build time in models.json. This does not work for OpenRouter.

## Design Decision Required

### Option A: Static Snapshot
- Hardcode the top N most popular OpenRouter models in models.json
- Periodically update the list (e.g., monthly)
- Simple but incomplete — users cannot access new models without a release

### Option B: API-Fetched Model List
- On first use (or periodic refresh), call `GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models`
- Cache the response locally (e.g., ~/.pi/cache/openrouter_models.json)
- Resolve models dynamically from cache
- More complex but complete — users always have access to current models

### Option C: Hybrid (Recommended)
- Ship a curated default list (top 20-30 models) in models.json
- Allow API fetch as an optional enhancement (behind --refresh-models flag)
- Any model ID matching the `provider/model-name` pattern auto-routes to OpenRouter
- Cache fetched list with 24h TTL

### OpenRouter-Specific Considerations
- **HTTP-Referer header**: Required by OpenRouter TOS for API calls
- **Pricing**: Different models have different per-token costs; should be visible in model selection
- **Fallback routing**: OpenRouter can auto-select a model if `openrouter/auto` is specified
- **Context window**: Varies dramatically by model (4K to 200K+)
- **Rate limits**: Per-model rate limits from upstream, plus OpenRouter-level limits

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Design decision documented (Option A/B/C)
- [ ] If Option B or C: API fetch + cache implementation specified
- [ ] Model resolver handles `provider/model-name` format
- [ ] HTTP-Referer header included in all OpenRouter requests
- [ ] Pricing metadata available in model selection (if fetched)
- [ ] Stale cache handling (TTL expiry, forced refresh)
- [ ] Unit tests for model name parsing and routing

## Dependencies
- Depends on PROVIDER-OPENROUTER-SPEC (bd-3uqg.11.7.1)
- Blocks PROVIDER-OPENROUTER-MODELS (bd-3uqg.11.7.4)
close_reason: Completed: Option-C dynamic model contract, provider/model resolver hardening, OpenRouter attribution header defaults, and targeted tests.

title: Dynamic validation: load each extension in pi-mono TS runtime
description:
# Dynamic validation: load each extension in pi-mono TS runtime

## Context
Static scanning finds candidate entry points. Dynamic validation PROVES they load. We use pi-mono loadExtensions() (from loader.ts) to actually try loading each extension. This is the GROUND TRUTH.

## Why Dynamic Validation
Some extensions may:
- Have correct patterns but fail at runtime (missing imports, type errors)
- Depend on external packages not available in our env
- Use Node.js APIs not available in Bun
- Have circular dependencies
- Require specific environment (Mac-only extensions like mac-system-theme.ts)

Dynamic validation tells us exactly which extensions work and which do not.

## What To Do
1. Build a Bun script that imports loadExtensions from pi-mono
2. For each candidate entry point from static scan:
   a. Try loadExtensions([path], cwd)
   b. Record: success/failure, error message if any
   c. If success: capture Extension object (handlers, tools, commands, flags, shortcuts, messageRenderers)
   d. Record load time
3. Output: JSON file with results for every extension

## Dependencies
- Requires bd-31f6 (pi-mono TS runtime validated and buildable)

## Important Notes
- Some extensions require specific capabilities (exec, http, etc.)
- The loader creates stub functions for action methods (notInitialized)
- Registration methods (on, registerTool, registerCommand, etc.) work during load
- Action methods (sendMessage, setModel, etc.) throw during load -- this is EXPECTED

## Acceptance Criteria
- All 60 official pi-mono extensions attempted
- All community/npm/third-party extensions attempted
- Results JSON includes: extension_id, path, load_success, error, registrations, load_time_ms

title: Fix package manifest empty-string pi.* contract mismatch
description:
# Goal
Align package manifest parsing so empty-string `pi.extensions` / related `pi.*` entries do not silently mean different things in different loaders.

# Problem
`src/extensions.rs` currently treats `"pi": { "extensions": "" }` as an explicit empty list that disables heuristic bundle expansion, while `src/resources.rs` and `src/package_manager.rs` reject empty paths. That split-brain behavior means the same malformed manifest can be accepted in one path and rejected in another.

# Scope
- Decide and implement one fail-closed contract for empty-string package manifest entries.
- Keep the string-vs-array support added in package-manager aligned with the chosen contract.
- Add regression tests for parser behavior and live extension/resource resolution where applicable.

# Acceptance Criteria
- Empty-string `pi.extensions` no longer silently disables or diverges between loaders.
- Manifest readers agree on empty-entry validation semantics.
- Targeted regression tests cover the chosen behavior.
- fmt/check/clippy pass for the touched surface.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
SEC-3.4 complete. Implemented enforcement state machine with hysteresis:

1. **EnforcementState enum** (5 states): Allow < Harden < Prompt < Deny < Terminate with Ord derive for total ordering. Prompt is new (not in RuntimeRiskAction) — sits between Harden and Deny for user-approval workflows.

2. **EnforcementScoreBands** per policy profile:
   - Safe: aggressive (harden=0.30, prompt=0.50, deny=0.65, terminate=0.80)
   - Balanced: moderate (harden=0.40, prompt=0.60, deny=0.75, terminate=0.90)
   - Permissive: tolerant (harden=0.55, prompt=0.70, deny=0.85, terminate=0.95)

3. **Hysteresis anti-flapping**:
   - De-escalation margin: score must drop 0.10 below entry threshold
   - Cooldown: 3 consecutive evaluations in lower band before de-escalation
   - Escalation is always immediate; de-escalation is one level at a time
   - Terminate is terminal — no de-escalation ever

4. **Policy integration**: merge_with_policy() takes max(enforcement_state, policy_floor) — policy Deny overrides risk Allow, but enforcement Terminate overrides everything.

5. **Tests**: 34 new tests covering state ordering, score band classification, immediate escalation, hysteresis prevention, cooldown mechanics, terminal state, flapping prevention (10-evaluation jitter test), policy merge, serde roundtrips, determinism verification, and profile comparison.

title: FUZZ-P1.10: Session Index Metadata — Proptest session listing, metadata row parsing, SQL result handling
close_reason: Session-index proptest coverage complete (2x128-case properties); targeted check passed

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## FUZZ-P1.10: Session Index Metadata Proptest

### Background
src/session_index.rs (1388 lines) manages a metadata cache/index for session files. It stores session metadata (message count, last model, timestamps) in either a JSONL file or SQLite database for fast listing.

### Key Functions to Fuzz

1. **`list_sessions()`** (line ~115-146): Queries session metadata from index
   - SQL query result parsing via `row_to_meta(&row)?`
   - Ordering and filtering logic

2. **`update_index()`**: Writes/updates metadata entries
   - Handles concurrent updates (file locking or SQLite WAL)
   - Partial write recovery

3. **Session metadata struct**: Includes fields like:
   - `message_count`: usize — what if 0? What if u64::MAX?
   - `last_model`: String — empty? Very long? Non-UTF-8?
   - `last_updated`: timestamp — invalid ISO 8601? Future dates?
   - `session_name`: Option<String> — null vs empty vs absent?
   - `project_path`: PathBuf — traversal? Non-existent?

### Specific Risks
1. **Metadata constraint violations**: negative message counts, timestamps before epoch
2. **Index file corruption**: Partial writes during crash
3. **SQLite query injection**: If user input reaches queries (check if session names are parameterized)
4. **Unicode in session names**: Emoji, RTL text, null bytes, control chars
5. **Very long session lists**: 100K+ sessions in index — performance

### Implementation Approach
- `arbitrary_session_meta()`: Generates random SessionMeta structs
- `corrupted_index_file()`: Generates malformed index JSONL
- Round-trip test: write → read → compare

### Acceptance Criteria
- At least 2 proptest functions
- Minimum 128 cases per property
- Tests verify no panic on any metadata input
- Round-trip invariant holds for valid metadata

title: [PROVIDER-LONGTAIL-DEFER-FOLLOWUP] azure-cognitive-services alias-vs-native disposition
description: Finalize deferred azure-cognitive-services disposition. Determine if current alias-to-azure-openai behavior is sufficient or if distinct cognitive-services routing/auth semantics require a dedicated implementation. Document user impact, migration guidance, and required tests.
close_reason: Decision: KEEP AS ALIAS. azure-cognitive-services is correctly an alias of azure-openai. Both .openai.azure.com and .cognitiveservices.azure.com expose identical OpenAI Chat Completions API. The AzureOpenAIProvider already handles both host suffixes via parse_azure_resource_from_host(). Test coverage explicitly validates: routing (NativeAzure), host parsing, auth (AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY), and URL construction for both domains. No distinct auth, rate-limiting, or protocol differences exist. A dedicated adapter would be redundant. The alias provides backward compatibility for users configured with the Cognitive Services domain.

title: [PROVIDER-LONGTAIL-DEFER-FOLLOWUP] local and ollama native lifecycle adapters
description: Resolve deferred local and ollama provider onboarding by specifying and implementing process lifecycle contracts (startup/health-check/shutdown), capability boundaries, and deterministic integration tests. Distinguish local runtime requirements from cloud variants.
close_reason: Decision: NO ADAPTER NEEDED. Both ollama (local, localhost:11434) and ollama-cloud (remote, ollama.com) use OpenAICompatiblePreset routing through shared OpenAIProvider. No process lifecycle management code exists in the codebase for any provider — this is by design (client library, not orchestrator). ollama-cloud has full VCR coverage (7 fixtures). Local ollama has no VCR fixtures but this is acceptable since mocking localhost is unreliable. LMStudio follows the same pattern. Recommendation: keep current architecture, document that local ollama requires user to start server separately. No code changes needed.

title: [PROVIDER-LONGTAIL-DEFER-FOLLOWUP] v0 API endpoint watchlist and graduation trigger
description: Track v0 deferred status until Vercel publishes a stable API endpoint and auth contract suitable for deterministic provider routing. Capture periodic evidence checks and define explicit graduation criteria to move from deferred to implementation planning.
close_reason: Decision: MAINTAIN DEFERRED. v0 is registered as NativeAdapterRequired with no routing_defaults. The graduation condition (Vercel publishes stable REST API endpoint with documented auth flow) remains unmet. v0 is SDK-first (@ai-sdk/gateway) with no static base URL — incompatible with Pi's deterministic preset routing model. The vercel gateway preset (https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1) provides viable workaround. Low user impact. Revisit when Vercel publishes documented REST API with stable endpoint, auth contract, and rate limit documentation.

title: [PROVIDER-LONGTAIL-DEFER-FOLLOWUP] google-vertex-anthropic native route decision
description: Resolve deferred google-vertex-anthropic path: validate whether existing google-vertex adapter can safely support Anthropic publisher semantics or whether a dedicated native adapter is required. Produce decision record with test-plan impact and rollout criteria.
close_reason: Decision: DEFER. The google-vertex-anthropic alias exists in PROVIDER_METADATA as an alias of google-vertex, and the VertexProvider has publisher-aware URL routing (streamRawPredict for Anthropic vs streamGenerateContent for Google). However, the request body is ALWAYS built with build_gemini_request() (Gemini format), which is incompatible with the Anthropic streamRawPredict endpoint that expects Anthropic-format payloads. A dedicated request builder or conditional format transformation is required. Recommendation: keep the alias for forward compatibility, document as unsupported until dual-publisher adapter is implemented. Test coverage exists for URL routing and alias resolution, but NO request payload or response parsing tests exist for Anthropic publisher. Impact: low (no users depend on this path today). Rollout criteria for future work: conditional request builder, VCR fixtures for both publishers, e2e smoke test.

title: [PROVIDER-QWEN-SPEC] Capability/profile contract and endpoint mapping
description:
Capture Qwen capability profile: supported API surfaces, streaming/tool-call shape expectations, finish semantics, usage fields, and compatibility caveats.

## Provider-Specific Details

- Qwen is by Alibaba Cloud (DashScope platform)
- TWO API options:
  a. DashScope native: `https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/api/v1/services/aigc/text-generation/generation`
  b. OpenAI-compatible: `https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1/chat/completions`
- Auth: `DASHSCOPE_API_KEY` env var, Bearer token
- Models: qwen-turbo, qwen-plus, qwen-max, qwen-long, qwen-vl (vision)
- RECOMMENDATION: Use OpenAI-compatible endpoint for consistency with other providers
- Streaming: standard SSE on OpenAI-compatible endpoint
- Tool use: supported on qwen-plus and qwen-max
- Vision: supported on qwen-vl models (image input)
- Chinese market primary — international availability varies
design: Specification-first approach: capture explicit capability and payload contracts before implementation to avoid retrofitting behavior assumptions. Focus areas: DashScope reasoning flags and Qwen family defaults.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Capability profile artifact defines streaming behavior, tool-call support, finish reasons, usage fields, and unsupported/partial features. 2) Endpoint mapping includes concrete request/response exemplars for happy and failure paths. 3) Spec references upstream evidence and records all intentional divergences from baseline provider contracts.
close_reason: Created docs/provider-qwen-capability-profile.json — comprehensive Qwen/Alibaba/DashScope provider spec covering 3 regional endpoints, CRITICAL tool+streaming incompatibility (must force stream=false with tools), auth chain DASHSCOPE_API_KEY+QWEN_API_KEY, 20+ models across commercial/qwen3/vision/open-source, stream_options.include_usage requirement, 429 qps vs quota discrimination, and 6 implementation decisions. Validated JSON, cargo test and cargo check clean.

Deterministic audit protocol (v1):

A) Code-surface checks

B) Test/evidence checks

C) Documentation parity checks

- PASS: claim is backed by code + tests + docs/evidence anchors.
- PARTIAL: code exists but missing tests/docs evidence, or evidence stale.
- FAIL: claim absent/contradicted by code/tests/docs.

comments.text:
AUDIT COMPLETE — Provider UX Discoverability Report (CopperBrook)

## Executive Summary
Provider parity is 100% at the technical level (confirmed by TopazFalcon in bd-3uqg.14.3.1). However, significant UX discoverability gaps exist: only 10 of 88 providers have aliases, the model selector doesn't search aliases, and there's no --list-providers command.

## Gap 1: Missing Aliases (78 of 88 providers have NONE)
High-impact providers missing obvious aliases:
- `togetherai` — users try 'together', 'together-ai' → NOT FOUND
- `xai` — users try 'grok', 'x-ai' → NOT FOUND
- `huggingface` — users try 'hf', 'hugging-face' → NOT FOUND
- `nvidia` — users try 'nim', 'nvidia-nim' → NOT FOUND
- `lmstudio` — users try 'lm-studio' → NOT FOUND
- `deepseek` — users try 'deep-seek' → NOT FOUND
- `perplexity` — users try 'pplx' → NOT FOUND
- `zhipuai` — users try 'zhipu', 'glm' → NOT FOUND
- `siliconflow` — users try 'silicon-flow' → NOT FOUND
- `kimi-for-coding` — users try 'kimi' (resolves to moonshotai, not this) → CONFUSING

## Gap 2: No display_name on ProviderMetadata
ProviderMetadata only has canonical_id and aliases. No human-friendly display name. Users see cryptic IDs like '302ai', 'xai', 'moonshotai' in --list-models and model selector.

## Gap 3: No --list-providers Command
--list-models exists and works well. But there's no way to list all available PROVIDERS with their aliases and auth env keys. User must know the canonical ID in advance.

## Gap 4: Model Selector Doesn't Search Aliases
model_selector.rs:matches_query() does fuzzy_match on provider+id but uses ModelEntry.model.provider (always canonical). User typing 'grok' in selector won't find xai/grok-2. User typing 'together' won't find togetherai/*.

## Gap 5: Limited Onboarding Provider Recognition
provider_from_token() in main.rs only recognizes 3 providers (anthropic/claude, openai/gpt, google/gemini) during initial setup. Users of other providers get no guidance.

## Gap 6: Error Messages Lack Provider Suggestions
When provider not found, error is generic ('Provider not implemented'). No fuzzy suggestion like 'Did you mean togetherai?' or list of similar providers.

## Recommended Mitigations (6 tasks)

comments.text:
AUDIT COMPLETE — Provider UX Discoverability Report (TopazFalcon, Claude Opus 4.6)

## Summary
Reconciled technical provider parity (88 providers, 10 native implementations) against user-visible discoverability. Key finding: 84 of 88 providers are technically available but effectively invisible to users.

## Technical Parity Status
- 10 native provider implementations (anthropic, openai, openai_responses, gemini, cohere, azure, bedrock, vertex, copilot, gitlab)
- 78+ OAI-compatible providers via shared adapter
- 88 total entries in provider_metadata.rs with aliases, env vars, base URLs
- All compile and route correctly via `create_provider()` factory

## Discoverability Gaps

### 1. `--list-models` Only Shows Keyed Providers
- `registry.get_available()` filters by `api_key.is_some()` (main.rs:1492)
- Without env var set, providers are completely invisible
- No hint shown about which env vars would enable more providers

### 2. First-Time Setup Limited to 3 Providers
- `PROVIDER_CHOICES` hardcodes only anthropic/openai/google (main.rs:1526-1542)
- 85+ other providers unreachable through interactive setup
- No 'other' option or search capability

### 3. CLI Help Shows 3 Examples Only
- `--provider` help text: 'e.g., anthropic, openai, google' (cli.rs)
- No documentation of aliases (gemini → google, kimi → moonshotai, etc.)
- No reference to models.json configuration path

### 4. Error Messages Lack Guidance
- 'No models available' message (main.rs:1494) doesn't list available providers
- Provider not found errors don't suggest closest matches
- No env var hints for common providers

### 5. Alias Resolution Works but Is Undiscoverable
- `canonical_provider_id()` resolves aliases perfectly (provider_metadata.rs:1450)
- But users have no way to discover which aliases exist
- Example: 'qwen' and 'dashscope' both resolve to 'alibaba' — not documented

## Mitigation Recommendations

### P1 (High Impact, Low Effort)
1. **Enhance 'No models available' message** — List top 10 providers with env vars
2. **Add `--list-providers` flag** — Show all 88 providers with env key, aliases, base URL
3. **Expand PROVIDER_CHOICES** — Add at least groq, cohere, deepseek, mistral to setup wizard

### P2 (Medium Impact)
4. **Add alias display to `--list-models`** — Show 'google (also: gemini)' format
5. **Document models.json location in --help** — Reference ~/.pi/models.json
6. **Add fuzzy provider matching** — 'Did you mean X?' on provider not found

### P3 (Enhancement)
7. **Generate models.json template** — `pi config --generate-models-json`
8. **Provider discovery docs** — Comprehensive table in README or docs/providers.md
9. **Interactive provider search** — Searchable list in setup wizard

- src/cli.rs:159-163 (--list-models flag)
- src/main.rs:1491-1550 (list_models + setup wizard)

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
Implementation complete. Changes:

**src/auth.rs**:
- Extended AuthCredential enum with 3 new variants: AwsCredentials (access_key_id, secret_access_key, session_token, region), BearerToken (token), ServiceKey (client_id, client_secret, token_url, service_url)
- Updated api_key() to handle all new variants: BearerToken returns token, AwsCredentials returns access_key_id, ServiceKey returns None (requires token exchange)
- Added AwsResolvedCredentials enum (Sigv4 vs Bearer) and resolve_aws_credentials() with env-injectable variant
- AWS credential chain precedence: AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK → AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID+SECRET → stored AwsCredentials/BearerToken/ApiKey
- Region resolution: AWS_REGION → AWS_DEFAULT_REGION → us-east-1
- Added SapResolvedCredentials struct and resolve_sap_credentials() with env-injectable variant
- SAP credential chain: AICORE_SERVICE_KEY JSON → individual SAP_AI_CORE_* env vars → stored ServiceKey
- parse_sap_service_key_json() handles both SAP-native (clientid/clientsecret/url/serviceurls) and generic (client_id/client_secret/token_url/service_url) field names
- 29 new unit tests covering: serialization round-trips, api_key() with new variants, AWS credential chain (11 tests), SAP credential chain (9 tests), metadata resolution

**src/provider_metadata.rs**:
- Expanded amazon-bedrock auth_env_keys from [AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID] to [AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN, AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, AWS_PROFILE, AWS_REGION]
- Added sap-ai-core provider metadata entry (aliases: [sap], env keys: [AICORE_SERVICE_KEY, SAP_AI_CORE_CLIENT_ID, SAP_AI_CORE_CLIENT_SECRET, SAP_AI_CORE_TOKEN_URL, SAP_AI_CORE_SERVICE_URL])

Test results: 138 auth tests pass, 0 failures. Clippy clean (0 errors from our changes).

title: Message queue: core data model + delivery boundaries
description:
# Goal
Implement the internal **queue state machine** and define the delivery boundaries where queued messages become new agent inputs.

# Deliverables
- Data structures for queued messages:
  - kind: steering | follow_up
  - text
  - seq (monotonic) and/or timestamp
- Deterministic ordering (FIFO within each kind, global stable order).
- Identify delivery boundaries in the Rust agent/interactive integration:
  - after tool completion
  - after assistant completion
  - after abort

# Behavioral Spec (must match legacy)
- Steering: delivered after the current tool execution completes; cancels remaining tool iterations for that request.
- Follow-up: delivered only after the agent becomes fully idle.

# Implementation Notes
- Keep the queue logic isolated and testable (pure functions where possible).
- Define explicit “agent busy phases” so boundary detection is not heuristic.

# Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Queue semantics are implemented independent of UI.
- [ ] No deadlocks/races when messages are queued during streaming.

title: Epic: TUI Graduation — complete interactive mode features and remove WIP label
description:
# Goal
Complete the remaining interactive TUI features that are currently missing or incomplete, then remove the "WIP" designation from README.md and docs.

# Background
The interactive TUI (src/interactive.rs, 9,368 lines) is already substantially functional: full bubbletea-style architecture with viewport, text editor, autocomplete, spinner, model/thinking cycling, /slash commands, session management, keybinding customization, and theming. 90 tests pass for TUI state.

However, README.md still labels it "(WIP)" and several advanced features are missing:
1. Session branching has no visual UI — users cant see or navigate conversation branches
2. Edit tool results show raw text instead of colorized diffs
3. Images returned by read tool are not rendered in-terminal
4. Long-running tool executions have no progress indication beyond spinner
5. Tool output is not collapsible — long grep/find results push conversation off-screen

# Why This Matters
- "WIP" label on a core feature discourages adoption
- Session branching is a DOCUMENTED feature (README, Architecture) but invisible in the UI
- Inline diffs dramatically improve the "edit" tool UX — users can SEE what changed
- Image rendering in modern terminals (Kitty, iTerm2, WezTerm, Ghostty) is expected for 2026
- The comparison table in README shows "TUI rendering" as Pi advantage — it should be polished

# Architecture Notes
- Session branching UI: branch indicator in viewport header ("Branch 2/3"), Ctrl+B for branch picker (list model with tree visualization)
- Inline diff rendering: Use similar crate (already a dependency), render with lipgloss colors (green=add, red=remove, gray=context)
- Image rendering: Detect terminal capabilities via TERM/TERM_PROGRAM, Kitty graphics protocol (widest modern support), Sixel fallback, text placeholder for unsupported
- Progress indicators: For bash tool show elapsed time + output line count; for grep/find show file count scanned
- Tool output folding: collapse toggle per tool result block in viewport

# Children
1. Session branching UI (visual branch picker + navigator)
2. Inline diff rendering for edit tool results
3. Terminal image rendering (Kitty/Sixel protocol)
4. Tool execution progress indicators
5. Collapsible tool output blocks
6. Remove WIP labels from README/docs (after above items complete)

# Performance Constraints
- Image rendering must not block event loop — decode/encode in background task
- Diff rendering must handle files up to 10K lines without lag
- Branch picker must handle sessions with 50+ branches
- All new features must maintain 60fps rendering target
close_reason: done

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
ARCHITECTURAL CONTEXT: The interactive TUI (src/interactive.rs) is a 9,368-line bubbletea-style application. Its already the most complete component in the codebase. This epic adds the "last 10%" features that turn it from functional to polished.

WHY P2 NOT P1: The core agent functionality (streaming, tools, sessions) works fine in both interactive and print mode. These TUI enhancements improve the EXPERIENCE but don't block any critical capability. Extensions, shims, and streaming hostcalls are P1 because they gate conformance and extension ecosystem adoption.

SESSION BRANCHING — THE BIG WIN: This is the highest-impact feature in this epic. Pi's session format ALREADY supports branching (tree structure, parent pointers), but there's no way to USE it. Adding visual branching gives Pi a unique advantage over Claude Code and Aider (neither has conversation branching UI).

IMAGE RENDERING — MODERN TERMINALS ONLY: Kitty graphics protocol is the primary target because Kitty, WezTerm, Ghostty, and Konsole all support it — that covers the majority of developer terminal users. Sixel is a fallback for edge cases. We explicitly do NOT try to support ancient terminals (xterm without sixel, basic macOS Terminal) — they get the text placeholder.

COLLAPSIBLE BLOCKS — UX ESSENTIAL: Without collapsing, a single grep with 200 results makes the conversation unusable. This is a must-have for the interactive experience. Claude Code has this (tool outputs are collapsed by default).

ESTIMATED EFFORT: Branching UI (12-16h), diff rendering (6-8h), image rendering (10-14h), progress indicators (4-6h), collapsible blocks (8-10h), docs update (2-3h). Total: ~42-57 engineering hours.

title: Session branching UI — visual branch picker and navigator
description:
# Goal
Build the visual UI for session branching: a branch indicator in the conversation header, and a branch picker modal (Ctrl+B) that lets users see, navigate, and create conversation branches.

# Background
Sessions already support tree-structured branching (src/session.rs): each message has a parent field, enabling multiple children from any message (creating branches). The data model is complete. What is missing is any way for users to SEE branches exist or SWITCH between them in the interactive TUI.

Currently, the session just follows the "leaf" (most recent message on current path). If a user asks a question, gets an answer, then wants to try a different approach from the same question, they must start a new session entirely — even though the session format supports branching natively.

# Implementation Plan

1. Branch indicator (always visible):
   - In the viewport header bar, show: "Branch 1/3 at msg #15"
   - Calculate branch count by counting children of each fork point
   - Update indicator when user navigates branches

2. Branch picker modal (Ctrl+B):
   - List model (charmed_rust bubbletea) showing all branches
   - Each branch: preview of first message on branch, message count, timestamp
   - Tree visualization using box-drawing characters:
     msg #1: "Help me refactor..."
       ├── Branch 1 (current): "Sure, lets use..."  (12 msgs)
       ├── Branch 2: "An alternative approach..." (8 msgs)
       └── Branch 3: "What if we try..." (3 msgs)
   - Arrow keys to select, Enter to switch, Escape to cancel

3. Branch creation:
   - When user sends a message that creates a new branch (message from mid-conversation), show brief notification: "Branch 2 created"
   - Add /branch command to explicitly create a named branch

4. Navigation:
   - Ctrl+Left / Ctrl+Right: cycle between branches at current fork point
   - Conversation viewport reloads with selected branchs messages

# Files to Modify
- src/interactive.rs: Add BranchPickerModel, branch indicator, Ctrl+B handler
- src/session.rs: Add branch enumeration/navigation helpers (may already exist)

# Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Branch indicator visible in header when session has branches
- [ ] Ctrl+B opens branch picker modal
- [ ] Branch picker shows tree structure with previews
- [ ] Enter switches to selected branch (conversation reloads)
- [ ] Ctrl+Left/Right cycles between branches
- [ ] Creating a branch shows notification
- [ ] Works correctly with sessions having 50+ branches

title: Inline diff rendering for edit tool results
description:
# Goal
When the edit tool returns results, render a colorized inline diff showing exactly what changed, instead of the current raw text "Successfully replaced X with Y".

# Background
The edit tool (src/tools.rs) returns a ToolOutput with a text description of the replacement. The similar crate (already a dependency) can compute line-level and word-level diffs. This task uses similar to generate diffs and lipgloss to render them with colors in the conversation viewport.

# Implementation Plan

1. Diff computation:
   - The edit tool already has the old text and new text
   - Use similar::TextDiff::from_lines() for line-level diff
   - For small changes (single line), use similar::TextDiff::from_words() for word-level highlighting

2. Diff rendering format:
   @@ src/main.rs (lines 42-45) @@
   -    let result = process(input);
   +    let result = process(input).await?;
        println!("{}", result);
   -    return result;
   +    result

3. Color scheme (lipgloss styles):
   - Red background: removed lines (-)
   - Green background: added lines (+)
   - Gray: context lines (unchanged)
   - Bold: changed words within a line (word-level highlighting)
   - File path + line range in header

4. Integration:
   - In the conversation viewport renderer, detect edit tool results
   - Replace raw text output with rendered diff
   - Keep raw text available via "show raw" toggle (for accessibility)

5. Truncation:
   - For large diffs (>50 lines changed), show first 20 + last 10 with "[...N lines...]" in between
   - Full diff available on expand

# Files to Modify
- src/tui.rs or src/interactive.rs: Diff rendering in conversation viewport
- src/tools.rs: Ensure edit tool output includes old_text and new_text for diff computation

# Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Edit tool results show colorized diff
- [ ] Added lines green, removed lines red, context lines gray
- [ ] Word-level highlighting for single-line changes
- [ ] File path and line range in diff header
- [ ] Large diffs truncated with expand option
- [ ] Raw text still accessible
- [ ] Diff rendering handles edge cases (empty old, empty new, whitespace-only changes)

title: Terminal image rendering via Kitty graphics protocol and Sixel fallback
description:
# Goal
Render images directly in the terminal when the read tool returns image data, using Kitty graphics protocol (primary) with Sixel fallback, instead of showing "[image: 800x600, 45KB]" placeholder text.

# Background
The read tool (src/tools.rs) already supports reading images: it base64-encodes them and returns ImageContent blocks. The LLM can see these images. But the USER cannot — the TUI just shows a placeholder. Modern terminals (Kitty, iTerm2, WezTerm, Ghostty, foot) support inline image rendering.

# Terminal Protocol Support
1. Kitty Graphics Protocol (most capable):
   - Supported by: Kitty, WezTerm, Ghostty, Konsole 22+
   - Transmission: base64 chunks via escape sequences
   - Features: placement, scaling, animation
   - Detection: query escape sequence response

2. Sixel (widest legacy support):
   - Supported by: xterm (with flag), mlterm, foot, contour
   - Transmission: sixel-encoded pixel data
   - Lower quality than Kitty but more broadly supported

3. iTerm2 Inline Images:
   - Supported by: iTerm2 only
   - Transmission: base64 in OSC escape sequence
   - Detection: TERM_PROGRAM=iTerm.app

4. Fallback (unsupported terminals):
   - Show ASCII art approximation using Unicode block characters
   - Or just show the existing placeholder with dimensions

# Implementation Plan

1. Terminal capability detection:
   - Check TERM_PROGRAM, TERM, and query responses
   - Determine best protocol: Kitty > iTerm2 > Sixel > Fallback
   - Cache detection result for session lifetime

2. Image preparation:
   - Decode base64 image data
   - Resize to fit terminal width (maintain aspect ratio)
   - Use image crate (behind image-resize feature flag, already exists) for resize

3. Kitty protocol implementation:
   - Chunk base64 data into 4096-byte frames
   - Write APC escape sequences with transmission parameters
   - Set placement ID for cleanup on scroll

4. Sixel fallback:
   - Convert image to 256-color palette
   - Encode as Sixel escape sequence
   - Libraries: consider image-to-sixel pure Rust conversion

5. Integration with TUI:
   - In conversation viewport, detect ImageContent blocks
   - Render image inline at that position
   - Handle scroll: images re-render when scrolled into view
   - Handle resize: images re-render on terminal resize

# Performance
- Image decode/resize in background task (dont block event loop)
- Cache rendered escape sequences (dont re-encode on every frame)
- Lazy rendering: only render images visible in viewport

# Files to Modify
- New: src/terminal_images.rs (protocol detection, encoding, rendering)
- src/interactive.rs: Wire image rendering into viewport
- src/tui.rs: Image rendering for non-interactive mode

# Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Images render inline in Kitty terminal
- [ ] Sixel fallback works in supported terminals
- [ ] Placeholder text in unsupported terminals
- [ ] Images scale to terminal width
- [ ] Scroll works correctly with inline images
- [ ] No event loop blocking during image rendering
- [ ] Terminal capability detection cached

title: Tool execution progress indicators (elapsed time, output count, file count)
description:
# Goal
Show meaningful progress indicators during long-running tool executions instead of just a generic spinner, giving users visibility into what is happening and how long it is taking.

# Background
Currently, when a tool executes (bash, grep, find), the TUI shows a spinner with text like "Running bash..." This gives no indication of progress, output volume, or whether the command is stuck. For commands that take 30-120 seconds, this is a poor user experience.

# Implementation Plan

1. Bash tool progress:
   - Show: "Running bash... 12s • 847 lines output"
   - Update elapsed time every second
   - Count output lines as they arrive (requires streaming tool output)
   - On timeout warning: "Running bash... 95s/120s • 2,341 lines ⚠️ timeout in 25s"

2. Grep tool progress:
   - Show: "Searching... 234 files scanned • 12 matches"
   - Parse ripgrep output for file count and match count
   - Update as results stream in

3. Find tool progress:
   - Show: "Finding files... 1,234 files found"
   - Count results as fd outputs them

4. Read tool progress:
   - Show: "Reading src/main.rs... 1,133 lines"
   - For large files: show size progress

5. Edit tool progress:
   - Show: "Editing src/main.rs... computing diff"
   - Brief, since edits are fast

# Architecture
- Modify the tool execution callback (on_update) to emit structured progress events
- The TUI spinner model receives progress events and updates display text
- Progress format: SpinnerText::Progress { tool, elapsed_secs, metrics: HashMap }
- Each tool type has its own metric formatting function

# Files to Modify
- src/tools.rs: Emit structured progress events from each tool
- src/interactive.rs: SpinnerModel parses progress events into display text
- src/tui.rs: Same for non-interactive print mode (optional)

# Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Bash tool shows elapsed time + output line count
- [ ] Grep tool shows files scanned + match count
- [ ] Find tool shows file count
- [ ] Updates at least once per second for long operations
- [ ] Timeout warning displayed when approaching limit
- [ ] No performance impact (progress events are lightweight)
- [ ] Spinner still works for tools with no streaming progress

title: Collapsible tool output blocks in conversation viewport
description:
# Goal
Add collapse/expand toggles to tool output blocks in the conversation viewport, so long tool results (grep with 200 matches, find with 1000 files) dont push important conversation content off-screen.

# Background
When a tool returns a large result (e.g., grep with 200 matches), the entire output is rendered inline in the conversation viewport. This pushes the AIs analysis and the users next input far off-screen, requiring extensive scrolling. In Claude Code and similar tools, tool outputs are collapsible — showing a summary line with an expand toggle.

# Implementation Plan

1. Tool output block structure:
   ▼ bash: cargo test (exit 0, 847 lines, 12.3s)    [collapse]
     running 90 tests
     test sse::tests::parse_basic ... ok
     test sse::tests::parse_multi ... ok
     ... (847 lines total)

   Collapsed:
   ▶ bash: cargo test (exit 0, 847 lines, 12.3s)    [expand]

2. Auto-collapse rules:
   - Tool output > 20 lines: auto-collapsed, show first 5 lines as preview
   - Tool output <= 20 lines: expanded by default
   - Configurable threshold in settings.json
   - User can always toggle manually

3. Interaction:
   - Click (or Enter when block focused) toggles collapse/expand
   - Keybinding: Tab cycles through collapsible blocks
   - Visual indicator: ▶ (collapsed) / ▼ (expanded) prefix
   - Summary line always visible: tool name, exit code, line count, duration

4. Implementation in viewport:
   - ViewportContent entries get a CollapsibleBlock variant
   - CollapsibleBlock { summary: String, content: String, is_collapsed: bool }
   - Viewport height calculation accounts for collapsed blocks (1 line vs full height)
   - Toggle updates viewport scroll position to keep context stable

5. Persistence:
   - Collapse state is session-transient (reset on session reload)
   - Not persisted to JSONL

# Files to Modify
- src/interactive.rs: CollapsibleBlock in viewport, toggle logic, keybinding
- May need viewport content model changes

# Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Large tool outputs auto-collapsed with preview
- [ ] Small tool outputs expanded by default
- [ ] Toggle works via keyboard
- [ ] Summary line shows tool name, exit code, duration, line count
- [ ] Viewport scroll position stable on toggle
- [ ] Configurable auto-collapse threshold
- [ ] Works with all 7 tool types

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
DESIGN REFINEMENT (from review):

Collapsible blocks should apply to ALL large output blocks, not just tool outputs:
1. Tool outputs (bash, grep, find, read) — primary use case
2. Thinking blocks — extended thinking can be 500+ lines, equally disruptive
3. Code blocks in assistant responses — long code listings push context off-screen

The auto-collapse threshold should be per-block-type:
- Tool output: 20 lines (per settings, configurable)
- Thinking blocks: 10 lines (thinking is usually auxiliary)
- Code blocks: 30 lines (code needs more context to be useful)

Summary line format per type:
- Tool: "▶ bash: cargo test (exit 0, 847 lines, 12.3s)"
- Thinking: "▶ Thinking (245 lines, 3.2s)"
- Code: "▶ Code: rust (89 lines)"

title: [AUTH-3] Token refresh E2E tests with VCR cassettes
description:
## Problem

Token refresh works in unit tests but no E2E test verifies: token near expiry -> refresh triggered -> agent continues seamlessly. This is tracked as bd-3pn.

## Solution

### VCR-Backed E2E Tests

1. **test_anthropic_refresh_during_agent_run**
   - Setup: auth.json with Anthropic OAuth credential, expires_at = now + 5 minutes
   - VCR cassette: refresh token request -> new access token
   - Run agent with prompt -> verify refresh happens -> verify agent completes
   - Assert: auth.json updated with new token

2. **test_openai_refresh_during_agent_run** (conditional on AUTH-SPIKE outcome)
   - If AUTH-SPIKE determines OpenAI supports OAuth: same pattern as Anthropic
   - If AUTH-SPIKE determines OpenAI uses API keys only: SKIP this test (API keys do not expire/refresh)
   - The test should be gated with `#[cfg_attr(not(feature = "openai_oauth"), ignore)]` or similar

3. **test_refresh_failure_shows_recovery_message**
   - VCR cassette: refresh returns 401 (invalid_grant)
   - Verify: error logged, user sees "/login anthropic" suggestion
   - **DEPENDS ON AUTH-4**: The recovery UX (RefreshFailure struct, system message, /login suggestion) must be implemented first

4. **test_refresh_race_condition**
   - Two concurrent refreshes (e.g., RPC + interactive modes)
   - Verify: file locking prevents corruption
   - Assert: only one refresh succeeds, other uses refreshed token

### Cassette Recording
- Record real refresh flows once (with test credentials)
- Store in tests/fixtures/vcr/oauth_refresh_*.json
- Playback is deterministic and fast

### JSONL Logging

title: FUZZ-P1: Expand Proptest Coverage (Low Effort, High Value)

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## FUZZ-P1: Phase 1 — Expand Proptest Coverage

### Strategy
Proptest (property-based testing) is the fastest path to fuzzing value. It's already a dev-dependency (proptest 1.6) and already used in 3 files. Expanding coverage requires NO new infrastructure — just writing more test functions in existing test modules.

### Why Proptest First?
1. Zero setup cost — already in Cargo.toml and proven working
2. Tests run with cargo test — no separate fuzzing command
3. Shrinking: proptest automatically minimizes failing inputs for debugging
4. Deterministic replay: seeds are recorded for reproduction
5. Quick feedback: 128-512 cases per property runs in seconds

### Current Coverage (3 targets, ~640 cases total)
- src/sse.rs: sse_chunking_invariant (64 cases)
- src/tools.rs: truncate_head/tail invariants (128 cases)
- src/extensions.rs: hostcall dispatch never panics (512 cases)

### Target Coverage (8 targets, ~2000+ cases total)
- P1.1: SSE parser expanded (5+ new properties, 1280+ cases)
- P1.2: Tool functions (4+ new properties, 512+ cases)
- P1.3: Provider stream parsers (3+ providers × 256 cases = 768+ cases)
- P1.4: Session JSONL (4+ properties, 512+ cases)
- P1.5: Config parser (3+ properties, 384+ cases)
- P1.6: Message types (4+ properties, 1024+ cases)
- P1.7: VCR cassette (3+ properties, 384+ cases)
- P1.8: Conformance comparator (3+ properties, 384+ cases)

### Key Pattern: asupersync Compatibility
For async functions, use run_test:
```rust
proptest\! {
    #[test]
    fn prop_foo(input in strategy()) {
        asupersync::test_utils::run_test(|| async move {
            // use assert\!() not prop_assert\!() — run_test requires () return
            let result = some_async_fn(input).await;
            assert\!(\!result.is_err());
        });
    }
}
```

For sync functions (most parsers), use prop_assert\!() directly.

### Task Independence
P1 tasks are mostly independent — agents CAN work on them in parallel. The only soft dependency is that SSE (P1.1) and Providers (P1.3) share some strategy patterns (SSE event generation), so whoever does P1.3 should look at P1.1's strategies for reuse.

### Definition of Done
- All 8 P1 tasks have proptest coverage passing on nightly
- Total proptest case count ≥ 2000
- Any bugs found during proptest development are fixed inline
- cargo test passes with no failures

title: Twelfth-wave semantic validation routing and cache-aware swarm scheduler
description:
Background:
- The queue is empty except deferred roadmaps, while README/AGENTS emphasize RCH-only heavy validation, massive-agent responsiveness, proof-memory reuse, validation scheduling, Agent Mail coordination, and explicit no-local-fallback behavior.
- Existing artifacts already include validation-scheduler plans, validation proof-memory, redundant-agent-work detection, operator work recommendations, RCH posture, and runpack handoff. The missing layer is a semantic route planner: given touched files/functions and current swarm state, it should explain exactly which proof obligations are required, which existing proof-memory records are relevant or invalid, how to order commands to maximize RCH/cache reuse, and where coordination collisions make a task unsafe to claim.

Goal:
Create a self-contained implementation track for read-only semantic validation routing and cache-aware swarm scheduling. This should make future agents faster and safer on large 64+ CPU / 256GB+ hosts by reducing duplicate validation, compile-cache churn, and coordination collisions while preserving source-system authority boundaries.

Scope:
- Define source-to-proof routing inventory and contract.
- Build a read-only planner that maps changed paths/categories to required validation groups and exact RCH command shapes.
- Add cache-heat/coalescing advice for RCH-heavy validation groups without executing commands.
- Join Agent Mail, Beads, git, validation proof-memory, and scheduler signals into deterministic advisory output.
- Add no-mock/golden evidence and runpack/docs projection.

Non-goals / boundaries:
- Must not execute cargo, launch RCH jobs, mutate Agent Mail, mutate Beads except through explicit br workflow, mutate git beyond normal committed source changes, delete files, or authorize release/drop-in/performance claims.
- Heavy validation remains explicit and RCH-only.

Acceptance:
- Child beads cover design, implementation, cache/admission heuristics, integration, tests, docs, and closeout evidence.
- The graph has no dependency cycles and leaves at least one small ready bead for immediate work.
- Every child bead includes concrete tests or evidence expectations and explicit read-only/advisory boundaries.
close_reason: Completed twelfth-wave semantic validation routing track. Child beads bd-4w2mw.1 through bd-4w2mw.7 are closed with concrete inventory, planner, cache/coalescing, coordination admission, runpack projection, golden/no-mock evidence, and closeout gate artifacts. Final closeout artifact commit 994574c13 was pushed to main and master before parent closeout.

title: SVR-1: Inventory source-to-proof routing gaps and contract shape
description:
Background:
The repo already has validation-scheduler plans, proof-memory records, redundant-agent-work projections, and operator work recommendations. Future semantic routing must not duplicate those surfaces; it must define the missing source-to-proof layer that turns touched paths into proof obligations and explains why existing proof evidence is or is not enough.

Scope:
1. Inventory current inputs that can feed a route planner: git changed paths, AGENTS/README validation rules, docs/contracts/validation-scheduler-plan-contract.json, docs/contracts/validation-proof-memory-index-contract.json, docs/contracts/operator-work-recommendation-contract.json, existing runpack outputs, Beads state, and Agent Mail health/reservations.
2. Define the proposed schema keys for pi.validation.semantic_route_plan.v1, including changed-path classifiers, required proof groups, exact RCH command templates, proof-memory invalidation reasons, cache/coalescing hints, coordination collision warnings, and claim boundaries.
3. Identify negative controls: missing source files, stale proof-memory, local cargo fallback, dirty worktree mismatch, unreserved overlapping edit surface, and advisory output being treated as authority.
4. Produce a compact inventory artifact or design note that downstream implementation beads can follow without rereading this planning conversation.

Acceptance:
- Output is read-only design/inventory; no cargo or RCH execution is required.
- The inventory explicitly distinguishes new semantic-route responsibilities from existing validation scheduler/proof-memory/redundant-work responsibilities.
- Follow-on beads remain valid and self-contained after this inventory.
- If code/docs files are changed, run formatting or JSON validation appropriate to the touched files plus br sync before commit.
close_reason: Completed semantic validation route inventory artifact at docs/evidence/semantic-validation-route-inventory.json; defines source inventory, proposed route plan contract, negative controls, follow-on bead graph, and advisory claim boundaries. Validated with python3 -m json.tool, git diff --check, and ./scripts/reconcile_beads_ledger.sh.

title: SVR-2: Implement read-only semantic validation route planner
description:
Background:
After SVR-1 defines the contract, implement a deterministic read-only planner that turns current changed paths and optional source artifacts into a semantic validation route plan. This should complement, not replace, validation-scheduler and proof-memory artifacts.

Scope:
- Add a script or existing runpack helper that emits pi.validation.semantic_route_plan.v1 JSON.
- Inputs should include changed paths (from git or fixture JSON), proof-memory index, validation-scheduler plan, Beads ready/in-progress state, and optional Agent Mail health/reservation summaries when available.
- Classify paths into provider/tool/session/extension/TUI/RPC/docs/scripts/evidence buckets and map each bucket to exact proof groups and RCH command templates.
- For every heavy cargo command, preserve explicit rch exec -- command text, CARGO_TARGET_DIR/TMPDIR requirements, and local-fallback rejection rationale.
- Emit fail-closed statuses for missing/malformed source artifacts, stale or mismatched proof-memory, dirty worktree mismatch, and unknown path classes.

Acceptance:
- Planner is read-only and deterministic over fixture inputs.
- Unit/self-test coverage exercises at least rust-only, docs-only, mixed Rust/Python, unknown-path, stale-proof, and RCH-unavailable scenarios.
- The planner never executes cargo/RCH and never mutates Beads, Agent Mail, git, temp files, or evidence sources.
- Output includes enough exact commands and rationale for a future agent to execute the next validation step manually through RCH.
close_reason: Implemented scripts/plan_semantic_validation_route.py as a read-only semantic route planner. It classifies changed paths, imports validation scheduler/proof-memory inputs, emits proof obligations with RCH-only command templates, assesses proof-memory reuse/degradation, adds cache/coalescing and coordination admission sections, and includes built-in self-tests for docs-only, provider Rust, mixed Rust/Python, unknown path, stale proof, and RCH-unavailable cases. Validated with python3 -m py_compile and python3 scripts/plan_semantic_validation_route.py --self-test plus focused live route probes.

title: SVR-3: Add RCH cache-heat and validation coalescing advice
description:
Background:
Large swarms waste CPU and wall time when agents independently trigger validation groups that rebuild the same Rust targets or evict each other's CARGO_TARGET_DIR caches. Existing validation-scheduler output ranks command groups, but it does not model route-level cache heat or coalescing opportunities from the changed-path/proof obligation graph.

Scope:
- Extend the semantic route plan with cache_heat and coalescing_advice sections.
- Estimate which command groups likely share build artifacts, target dirs, features, and test binaries.
- Recommend orderings such as fast scripts before Rust build groups, grouped provider/session tests before all-targets checks, and clippy/check sequencing when RCH posture allows.
- Surface when a proof-memory record is not enough but can still inform cache-warm command ordering.
- Preserve exact RCH-only command text and no-local-fallback language.

Acceptance:
- Fixture coverage proves deterministic cache/coalescing ranking for docs-only, scripts-only, rust-only, and mixed Rust/Python changes.
- Output distinguishes cache advice from proof reuse authority.
- The planner remains advisory and read-only; it never creates target dirs, executes commands, or mutates RCH state.
close_reason: Added deterministic cache_heat and coalescing_advice sections to the semantic route planner, including route heat levels, shared RCH target cache keys, proof-memory authority boundaries, advisory ordering, and self-test coverage for docs-only, scripts-only, rust-only, mixed Rust/Python, stale-proof, unknown-path, and RCH-unavailable cases. Validated with py_compile, planner self-test, and focused live route probes.

title: SVR-4: Join coordination collision risk into route admission
description:
Background:
Existing redundant-agent-work detection identifies overlap at a claim-readiness level. Semantic validation routing should consume those signals and explain route-specific admission risk: which touched surfaces are likely to collide, whether Agent Mail reservations are healthy, whether Beads ownership is the fallback lock, and which alternate validation or docs-only slice is safer.

Scope:
- Add coordination_risk/admission sections to the semantic route output.
- Inputs may include Agent Mail health/reservation summaries, br ready/in_progress state, git status, and redundant-agent-work report output.
- Emit deterministic statuses for safe_to_claim, claim_with_beads_soft_lock, defer_due_to_collision, and stop_surface_blocker.
- Include exact file/path patterns that future agents should reserve before editing and exact Beads thread IDs to use for coordination.
- Fail closed when coordination sources are missing, contradictory, or stale.

Acceptance:
- Fixtures cover healthy Agent Mail, degraded/read-only Agent Mail, empty ready queue, active overlap, stale in-progress issue, and dirty worktree admission denial.
- Output never claims, reserves, sends mail, updates Beads, or edits files by itself.
- The route planner clearly separates advisory admission from source-of-truth Beads and Agent Mail operations.
close_reason: Added coordination_risk plus enhanced coordination_admission output to the semantic route planner. The planner now detects Agent Mail recovery/read-only degradation, active overlap reservations, empty ready/open queues, stale in-progress issue markers, dirty worktree path mismatches, and unknown path blockers while preserving advisory-only source authority boundaries and exact thread/reservation hints. Self-test coverage now includes healthy Agent Mail, degraded/read-only Mail, empty ready queue, active overlap, stale in-progress issue, dirty worktree admission denial, plus prior route/proof/RCH cases.

title: SVR-5: Project semantic route plans into swarm runpacks and docs
description:
Background:
The planner only becomes useful for large swarms if it is visible in the operator handoff path. scripts/build_swarm_operator_runpack.py already projects validation scheduler, proof-memory, predictive telemetry, and operator recommendations; semantic route output should appear there as advisory context without changing source-system authority.

Scope:
- Add optional input/output wiring so runpacks can embed semantic_route_plan summaries.
