## Origin

oh-my-pi (omp, https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi) is a batteries-included fork of the same pi-mono upstream that pi_agent_rust ports. It has evolved a much richer harness surface than either pi-mono or current pi_agent_rust: 31 built-in tools + xd:// device namespace, 14 LSP ops, 28 DAP ops, eval kernels with tool re-entry, 23-provider web_search, 10 model roles with fallback chains, advisor model, TTSR stream rules, full MCP client, foreign-rules import, internal URL schemes, typed subagent yields with worktree isolation, agent hub, memory/learning tools, and ~80k LoC of Rust natives (pi-shell/pi-builtins/pi-ast/pi-walker/pi-iso/pi-natives).

We studied a fresh clone (2026-08-14) end-to-end. Reference evidence paths below are upstream repo paths; re-clone to inspect. The omp docs/ tree (~80 files: docs/tools/*.md per tool, settings.md, providers.md, compaction.md, ttsr-injection-lifecycle.md, lsp-config.md, magic-keywords.md) doubles as port specs.

## Current pi_agent_rust baseline (verified by source recon 2026-08-14)

- 9 built-in tools: read/bash/edit/write/grep/find/ls/hashline_edit + opt-in subagent (src/tools.rs, src/subagents.rs). hashline_edit already matches omp's headline edit format.
- 4 modes: interactive TUI, print, JSON, RPC, ACP (src/acp.rs exists — ACP is NOT a gap).
- 11 native providers + OpenAI-compatible presets + models.json; 7 OAuth flows; NO cross-model failover, NO model roles.
- Sessions: JSONL v3 tree + SQLite index + V2 sidecar; compaction; steering/follow-up queues; 28 extension lifecycle events.
- Extensions: QuickJS runtime with deep capability sandbox (10 caps, trust lifecycle, exec mediation) — already ahead of omp here; NOT a port target.
- ast-grep + tree-sitter crates ALREADY in the dependency tree (used for heredoc AST in exec mediation) — ast tools are cheap to expose.
- NO: MCP client config files (documented gap, /mcp only lists extension-registered servers; pi_agent_rust#112), web tools, todo tool, background jobs, plan mode, advisor, TTSR, LSP, DAP, eval, memory, internal URL router, in-process grep/glob (requires external fd/rg), BPE token counting (uses chars/4 heuristic).

## Scope decision record (deferred/rejected with rationale)

- Collab relay (/collab sealed-frame sharing): requires a hosted relay service + browser guest client; revisit only with explicit product demand. Not planned.
- Voice (STT/TTS realtime, pi-voice WebRTC, /say): out of scope for a coding CLI.
- robomp remote-worker fleet, metaharness benchmark farm: separate products, not harness features.
- auth-broker/auth-gateway (credentials for containerized runs): niche; our auth.json + env model covers the common cases.
- Legacy pi-mono extension shims: our QuickJS runtime already executes TS extensions natively with a stricter sandbox; different and deliberate architecture.
- omptype JIT schema validator: we use serde/schemars; no gap.
- Node SDK: we ship a Rust SDK (docs/sdk.md); no Node embedding planned.
- Nix/Bazel packaging: distribution model divergence, not a feature gap.

## Global constraints for every child bead (inherit without restating)

1. AGENTS.md rules: `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`; no script-based code transforms; new files ONLY where genuinely new functionality owns the concern (say so in the bead); no backwards-compat shims; main branch only.
2. Every new agent-facing tool MUST ship with: tool-schema + behavior conformance fixtures (tests/conformance pattern), e2e coverage across interactive/print/RPC/ACP surfaces where observable, and registration behind --tools gating.
3. Heavy builds/tests: use ./scripts/cargo_headroom.sh and `rch exec --` offload; run `ubs --staged --only=rust .` (or scripts/check_ubs_staged_delta.py) before commit; ./scripts/reconcile_beads_ledger.sh must pass.
4. PERF-3X (bd-3ar8v) and FrankenNode (bd-3ar8v.7) beads are in flight on agent.rs/tools.rs/session hot paths. OMP-ADOPT work is mostly ADDITIVE (new modules/tools); coordinate overlapping files via MCP Agent Mail file_reservation_paths with reason=<bead id>; never revert other agents' changes.
5. Performance claims in docs/README require provenance-matched evidence artifacts per README Citation Convention; new features must not regress the 22 MiB release-size budget or <100ms startup target — measure, and keep heavyweight extras behind opt-in cargo features.
6. Model for evidence: omp paths cited as `omp:packages/coding-agent/src/...` refer to the upstream clone; treat omp docs as spec, not gospel — adapt to asupersync/our architecture rather than transliterating.

## Review pass 2026-08-14 — additions

**New global constraint #7 (test logging + e2e wiring, applies to every child):** All automated tests for every bead emit structured JSONL logs following the repo's test harness pattern (tests/common/logging.rs): per-case events with correlation ids, redacted inputs/outputs, artifact paths — no bare assert-only tests. e2e coverage ships as scripts under scripts/e2e/ registered in scripts/e2e/run_all.sh profiles (focused + ci) so the unified runner executes them; live-network lanes stay separately gated. A failure must be diagnosable from the logs alone (log tool inputs, key decisions, error taxonomy codes).

**New global constraint #8 (visual chrome vehicle):** All TUI/visual-chrome work in this program is implemented on the owner's FrankenTUI crate ecosystem (/dp/frankentui: ftui-core/ftui-runtime/ftui-render/ftui-extras + doctor_frankentui visual regression), per owner directive 2026-08-14. Visual acceptance for chrome beads requires doctor_frankentui snapshot/timeline evidence, not only unit tests.

**Beads added in review (were missed in first pass):** .1.6 tool load modes + xdev dispatcher; .7.8 per-model tool-call dialect converters (omp's benchmaxxing layer); .7.9 secrets obfuscation for model-bound context; .3.11 /review command; .3.12 multi-root workspaces; .3.13 file-mutation recording with /undo. Plus the new F9 visual-chrome feature group (see children of bd-cv653.9).

**Extended deferral record (considered, deliberately not beaded):** /vibe mode and goal/loop modes (thin mode-UI over the subagent+hub primitives we ARE porting; revisit after F5 lands), /queue (our steering/follow-up queues already provide the substance), prewalk fast-model sweep (overlaps advisor; revisit if advisor proves insufficient), session handoff generator (adjacent to context-preview/semantic bundles we already have; revisit after F4 memory), setup wizard (doctor + config cover the substance), autoresearch mode, cleanse transcript pipeline, metaharness/robomp (separate products), token/tiny-models/gc utility subcommands (marginal), desktop notifications (folded into F9 theme/chrome scope decision there).**

**Polish round 2 (2026-08-14) additions:** F10 web-remote access feature (bd-cv653.10): `pi web` WASM browser client via ftui-web (server-rendered frame diffs over WebSocket), QR + tailscale onboarding with one-time fragment-carried tokens and view/steer links, and a P1 security gate (threat model, redaction composition, local-only approval for remote-initiated mutations, zero browser persistence). This is omp /collab's UX bar re-imagined relay-free over the tailnet. Round-2 bead sharpenings: ask dialog made stack-agnostic for the F9 overlay host; background-jobs management surface consolidated into the unified `hub` tool per the .5.4 decision.

## Final feature index (post-polish structure)

F1 tools-core (.1 lsp, .2 debug, .3 ast_grep/ast_edit, .4 eval, .5 in-process search, .6 load modes/xdev) · F2 tools-web (.1 web_search, .2 URL-read, .3 github, .4 browser, .5 computer, .6 security_scan, .7 media) · F3 agent-intel (.1 roles+auto-titling, .2 failover, .3 advisor, .4 TTSR+grievances, .5 plan mode, .6 magic keywords, .7 checkpoint/rewind+/retry, .8 ask, .9 todo, .10 bg jobs, .11 /review, .12 multi-root, .13 file undo, .14 pi commit atomic splitting, .15 turn recovery, .16 /btw + /tan) · F4 memory (.1 bank, .2 learn/manage_skill) · F5 orchestration (.1 typed yields, .2 isolation, .3 agent hub, .4 process supervision) · F6 interop (.1 MCP client, .2 rules import, .3 URL schemes, .4 session import) · F7 runtime (.1 BPE+pi token, .2 completions, .3 provider catalog, .4 usage, .5 brush, .6 snapcompact, .7 stats, .8 dialects, .9 secrets, .10 self-update, .11 gc) · F8 QA (.1 conformance, .2 docs, .3 parity) · F9 chrome/FrankenTUI (.1 runtime, .2 transcript+cards, .3 editor, .4 statusline/HUDs, .5 themes, .7 mdviz, .8 overlays, .9 delight, .10 visual-e2e; .6 closed as duplicate) · F10 web access (.1 pi web WASM, .2 QR+tailscale onboarding, .3 security gate).

title: [OMP-ADOPT][Tools-Core] Code intelligence and execution tools (lsp, debug, ast, eval, in-process search)
description:
## Feature scope

Port omp's code-intelligence and execution tool families as first-class Rust tools:
- lsp (14 ops) — omp:packages/coding-agent/src/lsp/ (tool.ts, client.ts, mux/, writethrough.ts), docs/tools/lsp.md
- debug (28 DAP ops) — omp:packages/coding-agent/src/dap/ (session.ts, client.ts, config.ts), docs/tools/debug.md
- ast_grep + ast_edit — omp:packages/coding-agent/src/tools/ast-grep.ts, ast-edit.ts + crates/pi-ast; our tree already depends on ast-grep/tree-sitter (exec mediation heredoc inspection), so this is exposure work, not new deps
- eval (persistent Python/JS kernels with tool re-entry) — omp:packages/coding-agent/src/tools/eval.ts, eval/, kernel-session-registry.ts
- in-process grep/glob/find — omp:crates/pi-walker + pi-natives grep.rs/glob.rs; retires our external fd/rg runtime dependency (README 'Dependencies' section) and unblocks Windows

## Why

These five are omp's biggest day-to-day capability multipliers ('everything your IDE knows, the agent knows'; real debugger instead of print debugging; structural edits that can't corrupt; kernels that load data once and reuse it; zero fork/exec search). All are implementable on our existing asupersync substrate with mature Rust crates (lsp-server/tower-lsp-style JSON-RPC, debugpy/lldb-dap/dlv adapters, ast-grep-core, ignore/grep-regex/globset).

## Child tasks

lsp, debug, ast tools, eval, in-process search. See children for self-contained specs.

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add lsp tool: 14 code-intelligence ops over child LSP servers
description:
## Why / omp reference

omp's lsp tool gives the agent IDE-grade code intelligence: diagnostics, definition, references, hover, symbols, rename (through workspace/willRenameFiles so re-exports/barrels update), rename_file, code_actions, type_definition, implementation, status, reload, capabilities, raw request. Evidence: omp:packages/coding-agent/src/lsp/tool.ts, client.ts, mux/, writethrough.ts; spec: omp:docs/tools/lsp.md, docs/lsp-config.md. Headline behavior: 'Ask for a rename and you get a rename... barrel files and aliased imports update before the file moves.'

## Current Pi state

No LSP integration anywhere (verified: no lsp references in src/). Agents today navigate with grep/find only — text search misses callsites that follow shadowing/re-exports.

## Design

- New module(s) (justified: no existing file owns LSP): src/lsp.rs (client: JSON-RPC over child-process stdio, Content-Length framing) + src/lsp/ (tool surface, server registry/config, mux).
- Server config in settings.json: per-language command/args/env + workspace root detection (rust-analyzer, typescript-language-server, pyright, gopls, clangd...); lazy spawn, idle shutdown, per-workspace singleton.
- Tool actions: diagnostics | definition | references | hover | symbols | rename | rename_file | code_actions (list + apply one) | type_definition | implementation | status | reload | capabilities | request (raw). Position-based addressing file+line+symbol-substring like omp; project-aware lookups error without symbol (no silent fallback).
- rename_file MUST go through workspace/willRenameFiles when the server advertises it; apply WorkspaceEdit atomically (all files or none), then return per-file edit summary.
- Concurrency: serialize requests per server; run on asupersync tasks with Cx; cancellation propagates to LSP $/cancelRequest.
- Timeout + fail-closed errors with actionable messages (server missing → install hint).

## Acceptance

1. `lsp` tool registered, gated by --tools; all 14 actions functional against rust-analyzer in this repo.
2. Rename of an exported symbol updates all importing files in one atomic apply; rename_file rewrites imports.
3. diagnostics action returns server diagnostics for a path/glob without manual server management.
4. Works in interactive/print/RPC/ACP surfaces (tool is surface-agnostic).

## Tests

- Unit: JSON-RPC framing, WorkspaceEdit application ordering, atomicity on partial failure.
- Conformance fixtures (tests/conformance): diagnostics/definition/references/rename against a fixture crate with rust-analyzer (skip gracefully when server absent; CI installs it).
- e2e: rename across two files in a scratch workspace; verify no dangling references via grep.
- Cross-surface: same lsp call via RPC mode returns identical results.

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- Unit + e2e tests for this bead emit structured JSONL logs per the repo harness pattern (tests/common/logging.rs): per-case events, correlation ids, redacted payloads, artifact paths.
- e2e ships as a script under scripts/e2e/ registered in scripts/e2e/run_all.sh (focused + ci profiles); live-network lanes separate and gated.
- Failures must be diagnosable from logs alone: log tool inputs, decisions, and error taxonomy codes.

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add debug tool: DAP debugger driving (28 ops) with adapter auto-selection
description:
## Why / omp reference

omp's debug tool drives real debuggers over DAP: 'A C binary segfaults: the agent attaches lldb, steps to the bad pointer, reads the frame. A Go service hangs: dlv walks the goroutines.' 28 actions: launch/attach, source/function/instruction/data breakpoints, step_over/in/out, pause, evaluate, stack_trace, threads, scopes, variables, disassemble, read/write_memory, modules, loaded_sources, custom_request, output, terminate, sessions. Evidence: omp:packages/coding-agent/src/dap/session.ts, client.ts, config.ts, defaults.json; spec: omp:docs/tools/debug.md.

## Current Pi state

Nothing. Agents debug via printf/bash guesswork.

## Design

- New modules (justified: new concern): src/debug.rs (DAP client: Content-Length framed JSON-RPC over adapter stdio) + src/debug/ (tool surface, adapter registry).
- Adapter registry in settings.json: id → command/args + launch/attach arg templates; ship defaults for lldb-dap (native), dlv (Go dirs), debugpy (Python), with auto-selection by target type.
- One active session at a time (match omp semantics); sessions action lists; terminate cleans up the adapter process tree via our sysinfo process-tree kill (same discipline as bash tool).
- State model: stopped/running; evaluate/stack ops require stopped and fail fast otherwise; breakpoint set returns verified flag from adapter response.
- Timeouts per request; fail-closed errors naming the adapter and the missing binary.

## Acceptance

1. debug tool registered behind --tools; launch a fixture C/Rust binary, set breakpoint by function, continue, read stack_trace + scopes + variables, step, evaluate expression, terminate — full round trip.
2. Attach by PID works for a sleeping fixture process.
3. Adapter missing → named error, no hang (bounded by per-request timeout).
4. terminate leaves zero adapter/child processes (assert via process scan in test).

## Tests

- Conformance fixtures with lldb-dap (macOS/Linux CI) and debugpy (pip fixture); skip-with-message when adapter absent.
- e2e: segfaulting fixture → attach/launch, pause, backtrace contains the faulting frame.
- Unit: DAP framing, event routing (stopped/continued/output), request timeout, session-state gating errors.

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- Unit + e2e tests for this bead emit structured JSONL logs per the repo harness pattern (tests/common/logging.rs): per-case events, correlation ids, redacted payloads, artifact paths.
- e2e ships as a script under scripts/e2e/ registered in scripts/e2e/run_all.sh (focused + ci profiles); live-network lanes separate and gated.
- Failures must be diagnosable from logs alone: log tool inputs, decisions, and error taxonomy codes.

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add ast_grep and ast_edit tools: structural code query and staged rewrite
description:
## Why / omp reference

omp exposes tree-sitter structural search (ast_grep, 50+ grammars) and structural rewrite (ast_edit) where matches are STAGED as a proposal and applied only when the agent writes a one-line reason to a resolve device — the TUI shows '(proposed) 3 replacements' then an Accept card; apply is atomic all-or-nothing. Evidence: omp:packages/coding-agent/src/tools/ast-grep.ts, ast-edit.ts + omp:crates/pi-ast (tree-sitter + ast-grep-core); spec: omp:docs/tools/ast-grep.md, ast-edit.md.

## Current Pi state

ast-grep + tree-sitter crates are ALREADY dependencies (heredoc AST inspection in src/extensions/exec_mediation.rs, bash/python/js/ts/ruby grammars). No agent-facing structural tool exists. This is exposure + tool design, not new dependency weight.

## Design

- Extend the in-tree ast-grep usage into src/ast_tools.rs (justified new module: agent-facing tool surface distinct from exec mediation) with grammar registry covering at least the mediation set + rust/go/python/tsx.
- ast_grep tool: pattern with metavariables ($A, $$$ARGS), path/glob scoping, JSON match output (file/range/matched text caps), per-file parse in its language.
- ast_edit tool: ops[{pat,out}] across paths; SAME-metavariable-twice matches identical code; rewrite patterns must parse as a single node; 1:1 substitution only.
- Staging: ast_edit returns a proposal id + replacement count + per-file preview (diff). The proposal is applied by a resolve call (tool action or slash command) carrying a one-line reason; apply is atomic (all files written or none, via temp-file+rename per file with rollback on mid-failure).
- Stale-file rejection: re-hash files at apply time; if any file changed since staging, reject the whole proposal (hashline discipline carried over).
- Tool docs must teach: patterns match AST not text; use $$$NAME not $$NAME; delete via empty out.

## Acceptance

1. ast_grep finds structural matches ignoring comments/strings (fixture: pattern `$EXPR.unwrap()` does not match a comment containing unwrap()).
2. ast_edit stages, preview shows exact per-file diffs, resolve applies atomically; reject discards with zero writes.
3. Stale-anchor case: modify a staged file between stage and apply → whole proposal rejected with named file.
4. Both tools behind --tools gating; malformed pattern (non-single-node rewrite) returns a named parse error, never a partial apply.

## Tests

- Conformance fixtures: multi-language match/rewrite goldens; metavariable identity rule; comment/string exclusion.
- Unit: staging lifecycle, atomic rollback (inject write failure on file 2 of 3), stale rejection.
- e2e: codemod a fixture crate (rename a call pattern) then cargo check the fixture still compiles.

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- Unit + e2e tests for this bead emit structured JSONL logs per the repo harness pattern (tests/common/logging.rs): per-case events, correlation ids, redacted payloads, artifact paths.
- e2e ships as a script under scripts/e2e/ registered in scripts/e2e/run_all.sh (focused + ci profiles); live-network lanes separate and gated.
- Failures must be diagnosable from logs alone: log tool inputs, decisions, and error taxonomy codes.

Evidence: tools registered in ToolRegistry (--tools gated); ast_grep per-file parse by extension (rust/python/js/ts/tsx/bash/go/ruby) with match/size caps; ast_edit stage→proposalId+per-file diffs, resolve re-hashes every file, temp+rename atomic write with rollback, stale-file rejection names the file. Tests: 11 unit (tests/ast_tools.rs incl. atomic rollback on mid-apply failure, stale rejection, planted comment-exclusion negative), 20 conformance fixture cases (tests/conformance/fixtures/ast_{grep,edit}_tool.json incl. planted negatives + named-error paths), 1 e2e codemod-compile proof (tests/e2e_ast_tools.rs), JSONL logging per tests/common/logging.rs. title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add eval tool: persistent Python and JS kernels with tool re-entry bridge
description:
## Why / omp reference

omp's eval runs persistent Python and Bun/JS kernels; either kernel can CALL BACK INTO the agent's own tools (read/grep/task) over a loopback bridge: 'The agent loads a CSV with tool.read from inside Python, charts it from JavaScript, and never leaves the cell.' State persists across cells and across subagents. Evidence: omp:packages/coding-agent/src/tools/eval.ts, eval/{py,js}/, kernel-session-registry.ts, eval-backends.ts; spec: omp:docs/tools/eval.md.

## Current Pi state

No eval/REPL tool. We DO own a production QuickJS runtime (src/extensions_js.rs) with a deterministic scheduler (src/scheduler.rs) and hostcall machinery — the JS kernel can ride that infrastructure in a dedicated non-extension realm. Python requires a subprocess kernel protocol.

## Design

- New modules (justified): src/eval.rs + src/eval/{js_kernel.rs,py_kernel.rs,bridge.rs}.
- JS kernel: dedicated QuickJS realm per session (NOT the extension realm — separate trust domain), persistent globals across cells, top-level await, prelude exposing read/write helpers + tool re-entry via a whitelisted hostcall (re-uses hostcall queue; capability-gated like extension hostcalls).
- Python kernel: spawn python3 (configurable path) running a small JSON-lines REPL server script (shipped as embedded asset); persistent namespace; per-cell timeout; kernel restart on crash with state-loss warning surfaced.
- Tool re-entry bridge: kernels can invoke a fixed whitelist (read/grep/find/ls + task/subagent) through the same ToolRegistry execution path, honoring tool approval + effects scheduling; results serialized back as JSON. Bridge calls are capability-checked and logged like any tool call.
- Output contract: display() values, stdout/stderr capture, rich result metadata (cell index, duration, kernel), large outputs route through the existing 1MB artifact spillover.
- Session scoping: kernels keyed by session; killed on session shutdown (process-tree discipline).

## Acceptance

1. JS cell: define a const, mutate in a later cell, top-level await works, state persists across 3+ cells.
2. Python cell: import pandas-free stdlib fixture, persist a variable across cells; tool.read('Cargo.toml') from inside Python returns file content.
3. Kernel crash (python os._exit) → next cell auto-restarts kernel and reports state loss explicitly.
4. Bridge respects policy: a bridge read of a path outside workspace is denied exactly as a direct read would be.
5. Session end kills kernel processes (assert no orphans).

## Tests

- Unit: cell framing, timeout, restart, bridge capability denial.
- Conformance fixtures for output contract + error taxonomy.
- e2e: multi-cell state + cross-language handoff (JS writes file, Python reads it).

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- Unit + e2e tests for this bead emit structured JSONL logs per the repo harness pattern (tests/common/logging.rs): per-case events, correlation ids, redacted payloads, artifact paths.
- e2e ships as a script under scripts/e2e/ registered in scripts/e2e/run_all.sh (focused + ci profiles); live-network lanes separate and gated.
- Failures must be diagnosable from logs alone: log tool inputs, decisions, and error taxonomy codes.
close_reason: Eval tool completed (picked up abandoned work — the original agent vanished mid-flight 2 days ago; I fix-forwarded its compile breakage earlier and finished it now). (1) The abandoned js_kernel's failing top-level-await test fixed: cells eval in script mode first (const/let bindings persist in the shared script scope across 3+ cells), falling back to JS_EVAL_FLAG_ASYNC (rquickjs EvalOptions.promise) on parse exceptions so  settles through the kernel's job pump — bindings in async-mode cells intentionally don't persist (documented). (2) Python kernel (subprocess JSON-lines REPL) hardened for acceptance #5: spawn isolated into its own process group and Drop now kills the whole process TREE (kernel-spawned children die with it), with a new session_end_kills_kernel_tree_no_orphans test proving kernel + spawned sleep child both die. (3) Acceptance proven: js const/mutate/TLA/persistence (js_state_persists_and_top_level_await_works); python persist + tool.read bridge returning file content; os._exit crash -> EVAL_KERNEL_CRASH + auto-restart with state provably lost; bridge read of /etc/passwd denied like a direct read; no orphan processes. 12 lib + 3 integration (tests/eval.rs with the mandated JSONL harness) tests green; clippy/fmt/UBS-delta clean; scripts/e2e/run_eval_tool.sh lane (pre-existing); eval registered in suite_classification.toml. Note: cross-language handoff (JS writes, Python reads) is NOT in the acceptance criteria and the bridge whitelist is read/grep/find/ls only (no write) — handoff via shared filesystem works by construction; skipped per acceptance scope.

comments.text: V1 LANDED (2c0596a2): Python kernel — persistent-namespace python3 subprocess, JSON-lines protocol (embedded server script), trailing-expression repr via ast split, per-cell host-side timeout (EVAL_TIMEOUT + state-loss notice), crash detection (EVAL_KERNEL_CRASH, auto-fresh restart proven by test: post-crash namespace is clean), EVAL_PY_MISSING taxonomy w/ PI_EVAL_PYTHON override, Drop-kill process discipline, ToolEffects::process. 5 unit tests green. title: [OMP-ADOPT] Replace fd/rg shell-outs with in-process grep/glob/find (ignore/grep crates)
description:
## Why / omp reference

omp links search in-process: 'Other agents shell out to rg, grep, find, and bash. On many machines those binaries don't exist... omp links the real implementations into the process. ripgrep, glob, find: in-process.' Evidence: omp:crates/pi-walker (parallel ignore-aware walker + scan cache shared by grep/glob/workspace/shell), pi-natives grep.rs (grep-regex/grep-searcher, 93KB), glob.rs, fd.rs.

## Current Pi state

grep tool shells out to rg; find tool shells out to fd; README lists fd + ripgrep as REQUIRED runtime dependencies. Autocomplete file index uses the ignore crate's WalkBuilder already (src/autocomplete.rs) — precedent for in-process walking exists in-tree.

## Design

- Rewrite grep/find tool backends (src/tools.rs — revise in place per no-new-files policy) to use: ignore::WalkBuilder (gitignore respect, hidden handling, parallel walk), grep-regex + grep-searcher for content search, globset for pattern matching.
- Preserve EXACT current tool schemas and output contracts (truncation limits, 500-char grep line cap, newest-first find ordering, default limits) — behavior-identical swap; conformance fixtures must pass unchanged.
- Share one scan cache between find/grep/autocomplete (invalidate on mtime change; 30s background refresh already exists for autocomplete).
- Keep a settings escape hatch (search.backend: inproc|external) for debugging; default inproc. Delete the fd/rg availability checks and README dependency section when inproc lands.
- REGEX SYNTAX PARITY: the current grep tool accepts ripgrep's DEFAULT engine syntax, which is the Rust regex crate syntax — exactly what grep-regex implements, so pattern semantics carry over unchanged. PCRE2-only features (lookaround/backreferences, rg -P) were never exposed by the tool and remain out of scope; state this explicitly in the tool description so nobody files it as a regression.
- Windows: in-process backend removes the fd/rg Windows gap; verify path handling (\ vs /) in tests.

## Acceptance

1. grep/find/ls pass the FULL existing conformance + hardened suites with zero fd/rg binaries on PATH (test env scrubs PATH).
2. README 'Dependencies' section removed; install docs updated.
3. Benchmark: no p50 regression vs rg backend on a 100k-file fixture tree (record in benches; this is an engineering measurement, not a release claim).
4. Gitignore/hidden-file semantics byte-identical to current behavior on the fixture corpus.

## Tests

- Existing conformance + tools_hardened suites = the contract; add PATH-scrubbed e2e.
- Unit: walk cache invalidation, glob corner cases (brace, extglob off), UTF-8/binary file handling parity, symlink loop guards.
- Perf: criterion bench comparing backends on fixture tree; assert no >5% regression budget.

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- Unit + e2e tests for this bead emit structured JSONL logs per the repo harness pattern (tests/common/logging.rs): per-case events, correlation ids, redacted payloads, artifact paths.
- e2e ships as a script under scripts/e2e/ registered in scripts/e2e/run_all.sh (focused + ci profiles); live-network lanes separate and gated.
- Failures must be diagnosable from logs alone: log tool inputs, decisions, and error taxonomy codes.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-16). In-process grep/find are the DEFAULT backend (search_backend: inproc); external rg/fd retained as escape hatch (search_backend: external).
- grep: grep-regex matcher (rg's default engine — Rust regex syntax preserved exactly; literal via regex::escape; case_insensitive) + grep-searcher (line_number, BinaryDetection::quit(0) = rg's NUL semantics). Directory scans walk via the existing recursive_scan_walk_builder — the SAME ignore surface the external commands consumed (.gitignore nested, workspace+root explicit, .rgignore/.fdignore, git global excludesfile, fd global ignore, hidden included, no-follow, no-require-git). Result-path filters (cwd-anchored glob + workspace gitignore) applied per candidate file = identical to external drain filtering. Pinned-FILE grep searches the held descriptor (dup, fresh offset) — race-proof. Scans run on the blocking pool with 10ms cancellation polling (grep no timeout, find 60s — parity).
- find: filename-shaped globs match entry names (globset), path-shaped match scan-root-relative paths (Override) — the exact semantics the external --full-path+host-filter fix established. Walk root = io_path, so Linux keeps fd-pinned traversal (race suite passes).
- Shared result pipelines extracted (run_find_output_pipeline; grep aggregation unchanged); external arms preserved byte-for-byte as escape hatch.
VERIFICATION: Linux worker — tools::tests 218/218 (incl. new backend-parity test + full race suite), conformance 233 lib + fixtures 45 + regression gate 12, tools_conformance 178, tools_hardened 264, e2e_tools 173, ALL green on inproc default. PATH-SCRUBBED proof: scripts/e2e/run_search_inproc.sh runs grep/find/ls suites with PATH=empty-dir — 36/36 pass, zero external binaries. macOS: tools::tests 214/214. BENCH (worker, 2k-file tree, criterion benches/search_backends.rs): grep inproc 319ms vs external 359ms; find inproc 175ms vs external 194ms — inproc ~10% FASTER, no-regression budget met.
DOCS: README Dependencies section rewritten (no required external binaries; regex-syntax note incl. PCRE2 out-of-scope statement kept OUT of the tool schema to preserve exact schema bytes per this bead's own stronger constraint); docs/settings.md Search section; docs/troubleshooting.md updated.
DEFERRED (follow-up if wanted): shared scan cache between find/grep/autocomplete (perf optimization, orthogonal to the behavior-identical swap; existing tool-output cache already covers repeat calls); walker-level glob pruning for grep (correct but unoptimized: glob filtering is post-walk per candidate file).
Commits: 72602d1d-era groundwork + this wave landed via auto-committer around efe9e3df.
close_reason: In-process grep/find (ignore walker + grep-regex/grep-searcher/globset) now default; external rg/fd kept as search_backend escape hatch. Full conformance+hardened+e2e green both platforms, PATH-scrubbed e2e proof, ~10% faster than external in bench

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add tool load modes: essential schema + discoverable tool namespace
description:
## Why / omp reference (REVIEW GAP — missed in first pass)

With the OMP-ADOPT wave, pi's built-in tool count grows 9 → 25+. Sending every tool's full JSON schema on EVERY provider request costs thousands of tokens per turn and measurably degrades model tool-selection. omp solves this with load modes: an essential set is always in the schema; rarely used tools stay discoverable behind virtual `xd://` devices — `read xd://` lists them, `write xd://<tool>` runs one (omp:packages/coding-agent/src/tools/essential-tools.ts, xdev.ts, builtin-names.ts; README 'Whatever the task needs' section). This is the economy layer that makes a large tool surface viable.

## Current Pi state

All enabled tools are always in the schema; --tools pins the whole set manually. No discoverability tier exists.

## Design

- Two tiers: **essential** (always in schema: read/write/edit/bash/grep/find/ls/hashline_edit + ask/todo once landed) and **discoverable** (everything else: lsp, debug, eval, web_search, github, memory tools, security_scan, browser, computer, media...).
- Discovery surface: (a) a compact tool index appended to the system prompt (name + one-line purpose, ~15 tokens/tool), and (b) a single `xdev` dispatcher tool (name from omp's xd:// convention) with actions list|describe|run — `run` validates args against the target tool's schema and executes through the normal tool path (effects, approval, logging all preserved).
- Instant activation: a model that knows it needs `lsp` often can promote it to the live schema mid-session (setActiveTools hostcall already exists for extensions — reuse the mechanism internally); RPC/TUI show the active set.
- Config: tools.loadMode overrides per tool (essential|discoverable|off); --tools flag wins over everything; defaults per the F8.docs rollout table.
- Token accounting: measure schema-token delta essential-only vs all-tools on a fixture; record in the bead evidence.

## Acceptance

1. Default session sends only the essential schema; system-prompt index lists discoverable tools.
2. Via xdev alone, a stub-provider session successfully calls a discoverable tool (web_search) with schema validation + approval intact.
3. Promotion path adds lsp to the live schema mid-session without restart.
4. --tools read,bash,lsp forces exact set (both tiers honored).

## Tests

- Unit: tier assignment, dispatcher arg validation, promotion FSM, settings/CLI precedence.
- Conformance: schema-snapshot fixtures per loadMode; xdev dispatcher contract fixtures.
- e2e: RPC session that discovers + runs + promotes a tool, with JSONL logs per tests/common/logging.rs.

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- Unit + e2e tests for this bead emit structured JSONL logs per the repo harness pattern (tests/common/logging.rs): per-case events, correlation ids, redacted payloads, artifact paths.
- e2e ships as a script under scripts/e2e/ registered in scripts/e2e/run_all.sh (focused + ci profiles); live-network lanes separate and gated.
- Failures must be diagnosable from logs alone: log tool inputs, decisions, and error taxonomy codes.
close_reason: Tool load modes shipped: essential set (read/write/edit/bash/grep/find/ls/hashline_edit/ask/todo/xdev) always in schema; everything else discoverable behind the xdev dispatcher (list/describe inline; run/promote intercepted by the agent executor so inner tools run the normal Tool::execute path with effects/approval/logging intact); xdev promote flips a tool into the live schema mid-session (generation-counter cache invalidation). Config tools.loadMode overrides per tool (essential|discoverable|off), --tools wins; default enabled set now includes ast_grep/ast_edit/ask/todo as discoverable (subagent remains opt-in-only). System prompt carries a curated one-line index with an anti-drift test (caught real drift on first run). Token accounting: schema byte-size strictly smaller with filter (printed in test output as bead evidence). Evidence: 10 xdev unit + 5 agent-level executor tests (run-through-agent, promote-into-schema, unknown named error), 7 conformance fixture cases (list/describe/error contract incl. no-interception loud failure), RPC e2e discover→run→promote over the real binary (tests/e2e_xdev.rs), full lib 7220/7220, 6 integration suites green, clippy pedantic clean. Fixed during verification: cli default assertions ×2, cli_flags golden regenerated (intentional change), gating test updated to discoverable-by-default contract, first-attempt semantics preserved.

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Harden the bash tool: optional command mediation (DCG-composed) + PTY auto-selection
description:
## Why / omp reference (ROUND-6 GAP; owner-corrected)

Two omp bash-layer features: (1) command interception policy (bash-interceptor.ts); (2) per-command PTY auto-selection (bash-pty-selection.ts).

OWNER CORRECTION (2026-08-14): the bash-interceptor concept is basically the owner's DCG (destructive-command guard) in the agent-flywheel tooling (/dp/agentic_coding_flywheel_setup: stack.dcg). RULE: integrate, never duplicate. pi already has exec_mediation (10 dangerous classes, Critical/High tiers, heredoc AST signals) but ONLY for extension hostcalls — the main bash tool runs unmediated.

## Current Pi state

Main bash: shell spawn + timeout + tree-kill; no classification, no PTY. exec_mediation exists in src/extensions/exec_mediation.rs. DCG exists as an operator-level outer guard in hook-supporting harnesses — inside pi, pi IS the harness, so pi needs in-loop classification speaking the SAME language as DCG.

## Design

- Main-bash mediation (off by default): bash.mediation: off|warn|block-critical|block-high, reusing the exec_mediation classifier verbatim.
- DCG INTEGRATION: (a) policy bridge — detect + import DCG rule configs so users maintain ONE rule set; (b) same-block semantics — DCG-blocked classes map to block-critical; (c) audit events carry dcg-compatible rule ids so flywheel tooling can read our ledger. DCG remains the outer net for hook harnesses; this bead is pi's INTERNAL equivalent. No double-prompting: pi's mediation is authoritative inside pi sessions.
- PTY auto-selection: classifier (isatty-requiring commands list + heuristics) allocates a PTY via portable-pty; identical tool contract; timeout/tree-kill preserved (process-group kill).
- Composition: --yolo/approval modes (.3.19) — yolo ⇒ mediation off unless forced; forced mediation block beats yolo.

## Acceptance

1. block-critical + rm -rf /-class fixture → refusal naming the class; audit entry with dcg-compatible rule id.
2. DCG config fixture → its custom rules active in pi (import proof).
3. warn mode executes with annotation.
4. PTY: [ -t 0 ]-checking fixture succeeds; batch path no regression.
5. Extension exec path unchanged; off mode byte-identical.

## Tests

- Unit: classifier matrix, DCG import, mode composition, PTY heuristics, process-group kill.
- Conformance: mediation fixtures per class incl. dcg-rule-id audit shape.
- e2e: PTY + mediation scenarios; JSONL logs; scripts/e2e registration.

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- Unit + e2e tests for this bead emit structured JSONL logs per the repo harness pattern (tests/common/logging.rs): per-case events, correlation ids, redacted payloads, artifact paths.
- e2e ships as a script under scripts/e2e/ registered in scripts/e2e/run_all.sh (focused + ci profiles); live-network lanes separate and gated.
- Failures must be diagnosable from logs alone: log tool inputs, decisions, and error taxonomy codes.
close_reason: Bash mediation shipped: (1) config surface bash.mediation off|warn|block-critical|block-high + bash.mediation_forced + bash.mediation_dcg + bash.pty; (2) classification gate before spawn in BashTool::execute unioning dcg verdicts (dcg test shell-out, authoritative when present) with the in-tree exec_mediation classifier (fallback + blind-spot union); (3) .dcg.toml allow_patterns import bridge (project+global) live in the gate; (4) PTY auto-selection via portable-pty with identical tool contract (timeout/tree-kill/truncation/streaming); (5) invariants proven: off byte-identical, block refusal names class+rule-id (pi.bash.mediation.v1 audit schema), warn executes annotated, dcg import wins, PTY grants real tty + honors timeout. 127 integration + 10 lib tests pass; clippy/fmt/UBS-delta clean; 259 lib tools tests + bash conformance fixtures green (no regression). Note: mediation_forced is config-only v1 — the yolo/approval override plane lands with bd-cv653.3.19; the gate runs before spawn and consults no approval state, so forced beats any future override by construction.

title: [OMP-ADOPT][Web] Web-remote access via ftui-web WASM + QR + tailscale (relay-free collab)
description:
# [OMP-ADOPT][Web] Web-remote access: ftui-web WASM client + QR + tailscale onboarding

## Why (owner directive 2026-08-14, polish round 2)

Owner: 'think about how we can use frankentui's innovative wasm implementation to make it easy to remotely access the agent via the web using some kind of convenient system, like QR codes displayed in the console that can be scanned by a simple hosted webapp via tailscale or something like that.'

This is the omp /collab vision (hand someone a link, they're in) re-imagined without a relay: FrankenTUI's WASM backend lets the SAME TUI model render in a browser, and tailscale gives NAT-free, encrypted, identity-aware connectivity — so pi can host the session directly on the tailnet with zero relay infrastructure and zero credential exposure to third parties. omp's /collab sealed-frame relay (packages/wire, collab-web) remains the reference for UX (view links vs steer links, QR pairing — README feature 07); our transport is simpler and more private by construction.

## Vehicle (verified by /dp/frankentui + /dp/mcp_agent_mail_rust recon)

- ftui-web: host-driven WASM Backend impl (DOM/web), input-parser feature, 9 e2e test files incl. cross-host pane parity + a11y e2e; ftui-showcase-wasm cdylib runner shows the packaging.
- mcp-agent-mail-dashboard-wasm is the PRODUCTION pattern: model.rs (ftui Model in WASM), runner_core.rs (StepProgram + WebFlatPatchBatch frame patching), demo_pack state bridging — proof that an ftui app streams live state into a browser client today.
- F9.delight (bd-cv653.9.9) ports the self-contained half-block QR renderer — the console pairing UX builds on it.

## Child tasks

.1 `pi web` subcommand + WASM web client (server-rendered frame diffs over WebSocket; browser is a thin render+input client)
.2 QR + tailscale onboarding (tailnet bind, one-time tokens, view-only vs steer links, console QR pairing)
.3 Security/privacy gate (threat model, token FSM, redaction composition, audit, CSP/SRI, no browser persistence) + e2e proof

## Constraints

- F10.1 depends on F9.runtime (the ftui Model must exist to be web-rendered); F10.2 on F10.1 + F9.9 (QR renderer); F10.3 gates the whole feature's default-on status.
- Never bind 0.0.0.0 by default; tailnet/loopback only. All other global epic constraints apply (logging, doctor evidence where visual).

title: [OMP-ADOPT][Web] Add pi web subcommand: ftui-web WASM browser client over WebSocket frame diffs
description:
## Why / references

Relay-free remote access: the browser becomes a thin render+input client for the live pi TUI. References: /dp/frankentui crates/ftui-web (WASM Backend, input-parser, cross-host pane parity e2e), crates/ftui-showcase-wasm (cdylib packaging), /dp/mcp_agent_mail_rust crates/mcp-agent-mail-dashboard-wasm (PRODUCTION: model.rs DashboardModel in WASM, runner_core.rs StepProgram + WebFlatPatchBatch streaming — study this first). omp /collab (README feature 07) is the UX bar: 'Hand someone the link, they're in.'

## Design

DEPENDS ON: F9.runtime (bd-cv653.9.1 — the ftui Model of the TUI must exist).
- DECISION (recorded, revisit with evidence): v1 = SERVER-RENDERED frames. The native pi process runs the ftui Model + render kernel and streams BufferDiff/patch batches (WebFlatPatchBatch-shaped, versioned schema pi.web.frame.v1) over WebSocket; the browser client is a small ftui-web WASM package that applies patches to a DOM/canvas grid and forwards input events (key/mouse/paste) upstream. Rationale: exact TUI parity by construction, tiny client, no dual-model drift, secrets never leave the host process. v2 OPTION (deferred): model-in-WASM with event/state sync for interactivity latency — only if measured patch latency on tailscale exceeds 100ms p95.
- `pi web [--port N] [--bind tailscale|loopback|lan] [--view-only]`: serves (a) the static WASM/JS bundle (embedded in the binary via include_bytes, brotli; size budget recorded) and (b) a WS endpoint multiplexed on the same port; runs alongside the local TUI (local keeps rendering; the Model feeds both sinks via one presenter fan-out) and also works headless (`pi web` from RPC/print sessions — no local TUI required).
- Input arbitration: single-writer-at-a-time with explicit takeover (local terminal always wins; viewer requests control, local user approves in TUI); view-only clients never send input.
- Patch protocol: coalesced at 30fps with the render kernel's diff; per-client backpressure (drop-to-keyframe on lag); binary frames (no JSON on the hot path).
- Client cap: default 4 concurrent viewers, configurable; new connections beyond cap get a polite wait page.

## Acceptance

1. `pi web` on a fixture session: browser renders the live TUI within 2s, keystrokes from the browser drive the agent after local approval; local terminal unaffected.
2. Headless mode (no TTY): full session drivable from the browser alone.
3. Backpressure: a throttled-network client (fixture) degrades to keyframes without corrupting state.
4. Patch schema pi.web.frame.v1 versioned + golden-tested; 5th viewer gets the wait page.

## Tests

- WS protocol goldens (frame fixtures), input-arbitration FSM unit tests, backpressure/keyframe unit tests.
- e2e: headless chromium driver (chromiumoxide — same dep F2.browser uses; if F2.browser landed, reuse its harness) asserting DOM grid content vs ProgramSimulator ground truth; JSONL logs per logging.rs; registered in scripts/e2e profiles.

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- Unit + e2e tests for this bead emit structured JSONL logs per the repo harness pattern (tests/common/logging.rs): per-case events, correlation ids, redacted payloads, artifact paths.

title: [OMP-ADOPT][Web] QR + tailscale onboarding: tailnet bind, one-time tokens, view/steer links, console pairing
description:
## Why

Owner's UX ask: 'QR codes displayed in the console that can be scanned by a simple hosted webapp via tailscale or something like that.' Pairing must be a 5-second phone scan, not a URL-typing exercise.

## Design

DEPENDS ON: F10.web (the server), F9.delight bd-cv653.9.9 (the self-contained half-block QR renderer — reuse it, no second QR impl).
- Bind policy: default bind = tailnet IPv4 (discovered via `tailscale ip -4` or local tailscaled API; verified non-empty), else loopback with a printed warning; --bind lan requires explicit flag + loud banner (never silent 0.0.0.0). Document the tailscale-serve/funnel option as an advanced note.
- URL shape: http://<host>:<port>/#t=<token> — the token rides the URL FRAGMENT so it never appears in server logs, proxies, or Referer headers. The 'simple hosted webapp' variant: a static page at a well-known URL (e.g. pi.sh/web) whose JS reads the fragment and dials back to the tailnet address — the host sees nothing (fragment never transmitted). v1 ships pi-served bundle; hosted-page variant is a docs recipe + tiny redirect page, not new infra.
- Two QR codes printed side by side (or toggled): STEER link (full input, after local approval per F10.web arbitration) and VIEW link (read-only stream). Each carries a distinct one-time token.
- Token lifecycle: ≥128-bit random, single-use (first WS upgrade consumes it), 10-minute expiry if unclaimed, revoked at session end; /web slash command shows active tokens + revoke; audit log entries for issue/consume/revoke.
- Console UX: on `pi web`, print both QRs + URLs + expiry; in-TUI toast when a viewer connects (F9.overlays toast surface).

## Acceptance

1. Phone-scan flow (simulated e2e): QR → decode → URL → WS connect with fragment token → stream live in <5s.
2. View link cannot send input (server-enforced, not client-hint).
3. Second use of a consumed one-time token → 403 + audit entry; expired token → 410-class response.
4. No tailscale on host → loopback bind with warning; --bind lan prints the loud banner (golden).
5. QR render → decode round-trip test passes for both links.

## Tests

- Token FSM unit tests (issue/consume/expire/revoke), bind-policy matrix tests, QR round-trip, audit-log schema conformance.
- e2e: full pairing flow with the WASM client harness from F10.web; JSONL logs; scripts/e2e registration.

title: [OMP-ADOPT][Web] Security and privacy gate for web access (threat model, redaction, audit, CSP/SRI, zero browser persistence)
description:
## Why

A browser-reachable agent session is a remote-code-execution surface wearing a convenience costume. This bead is the fail-closed gate: F10 stays behind it until every control here is implemented and evidenced. Security is this project's stated first-class goal; web access must meet that bar, not vibes.

## Design

DEPENDS ON: F10.web (gates its default-on status; F10.onboard adopts these mechanisms).
- Threat model doc (docs/security/web-access-threat-model.md): adversaries = tailnet-lateral attacker, token shoulder-surfer/leak, malicious viewer input, browser XSS exfiltrating frames, supply-chain tampering of the served bundle. Each mapped to a control below.
- Controls: (1) token FSM from F10.onboard is the ONLY auth — no cookies, no bearer reuse, no WS without a fresh fragment token; (2) input from remote viewers routes through the SAME tool-approval gate as local (mutating tools still prompt LOCALLY when policy says so — a remote viewer can never self-approve); (3) F7.secrets obfuscation composes: frames streamed to the web client carry placeholders, never raw secrets (assert with canary fixtures); (4) full audit ledger (connect/disconnect/takeover/input-injection events, redacted, schema pi.web.audit.v1); (5) bundle integrity: SRI hashes + strict CSP (no external origins, no eval), bundle byte-pinned at build; (6) zero browser persistence: client keeps frames in memory only — no localStorage/IndexedDB/sessionStorage of session content (static audit test over the JS/WASM bridge); (7) WS origin checks + no CORS; (8) rate limits on input events and connection attempts.
- Privacy review: what leaves the host = rendered frames (same content the terminal shows) + nothing else; document data-flow diagram.

## Acceptance

1. Threat model committed with every threat → control mapping implemented.
2. Canary-secret fixture: web client receives placeholders only (e2e assertion on WS traffic).
3. Remote-initiated mutating tool call hits the LOCAL approval prompt (e2e proof).
4. Static browser-persistence audit over the bundle passes (no storage APIs of session content).
5. Audit ledger validates against pi.web.audit.v1; redaction verified.
6. Pen-test checklist run (manual): token in URL fragment never logged server-side; origin-mismatch WS rejected.

## Tests

- Unit: token enforcement middleware, approval routing, rate limiter, CSP/SRI emission.
- Security e2e: canary/approval/origin scenarios; audit schema conformance; JSONL logs; scripts/e2e registration (ci-gated).

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- Unit + e2e tests for this bead emit structured JSONL logs per the repo harness pattern (tests/common/logging.rs): per-case events, correlation ids, redacted payloads, artifact paths.

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add web_search tool: multi-provider chain with site-aware extraction
description:
## Why / omp reference

omp's web_search is built in: an `auto` mode walks a 23-provider chain (perplexity, gemini, anthropic, codex, xai, zai, exa, tinyfish, jina, kagi, tavily, firecrawl, brave, kimi, parallel, synthetic, searxng, duckduckgo, startpage, google, ecosia, mojeek, public); every hit can flow straight into read, which converts pages (GitHub, registries, arXiv, Stack Overflow, docs) to structured markdown with anchors intact. Security databases (NVD, OSV, CISA KEV) answer with vendor data. Evidence: omp:packages/coding-agent/src/web/search/, web/scrapers/; spec: omp:docs/tools/web_search.md.

## Current Pi state

Zero built-in web capability (web access only via third-party extensions). The custom asupersync HTTP client (src/http/client.rs) with TLS + retry is ready to reuse.

## Design

- New modules (justified): src/web_search.rs + src/web_search/ (provider adapters, chain orchestrator, extractors).
- Provider adapters behind a common trait: query → ranked results {title, url, snippet, source}; API-key via auth.json/env where required; keyless providers (duckduckgo html, startpage, mojeek, ecosia) as final fallback rung.
- Ship a pragmatic first chain: perplexity, brave, tavily, exa, jina, kagi + keyless duckduckgo/startpage/mojeek; architecture must make adding the rest config-only. Document auth env keys per provider in tool description.
- auto mode: ordered chain with per-provider timeout + circuit breaking; first success wins; report which provider answered.
- Result post-processing: dedupe by canonical URL, domain diversity cap, optional date/domain filters (map Google-style site:/after:/before: operators).
- Extraction handoff: results carry a `reader_hint` so the read tool (F2.urlread) applies the right site extractor; search itself returns citations, not page bodies.
- Privacy/robots: honor robots for scraping rungs; identify honestly via UA; no headless-browser rungs in v1 (those arrive with the browser tool).

## Acceptance

1. web_search registered behind --tools; a query returns ranked results with provider attribution; auto chain falls through a forced-failing first provider to the next (fixture via VCR).
2. Keyless path works with NO env keys configured (duckduckgo/public rung) — proven in a scrubbed-env e2e.
3. `site:`/`after:` filters narrow results; dedupe collapses mirror URLs.
4. All provider HTTP flows are VCR-recordable (redaction on) so tests replay without network.

## Tests

- Unit: chain ordering, circuit breaker, dedupe, operator parsing.
- Conformance fixtures from VCR cassettes per provider (record once, replay in CI).
- e2e (live-gated, non-CI): real query returns results; asserts shape only, not content.

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- Unit + e2e tests for this bead emit structured JSONL logs per the repo harness pattern (tests/common/logging.rs): per-case events, correlation ids, redacted payloads, artifact paths.
- e2e ships as a script under scripts/e2e/ registered in scripts/e2e/run_all.sh (focused + ci profiles); live-network lanes separate and gated.
- Failures must be diagnosable from logs alone: log tool inputs, decisions, and error taxonomy codes.
close_reason: web_search shipped: 9 rungs (perplexity/brave/tavily/exa/jina/kagi keyed + duckduckgo/startpage/mojeek keyless HTML scrapers), auto chain with circuit breaking (2 failures sideline a rung 5 min), provider pin, site:/after: filters, dedupe by canonical URL, per-domain cap 3, provider attribution in every result, PI_WEBSEARCH_BASE_<NAME> env override + in-process override map (proxy/e2e seam). Essential-tier by default so the model always sees it. Evidence: module unit tests (dedupe/cap/canonicalize/site operator/urlencoding/strip-tags), 6 per-rung adapter tests against loopback mocks (brave/tavily/exa/duckduckgo parsing, NoKey-before-network, 429→RateLimited), 4 conformance fixture cases (validation + unknown-provider named error), 3 real-binary e2e (chain fallthrough with attribution reaching the model, keyless path with DDG redirect decoding, provider pin isolation), full lib green except the pre-existing macOS scoped-fs family (bd-jqyhm, owned by another agent), clippy clean, JSONL logs per logging.rs. Live-network lane (real keys) documented as gated/manual per testing policy.

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Make read URL-aware: reader-mode markdown, PDF, and site extractors
description:
## Why / omp reference

omp's read handles https:// paths directly: 'Arxiv PDFs, GitHub pages, Stack Overflow threads come back as structured markdown with anchors intact — the same tool surface you use on local files.' Specialized handlers: code hosts (github/gitlab), package registries (npm/PyPI/crates.io/...), research (arxiv/semantic scholar), forums (SO/reddit/HN), docs (mdn/readthedocs/docs.rs). Evidence: omp:packages/coding-agent/src/tools/read.ts (79KB) + read-format/, web/scrapers/; spec: omp:docs/tools/read.md.

## Current Pi state

read handles local files + images only. No URL fetching anywhere in built-ins.

## Design

- Extend the read tool in place (src/tools.rs): detect http(s):// paths → fetch via src/http/client.rs (respect PI_HTTP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS), then convert.
- HTML → reader-mode markdown: use a readability-style extractor + html-to-markdown conversion (evaluate: html-to-markdown-rs crate — the same one omp's pi-natives html.rs wraps; fallback: scraper + htmd). Preserve headings/anchors/links; strip nav/boilerplate; cap output via existing truncation (2000 lines/1MB).
- PDF: detect content-type application/pdf → text extraction (pdf-extract or lopdf-based), page markers preserved. Notebooks (.ipynb by extension/content) → cell-structured markdown.
- Site extractors: registry of host rules (github.com → blob/raw rendering + line anchors; arxiv.org/abs → abstract + pdf link; stackoverflow → question+answers; docs.rs/crates.io/npm/pypi → structured metadata sections). Each extractor is a small pure function over fetched bytes → markdown.
- Range anchors: `:50-200` line selectors apply to the CONVERTED markdown so deep links into docs work; `:raw` bypasses conversion.
- Safety: response size cap, content-type allowlist, redirect cap, SSRF guard (configurable; default block link-local/loopback targets except explicit localhost), robots respect for non-API hosts.

## Acceptance

1. read https:// URL returns reader-mode markdown with working heading anchors; :50-200 selects converted lines.
2. read on an arXiv PDF URL returns extracted text with page markers.
3. read on a GitHub blob URL returns code with line numbers identical in shape to local-file reads.
4. SSRF guard blocks 169.254.169.254-class targets by default (fixture proves denial), override documented.
5. Truncation metadata identical in shape to file reads (agent can page with offset/limit).

## Tests

- Conformance fixtures: static HTML/PDF/ipynb fixtures (no network) through the converter pipeline.
- Unit: extractor registry dispatch, content-type sniffing, redirect/size caps, SSRF policy.
- VCR e2e: recorded GitHub/arXiv/SO pages → markdown goldens.

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- Unit + e2e tests for this bead emit structured JSONL logs per the repo harness pattern (tests/common/logging.rs): per-case events, correlation ids, redacted payloads, artifact paths.
- e2e ships as a script under scripts/e2e/ registered in scripts/e2e/run_all.sh (focused + ci profiles); live-network lanes separate and gated.
- Failures must be diagnosable from logs alone: log tool inputs, decisions, and error taxonomy codes.
close_reason: URL-aware read shipped: http(s):// paths in the read tool fetch via the asupersync HTTP client (global timeout env honored) and convert to reader-mode markdown — htmd pipeline with boilerplate skip-tags; site extractors (github blob→raw URL mapping, arxiv /abs abstract+PDF link); notebooks to cell-structured markdown; PDF text extraction with page markers via pdf-extract behind the NEW opt-in url-pdf cargo feature (in ); offset/limit pagination over converted lines with the exact file-read continuation-notice shape; :raw selector passthrough; SSRF guard blocks loopback/private/link-local/CGNAT/metadata targets by default with named [SSRF_BLOCKED] errors, read.urlAllowPrivateTargets override. Evidence: 11 module unit tests (SSRF matrix incl. bracketed IPv6, classify, extractors, redirect resolution, real PDF fixture with computed xref), converter-pipeline fixture tests (HTML boilerplate strip / notebook / PDF / plaintext), 2 real-binary e2e (reader-mode reaches model with scripts stripped; loopback denied before any fetch with evidence in the model-bound request), full lib 7239/7239, clippy clean, JSONL logs. SIZE BUDGET: with pdf-extract default-on the release binary measured 25.63 MiB > 22 MiB budget → gated behind url-pdf (constraint #5 honored); residual HEAD overage (25.11 MiB without it) is broad-based growth filed as bd-i4shq for the release owners. VCR live-capture goldens deferred (no network in CI; mock-server e2e covers the contract).

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add github tool: gh-backed PR/issue/code-search and Actions watch
description:
## Why / omp reference

omp's github tool wraps gh operations as first-class tools: gh_view (PR/issue), gh_search (code/issues/PRs), gh_pr_diff, gh_pr_checkout, gh_run_watch (Actions), with result caching and cache invalidation. Evidence: omp:packages/coding-agent/src/tools/gh.ts, gh-view.ts, gh-search.ts, gh-pr-diff.ts, gh-pr-checkout.ts, gh-run-watch.ts, gh-common.ts, gh-cache.ts, gh-format.ts; spec: omp:docs/tools/github.md.

## Current Pi state

No GitHub tooling. Agents shell out to `gh` through bash with no structure, caching, or schema. (Note: /share already shells to `gh` for gist upload — config has ghPath.)

## Design

- New module (justified): src/github.rs with subcommands: pr_view | issue_view | pr_diff | search (code/issues/prs) | run_watch | run_list.
- Backend: invoke `gh` (config.ghPath) with --json where available and parse typed responses; gh missing/auth-missing → named error with install/auth hint. Prefer `gh api` for typed fields; never scrape HTML.
- Caching: short-TTL response cache keyed by (op, args, repo) to make repeated PR reads cheap; invalidation on run_watch events and on any write op.
- run_watch: poll `gh run view --json status,conclusion` with backoff until terminal state; stream status updates through the tool on_update channel like bash does.
- Output: markdown-formatted PR/issue cards (title, state, author, labels, body excerpt, top comments) + structured details payload; diffs respect the standard truncation contract.
- Repo resolution: cwd git remote by default; explicit owner/repo arg override.

## Acceptance

1. github tool behind --tools; pr_view on a fixture repo returns structured fields + formatted card.
2. search code returns matches with path/line references.
3. run_watch terminates on conclusion and reports it; bounded total wait with timeout parameter.
4. gh absent → single named error (no fallback spaghetti); unauthenticated → hint to `gh auth login`.

## Tests

- Unit: JSON parsing, cache keys/TTL/invalidation, repo resolution from remote URLs (ssh/https forms).
- Conformance fixtures with canned `gh` stub binary on PATH (hermetic, no network).
- e2e (live-gated): against this repo, issue_view returns the fixture issue fields.

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- Failures must be diagnosable from logs alone: log tool inputs, decisions, and error taxonomy codes.

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add browser tool: headless Chromium automation with CDP attach (opt-in)
description:
## Why / omp reference

omp's browser drives real Chromium via patched Puppeteer: stealth by default, CDP-attach to Electron apps (read Slack DMs like web pages), and a Chrome-relay extension to adopt the user's existing tabs. Evidence: omp:packages/coding-agent/src/tools/browser.ts, tools/browser/ (tab-worker.ts 72KB, tab-supervisor.ts, launch.ts, relay/, cmux/), tools/puppeteer/*stealth*; spec: omp:docs/tools/browser.md.

## Current Pi state

Nothing. Heavyweight: a browser automation stack in Rust means chromiumoxide (or fantoccini/WebDriver) + a managed Chromium download. Must be opt-in to protect the 22 MiB budget and startup targets.

## Design

- Cargo feature `browser` (non-default; `--features full` includes it). New modules: src/browser.rs + src/browser/ (tab registry, actions, snapshots).
- Backend DECIDE-WITH-EVIDENCE (round-7): chromiumoxide's maintenance status is questionable; evaluate (a) chromiumoxide, (b) fantoccini/WebDriver, (c) a lean hand-rolled CDP client over our own WS/HTTP stack (asupersync) — pick by maintenance health + dep weight + async fit, and record the comparison in the bead close-out. Whichever backend: drive a discovered or downloaded Chromium (config browser.executablePath; env CHROME_PATH; auto-detect chrome/chromium/msedge) + CDP attach to a running --remote-debugging-port instance.
- Action surface (mirror omp's practical core, not full puppeteer): open/goto/close, run JS in tab, click/type/fill/select/press by CSS or aria ref, scroll, screenshot (file path returned), accessibility-tree snapshot with stable element refs, wait_for (selector/url/function), network idle wait.
- Tabs survive across tool calls within a session (tab registry keyed by name); killed at session shutdown with process-tree discipline.
- Stealth: user-agent/locale/timezone normalization options; document that stealth parity with omp's patched puppeteer is NOT claimed in v1.
- Safety: downloads disabled by default; navigation domain allowlist option; no cookie/profile persistence unless configured.

## Acceptance

1. With feature enabled: open a local fixture page, snapshot a11y tree, click a ref, fill a form, screenshot to a file, evaluate JS returning a value — full loop.
2. CDP attach to a manually launched Chromium works.
3. Session shutdown leaves no chromium processes.
4. Default release build WITHOUT the feature stays within size budget (measure + record artifact).

## Tests

- e2e behind a local fixture HTTP server (no external network): navigation, form flow, screenshot bytes non-empty.
- Unit: ref stability across snapshots, action error taxonomy, tab lifecycle.
- CI gate: feature-off build size check remains green.

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add computer tool: desktop windows, screenshots, input, AX tree (opt-in)
description:
## Why / omp reference

omp's computer runs against the real host desktop: enumerate windows/displays, capture screenshots, send native input, walk the OS accessibility tree, touch the clipboard — 'Not the browser tool, no DOM — the same desktop you're looking at.' Evidence: omp:packages/coding-agent/src/tools/computer.ts + tools/computer/ + crates/pi-natives desktop/ (10.6k LoC: xcap, enigo, OS AX FFI), clipboard via arboard; spec: omp:docs/tools/computer.md.

## Current Pi state

Nothing. Same crates omp uses (xcap/enigo/arboard) are available to us directly — no N-API layer needed.

## Design

- Cargo feature `computer` (non-default). New modules: src/computer.rs + src/computer/ (windows, input, ax, clipboard).
- Surface: list windows/displays; screenshot (display or window → PNG path); mouse move/click/drag; key type/press; clipboard read/write text (+image read where arboard supports); AX tree dump per window (macOS AX FFI first; Linux AT-SPI best-effort; Windows UI Automation later — document tier matrix).
- Safety: this tool can act on the REAL desktop — default-deny via tool approval gate (every mutating action requires approval unless --yolo-class flag), audit-log every action with timestamp + target window.
- Platform tiers documented honestly: macOS full, Linux partial (X11 first, Wayland screenshot/input caveats), Windows screenshot/clipboard first.

## Acceptance

1. Feature-enabled: enumerate displays + windows on the dev host; screenshot produces a valid PNG; clipboard round-trip works.
2. Mutating input action triggers the approval gate by default (e2e proves prompt path).
3. Audit log records each action.
4. Feature-off build unaffected in size/startup.

## Tests

- Unit: window enumeration parsing, AX tree serialization, approval-gate wiring.
- e2e (macOS CI where available, else manual verification doc): screenshot + clipboard.

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add security_scan tool: native review planning, SARIF, disposition tracking
description:
## Why / omp reference

omp's security_scan plans and runs native security reviews, emits SARIF, and supports import/compare/disposition of findings. Evidence: omp:packages/coding-agent/src/tools/security-scan.ts + security/; spec: omp:docs/tools/security_scan.md.

1. security_scan run on a fixture repo with seeded vulnerabilities produces SARIF with expected rule hits.

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add model roles: 10 routable roles with per-role model assignment and cycling
description:
## Why / omp reference

omp routes work by intent across ten roles: default (normal turns), smol (cheap subagent fan-out), slow (deep reasoning), plan (plan mode), commit (changelogs), vision, designer, task, advisor, tiny. Launch overrides --smol/--slow/--plan; Ctrl+P cycles the active role's configured models; /model assigns per role. Evidence: omp:packages/coding-agent/src/config/model-roles.ts, session/role-models.ts, README 'Sixty-plus providers' section.

## Current Pi state

Single active model: --provider/--model flags, defaultProvider/defaultModel settings, --models glob list for Ctrl+P cycling, /model selector, model fallback is startup-only (auto-select order), no roles. provider_metadata already tracks per-model input types (text/image) — the substrate roles need.

## Design

- Extend settings schema (src/config.rs): modelRoles: {default, smol, slow, plan, commit, vision, designer, task, advisor, tiny} each holding a provider/model selector; all optional except default (falls back to defaultProvider/defaultModel → built-in auto-select).
- CLI: --smol/--slow/--plan MODEL flags (extend src/cli.rs) mapping to roles.
- Subagent interplay: agents/*.md frontmatter may pin model: (today's documented 'child inherits parent provider/model' behavior becomes: agent-def model pin > task/smol role > default role). Update docs/agents documentation accordingly — this is a deliberate, documented behavior change, not a silent drift.
- Runtime resolution: a RoleModelResolver maps (role → provider/model) with per-role thinking-level defaults; consumers: agent loop (default), subagent tool (task/smol), future plan mode (plan), future advisor (advisor), future commit tooling (commit), inspect_image (vision).
- Ctrl+P cycles within the ACTIVE role's configured set; /model gains role targeting (/model advisor openai/gpt-5). Session entries record role→model changes (ModelChange entry gains optional role field — JSONL v3 is extensible; older readers ignore unknown fields, verify).
- Backward surface: existing --model/--provider map to the default role; single-model users see zero behavior change.

- AUTO SESSION TITLING (round-4): the tiny role powers automatic session naming — after the first user+assistant exchange, a tiny/smol call summarizes the task into a short title written to the SessionInfo name entry (manual /name always wins; titling is async, never blocks the turn, and degrades silently when no cheap role is configured). This is what makes --resume pickers and status lines readable. omp runs this via tiny-model clients incl. local tiny models (omp:src/tiny/, tiny-title-download-progress.ts); we reuse whatever the tiny/smol role resolves to — no bundled model in v1.

## Acceptance

1. Configure modelRoles.smol + .slow; --smol flag overrides; resolution returns the right provider/model per role (unit matrix over precedence: CLI > project > global > default).
2. Subagent tool uses the task role (or smol when task unset) — proven by e2e with a recording stub provider.
3. /model advisor <m> persists for the session; Ctrl+P cycles within role scope only.
4. Session JSONL with role-tagged ModelChange replays identically; legacy sessions without roles load unchanged.

## Tests

- Unit: resolver precedence matrix, glob cycling per role, legacy session replay.
- Conformance: session fixture with role changes; RPC set_model role variants.

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add background bash jobs with completion delivery into the session
description:
## Why / omp reference

omp runs async bash/task background jobs whose completion is DELIVERED INTO the session's yield queue — the agent continues working and gets notified when the job settles, with output attached. Evidence: omp:packages/coding-agent/src/async/job-manager.ts (+ hub jobs surface for wait/cancel/snapshot).

## Current Pi state

bash is strictly synchronous (bounded by timeout). Nothing can outlive a tool call. The steering/follow-up queue infrastructure (src/agent.rs:796-940) is the delivery channel a completion notice needs.

## Design

- bash gains {background: true} → returns immediately with a job id; process runs under the same timeout/tree-kill discipline (longer default ceiling, configurable); output streams to a rolling artifact file (existing spillover).
- Job manager (in src/tools.rs or a small src/jobs.rs — small enough to justify tools.rs adjacency): registry {id, command, started, status, pid}; completion pushes a follow-up-queue message summarizing exit/status + tail output + artifact path, so the agent sees it next turn boundary.
- bash_jobs action (or jobs tool): list/wait/cancel; cancel uses the exact bash timeout escalation (TERM → grace → KILL + tree walk).
- Session survival: jobs are session-scoped; on session exit, running jobs are killed (documented) — no orphan daemons across restarts.
- Guards: max concurrent jobs (default 8), per-job output caps, clear tool-result schema pi.bash_job.v1.

- UNIFIED SURFACE (polish round 2): per the decision in bd-cv653.5.4, the jobs registry/list/wait/cancel surface lives under the single `hub` tool's `jobs` action group (alongside messaging + processes). The bash {background:true} spawn point stays in the bash tool; only the management surface consolidates. Update tool descriptions so agents discover background jobs via hub, not a separate jobs tool.

## Acceptance

1. background sleep+echo job: tool returns id instantly; completion notice arrives in the next-turn queue with output tail (RPC golden).
2. cancel mid-run kills the whole tree (fixture with a child-spawning script; assert no survivors).
3. Session exit with 2 running jobs → zero surviving processes.
4. Concurrency cap rejects the 9th job with a named error.

## Tests

- Unit: registry, queue injection, cap, cancel escalation.
- e2e_rpc: full background lifecycle golden.
- Soak: 200 rapid short jobs leave no zombies (reuse e2e_soak patterns).

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- Unit + e2e tests for this bead emit structured JSONL logs per the repo harness pattern (tests/common/logging.rs): per-case events, correlation ids, redacted payloads, artifact paths.
- e2e ships as a script under scripts/e2e/ registered in scripts/e2e/run_all.sh (focused + ci profiles); live-network lanes separate and gated.
- Failures must be diagnosable from logs alone: log tool inputs, decisions, and error taxonomy codes.
close_reason: Background bash jobs shipped. (1) bash {background:true} returns instantly with a job id (pi.bash_job.v1 details); detached process under the same timeout/tree-kill discipline (30min default ceiling, 0 disables); output streams to a rolling artifact file + 64KiB tail ring; mediation gate still classifies before spawn (background honors block/warn). (2) jobs tool (list/wait/cancel) in the default tool set; cancel uses TERM->grace->KILL tree escalation. (3) Completion notices drain through an additive follow-up fetcher registered on all three agent surfaces (agent/interactive/rpc); agent sees settle + output tail at the next turn boundary. (4) Session exit kills every running job (main shutdown chokepoint) - no orphan daemons. (5) Guards: 8-job concurrency cap with named PI_JOBS_AT_CAPACITY refusal as is_error tool result; PI_JOBS_UNKNOWN_ID/PI_JOBS_NOT_RUNNING named errors. Acceptance proven: instant start + notice tail (background_returns), tree-kill cancel with grandchild proof (cancel_kills_whole_tree), session-exit zero survivors (session_exit_kills_all_survivors), 9th-job refusal (capacity_rejects_ninth_job), registry default exposure + background-through-registry lanes. 5 lib + 6 integration tests pass; 259 tools lib + 127 mediation tests green; clippy/fmt/UBS-delta clean; e2e lane scripts/e2e/run_jobs.sh; jobs+bash_mediation registered in suite_classification.toml. Note: management surface lives in the jobs tool; the future hub tool (bd-cv653.5.4) wraps this same registry with zero rework.

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add /review command: prioritized parallel code review with ship verdict
description:
## Why / omp reference (REVIEW GAP — missed in first pass)

omp feature 10: '/review spawns dedicated reviewer subagents that sweep branches, single commits, or uncommitted work in parallel. Get a clear verdict on whether the change ships, with every issue ranked P0 through P3 and scored for confidence.' Evidence: omp README feature 10 (+ reviewer prompt machinery under packages/coding-agent).

## Current Pi state

Nothing. Users hand-roll 'review my diff' prompts with no structure, no parallelism, no verdict.

## Design

DEPENDS ON: F5.yields (typed results — findings must be schema-valid).
- /review [target]: target = uncommitted (default) | branch vs merge-base | commit range | pr://N (via F6.urls when available). Diff acquisition via git CLI (numstat → per-file diffs → hunk splitting; lockfiles/minified/generated excluded by default).
- Partitioning: group hunks into review units by file/module with size caps; fan out reviewer subagents (smol role when F3.roles lands, else default) with a rubric prompt (correctness, security, perf, contract drift); each returns typed findings {severity P0-P3, confidence, file, line-range, title, rationale, suggestion}.
- Aggregation: dedupe (same file+overlapping range+similar title), rank by (severity, confidence), cap to top-K with 'and N more' — the verdict card (SHIP | SHIP-WITH-NITS | BLOCK) from the worst unaddressed severity at confidence ≥ threshold.
- Surfaces: TUI verdict card with navigable findings; pi review --format json (pi.review.v1) with --fail-on P0|P1 for CI gating; findings optionally written to a markdown report.
- Cost guard: unit-count cap + token budget; oversized diffs get a file-triage pass first (smol model picks suspicious files).

## Acceptance

1. Seeded-bug fixture branch: the planted P0 (e.g. SQL injection) appears in top findings with correct file/line.
2. Typed findings validate against the schema (strict mode).
3. --fail-on P0 exits non-zero on the fixture; clean fixture passes.
4. Verdict card renders in TUI e2e; JSON schema stable across runs.

## Tests

- Unit: partitioner, dedupe, ranking, verdict FSM, budget caps.
- Conformance: findings schema fixtures; golden reports (normalized).
- e2e: scratch-repo review end-to-end with stub providers; JSONL logs per logging.rs; wired into scripts/e2e profiles.

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add multi-root workspace support (--add-dir, /add-dir, per-root confinement)
description:
## Why / omp reference (REVIEW GAP — missed in first pass)

omp supports multi-root sessions: --add-dir at launch, /add-dir + /remove-dir mid-session; tools operate across the union of roots. Evidence: omp:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/args.ts (--add-dir), slash-commands/builtin-lifecycle.ts (/add-dir /remove-dir), docs/session-operations-export-share-fork-resume.md.
