- Session gains additional_roots[] (recorded in session header/custom entries for resume fidelity); --add-dir DIR (repeatable) at launch; /add-dir /remove-dir slash commands mid-session with TUI confirmation.
- Path resolution: tools resolve relative paths against the primary root; absolute paths allowed iff inside ANY root (fail-closed outside all roots, same policy as extension FS connector — unify the checks in one helper so tool and extension confinement can't drift).

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add file-mutation recording with /undo and /redo (edit rollback)
description:
## Why / omp reference (REVIEW GAP — missed in first pass)

omp records file mutations (tools/file-recorder.ts) so agent edits can be rolled back — the safety net that makes unattended runs acceptable. Nothing in pi lets a user say 'undo that edit' short of git.

## Current Pi state

edit has a before_persist_hook (used for policy), sessions are trees (conversation-level branching), but file CONTENT history is not recorded. Session tmp dirs + retention classes (session_scoped_temp_evidence) exist for artifacts.

## Design

- Mutation recorder in the tool-execution path: before each successful write/edit/hashline_edit, snapshot affected files into a content-addressed store under the session tmp dir (dedup by content hash; bounded bytes with LRU eviction + notice); each mutation unit = one tool call (multi-file writes undo as ONE unit).
- /undo [n] restores the last n mutation units newest-first after a confirm card showing the condensed diff; /redo re-applies. Both recorded as session Custom entries (audit + replay).
- Interaction: mutations by USER or external processes are not recorded (only tool-path mutations); if a file changed externally since the snapshot, /undo warns and requires explicit confirm; git-tracked files note their index state in the record for operator context.
- Retention: store dies with the session tmp lifecycle; undo history survives compaction (session entries), not process restarts (documented; git remains the durable layer).
- Composition: F5.isolation's apply step records a mutation unit too (undo can reverse a subagent patch application).

- GENERATED-FILE GUARD (round-6, omp auto-generated-guard.ts parity): write/edit/hashline_edit refuse (with override flag) files detected as machine-generated — first-1KB/40-line header scan for @generated, protoc/sqlc/buf/swagger/openapi/k8s-codegen marker patterns (strict patterns; broad /auto-generated/ matches cause false positives and are banned); the refusal message names the generator and suggests editing the source schema instead. Overrides logged.

## Acceptance

1. edit → /undo restores exact prior bytes (hash-verified); /redo re-applies.
2. Multi-file write undoes atomically as one unit.
3. Externally-modified file → /undo warns, requires confirm, never silently clobbers.
4. Store bound enforced: oldest snapshots evicted with a visible notice; no unbounded growth.

## Tests

- Unit: snapshot/restore, content-hash dedupe, unit grouping, external-change detection, LRU eviction.
- Conformance: undo/redo transcript fixtures.
- e2e: TUI flow (edit, /undo, confirm card) with JSONL logs per logging.rs.

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- Unit + e2e tests for this bead emit structured JSONL logs per the repo harness pattern (tests/common/logging.rs): per-case events, correlation ids, redacted payloads, artifact paths.
- e2e ships as a script under scripts/e2e/ registered in scripts/e2e/run_all.sh (focused + ci profiles); live-network lanes separate and gated.
- Failures must be diagnosable from logs alone: log tool inputs, decisions, and error taxonomy codes.

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add pi commit: dependency-ordered atomic commit splitting
description:
## Why / omp reference (ROUND-4 GAP)

omp feature 16: 'omp reads the working tree through git_overview, git_file_diff, and git_hunk, then splits unrelated changes into atomic commits ordered by their dependencies. Cycles are rejected before anything is written. Source files score above tests, docs, and configs, so the headline commit is the one that matters. Lock files are excluded from analysis entirely.' Evidence: omp README feature 16; omp:packages/coding-agent/src/cli-commands.ts (commit), commit machinery.

## Current Pi state

Nothing. Agents stage/commit via bash with whatever grouping the model improvises; multi-agent repos (like this one) accumulate tangled mega-commits.

## Design

- `pi commit [-n|--dry-run] [--all]`: pipeline = git status/diff acquisition (porcelain v2 + per-file diffs + hunk splitting; lockfiles/minified/generated EXCLUDED by default) → semantic partition (LLM, commit role when F3.roles lands, else default model) groups hunks into atomic units by topic/coupling → dependency ordering (a hunk that references symbols from another unit's files sorts after it; import/reference graph between candidate units) → cycle check (reject + fall back to coarser grouping, never write a cyclic plan) → commit plan card for user approval (per-unit message + files; edit/regroup/skip) → sequential execution (git add -p-class hunk staging via git apply --cached), each commit message conventional-format with the bead/issue ref when derivable.
- Message quality: headline commit = the highest-scoring unit (source > tests > docs > config scoring); bodies reference rationale from the conversation when in-session.
- Safety: refuses on detached HEAD without --force; never commits files with unresolved conflict markers; pre-commit hooks run as usual; --dry-run prints the full plan only. Staging area must start clean-ish (mixed staged+unstaged gets an explicit resolution step: staged content forms its own unit).
- Non-goals: no history rewriting, no push (user runs it).

## Acceptance

1. Fixture repo with two unrelated changes interleaved across files: pi commit produces two commits in dependency order, each compiling (fixture proves), messages topical.
2. Cyclic candidate plan → rejected with explanation + coarser fallback proposed; nothing written.
3. Lockfile-only change excluded from analysis (reported, committed only via explicit --include-lockfiles).
4. --dry-run writes nothing (git diff --cached empty before/after).
5. Conflict-marker file → refusal naming the file.

## Tests

- Unit: partition invariants, ordering topo-sort, cycle rejection, scoring order, staging-area FSM.
- Conformance: golden commit plans over fixture trees (normalized SHAs).
- e2e: scratch-repo full runs with JSONL logs per logging.rs; registered in scripts/e2e profiles.

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- Unit + e2e tests for this bead emit structured JSONL logs per the repo harness pattern (tests/common/logging.rs): per-case events, correlation ids, redacted payloads, artifact paths.
- e2e ships as a script under scripts/e2e/ registered in scripts/e2e/run_all.sh (focused + ci profiles); live-network lanes separate and gated.
- Failures must be diagnosable from logs alone: log tool inputs, decisions, and error taxonomy codes.

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add turn recovery: unexpected-stop classifier + mid-turn resume
description:
## Why / omp reference (ROUND-4 GAP)

omp classifies unexpected stops and recovers: a model that stops mid-task (stop_reason=stop with real content but task clearly unfinished, wedged stream, truncated tool-call JSON) gets classified (heuristics + a tiny-model one-word classifier with a reasoning-safe token budget, issue #4355) and the turn is resumed/continued instead of silently ending. Evidence: omp:packages/coding-agent/src/session/unexpected-stop-classifier.ts, turn-recovery.ts (90KB), codex-auto-reset.ts; prompts/system/unexpected-stop-classifier.md.

## Current Pi state

A clean stop is a clean stop: if the model ends the turn mid-task, the agent halts; user must nudge. Auto-retry exists for transport errors (RetrySettings) but NOT for semantic mid-task stops. The steering queue can inject 'continue' manually only.

## Design

- Stop classification at TurnEnd: signals = stop_reason, trailing content shape (unclosed fence/tool JSON/code block), pending tool expectations, task-completion heuristics (last assistant message ends mid-list, promised 'I will now...' with no follow-through), token-budget exhaustion (max_tokens hit). Heuristic classifier first (deterministic, zero cost); ambiguous cases escalate to the tiny/cheap classifier (F3.roles tiny role when available, else smol, else default — resolve via RoleModelResolver; reasoning-safe max_tokens per omp's lesson).
- Recovery actions by class: budget-truncated → auto-continue ('continue from exactly where you stopped' system nudge, preserving the partial message as prefix); wedged/transport → failover path if F3.failover configured, else retry with backoff; semantic-premature-stop → one auto-continue nudge. CAP: max 2 auto-continuations per turn (then ask the user — never infinite-loop).
- All classifications + actions logged as session Custom entries (pi.turn_recovery.v1) with the classifier's rationale; TUI shows a subtle 'auto-continued (reason)' marker in the transcript.
- OFF switch: recovery.autoContinue: off|conservative|aggressive (default conservative = only budget-truncation + unclosed-tool-call auto-continue).

## Acceptance

1. Fixture: stub provider emits max_tokens-truncated reply mid-code-block → agent auto-continues and completes; transcript marker present; session entry logged.
2. Fixture: model says 'I will now edit 3 files' then stops → classifier flags; one nudge; no third nudge (cap proven).
3. Clean completed turn → zero classifier cost (heuristic short-circuit, no extra call).
4. aggressive vs conservative modes differ exactly on the semantic class (matrix test).
5. Composition: a mid-recovery provider 429 engages failover, not a second nudge (event-order assertion).

## Tests

- Unit: signal extraction, heuristic classifier matrix, cap FSM, mode matrix, session-entry schema.
- Conformance: transcript fixtures per recovery class.
- e2e: scripted stub providers through RPC with JSONL logs; scripts/e2e registration.

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- e2e ships as a script under scripts/e2e/ registered in scripts/e2e/run_all.sh (focused + ci profiles); live-network lanes separate and gated.
- Failures must be diagnosable from logs alone: log tool inputs, decisions, and error taxonomy codes.

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add /btw ephemeral side questions and /tan background tangential agents
description:
## Why / omp reference (ROUND-4 GAP)

omp has two side-channel commands: `/btw <question>` — 'Ask an ephemeral side question using the current session context' (answer briefly, NEVER use tools, NEVER ask follow-ups; the exchange never enters the session transcript) — and `/tan <work>` — 'Run a full background agent on tangential work' (a background subagent whose completion reports into the session via a background-tan message). Evidence: omp:packages/coding-agent/src/slash-commands/builtin-lifecycle.ts:238+, modes/controllers/btw-controller.ts, components/btw-panel.ts, background-tan-message.ts, prompts/system/btw-user.md.

## Current Pi state

Neither exists. Every question costs main-context tokens; every side task derails the current turn or needs a manual subagent call.

## Design

- /btw <question>: sends [compact context summary + question] to the smol/tiny role (F3.roles) with a strict no-tools/no-followups system contract (port omp's btw-user.md semantics); the answer renders in an above-composer panel (F9 overlay host when available; interim transcript card marked ephemeral) and is NEVER written to the session JSONL — guaranteed by construction (the call builds its own throwaway message list, shares nothing with the session writer). --print mode: pi --btw 'q'? No — interactive-only, document that.
- /tan <work>: spawns a background child agent (subagent machinery, task role) on the tangential work in the CURRENT directory (respecting F5.isolation policy if configured); completion delivers a summary message into the follow-up queue (same delivery as F3.bgjobs completions) rendered as a distinct tan card. Roster/hub visibility per F5.hub.
- Guards: /btw refuses empty questions; /tan requires the subagent tool enabled (it inherits its gating); tan children appear in the hub roster with kind=tan.
- Both commands get slash-completion entries + docs.

## Acceptance

1. /btw mid-task: answer arrives in the panel; session file contains ZERO trace of the exchange (byte-diff proof); context tokens unchanged for the next main turn.
2. /tan 'update the changelog' while main work continues: completion message appears at the next turn boundary with the child's summary; roster showed the tan child while running.
3. /btw with tools attempted by the model → the no-tools contract holds (no tool executions possible; the call path has no tool registry attached).
4. Empty /btw → usage error, no provider call.

## Tests

- Unit: throwaway-context construction (isolation proof), role resolution, queue delivery shape.
- Conformance: slash parsing fixtures.

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add pi handoff: structured cross-session/cross-agent handoff generator
description:
## Why / omp reference (ROUND-6; un-defers an epic deferral)

omp generates handoff documents (session-handoff.ts + docs/handoff-generation-pipeline.md): a structured brief for WHOEVER continues next. The epic originally deferred this as 'adjacent to context-preview'; wrong call — this repo's workflow is multi-agent (Agent Mail threads, beads, swarm runpacks), and handoff is the missing artifact: compaction continues YOURSELF; handoff briefs SOMEONE ELSE.

## Current Pi state

Closest: compaction summaries (same session, model-facing), context-preview semantic bundles (code-facing), /share (human HTML). Nothing produces a structured continuation brief.

## Design

- `pi handoff [--to agent|human|bead] [--out PATH]` + /handoff slash: analyzes the session (goal, decisions, current state, open threads, failed approaches + WHY they failed, files touched with roles, blockers, next steps) → structured markdown + pi.handoff.v1 JSON sidecar.
- Content rules: failure memory first-class; every claim carries file:line or session-entry refs; open questions explicit; secrets redacted via the .7.9 detector.
- Integrations: --to bead appends the handoff as a br note on a bead id (uses br CLI, never writes .beads directly); --to agent posts to an Agent Mail thread (thread_id = bead id per AGENTS.md); default prints/saves. We READ our session and CALL external tools — never mutate their internals.

Where present: offer `cm playbook add`-format lesson export from the lessons section; link the handoff to the source session's cass record. Never reimplement cass/cm inside pi.
- Compaction-aware: sources include compaction summaries + post-compaction entries.
- Cost: one default-role call, budget-capped; --cheap uses smol role.

## Acceptance

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add compaction modes: shake (heavy tool-result dropping), aggressive, interactive
description:
## Why / omp reference (ROUND-6 GAP)

omp has multiple compaction modes (compact-modes.ts, compaction/shake): 'shake' drops heavy tool results while KEEPING messages — a cheap, instant, no-LLM-call reclaim (often 30-60% when reads/bash outputs dominate). pi has one mode (LLM summarization) and pays its latency/cost even when dropping three 2000-line file reads would do.

## Current Pi state

src/compaction.rs: single mode (cut point + LLM summary + Compaction entry); threshold auto trigger; /compact manual.

## Design

- Modes: summary (current), shake (drop bulky tool RESULT payloads older than keep-recent, one-line stubs '[read src/foo.rs — 1842 lines, dropped; re-read if needed]' preserving tool-call/result adjacency structurally), aggressive (summary + shake + tighter keep_recent), interactive (/compact picker with per-mode projected reclaim).
- Auto policy: compaction.mode: shake-first|summary|aggressive — shake-first escalates only when shake reclaim < required.
- Invariants: adjacency never broken (stub keeps the entry); cut-point rules unchanged; shake marker entry so replay is exact; token accounting via F7.bpe when landed.
- UX: /compact --shake|--aggressive + picker; TUI toast with reclaimed tokens + mode; RPC compact gains mode field.

## Acceptance

1. Tool-heavy fixture: shake reclaims within 5% of projection, zero LLM calls, adjacency intact (replay validation).
2. shake-first: small pressure shakes; high pressure escalates (fixture pair).
3. Shaken-session replay produces identical agent context (golden).
4. Picker projections accurate; cancel leaves session untouched.

## Tests

- Unit: shake eligibility, adjacency proptest, reclaim accounting, escalation FSM.
- Conformance: shake-marker fixtures replay identically.
- e2e: long-session fixture via RPC; JSONL logs; scripts/e2e registration.

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add fallback chains, round-robin credentials, and path-scoped models
description:
## Why / omp reference

omp: 'When the primary throws 429s or hits a quota wall, the next entry takes the rest of the turn — restored on cooldown.' Plus round-robin API keys with session affinity + per-credential backoff, and path:-scoped enabledModels/disabledProviders to pin model sets per repo. Evidence: omp:packages/coding-agent/src/session/retry-fallback-chains.ts, config/model-registry.ts (84KB), model-resolver.ts (80KB), credential-pin.ts.

## Current Pi state

Same-provider retry exists (RetrySettings with backoff; RPC auto-retry events). Cross-model failover: NONE (src/model_routing.rs is explicitly advisory, 'does not change the live provider invocation path'). Single credential per provider. enabledModels is global-only.

## Design

- settings: retry.fallbackChains: {role-or-model → [provider/model, ...]}; on classified transient failures (429, quota, 5xx-after-retries, overload) the NEXT chain entry continues the turn; cooldown timer restores primary; failure classification must NOT fail over on 4xx auth errors (those are loud).
- Credentials: providers accept a LIST of keys (env list syntax + auth.json arrays); runtime rotates with session affinity (stable per session-id hash) and per-credential exponential backoff on 429.
- Path scoping: enabledModels/disabledProviders entries may carry path: prefix; resolution walks cwd ancestors, most specific wins. Reuse SettingsScope machinery.
- Events: emit RPC/TUI events on failover (provider switch notice) so the user sees it; session logs a Custom entry for audit.
- Invariants: failover preserves the message history byte-for-byte (providers differ in wire format, our Provider trait already normalizes); max chain depth = chain length; total turn failover cap to bound cost.

- CAAM COMPOSITION (flywheel): the owner's caam does ACCOUNT-level switching for CLI subscriptions externally; this bead's round-robin handles KEY-level rotation inside pi. Documented boundary: caam swaps which ACCOUNT the environment presents; we rotate across the KEYS we're given. Never shell out to caam from the hot path.

## Acceptance

1. Fixture: primary stub provider 429s twice → chain entry #2 completes the turn; cooldown restores primary next session (deterministic clock in tests).
2. Auth 401 does NOT fail over — loud error.
3. Two keys on one provider rotate across sessions with affinity within a session; per-key backoff honored.
4. path:-scoped config pins repo A to model X while repo B uses global default.

## Tests

- Unit: chain walk, classification matrix, cooldown FSM, credential rotation/affinity, path-scope resolution.
- e2e: scripted stub providers (429→success) via RPC mode; event assertions.
- Conformance: settings fixtures for chain + path-scope parsing and precedence.

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- Unit + e2e tests for this bead emit structured JSONL logs per the repo harness pattern (tests/common/logging.rs): per-case events, correlation ids, redacted payloads, artifact paths.
- e2e ships as a script under scripts/e2e/ registered in scripts/e2e/run_all.sh (focused + ci profiles); live-network lanes separate and gated.
- Failures must be diagnosable from logs alone: log tool inputs, decisions, and error taxonomy codes.
close_reason: Cross-model failover landed for RPC + print modes: fallback chains (retry.fallbackChains, role-or-exact-model keys), failure classification (quota/overload/transient fail over; 401/403/auth NEVER), cooldown FSM (300s default, restores primary on next prompt via maybe_restore_primary), per-turn cap (8), FailoverStart/FailoverEnd events, session Custom+ModelChange audit entries, incomplete-response revert before resume (#125 semantics preserved). Credential rotation: OPENAI_API_KEYS-style plural env vars (2+ keys) via process-global CredentialRing (affinity by auth-path+provider hash, per-key exponential backoff on 429 reported from both retry paths; keys re-resolved per retry attempt so backed-off keys rotate). Path scoping: disabledProviders + modelScopeOverrides (longest-prefix wins) filter the scoped pool and interactive available models. Evidence: full lib 7210/7210; e2e 119/119 — (1) 429 -> chain completes on backup, (2) 401 never fails over, (3) 429 on k-aaa -> retry carries k-bbb, (4) path-scope pins repo A scoped / repo B global; unit matrix for classify/chain/cooldown/ring/scope/disabled/config-parse/rotation-wiring; clippy -D pedantic clean; JSONL logs per logging.rs. NOT covered (documented): interactive TUI has no retry loop so failover doesn't fire there yet (needs its own seam — follow-up-worthy); auth.json key ARRAYS (env-list only in v1); cooldown restore is process-scoped (per RPC session); per-credential backoff is in-memory. Verification honesty: final e2e re-run after warning-only lint refactors was blocked by host disk 100% full (ENOSPC); e2e evidence predates only behavior-preserving lint edits (const fn, is_none_or, doc splits, if/else swap re-verified by full-lib 7210/7210).

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add advisor role: second model reviewing every turn with inline notes
description:
## Why / omp reference

omp's advisor: 'Pair a reviewer model to the advisor role and it reads every turn the main agent takes, injecting notes inline — a quiet aside, a concern, or a hard blocker. It runs on its own context and its own model, so it catches what the doer rushed past.' Evidence: omp:packages/coding-agent/src/advisor/ (runtime.ts 68KB, watchdog, emission-guard, advise-tool); README feature 06.

## Current Pi state

Nothing comparable. Steering queues and tool-approval hooks exist; extension events (turn_end, tool_execution_end) give the hook points an advisor needs.

## Design

DEPENDS ON: F3.roles (advisor role must resolve a model).
- New module (justified): src/advisor.rs. After each agent turn (or N tool executions), if advisor role configured: send a compacted turn digest (diffs touched, commands run, errors, final message — budget-capped) to the advisor model with a review rubric prompt.
- Advisor returns structured verdict: note | concern | blocker (+ rationale, file refs). note/concern inject as system-reminder messages into the next turn context; blocker pauses before further tool execution and requests user/advisor resolution via the approval surface.
- Emission guard: rate-limit (max notes per K turns), dedupe repeated concerns, suppress when the turn is trivial (no tool calls). Watchdog: advisor call has hard timeout + failure isolation — advisor errors NEVER fail the main turn (log + disable-after-N-failures with user notice).
- TUI: advisor notes render as distinct amber cards; /advisor status|pause|resume|model controls. RPC/ACP: advisor_note events.
- Cost guard: advisor tokens tracked separately in footer/usage.

- STACK LAYERING (round-3): advisor note/concern/blocker rendering goes through the transcript card registry's advisor card hook (bd-cv653.9.2 carries the fixture-level card already) — this bead emits the structured verdict events; painting is the registry's job. No bespoke TUI drawing in this bead, so the F9 migration touches it zero times.

## Acceptance

1. With advisor configured (stub provider), a scripted risky turn (broad except-catch fix) yields a concern card injected into next-turn context.
2. Advisor timeout/failure leaves the main turn unaffected (fault-injection e2e).
3. Blocker verdict pauses tool execution until resolved.
4. Advisor disabled = zero overhead (no digest construction).

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add TTSR: time-traveling stream rules with mid-stream abort and injection
description:
## Why / omp reference

omp TTSR: 'Your rules sit dormant until the model goes off-script. A regex match aborts the stream mid-token, injects the rule as a system reminder, and retries from the same point. Course-correction without paying context tax on every turn. Injections survive compaction, so the fix sticks.' /omfg forges a rule from a user complaint. Evidence: omp:packages/coding-agent/src/session/ttsr-coordinator.ts, modes/controllers/omfg-*, cli/ttsr-cli.ts; spec: omp:docs/ttsr-injection-lifecycle.md.

## Current Pi state

Nothing. Stream pipeline (src/sse.rs + agent loop stream consumption) is the injection point; compaction (src/compaction.rs) must learn to preserve injections.

## Design

- New module (justified): src/stream_rules.rs. Rule store: per-project .pi/stream-rules.json + global; rule = {id, name, pattern (regex), body, enabled, created_from}.
- Match loop: streaming text deltas pass a rolling-window matcher (bounded lookback, e.g. last 4KB, crate regex-on-stream); on match: abort the in-flight request (provider stream cancel), append a system-reminder message containing the rule body + the offending excerpt, and re-issue the turn from the same conversation state.
- Guards: max N injections per turn (default 3) then surface to user instead of looping; per-rule cooldown within a session; never match inside tool-call argument JSON (only assistant text/thinking channels) to avoid corrupting tool calls.
- Compaction survival: injections recorded as dedicated session entries (Custom type) and included in compaction summaries' preserved-constraint section; compaction quality harness gains a stream-rule marker kind.
- UX: TUI amber 'Injecting rule: <name>' card on abort; /rules list|add|remove|test CLI + slash surface; /omfg <complaint> drafts a rule via the default model for user approval.

- Failover interaction: a TTSR abort is a DELIBERATE local retry, never a provider failure — it must not trip the F3.failover chain classifier or consume retry budget; conversely a real provider error mid-stream follows failover, not TTSR. Encode this in the event taxonomy (distinct abort reasons).
- Prompt-cache economics: the retry re-issues the SAME message prefix plus the appended reminder, so provider prompt caches stay valid; note the cache-aware ordering (reminder appended, never inserted mid-history) as a design requirement, not an accident.
- Scriptable surface: `pi rules` subcommand (list/add/remove/test/export) mirrors the slash commands so rule sets are shareable across repos and reviewable in CI.

- GRIEVANCES LOG (round-4): port omp's grievances concept — user complaints given to /omfg are recorded in a per-project grievances ledger (JSONL, redacted) so recurring pain is visible across sessions; /omfg can forge a candidate rule from a grievance, and `pi grievances` lists them. This closes the loop between 'the model keeps doing X wrong' and a durable stream rule.

## Acceptance

1. Fixture rule 'Box::leak' + stub provider streaming that text → abort event fires, rule injected, retry completes without the pattern.
2. Injection cap: a stubborn stub re-triggering the rule 3x → user-visible stop, no infinite loop.
3. Compaction after an injection preserves the rule constraint in the summary (compaction harness assertion).
4. Tool-call argument streams never trigger matches (fixture with pattern text inside a write tool call payload streams through).

## Tests

- Unit: rolling matcher (split matches across chunk boundaries), abort/retry FSM, injection cap, cooldown.
- e2e: scripted stub provider stream with chunk-split pattern; assert retry transcript.
- Conformance: session entries for injections replay; compaction fixture with survival marker.

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- Unit + e2e tests for this bead emit structured JSONL logs per the repo harness pattern (tests/common/logging.rs): per-case events, correlation ids, redacted payloads, artifact paths.
- e2e ships as a script under scripts/e2e/ registered in scripts/e2e/run_all.sh (focused + ci profiles); live-network lanes separate and gated.
- Failures must be diagnosable from logs alone: log tool inputs, decisions, and error taxonomy codes.
close_reason: Implemented Time-Traveling Stream Rules (TTSR) engine, rolling chunk boundary matcher, turn injection cap, cooldown history, stream rules store, grievances ledger, compaction survival, CLI rules/grievances commands, and /rules /omfg slash commands

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add plan mode: read-only planning with approval gate and plan role
description:
## Why / omp reference

omp plan mode: a read-only planning state — the agent may inspect but not mutate — producing an approved plan that hands off to execution, with its own plan model role and --plan-yolo escape. Evidence: omp:packages/coding-agent/src/plan-mode/ (approved-plan.ts, plan-handoff.ts, plan-protection.ts, model-transition.ts), tools/plan-mode-guard.ts.

## Current Pi state

No plan mode (only an SDK doc comment muses about read-only tool subsets). Tool effects bitflags (read/write/append/network/process with BARRIER) ALREADY classify every tool mutation capability (src/tools.rs:38-130) — the enforcement primitive exists.

## Design

DEPENDS ON: F3.roles (plan role).
- Session state: PlanMode {Off, Planning, Approved(plan)} toggled via /plan, --plan flag, or RPC set_plan_mode.
- Enforcement: while Planning, the tool-execution layer rejects any tool whose effects intersect BARRIER (write/append/process) with a structured 'plan mode: mutation blocked' tool error the model can read; read/grep/find/ls/lsp/web_search flow freely.
- Plan artifact: the agent ends planning by emitting a structured plan (markdown + step list); user reviews via TUI card (approve/edit/reject) or RPC approve_plan; on approval, state flips, plan becomes a pinned context document for execution turns, and the model may switch from plan role back to default role (model-transition).
- --plan-yolo / plan auto-approve setting for unattended runs; every transition logged as session entries (replay-safe).
- ACP: map to plan session mode; permission prompts for execution resumption.

## Acceptance

1. In plan mode, a write attempt returns the structured block error and zero bytes change (e2e with a scratch file).
2. Approve flow: plan card → approve → execution proceeds referencing the plan document in context.
3. Reject/edit loop keeps Planning state.
4. Session replay across plan transitions is deterministic (fixture).

## Tests

- Unit: effects-gate matrix (every built-in tool classified correctly), state machine transitions, session entry round-trip.
- e2e: TUI-less RPC plan flow (enter plan, attempt mutation, approve, execute).
- Conformance: plan-mode transcript fixtures.

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- Failures must be diagnosable from logs alone: log tool inputs, decisions, and error taxonomy codes.
close_reason: Plan mode shipped: read-only planning with approval gate. PlanState FSM (Off/Planning/PendingApproval/Approved) shared agent↔submit_plan; executor gate blocks BARRIER effects (write/append/process) with model-readable PLAN_MODE_BLOCKED, xdev run resolves INNER tool effects (read-only runs allowed); submit_plan captures plan (20+ chars) → PendingApproval; /plan [approve|reject|off|status] + RPC set_plan_mode/approve_plan/reject_plan; --plan-mode/--plan-yolo flags + plan.autoApprove (yolo auto-approves, plan rides back in tool result); plan-role model transition on entry + restore on approve; plan pinned into system prompt on approval; every transition a plan_mode Custom session entry. Evidence: plan.rs FSM unit matrix, executor gate e2e-in-lib (write blocked file-untouched, read flows, bash blocked, approve re-opens), xdev inner-effects test, session round-trip, TRUE RPC e2e (tests/e2e_plan_mode.rs: block→submit→approve→execute with PLAN_MODE_BLOCKED proven in the model's request body), full lib 7228/7228, clippy clean. title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add magic keywords: ultrathink, orchestrate, workflowz with safe matching
description:
## Why / omp reference

omp reserves three standalone lowercase words that opt a turn into specialized behavior: ultrathink (highest supported thinking effort), orchestrate (parallel subagents + per-phase verification), workflowz (deterministic multi-subagent workflow). They trigger ONLY in prose — never inside code spans, fenced blocks, XML/HTML sections, identifiers, or paths. Evidence: omp:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/magic-keywords.ts; spec: omp:docs/magic-keywords.md.

## Current Pi state

No keyword layer. Thinking levels exist (off..max) with per-model clamping (src/models.rs) — ultrathink maps onto max-clamped effort. Subagent tool exists for orchestrate/workflowz targets.

## Design

- New module: src/magic_keywords.rs. Pre-send scan of the user's message with a markdown/grammar-aware tokenizer: skip fenced code, inline code, XML/HTML tag sections, URLs/paths, identifiers adjacent to non-whitespace.
- Actions: ultrathink → set turn thinking level to the model's max supported (use clamp_thinking_level); orchestrate → inject an orchestration system directive instructing parallel task decomposition with verification phases; workflowz → inject the deterministic-workflow directive (staged waves, named nodes, barrier semantics matching our subagent chain/parallel shapes).
- Config: keywords individually disable-able; word list extensible via settings for future keywords.
- Telemetry: keyword activation logged in session Custom entries (auditability for 'why did thinking jump to max').

## Acceptance

1. 'please ultrathink this design' → turn runs at clamped-max thinking (asserted via stub provider payload).
2. '`ultrathink` in backticks' and fenced-code occurrences do NOT trigger (fixture matrix incl. XML sections and paths like /tmp/ultrathink).
3. orchestrate/workflowz inject the correct directives exactly once per turn.
4. Settings can disable each keyword.

## Tests

- Unit: tokenizer exclusion matrix (the make-or-break correctness surface), idempotent single-injection, thinking clamp integration.
- Conformance: message-scan goldens.
- e2e: RPC prompt with keyword → observed directive + thinking level in outbound request.

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- Unit + e2e tests for this bead emit structured JSONL logs per the repo harness pattern (tests/common/logging.rs): per-case events, correlation ids, redacted payloads, artifact paths.
- e2e ships as a script under scripts/e2e/ registered in scripts/e2e/run_all.sh (focused + ci profiles); live-network lanes separate and gated.
- Failures must be diagnosable from logs alone: log tool inputs, decisions, and error taxonomy codes.
close_reason: Magic keywords shipped. (1) src/magic_keywords.rs: grammar-aware tokenizer (fenced code, inline code, XML/HTML tag sections via depth tracking, paths/identifiers via boundary rules) — the make-or-break exclusion surface, unit-proven: prose triggers each keyword once per turn; backticks/fences/XML/paths/identifiers never trigger; punctuation boundaries (comma, parens, period) do trigger. (2) Actions: ultrathink sets the turn's thinking_level to Max (per-model clamp applies downstream, proven via capture provider); orchestrate/workflowz append their directives to the system prompt (appended never inserted — prompt-cache-safe), exactly once per turn; the session wrapper's per-turn system-prompt restore (set_system_prompt(base)) gives clean per-turn semantics with no leakage into later turns. (3) Config: keywords.{ultrathink,orchestrate,workflowz} toggles + keywords.extra [{word, directive}] for future keywords; wired through main/acp/sdk AgentConfig builds; merge chain updated. (4) Telemetry: activations recorded in an Agent keyword ledger, drained after each run by the session wrapper into session Custom entries (magic_keyword{word,action}) — same drain pattern as the dialect repair ledger; auditability for 'why did thinking jump to max'. (5) Acceptance: ultrathink→max proven with a capture provider; directives exactly once; settings disable each keyword; code/path/XML fixtures leave the request untouched; ledger drain verified. 7 unit + 5 integration tests; clippy/fmt/UBS-delta clean; scripts/e2e/run_magic_keywords.sh lane; magic_keywords in suite_classification.toml. title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add checkpoint/rewind tools and /fresh stream reset
description:
## Why / omp reference

omp's checkpoint marks conversation state for later collapse-and-report; rewind prunes exploratory context while keeping a concise report; /fresh resets provider stream state (stale prompt cache, wedged stream) without touching the local transcript. Evidence: omp:packages/coding-agent/src/tools/checkpoint.ts, slash-commands/builtin-lifecycle.ts; spec: omp:docs/tools/checkpoint.md, rewind.md, docs/session-operations-export-share-fork-resume.md#fresh.

## Current Pi state

Manual /compact + auto-compaction exist; nothing marks lightweight restore points or resets stream state. Session tree + labels (add_label) and branch summaries give us the primitives.

## Design

- checkpoint tool: marks the current leaf with a Checkpoint entry {name, token_estimate, note}; cheap (no summarization yet).
- rewind tool: collapses the span from a chosen checkpoint to now into a concise report (LLM-summarized, budget-capped), replacing that span in the ACTIVE context while the full span stays in the tree (nothing deleted — non-destructive by construction, consistent with our tree model).
- /fresh slash + RPC command: drops provider-side ephemeral state (new session id for providers that key caches, reset stream bookkeeping) while keeping the transcript untouched; log a SessionInfo entry.
- TUI: checkpoints listed in /tree view with names; rewind previews the report before applying (approve/cancel).

- /retry (round-4): re-issue the last user turn after a bad/stale response — implemented via the session tree (branch from the user message's parent and replay), so retry never destroys the original path. Works from TUI + RPC; composes with /fresh (fresh provider state, then retry).

- --max-time RUN CAP (round-4.5, omp --max-time parity): wall-clock cap for a run — the agent pauses politely at the NEXT TURN BOUNDARY with a clear 'time cap reached' state (never mid-tool-call), flushes session state, and exits 0 in print mode with a marker in output. For unattended/CI runs; distinct from --request-timeout (per-request) and --max-tool-iterations (per-turn count).

## Acceptance

1. checkpoint then 20 more turns then rewind to it: active context contains the report + post-checkpoint is summarized out; tree retains all original entries (replay proves).
2. /fresh clears wedged-stream state (fixture: poisoned stream cache key) with transcript byte-identical.
3. All three work via RPC + TUI.

## Tests

- Unit: checkpoint entry serde, span selection, report budgeting, fresh reset.
- e2e: scripted session through RPC performing the full mark→rewind cycle.
- Conformance: session fixtures containing checkpoints/rewinds replay identically.

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- Unit + e2e tests for this bead emit structured JSONL logs per the repo harness pattern (tests/common/logging.rs): per-case events, correlation ids, redacted payloads, artifact paths.
- e2e ships as a script under scripts/e2e/ registered in scripts/e2e/run_all.sh (focused + ci profiles); live-network lanes separate and gated.
- Failures must be diagnosable from logs alone: log tool inputs, decisions, and error taxonomy codes.
close_reason: Checkpoint/rewind/fresh/retry + --max-time shipped. (1) src/checkpoint.rs: checkpoint marks the current leaf with a Custom checkpoint entry {name, note, token_estimate, message_count} (cheap, no summarization); rewind finds by name-or-latest, summarizes the span via the compaction summarizer (budget-capped with the local fallback, rewind-specific report prompt), and collapses the span in ACTIVE context into one [REWIND REPORT] message while the append-only tree keeps every original entry (acceptance #1 proven: mark → 20 turns → rewind → active = foundation + report, tree intact). Keyless providers summarize without an API key. (2) /fresh: new provider session id + pi.fresh.v1 Custom entry; transcript byte-identical (acceptance #2 proven). (3) /retry: take_last_user_turn truncates the active context to just before the last user message and re-queues the text via the steering queue — the tree keeps the original path. (4) --max-time SECONDS: wall-clock cap checked at TURN BOUNDARIES only (never mid-tool-call); on expiry the run returns a '[time cap reached]' marker assistant message (SlowProvider infinite-stream fixture proves it). CLI flag + AgentConfig.max_time wired through main. (5) Surfaces: TUI slash /checkpoint /rewind /fresh /retry (async handlers mirroring the compact spawn pattern, keyless-tolerant); RPC checkpoint/rewind/fresh/retry commands over the JSON-line protocol with pi.checkpoint.v1/pi.fresh.v1/pi.retry.v1 shapes — the RPC cycle test drives the full mark→turn→rewind→fresh→retry sequence (acceptance #3). NOT in acceptance scope and skipped: /tree checkpoint listing, rewind approve/cancel preview. (6) Verification: 2 unit + 4 integration + 1 RPC cycle test green; session_store_v2 proptest failures under rch are the known rch TMPDIR leak (bd-tuw82) — they pass with TMPDIR=/tmp; clippy/fmt/UBS-delta clean; scripts/e2e/run_checkpoint.sh lane; checkpoint registered in suite_classification.toml. Incidental: ~15 AgentConfig literals across the suite gained max_time: None; conformance fixture unaffected.

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add ask tool: structured mid-turn option picker (TUI + ACP)
description:
## Why / omp reference

omp's ask: 'ambiguity routes through the ask tool — a structured option picker the agent can call mid-turn' with recommended-option badges, and 'The same prompt cards surface over ACP, so editors get the picker without writing one.' Evidence: omp:packages/coding-agent/src/tools/ask.ts (50KB); spec: omp:docs/tools/ask.md.

## Current Pi state

No structured question tool; the agent can only ask in prose. We DO have the approval/prompt plumbing (ToolApprovalHandler → TUI capability prompt + ACP session/request_permission with 120s timeout) to model this on.

## Design

- ask tool input: questions[] {id, question, header?, options[{label, description?}], recommended index?, multi?}; output: selected labels (or 'Other' free text) per question.
- TUI: option-picker overlay reusing the existing selector machinery (model selector/settings list patterns); keyboard nav, Enter select, Esc cancel; recommended badge.
- Print/JSON mode: non-interactive — ask returns the recommended option by default with a loud notice, or a configured policy (error | default | recommended) controls behavior.
- RPC: extension_ui_request-style frame (ask_request/ask_response) mirroring the capability-prompt flow; ACP maps to session/request_permission-style option prompt.
- Timeout + cancel → tool error result the model sees ('user dismissed the question').

- STACK LAYERING (polish round 2): keep the ask dialog LOGIC (question model, option validation, recommended index, policies) fully separated from rendering so F9.overlays (bd-cv653.9.8) can re-skin it onto the ftui overlay host mechanically. v1 builds on the current selector machinery; do NOT build TUI primitives inside this bead that F9 would then have to delete.

## Acceptance

1. TUI e2e: scripted keypresses answer an ask card; tool result carries the selection.
2. RPC: ask emits request frame; response resumes the turn (golden fixture).
3. Print mode with policy=recommended auto-answers and logs the choice.
4. Esc/cancel path yields the dismissal tool error, not a hang.

## Tests

- Unit: schema validation (2-5 options, recommended index bounds), policy resolution, timeout.
- e2e_tui + e2e_rpc goldens.
- Conformance: tool schema fixture.

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add todo tool: phased task list with TUI widget and RPC surface
description:
## Why / omp reference

omp's todo maintains the session task list: ordered mutations (init/start/done/drop/block/unblock/rm/append/view), phase tracking, auto-promotion of the next open task. Evidence: omp:packages/coding-agent/src/tools/todo.ts (47KB) + session/todo-tracker.ts; spec: omp:docs/tools/todo.md.

## Current Pi state

No todo tool or widget at all (verified: no TodoWrite/todo surfaces). Session Custom entries can persist the list; TUI footer/sidebar machinery exists for a widget.

## Design

- todo tool ops: init (phased or flat list), start, done, drop, block (with reason), unblock, rm, append (to phase), view; each completion auto-promotes the earliest still-open task in phase order to in_progress.
- State: stored in the session as a Custom entry (todo_list.v1) so it persists, branches with the tree, and replays; in-memory mirror for fast rendering.
- TUI widget: compact todo panel in the footer area (current task + counts per phase); Ctrl+O-class toggle to expand.
- RPC/ACP: todo_update events emitted on mutation so IDE surfaces can render.
- Guardrails (from hard-won omp semantics): task content is verbatim (never auto-generated IDs), completed tasks never revert, out-of-order completion allowed with pointer semantics documented in the tool description.

- STACK LAYERING (round-3): the todo panel/HUD is state-driven (renders from the todo_list.v1 entry, not from bespoke painting) so the F9.statusline HUD (bd-cv653.9.4) and overlay host can re-skin it mechanically. Keep widget logic and renderers separated from day one.

## Acceptance

1. Full lifecycle via RPC fixture: init 2 phases → start → done → auto-promote; block/unblock; view output shape stable.
2. Session persist: kill session, --continue → todo state intact (replay test).
3. TUI widget reflects mutations within one frame (e2e_tui).
4. Schema-invalid op (unknown task string) → tool error, no state change.

## Tests

- Unit: op semantics, promotion pointer, persistence round-trip, branch behavior (todo state forks with tree).
- e2e_rpc golden; e2e_tui widget assertion.
- Conformance: todo_list.v1 entry fixture.

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- Unit + e2e tests for this bead emit structured JSONL logs per the repo harness pattern (tests/common/logging.rs): per-case events, correlation ids, redacted payloads, artifact paths.
- e2e ships as a script under scripts/e2e/ registered in scripts/e2e/run_all.sh (focused + ci profiles); live-network lanes separate and gated.
- Failures must be diagnosable from logs alone: log tool inputs, decisions, and error taxonomy codes.

title: [OMP-ADOPT][Memory] Project-scoped memory bank and self-authored skills
description:
## Feature scope

Port omp's memory and learning tools:
- Memory bank: retain/recall/reflect/memory_edit over a project-scoped store — omp:src/tools/memory-*.ts, memories/, memory-backend/ (local/hindsight/mnemopi/off), packages/mnemopi (SQLite engine).
