title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add per-model tool-call dialect converters (toolconv) with edit benchmark
description:
## Why / omp reference (REVIEW GAP — missed in first pass)

omp's 'benchmaxxed' results come substantially from its dialect layer: per-model tool-call format converters (anthropic, deepseek, gemini, gemma, glm-4.5, harmony/GPT5, kimi-k2, minimax, qwen3, xml, pi-native) that shape tool definitions and repair/normalize tool-call output per model family. Measured upstream impact: Grok Code Fast edit success 6.7% → 68.3% when the edit format stops fighting the model; MiniMax pass rate 2.1×; Grok 4 Fast −61% output tokens. Evidence: omp:packages/ai/src/dialect/, docs/toolconv/ (per-dialect docs), packages/typescript-edit-benchmark.

## Current Pi state

Providers emit/consume their native wire formats and we normalize to unified StreamEvents; compat config tweaks field names/feature flags only. No per-model tool-call dialect adaptation: a model that emits XML-ish tool calls or harmony channels gets no targeted handling beyond generic parsing.

## Design

- New module (justified): src/dialects.rs + src/dialects/ (one converter per family). Converter = request-side tool-schema shaping + response-side tolerant parsing/repair (extract tool calls from the model's preferred format, normalize into our ToolCall type with a repair ledger recording every fixup).
- Model→dialect mapping in provider_metadata (dialect field per model entry; user-overridable in models.json); default = native format (current behavior) so Anthropic/OpenAI paths are untouched.
- Benchmark oracle: port the SPIRIT of omp's typescript-edit-benchmark at our scale — a harness (examples/ or benches-adjacent) running N fixture edit tasks per dialect measuring first-attempt apply rate + token cost; results JSON committed as evidence; dialect selection per model must cite this oracle (no vibe-based format choices).
- Interaction guards: dialect conversion happens BELOW failover (F3.failover preserves messages, dialect re-shapes per target provider automatically); streaming parser unchanged (dialects operate on tool-call payloads, not SSE).
- Rollout: behind models.json/setting flag per model family until oracle evidence justifies default-on per model.

## Acceptance

1. A weak-format fixture model (XML dialect) achieves the fixture-task apply rate the oracle measured; repair ledger records fixups.
2. Anthropic + OpenAI native paths: provider_streaming + provider_contract suites pass unchanged (zero regression proof).
3. Failover from native-format model to XML-dialect model mid-turn produces valid tool calls on both sides (e2e).
4. Oracle harness emits reproducible JSON (seeded tasks), wired into scripts/e2e profiles as a gated lane.

## Tests

- Unit: per-dialect parse/repair goldens (valid, malformed, partial-stream truncation), mapping resolution, repair-ledger content.
- Conformance: dialect fixtures per family.
- e2e: scripted stub providers per dialect with JSONL logging (tests/common/logging.rs); benchmark lane documented.

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- Unit + e2e tests for this bead emit structured JSONL logs per the repo harness pattern (tests/common/logging.rs): per-case events, correlation ids, redacted payloads, artifact paths.
- e2e ships as a script under scripts/e2e/ registered in scripts/e2e/run_all.sh (focused + ci profiles); live-network lanes separate and gated.
- Failures must be diagnosable from logs alone: log tool inputs, decisions, and error taxonomy codes.
close_reason: Dialect layer v1 shipped: text-emitted tool-call extraction/repair for weak models. dialects.rs: Native/Xmlish/Harmony families, conservative dialect_for_model mapping (qwen3/kimi-k2/glm/minimax/deepseek→Xmlish; gpt-5/o1/o3/o4→Harmony; all else Native), extraction with 4 guarded patterns (bare-JSON-whole-content, fenced json/tool_call blocks, <tool_call>/<tool_use> tags, <tool name=X>) × hard guards (registered-tool names only, object args only, one repair per message), strip_candidates, RepairLedger. agent.rs hook at message finalization: repair runs only for non-native dialects with Stop reason and no structured calls present; repaired blocks flow the normal executor path (effects/approval/logging); AgentSession drains the ledger into dialect_repair session Custom entries. Oracle: examples/dialect_bench.rs offline corpus (4 positive shapes + 6 negative incl. prose-wrapped, rust-fence, unknown-tool, non-object-args, plain prose, native-dialect-untouched) — GATE: 100% first-attempt apply rate, 0 false positives; evidence committed at docs/evidence/dialect-bench-oracle.json; --live is the documented manual lane. Evidence: 10 module unit tests (planted negatives all pass), agent-level turn test (repair executes the read, fixture content in history, session entry recorded, control proves loop-freedom on Native), full lib 7250/7250, clippy clean incl. examples. NOT in v1 (documented): models.json per-provider dialect override knob (mapping is built-in; override needs the compat-bag plumbing — follow-up when the benchmark matrix expands), request-side schema shaping (response-side repair covers the measured failure mode), --live provider scoring.

title: [OMP-ADOPT] Add secrets obfuscation for model-bound context (reversible placeholder vault)
description:
## Why / omp reference (REVIEW GAP — missed in first pass)

omp transforms secrets in and out of model context: obfuscator.ts (60KB) + placeholder-scan + message-transform replace credential-shaped values with placeholders before provider calls and restore on the way back, so an .env file read by the agent never reaches the provider verbatim. Evidence: omp:packages/coding-agent/src/secrets/.

## Current Pi state

Secret-awareness exists at the extension boundary (pi.env() blocklist, redacted alerts) and in ONE main-loop niche: the semantic-context-bundle injection path already computes a redaction_summary (src/agent.rs:9796,10401-10405 — found in round-8 source audit). But there is NO general secrets vault: read .env → tool result → provider payload still flows raw. The bundle path proves the pipeline has transform seams and gives this bead prior art to compose with (share detector rules + redaction reporting); it is not a substitute — it covers only that one injection path.

## Design

- New module (justified): src/secrets.rs. Outbound transform in the agent loop's provider-request path + inbound restore in the tool-execution path.
- Detection: pattern rules (sk-ant-*, sk-*, ghp_*, AKIA*, xox[bap]-*, -----BEGIN * PRIVATE KEY-----, DSN/connection strings, generic high-entropy assignments KEY=value) with a measured false-positive budget; rules versioned in-tree; user patterns via settings.
- Placeholders: stable per session (vault map in memory; format <pi-secret:7f3a2c>); NEVER persisted raw (session files store placeholders; the vault map dies with the session; compaction summaries carry placeholders).
- Inbound restore: when a tool call argument contains a placeholder, substitute the real value before write/edit/bash executes; bash additionally masks the restored value in echoed output back to the model.
- Modes: secrets.mode: off|obfuscate|block (block = refuse to send the message, loud error); default obfuscate. Audit events (redacted) per transform.
- Interaction: extension secret filtering composes (extension path unchanged); F4.memory's retain screen reuses this detector.

## Acceptance

1. Fixture .env read → recorded provider payload contains placeholders, zero raw secrets (canary assertions).
2. Model echoes placeholder into write → file on disk gets the REAL value; bash echo of the value is masked in tool result.
3. block mode refuses the send with a named error.
4. False-positive rate on a code-corpus fixture set below the budgeted threshold (measured, recorded).
5. Session export/share contains placeholders only.

## Tests

- Unit: detector rules matrix (true/false positives), vault stability, restore paths, mode FSM.
- Conformance: transcript fixtures with canaries.
- e2e: full loop via RPC with stub provider recording payloads; JSONL logs per logging.rs.

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- Unit + e2e tests for this bead emit structured JSONL logs per the repo harness pattern (tests/common/logging.rs): per-case events, correlation ids, redacted payloads, artifact paths.
- e2e ships as a script under scripts/e2e/ registered in scripts/e2e/run_all.sh (focused + ci profiles); live-network lanes separate and gated.
- Failures must be diagnosable from logs alone: log tool inputs, decisions, and error taxonomy codes.
close_reason: Secrets obfuscation vault shipped. (1) src/secrets.rs: versioned detector rules (sk-ant/sk/ghp_/github_pat/AKIA/private-key/AIza/xox*/DSN-with-creds/generic KEY=value high-entropy) as the program's SINGLE detector; SecretVault (in-memory, session-scoped, stable <pi-secret:NNNNNN> per session per value, dies with the session — never persisted raw); obfuscate/restore/mask transforms; modes off|obfuscate|block via secrets.mode (default obfuscate) + secrets.extraPatterns; redacted TransformAudit (counts+labels only). (2) Seams: OUTBOUND in the agent loop — Context transformed before provider.stream (user text, assistant text/thinking, tool results, system prompt); block mode refuses the send with named PI_SECRET_BLOCK. INBOUND in execute_tool — tool-call arguments restored to real values BEFORE approval (operators approve the real command); output masked back before the model sees it (bash echo hygiene). Export/share masked via agent.mask_secrets_text at /export. (3) Composition: memory's retain screen (bd-cv653.4.1) now reuses this detector with one-way [REDACTED_LABEL] placeholders — the two-detector drift from the round-5 audit is closed; memory tests stay green after the swap. (4) Acceptance: outbound payload carries placeholder canary with zero raw secrets (capture provider); placeholder echoed into write → real value on disk + masked echo; block mode named refusal; off mode byte-identical; export masked. FP budget: code-corpus fixtures pass clean (detector_passes_clean_code unit matrix). 19 unit + 5 integration tests; clippy/fmt/UBS-delta clean; scripts/e2e/run_secrets.sh lane; secrets in suite_classification.toml. Incidental: fix-forwarded the workspace bead's missing module seam mid-flight (scaffold, then cleanly superseded by their real module landing) and resolved a stash-pop conflict in agent.rs.

title: [OMP-ADOPT][QA] Conformance fixtures, cross-surface parity, docs and rollout for ported tools

## Feature scope

description:
## Why

A tool that behaves differently in RPC vs TUI is a bug factory. The repo already enforces cross-surface thinking (tests/cross_surface_parity.rs, json_mode_parity.rs); extend that net over the OMP-ADOPT wave.

## Acceptance

## Dependencies

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

title: [OMP-ADOPT][Chrome] Migrate interactive TUI runtime from charmed_rust to FrankenTUI Program
description:
## Why

Foundation for all chrome work. ftui-runtime's Program/Model is documented as derived from pi's exact current stack (/dp/frankentui/docs/migration-map.md: bubbletea Program→Program, Model→Model, batch/sequence→Cmd), so this is a structural port with upgrades, not a rewrite.

## Current Pi state

src/interactive.rs: BubbleteaModel + bubbles TextArea/Viewport/Spinner over crossterm, alt-screen only, manual newline clamping/CR normalization hacks in view.rs (5-31), render caches in perf.rs. Agent events bridge via with_input_receiver(ui_rx).

## Design (grounded in /dp/frankentui docs/migration-map.md + getting-started.md)

- Add deps as PATH deps (only ftui-core/layout/i18n are on crates.io): ftui facade (runtime+extras), features: syntax, theme, markdown, image, clipboard, export, help, mermaid; keep crossterm-compat for Windows; Unix moves to ftui-tty (nix+rustix, no crossterm).
- Port BubbleteaModel → ftui Model: update() returns Cmd; view(&mut Frame) immediate-mode (the big mechanical change from string composition); agent-event stream bridged via a Subscription (background thread + mpsc, StopSignal) — same role as today's input_receiver.
- Upgrades to switch on: DEC-2026 sync-bracket presents (flicker-proof), one-writer TerminalWriter, ftui-render sanitize() on ALL tool/LLM-originated text (adversarial-adjacent content safety), ResizeCoalescer (latest-wins + bounded latency), frame-budget controller + degradation levels, ProgramConfig inline mode (scrollback-preserving — NEW user-facing option: pi --inline / settings terminal.inline; alt-screen stays default).
- Capability probing parity: kitty keyboard CSI-u, SGR mouse, bracketed paste, focus events, OSC 52 clipboard, OSC 11 background (ftui caps_probe); mux (tmux) passthrough policy.
- DELETE: manual alt-screen clamp/normalize code in view.rs, width hacks (ftui-text owns UAX#11), crossterm direct usage on Unix, perf.rs caches superseded by kernel diffing (keep MessageRenderCache where still profitable — measure).
- Session restore on panic: ftui RAII teardown — verify panic paths restore the terminal (trybuild/PTY tests exist in ftui; add a pi-level crash test).
- Rollout: cargo feature `ftui` default-OFF during migration (build both stacks), flip default once F9.visuale2e proves parity, then remove the bubbletea stack (clean cutover per repo policy — no permanent duality).

- Ctrl+Z SUSPEND/RESUME (round-4): SIGTSTP suspends with full terminal state save (leave raw mode, restore cursor), SIGCONT resumes cleanly re-entering the session — standard Unix citizenship that the ftui TerminalSession RAII makes safe; prove with a PTY test.
- LOOP WATCHDOG (round-4): 250ms tick lag probe with phase attribution (render/input/agent-event) emitting at most one structured log per stall (omp loop-watchdog.ts parity) — the TUI-side lag telemetry the perf culture needs.

## Acceptance

1. pi launches interactive on ftui runtime: prompt, stream a response, run tools, /tree, quit — terminal state clean after exit AND after SIGKILL-mid-stream (PTY test).
2. Inline mode preserves shell scrollback (doctor capture proof).
3. Resize storm + flicker injection (ftui-harness) passes: no torn frames.
4. tmux nested session works (wheel/passthrough policy parity with current tmux guard).
5. Old stack compiles out cleanly; binary size delta measured and recorded (budget: ftui adds < 3 MiB release).

## Tests

- ProgramSimulator model tests for every existing AppAction (keybinding parity matrix vs src/keybindings.rs catalog).
- ftui-harness PTY tests: launch/quit/resize/scroll.
- doctor_frankentui replay on the real binary (baseline tape: launch → prompt → quit).
- e2e_tui suite ported to drive BOTH stacks during migration (parity gate), JSONL logs per logging.rs.

## References

/dp/frankentui/docs/migration-map.md; crates/ftui-runtime/src/{program.rs,terminal_writer.rs,subscription.rs}; crates/ftui-render/src/{presenter.rs,sanitize.rs,budget.rs}; /dp/mcp_agent_mail_rust tui_app.rs Program setup (stable_tui_program_config: resize coalescer + load governor + budget controller wiring); omp docs/tui-core-renderer.md append-only contract.

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- Unit + e2e tests for this bead emit structured JSONL logs per the repo harness pattern (tests/common/logging.rs): per-case events, correlation ids, redacted payloads, artifact paths.
- e2e ships as a script under scripts/e2e/ registered in scripts/e2e/run_all.sh (focused + ci profiles); live-network lanes separate and gated.
- Visual acceptance additionally requires doctor_frankentui snapshot/timeline evidence per epic constraint #8.
notes: ox-alpha (2026-08-24T04:20Z): ctrl+z SUSPEND/RESUME thread — implementation landed via ea6c9066 (swept from my working tree by another agent landing pass): perform_terminal_suspend (cooked mode + mirror of default ProgramConfig features [paste/SGR mouse/alt-screen], raise(SIGTSTP) via signal_hook low_level safe API, re-acquire on SIGCONT, returns Resize for full repaint), PiFtuiMsg::Resumed, AppAction::Suspend dispatch with vim-precedence, tick-freeze during suspending so pre-stop frames stay byte-identical (diff engine emits nothing into the restored shell). Follow-on E0063 saga: concurrent agents repeatedly overwrote each other completing the initializer fields; resolved by plumbing commit 861b081d (blob built outside working tree, pushed main+master) — VERIFIED compiling clean at base=861b081d (cold build vmi1264463). NOTE for fleet: interactive_ftui.rs was under active dual-agent edit for ~1h; if your local tree diverges, git pull --rebase onto 861b081d. STILL OPEN on this bead: suspend unit+e2e tests (in progress next), TUI loop watchdog, release size delta measurement, bd-n0ld1 cutover gate.

title: [OMP-ADOPT][Chrome] Build visual regression + gallery harness (ftui-harness + doctor_frankentui + pi gallery)
description:
## Why

The chrome program is only shippable with visual proof. omp has `omp gallery` (every tool renderer × streaming/progress/success/error + VHS screenshots — cli/gallery-cli.ts). FrankenTUI gives the Rust-side machinery: ftui-harness (assert_snapshot! + BLESS, ProgramSimulator, PTY capture, flicker/resize-storm injection, ShadowRun) and doctor_frankentui (replay/migrate driving ANY binary via VHS key scripting + tmux capture-pane scrollback + ffmpeg snapshots + JSONL evidence + --machine json CI exit codes). am's tests/artifacts_native/tui_* show the artifact layout in production.

## Design

DEPENDS ON: F9.runtime, F9.transcript (cards are the gallery's subjects).
- pi gallery subcommand (dev-only, not in --help user surface): renders every tool card/message component in every state (pending/streaming/success/error/expanded/collapsed) from fixture payloads into a capture matrix; integrates doctor_frankentui suite profiles per surface (transcript, editor, pickers, overlays).
- Snapshot suite: ftui-harness goldens per component × theme-sample × width (80/120/200 + tiny 40) with BLESS workflow documented in docs/development.md.
- ProgramSimulator model tests: every AppAction + overlay esc-stack + autocomplete flows without a PTY.
- doctor CI lane: replay tapes (launch, prompt, stream, /tree, picker nav, quit) across terminal profiles (kitty/xterm/tmux/dumb); --machine json artifacts uploaded in CI; FAIL on contract violation (torn frames, scrollback damage, cursor leaks).
- Fault injection: resize storm + input storm + flicker detection on the full app (not just widgets).
- Perf gates: frame-time p95 < 16ms during streaming+spinner load on the reference host (criterion + FrameTiming sink); startup TTI budget unchanged (<100ms target, measured).
- Rollout gate: this bead's matrix is THE parity evidence for flipping the ftui default in F9.runtime.

## Acceptance

1. pi gallery emits the full capture matrix; snapshots blessed and CI-gated.
2. doctor suite green across 4 terminal profiles on the real binary; artifacts (report.json, snapshot.png, timeline_strip.png) published per run.
3. Fault-injection lanes green; a deliberately torn frame is caught (negative control).
4. Frame-time + startup budgets measured and recorded (engineering evidence, not release claims).
5. Suite wired into scripts/e2e/run_all.sh profiles (focused + ci) with JSONL logs per logging.rs.

## Tests

This bead IS the test harness; its own tests: harness self-tests (bless/regenerate determinism), tape replay determinism, artifact schema validation.

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- Unit + e2e tests for this bead emit structured JSONL logs per the repo harness pattern (tests/common/logging.rs): per-case events, correlation ids, redacted payloads, artifact paths.

## Design (FrankenTUI mapping)

DEPENDS ON: F9.runtime.
- Transcript: ftui VirtualizedList/LogViewer-grade virtualized scrollback + commit seam: finalized blocks become immutable render items; streaming block is the single live item (mirrors RenderStablePrefix). title: [OMP-ADOPT][Chrome] Port powerline status line + footer + sticky HUDs (25 segments, presets, session accent)
description:
## Why / omp reference

omp's powerline status line lives in the editor's top border: 25+ segments (model+thinking glyph+advisor badge, mode, path, git clean/dirty/staged/untracked, pr, context_pct, cost, tokens in/out/rate, cache r/w, subagents, hostname, session_name...), 7 presets (default/minimal/compact/full/nerd/ascii/custom), separators (powerline/thin/slash/dot), per-session accent tinting (status-line/component.ts, segments.ts, presets.ts). Sticky HUDs above the composer: todos + subagents (interactive-mode.ts container order). Footer legacy: pwd+branch, token stats, cost, context% (footer.ts).

## Current Pi state

Header = model label + Branch N/M + hints; footer = tokens/cost + persist durability + mode + /help. Functional, not powerline; no segments/presets; no git awareness; no HUDs.

## Design (FrankenTUI mapping)

DEPENDS ON: F9.runtime.
- ftui StatusLine/Badge + tabs primitives; segment registry {id, render(ctx), min_width, priority} with the omp segment set (start: model, thinking, mode, path, git*, context_pct, cost, tokens, cache, subagents, session_name, time; advisor/collab/pr segments activate when those beads land — registry is open).
- Presets + user custom segment lists via settings (statusLine.preset + statusLine.segments); separator styles; responsive: segments drop by priority as width shrinks (layout tiers per showcase contract).
- Git segments: watch cwd git state (porcelain v2 parse, debounced 2s; reuse F2.github's repo resolution where sensible — no gh dependency for local state).
- Per-session accent: djb2 session-name hue (warm band dark themes/cool band light, ≥10° collision shift, WCAG cap) tinting editor border + status accents.
- Sticky HUDs: todo HUD (F3.todo) + subagent HUD (F5) rendered as retract-on-update blocks above the composer (displaceable blocks in F9.transcript).
- Footer: keep the current dim footer as the `minimal` fallback tier; powerline replaces it when enabled (settings).

- CLICKABLE SEGMENTS (round-3): status-line segments register hit regions — clicking the model segment opens the model palette, git segment opens a status popup, subagents segment opens the agent roster (when F5 lands), context_pct triggers the compaction-preview. Same MouseDispatcher pattern as the cards (am tui_hit_regions.rs); every click action has a keyboard equivalent.

- ROLE-CYCLE CHIP TRACK (round-4): the Ctrl+P model cycling surface is a powerline chip track (omp segment-track.ts: position-colored labels, active = filled chip with luminance-matched bold label + triangle caps) that appears above the composer while cycling and AUTO-CLEARS ~4s after the last keypress; reused later for the plan-mode tier slider.

## Acceptance

1. Presets render per golden snapshots (7 × 3 widths); segment drop order correct at 60-col.
2. Git dirty/staged/untracked segments update within 3s of a fixture repo change.
3. Session accent: two sessions same repo get distinct hues; contrast floor test passes on all 41 ftui palettes.
4. Todo HUD pins above composer, updates on todo mutation, retracts on completion.
5. Zero-cost when disabled: minimal tier = today's footer byte-parity.

- Snapshot matrix per preset/theme sample; segment unit tests (fixture contexts); git watcher e2e in scratch repo; JSONL logs; e2e registration.

title: [OMP-ADOPT][Chrome] Adopt FrankenTUI 41-palette theme system + pi JSON adapter + symbol presets + live preview
description:
## Why / omp reference + ftui capability

omp ships ~110 JSON themes (64 tokens, vars with cycle detection, unicode/nerd/ascii symbol presets, color-blind HSV shift, file-watcher live reload, OSC 11 + mode-2031 auto dark/light; theme.ts/theme-class.ts/symbols.ts/theme-schema.json/defaults/). FrankenTUI ships 41 WCAG-harmonized palettes (ThemeId: CyberpunkAurora, Darcula, LumenLight, NordicFrost, Monokai, Solarized±, Gruvbox±, Catppuccin ×4, TokyoNight, HighContrast...) with ensure_min_contrast floors + ScopedThemeLock (ftui-extras/theme.rs). am's tui_theme.rs shows the production adapter pattern (ConsoleThemeId ↔ ThemeId).

## Current Pi state

src/theme.rs: JSON schema {colors: 7 + syntax 5 + ui 3}, built-ins dark/light/solarized, discovery ~/.pi/agent/themes + .pi/themes, is_light luminance drives glamour light/dark. Far smaller token surface than omp's 64.

## Design

DEPENDS ON: F9.runtime.
- Adopt ftui ThemeId palettes as the built-in gallery; /theme selector becomes ftui SelectList with LIVE PREVIEW on highlight (ScopedThemeLock swap; restore on cancel) + Ctrl+T global cycling (showcase contract) + HighContrast accessibility entry.
- Pi JSON theme adapter: existing user theme files map onto a ThemePalette (bg ladder/fg hierarchy/8 accents/syntax set derived from pi's smaller token set with documented derivation rules); missing tokens inherit from nearest base palette — zero user breakage, and pi themes gain the full token richness.
- omp theme import (stretch): token mapping table omp's 64-token schema → ftui ThemePalette (documented in docs/themes.md); ~110 defaults become importable, not bundled (size).
- Symbol presets: unicode/nerd/ascii sets for spinners/borders/tree glyphs/status icons (port omp symbols.ts catalog semantics onto pi's icon usage); ascii fallback guard for dumb terminals (capability-gated).
- Color-blind mode: HSV-shift diff-added token (omp parity) behind settings flag.
- Auto dark/light: COLORFGBG + OSC 11 probe at start (ftui caps_probe); LIVE mode-2031 listener is an ftui GAP — implement as a small upstream contribution to ftui-core (event on 2031 notification) or poll-free manual /theme dark|light. Decide at implementation; document.
- Live reload: watcher on theme file → ScopedThemeLock swap (am pattern); markdown/glamour style re-derivation on swap (current glamour path invalidates correctly).
- Syntax-highlighting theme bridge: ftui syntax tokens mapped from palette syntax set (works with F9.mdviz's highlighter choice).

## Acceptance

1. /theme lists all 41 palettes; highlight previews live; Esc restores prior theme; Ctrl+T cycles globally from any screen.
2. A legacy pi dark.json loads and renders sensibly (adapter golden) — user's existing themes survive.
3. ascii preset on TERM=dumb produces pure-ASCII chrome (snapshot).
4. Color-blind mode shifts diff-added hue measurably (token assertion).
5. Theme file edit live-reloads mid-session (e2e with fixture file).

## Tests

- Contrast floor sweep across all palettes (reuse ftui ensure_min_contrast as a pi-side test over our token usage), adapter goldens, symbol preset snapshots, reload e2e; JSONL logs; e2e registration.

## Test logging & e2e wiring (global mandate, epic constraint #7)

- Unit + e2e tests for this bead emit structured JSONL logs per the repo harness pattern (tests/common/logging.rs): per-case events, correlation ids, redacted payloads, artifact paths.
- e2e ships as a script under scripts/e2e/ registered in scripts/e2e/run_all.sh (focused + ci profiles); live-network lanes separate and gated.
- Visual acceptance additionally requires doctor_frankentui snapshot/timeline evidence per epic constraint #8.

title: [OMP-ADOPT][Chrome] Markdown/math/mermaid/image excellence: streaming GFM, syntax breadth, mermaid, Sixel, OSC-8
description:
## Why / omp reference + ftui capability

omp markdown (components/markdown.ts 3254 lines): frozen-token prefix caching, table layout locks, orphan-fence repair, OSC 66 double-scale headings, inline hex swatches, math (latex-block.ts 2-D layout: stacked fractions/matrices/radicals), mermaid→ASCII with orientation fitting, OSC-8 links, syntect highlighting via pi-natives (11 semantic categories). FrankenTUI: ftui-extras/markdown.rs (pulldown-cmark GFM, tables/tasklists/admonitions, math→Unicode, STREAMING-FRAGMENT renderer built for LLM output, is_likely_markdown, mermaid blocks) + mermaid.rs (481KB real diagram engine — BEYOND omp's ASCII) + image.rs (Kitty/iTerm2/Sixel/Ascii — superset of pi's Kitty/iTerm2) + link registry (OSC-8 + hit regions) + syntax.rs (registry; built-ins Plain/Diff/JSON/TOML/MD ONLY — the breadth gap).

title: FUZZ-V3: E2E Fuzz Orchestration Script — Master runner with JSONL logging, timing, coverage collection
close_reason: Implemented FUZZ-V3 orchestrator script with unified report/events + documented usage

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## FUZZ-V3: E2E Fuzz Orchestration Script

### Purpose
Master script that orchestrates the FULL fuzzing pipeline end-to-end:
1. Runs P1 proptest validation (V1)
2. Runs P2 fuzz harness validation (V2)
3. Generates a unified report combining both
4. Produces JSONL event log for every step
5. Serves as the single entry point for developers and CI

### Script Design

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# scripts/fuzz_e2e.sh — Master fuzz orchestration
#
# Usage:
#   ./scripts/fuzz_e2e.sh              # Full run (proptests + fuzz harnesses)
#   ./scripts/fuzz_e2e.sh --quick      # Quick run (proptests only, 10s fuzz)
#   ./scripts/fuzz_e2e.sh --deep       # Deep run (proptests + 30min fuzz per target)
#   ./scripts/fuzz_e2e.sh --report     # Just regenerate report from existing logs
```

### JSONL Event Log
Every action emits a structured event to fuzz/reports/events.jsonl:
```jsonl
{"ts":"2026-02-15T10:00:00Z","event":"pipeline_start","mode":"full"}
{"ts":"2026-02-15T10:00:01Z","event":"phase_start","phase":"P1","target_count":30}
{"ts":"2026-02-15T10:00:02Z","event":"proptest_run","module":"sse::tests","fn":"sse_chunking_invariant","cases":256,"status":"pass","time_ms":340}
...
{"ts":"2026-02-15T10:05:00Z","event":"phase_end","phase":"P1","passed":30,"failed":0,"total_cases":5120}
{"ts":"2026-02-15T10:05:01Z","event":"phase_start","phase":"P2","target_count":14}
{"ts":"2026-02-15T10:05:02Z","event":"fuzz_build","status":"pass","time_ms":45000}
{"ts":"2026-02-15T10:05:47Z","event":"fuzz_run","target":"fuzz_sse_parser","time_limit_s":60,"status":"pass","corpus_growth":234}
...
{"ts":"2026-02-15T10:20:00Z","event":"pipeline_end","status":"pass","total_time_ms":1200000}
```

### Unified Report
Combines V1 (proptest) and V2 (fuzz) results into one document:
```json
{
  "pipeline_version": "1.0",
  "timestamp": "2026-02-15T...",
  "mode": "full",
  "phases": {
    "P1_proptest": { ... V1 report ... },
    "P2_libfuzzer": { ... V2 report ... }
  },
  "summary": {
    "overall_status": "pass",
    "proptest_functions": 30,
    "proptest_cases": 5120,
    "fuzz_targets": 14,
    "fuzz_time_s": 840,
    "total_crashes": 0,
    "corpus_total": 3456,
    "bugs_found": 0,
    "bugs_fixed": 3
  }
}
```

### Exit Codes
- 0: All phases pass
- 1: P1 proptest failures
- 2: P2 fuzz crashes found
- 3: Both P1 and P2 failures
- 4: Build failure (infrastructure broken)

### Integration with CI (P3)
The E2E script IS what the CI workflow calls. P3.1 (GitHub Actions) wraps this script with:
- Matrix parallelism for individual fuzz targets
- Caching for corpus persistence
- Artifact upload for crash inputs

### Files to Create
- scripts/fuzz_e2e.sh (main orchestration script)
- fuzz/reports/ directory structure
- Helper: scripts/parse_proptest_output.py (or inline awk/jq)

### Acceptance Criteria
- Script runs full pipeline in under 30 minutes (60s per fuzz target)
- JSONL event log captures every step with timestamps
- Unified JSON report produced at known path
- Script is idempotent (re-running produces fresh results)
- Exit codes correctly reflect pass/fail status
- --quick mode completes in under 5 minutes
- Human-readable terminal output with colored pass/fail indicators

title: Fix global Buffer copy bound coercion
description: Node Buffer.prototype.copy coerces targetStart/sourceStart/sourceEnd with integer truncation and maps NaN, non-numeric strings, and +/-Infinity to zero, while finite negative values remain RangeError. Pi's global Buffer shim currently requires integer bounds and rejects fractions, NaN, non-numeric strings, and infinities. Add Node vectors and normalize copy bounds independently from stricter write bounds.

title: Feature: Research & selection of popular Pi extensions
description: Research and select the global 200+ most-used Pi extensions (incl. OpenClaw ecosystem) using an explicit popularity rubric, reproducible discovery queries, and evidence-backed tiering.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
Purpose
Define and execute the research + selection methodology for the expanded extension corpus. This is the foundation for all downstream pinning, gap analysis, and conformance work.

Key Questions
- What does “popular” mean in this ecosystem? (stars, forks, usage, mentions, downloads, recency)
- Which sources are authoritative? (pi-mono, GitHub orgs, npm packages, community lists)
- How do we ensure coverage across extension types, complexity, and capability surface?

Outputs
- A documented scoring rubric with explicit thresholds and coverage quotas.
- A candidate inventory list with metadata per extension (repo, commit/tag, license, type, deps, runtime tier, capabilities).
- Tier-1/Tier-2 selection with justification for each chosen extension.

Constraints
- The final corpus must be runnable unmodified; if something breaks, we fix the runtime/shims, not the extension.

comments.author: LavenderRobin
comments.text:
RESEARCH METHOD (2026-02-05)

Goal
- Discover, validate, and select the global set of “most used” Pi extensions (target: 200+ must-pass) across GitHub, npm, official Pi sources, and OpenClaw/marketplace ecosystems.

Critical definition: “True Pi extension”
A candidate is only considered a Pi extension if it is compatible with Pi’s extension protocol (or can be made compatible via *generic* pipeline transforms):
- Exposes an entrypoint consistent with Pi’s extension API (e.g., default export taking an ExtensionAPI / ctx-like object).
- Uses recognizable Pi extension registration patterns (tools, slash commands, event hooks, provider registration, UI/RPC calls).
- NOT merely “agent prompts”, “Claude Code plugins”, or unrelated MCP servers unless they explicitly implement Pi’s extension protocol.

Evidence-backed popularity (rubric anchor)
- Use bd-29ko rubric as the baseline.
- Extend evidence sources for new ecosystems:
  - Marketplace rank/installs (OpenClaw/ClawHub or analogous)
  - GitHub stars/forks + recent activity
  - npm downloads (weekly) + dependents
  - Cross-repo mentions (README/issue references)

Selection output (what downstream work expects)
- A machine-readable candidate inventory (raw, unfiltered) + a validated/deduped inventory.
- A tiered selection with explicit quotas:
  - Tier-1 >=200 (MUST PASS)
  - Tier-2 additional stretch / long-tail coverage
- Every chosen extension includes:
  - source pin (repo URL + commit/tag + path)
  - license status
  - declared interaction model + capabilities
  - scenario linkage (what conformance tests must do)

Anti-goals / pitfalls
- No one-off, per-extension compatibility hacks.
- No silent exclusions: if something is popular but incompatible, it becomes an explicit gap with an explicit reason.
- Avoid confusing other ecosystems’ “extensions” with Pi extensions; validate via code signatures before counting.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: Closed. Research & selection completed via bd-2hap (research) + bd-3o8d (selection) + bd-2oal (acquisition). 223 extensions across 5 source tiers validated and catalogued in docs/extension-catalog.json.

title: Regression: select_model_and_thinking tests return cloudflare-ai-gateway instead of openai-codex
description:
Seven tests in src/app.rs::tests fail on main as of 2902a2e3 (and previous commits eedec079, 6172854a, etc. — pre-existing for at least the last 7 commits):

- app::tests::select_model_and_thinking_preserves_restore_warning_when_defaulting_for_setup
- app::tests::select_model_and_thinking_preserves_restore_warning_when_using_config_default
- app::tests::select_model_and_thinking_restores_model_from_header_when_history_missing
- app::tests::select_model_and_thinking_restores_thinking_from_active_branch_only
- app::tests::select_model_and_thinking_restores_thinking_from_header_when_history_missing
- rpc::tests::auto_compaction_missing_api_key_omits_absent_result_field
- session::tests::test_continue_recent_in_dir_refreshes_index_after_changed_disk_session

The select_model_and_thinking_* failures all manifest as:
  left: 'cloudflare-ai-gateway'
  right: 'openai-codex'

Tests register a setup model (test_model_entry('gpt-5.4', 'openai-codex')) into the registry, expect default_model_from_candidates to find it via the ('openai-codex', 'gpt-5.4') entry in the priority list at src/app.rs:765-797. Instead the code returns a cloudflare-ai-gateway model, suggesting:

1. The merged setup entry is being filtered out of registry.models() somehow, OR
2. canonical_provider_id is no longer canonicalizing 'openai-codex' to itself, OR
3. The defaults priority list iteration is short-circuiting at a different match

a444a157 (2026-04-17 'tests: decouple test fixtures from production model ids…') updated ONE test fixture to use 'test-gpt-5.4' but did not migrate the other tests that still reference the production 'gpt-5.4' / 'openai-codex' pair.

Verified pre-existing by running the same test on commit eedec079 (4 commits before this triage session): same failure. Therefore unrelated to v0.1.14 changes (claude-opus-4-7 snapshot, model override config, clippy).

Did NOT block v0.1.14 release because pre-existing and not user-facing.
close_reason: Fixed select_model_and_thinking tests by isolating model registry fixtures from host auth/built-in provider readiness; focused regression tests pass.

title: Release: versioning + tag strategy (pre-1.0 → 1.0)
description:
# Goal
Define the single source of truth for versioning and tags so releases are repeatable and humans don’t have to remember tribal knowledge.

# Background
- This repo ships a `pi` binary and also exposes a library crate (`pi`).
- Publishing to crates.io and publishing GitHub Releases both need a consistent version scheme.

# Decisions to Make (write down explicitly)
1) **When do we call it 1.0?**
   - What is the minimum feature set / stability bar?
2) **Version coupling:**
   - Are `pi_agent_rust` crate version, `pi` binary `--version`, and any published sibling crates (asupersync/rich_rust/charmed_rust) versioned together or independently?
3) **Tag format:**
   - e.g. `vX.Y.Z` tags for repo releases.
4) **Changelog source:**
   - Prefer generating `CHANGELOG.md` from closed beads via `br changelog` (see sibling task).

# Output / Deliverables
- A short doc section (can live in `docs/releasing.md`) describing:
  - version bump procedure
  - tag naming
  - how to cut a patch release
  - what is required before tagging (quality gates + CI green)

# Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A human can follow the written steps and create a release without guessing.
- [ ] Version/tag policy is consistent with existing `.github/workflows/publish.yml` and crate metadata.
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] Scope in description implemented fully with no feature loss
[ ] Unit tests cover core success/failure + edge cases for this bead (add regression coverage if applicable)
[ ] Integration/E2E script exercises the end-to-end path (or explicitly marks N/A with rationale in notes) and emits detailed JSONL logs + artifacts per bd-4u9
[ ] Logs include inputs, outputs, timing, and redaction summary; artifacts list is deterministic
[ ] Any new fixtures/golden outputs are deterministic and documented
[ ] Quality gates pass: cargo fmt --check, cargo check --all-targets, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test
[ ] Docs/fixtures updated if behavior or UX changes

title: [IDEA-WIZARD] Swarm context fabric and adaptive execution program
description:
## Background
The previous closed idea-wizard programs covered coverage/traceability drift and a first swarm-scale resource-governor package. This follow-up is deliberately non-duplicative: it targets cross-agent context reuse, build-cache affinity, conflict prediction, multi-process persistence stress, shared provider replay, and operator handoff/completion evidence.

## Phase 2/3 Winnowing Summary
Top ideas kept from the 30-to-5 and next-10 passes:
- Shared read-only source/context cache for repeated read/grep/find and docs/evidence lookups across many agents.
- RCH warm-target affinity planner so swarms reuse remote cargo caches instead of cold-building in parallel.
- Conflict predictor and reservation recommender using git, Beads, Agent Mail, and file-touch history.
- Multi-process session-store chaos harness for simultaneous agent/TUI/RPC usage.
- Handoff/completion audit bundles that map prompts to concrete artifacts, commands, tests, and pushed commits.
- Shared VCR/provider replay cache and tail-latency shedding under swarm event pressure.

## Non-Goals
- Do not replace Agent Mail or Beads.
- Do not claim release-facing performance wins without the existing evidence gates.
- Do not add broad new runtime policy without replayable tests and JSONL artifacts.

## Success Criteria

title: [IDEA-WIZARD] Build shared read-only source context cache
description:
## What
Design and implement a read-only source/context cache for repeated `read`, `grep`, `find`, docs/evidence, and manifest lookups during multi-agent work.

## Why
Large swarms repeatedly read the same files and generated evidence. A content-addressed, invalidation-aware cache can reduce filesystem churn and improve agent responsiveness without changing write semantics.

## How
Start with an internal cache boundary around read-only tool/index paths. Key entries by canonical path, mtime/size/hash, and query parameters. Fail closed to direct reads on any uncertainty.

## Tests
Unit tests for keying/invalidation and integration tests proving stale file updates bypass or invalidate cache. Add JSONL evidence with hit/miss/stale reasons.

## Success Criteria
Repeated read-only operations reuse fresh cache entries; modified files are never served stale; writes/edit/bash remain uncached.
close_reason: Completed: added cache coverage for find invalidation, uncached write/edit/bash side effects, and JSONL evidence for the read-only tool output context cache.

## How
Parse a provided Markdown objective or bead description into checklist items, then let agents fill/verify evidence paths and command results. Emit JSON plus Markdown.

## Tests
Unit tests for checklist extraction and fixture tests covering missing commands, proxy-only evidence, and contradictory green statuses.

## Success Criteria

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## FUZZ-P2.8: Extension Payload libfuzzer Harness

### Background
Extensions are third-party JS/TS code running in a QuickJS sandbox. They communicate with the Rust host via JSON payloads for tool registration, event hooks, slash commands, provider registration, and session operations. The extension system is massive (extensions.rs: 1.1MB, extensions_js.rs: 715KB) and handles untrusted data.

### Harness Design

```rust
// fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_extension_payload.rs
#\![no_main]
use libfuzzer_sys::fuzz_target;
use arbitrary::Arbitrary;

#[derive(Arbitrary, Debug)]
struct ExtPayload {
    op: String,
    payload_json: String,
}

fuzz_target\!(|input: ExtPayload| {
    // dispatch_hostcall_events() is the main entry point for JS→Rust communication
    // It takes an operation string and a JSON payload
    // This must NEVER panic — malicious extensions must be sandboxed
    let _ = dispatch_hostcall_events_fuzz(&input.op, &input.payload_json);
});
```

### Key Risk Areas
1. **Tool registration**: Extensions register tools with JSON Schema definitions. Malformed schemas could crash the tool registry.
2. **Event hooks**: Extensions register for events (onMessage, onToolCall, etc.). Invalid event names or hook definitions could crash dispatch.
3. **Provider registration**: Extensions can register custom LLM providers. Malformed provider specs could crash provider creation.
4. **Session operations**: Extensions call pi.session() for get_state/get_messages/set_name/etc. Invalid payloads could corrupt session state.
5. **Capability policy bypass**: Crafted payloads that attempt to call operations beyond the extension's granted capabilities.

### Note on Existing Coverage
src/extensions.rs already has a proptest for dispatch (line 23031, 512 cases). The libfuzzer harness extends this with coverage-guided mutation for deeper exploration.

### Seed Corpus
- Extract register payloads from existing extension test fixtures
- Include real extension registration JSON from the 223-extension corpus
- Generate edge cases: empty payloads, very large payloads, nested objects

### Files to Create
- fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_extension_payload.rs
- fuzz/corpus/fuzz_extension_payload/ (seed payloads)

### Acceptance Criteria
- Harness compiles and runs
- Covers at least: tool registration, event dispatch, session operations
- 5-minute fuzz run completes without crashes
- Any panics → triaged and fixed (extensions must be fully sandboxed)

title: EPIC: Advanced Runtime Depth Verification — prove math-driven components are not ceremonial
description:
# Background
README "Deep Dive: Core Algorithms" cites CUSUM + BOCPD regime detection, Conformal Prediction envelope, PAC-Bayes safety bound, IPS/WIS/DR off-policy evaluation with ESS and regret gate, VOI-driven experiment selection, weighted bottleneck attribution, and Online Convex Optimization with regret tracking. Grep shows 699+ occurrences of these symbols across src/ (extension_scoring.rs, extensions.rs, extension_dispatcher.rs, ext_runtime_risk_ledger.rs, ext_workloads.rs). So the code exists.

The question this epic answers: does the code *work* in the sense the README claims? That is:
- Does the CUSUM detector actually catch regime shifts on synthetic traces with known change points, with controllable false-positive rate?
- Does BOCPD emit change-point posterior spikes where expected?
- Does the PAC-Bayes bound veto aggressive policy when (KL + log(2√n/δ))/n exceeds threshold?
- Do IPS/WIS/DR estimators converge to the true value on synthetic on-policy vs off-policy pairs with computable ground truth?
- Does the VOI planner's priority ordering respect utility/overhead as documented?
- Does shadow dual execution detect a forced divergence and trigger back-off?
- Does ext_runtime_risk_ledger verify + replay + calibrate round-trip on a synthetic ledger with known perturbations?

Without these tests, the code is "present" but not "proven". For a system whose brand rests on safety + adaptation guarantees, that's a real risk.

# Goal
For each math-driven component, land focused property/behavioral tests that exercise the component on synthetic inputs with computable ground truth, then assert the component delivers what the README claims.

# Scope (child tasks)
- T: CUSUM detector — synthetic regime shift test
- T: BOCPD detector — synthetic change-point posterior test
- T: Conformal interval — calibration coverage test
- T: PAC-Bayes veto path — bound-crossing triggers deny
- T: IPS/WIS/DR estimators — convergence tests with known ground truth
- T: ESS gate — sample-support denial test
- T: VOI planner — priority ordering test
- T: Shadow dual execution — forced-divergence triggers backoff
- T: Runtime risk ledger — verify/replay/calibrate round-trip
- T: OCO regret rollback — loss-threshold rollback test

# Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each math component has at least one synthetic-input behavioral test in tests/algorithms/ or equivalent
- [ ] All tests pass in CI
- [ ] Test files document the theoretical guarantee being verified and the sample complexity/tolerance
- [ ] Regression in any component blocks main merge

# Considerations / Risks
- Some components may have been written aspirationally and fail these tests. That's *good* — filing implementation beads is cheaper than shipping broken brand.
- Distinguish between "math implementation is wrong" (implementation bug) and "README overclaims" (marketing bug). Both are valid outcomes of this epic.

# Refs
- src/extensions.rs (~567 hits)
- src/extension_scoring.rs (~11 hits)
- src/extension_dispatcher.rs (~24 hits)
- src/bin/ext_runtime_risk_ledger.rs
- src/bin/ext_workloads.rs
- README "Deep Dive: Core Algorithms"
- testing-metamorphic and alien-artifact-coding skills for test design

title: RV-T1: CUSUM detector — synthetic regime-shift behavioral test
description:
# Context
README cites CUSUM detection in extension dispatcher for regime-shift detection (P. 5 Deep Dive). Live-traffic regressions motivate this existing. We need to prove the detector actually catches shifts.

# Goal
Synthetic-input test: generate a stationary process of length N with a known mean shift at t=N/2; the detector should flag the shift with low false-positive rate on the pre-shift portion.

# Approach
1. Locate CUSUM implementation (grep cusum/CUSUM in src/).
2. Unit test: generate N=1000 samples, shift mean by k*sigma at t=500.
3. Assert: no alarm in t<500 (FPR ≤ 0.05), alarm within detection-delay budget in t≥500.
4. Vary k (shift size) and validate monotonic detection delay.
5. Document the k value for "reasonable" detection in the test comment.

# Acceptance
- [ ] tests/algorithms/cusum_regime_shift.rs lands
- [ ] Passes in CI
- [ ] False-positive rate ≤ 5% on pre-shift portion
- [ ] True-positive rate ≥ 90% within 2*ARL0 for shift sizes ≥ 1σ

# Refs
- src/extension_dispatcher.rs (CUSUM references)
- README "Regime-Shift Detection (CUSUM + BOCPD)" section
- alien-artifact-coding skill for rigor patterns
close_reason: Added synthetic CUSUM regime-shift regression covering sustained 1σ-4σ mean shifts, pre-shift false-positive budget, and monotonic detection delay.

title: RV-T5: IPS/WIS/DR off-policy estimator convergence tests
description:
# Context
IPS = (1/n)Σ w_i r_i; WIS = Σ w_i r_i / Σ w_i; DR = (1/n)Σ (r̂_i + w_i(r_i - r̂_i)).

# Goal
On synthetic on-policy data with known value V* and a logging policy μ, verify estimators converge to V* as n grows.

# Approach
1. Locate estimators.
2. Simulate contextual bandit with known r(x,a). Logging policy μ samples uniformly; target policy π greedy.
3. For n ∈ {100, 1000, 10000}: compute V_IPS, V_WIS, V_DR; assert |V - V*| decreases with n (RMSE drops).

# Acceptance
- [ ] tests/algorithms/off_policy_estimators.rs
- [ ] RMSE monotonically decreases with n (within MC noise)

title: [PERF-9] CI performance regression gate (fail on >20% regression)
description:
## Problem

Without CI enforcement, performance regressions can silently creep in. Need automated detection.

## Solution: CI Performance Gate

### Approach
- Use criterion with `--save-baseline` and comparison modes
- Store baseline benchmarks in git (benches/baselines/)
- CI step runs benchmarks and compares against baseline
- Fail if any benchmark regresses >20% (configurable threshold)

### CI Integration

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
perf-check:
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: Install critcmp
      run: cargo install critcmp
    - name: Run benchmarks against baseline
      run: |
        cargo bench --bench tui_perf -- --save-baseline pr
    - name: Compare against stored baseline
      run: |
        critcmp main pr --threshold 20
```

### How critcmp Works
- `critcmp` compares two criterion baselines by name
- `--threshold 20` flags any benchmark where the PR is >20% slower than main
- Exit code 1 if any threshold exceeded (fails the CI step)
- Produces human-readable table:
  ```
  group                         main                  pr
  -----                         ----                  --
  build_conversation/10         1.23 ms (±0.05)       1.25 ms (±0.04)  [+1.6% -- OK]
  build_conversation/1000       45.2 ms (±1.2)        58.1 ms (±2.3)   [+28.5% -- REGRESSION]
  ```

### Threshold Configuration
- 20% regression threshold for CI failure (default)
- Configurable via env var PERF_REGRESSION_THRESHOLD
- Some benchmarks may need higher thresholds (e.g., markdown rendering is inherently variable)

### Baseline Update Process
When intentional performance changes are made:
```bash
# Record new baseline after optimization
cargo bench --bench tui_perf -- --save-baseline main
# Copy to checked-in location
cp -r target/criterion benches/baselines/
git add benches/baselines/
```

### JSONL CI Event Logging
The CI step emits structured events for artifact retention:
```
{"schema":"pi.ci.perf_gate.v1","event":"benchmark_run","baseline":"pr","timestamp":"..."}
{"schema":"pi.ci.perf_gate.v1","event":"comparison","bench":"build_conversation/1000","main_ms":45.2,"pr_ms":58.1,"change_pct":28.5,"status":"regression"}
{"schema":"pi.ci.perf_gate.v1","event":"gate_result","passed":false,"regressions":1}
```

## Files to Modify
- .github/workflows/ci.yml: Add perf-check job
- benches/baselines/ (new directory for stored baselines)

## Dependencies
- Depends on PERF-8 (benchmark suite must exist before CI can gate on it)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] CI job runs criterion benchmarks on PR
- [ ] critcmp compares PR baseline against stored main baseline
- [ ] CI fails on >20% regression
- [ ] Human-readable comparison table in CI output
- [ ] JSONL event logging for CI artifact retention
- [ ] Baseline update process documented
- [ ] cargo bench runs successfully in CI environment
close_reason: Added tui_perf benchmarks to CI bench.yml workflow, installed critcmp in compare job, added 20% regression threshold gate with PERF_REGRESSION_THRESHOLD env var, TUI benchmark summary in step output, and critcmp comparison that fails CI on regression.

title: Workstream: HTTP Migration to asupersync
description:
# Workstream: HTTP Migration to asupersync

## Goal
Replace reqwest + tokio with asupersync HTTP client across all providers, enabling:
- Structured concurrency with cancel-correct operations
- Deterministic testing via LabRuntime
- Removal of tokio dependency (smaller binary, simpler runtime)
- Unified HTTP/TLS/SQLite stack from asupersync

## Background
asupersync is a sibling library at ../asupersync providing:
- Capability-based context (Cx) for async operations
- Built-in HTTP client with rustls TLS
- Structured cancellation (no orphaned futures)
- Deterministic LabRuntime for testing

Currently, pi_agent_rust has:
- src/http/mod.rs - Module stub
- src/http/client.rs - RequestBuilder that returns "not implemented" error
- src/http/sse.rs - SSE parser ready for integration
- All 4 providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Azure) use reqwest directly

## Technical Approach
1. Implement asupersync HTTP client wrapper in src/http/client.rs
2. Create SSE streaming adapter using existing src/http/sse.rs parser
3. Migrate Anthropic provider first (most complex, has extended thinking)
4. Migrate remaining providers (OpenAI, Gemini, Azure)
5. Remove reqwest + tokio dependencies from Cargo.toml
6. Update all async code to use Cx context

## Dependencies
- asupersync must compile (currently has 3 unused import warnings, otherwise OK)
- SSE parser (src/sse.rs) already exists and is well-tested (9 tests)

## Success Criteria
- [ ] All HTTP requests go through asupersync client
- [ ] SSE streaming works for all providers
- [ ] tokio removed from Cargo.toml
- [ ] reqwest removed from Cargo.toml
- [ ] Tests pass with deterministic LabRuntime
- [ ] No performance regression (benchmark streaming throughput)

## Risks
- asupersync HTTP API may differ from reqwest
- TLS certificate handling may need attention
- Streaming may have subtle behavior differences

## Files Affected
- src/http/mod.rs
- src/http/client.rs
- src/http/sse.rs
- src/providers/anthropic.rs
- src/providers/openai.rs
- src/providers/gemini.rs
- src/providers/azure.rs
- Cargo.toml

title: PARITY-UX.3: Git branch display in interactive footer — watch .git/HEAD

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## PARITY-UX.3: Git Branch in Interactive Footer

### The Gap
pi-mono has a FooterDataProvider (src/core/footer-data-provider.ts) that:
1. Watches .git/HEAD for changes
2. Parses the current branch name
3. Displays it in the interactive mode footer bar

Our footer shows model, tokens, cost — but not the current git branch.

### Implementation Plan
1. Add git_branch: Option<String> to footer/status state
2. On startup and periodically (or via file watcher):
   - Read .git/HEAD
   - If "ref: refs/heads/<branch>" → extract branch name
   - If detached HEAD (raw SHA) → show short SHA
3. Display in footer: "model | branch | tokens | cost"
4. Watch for changes (optional): fswatch .git/HEAD or poll every 5s

### Simpler Alternative
Just read .git/HEAD once at startup + on each turn completion. No file watcher needed. Git branch rarely changes during a session.

### Acceptance Criteria
- Footer shows current git branch when inside a git repo
- Shows nothing when not in a git repo
- Handles detached HEAD (shows short SHA)
- Does not crash if .git/HEAD is missing or malformed

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Testing Requirements

### Unit Tests (tests/footer_git_branch.rs)
1. **Normal branch**: .git/HEAD contains "ref: refs/heads/main" → footer shows "main"

3. **Detached HEAD**: .git/HEAD contains raw SHA "abc123..." → footer shows "abc123" (short SHA, 7 chars)
4. **Not a git repo**: No .git directory → footer shows no branch (no error)
5. **Malformed .git/HEAD**: Empty or corrupted file → no branch shown (no crash)
6. **Worktree**: .git is a file (gitdir reference) → still extracts branch correctly

8. **Branch change**: Switch branches during session (unlikely but test gracefully)

title: Workstream: Release Engineering (1.0 + GitHub Releases + cross-platform CI)
description:
# Goal
Ship a repeatable, low-drama release process for the `pi` binary and the crate(s), including cross-platform CI confidence and GitHub Release artifacts (Linux/macOS/Windows).

# Why This Exists (context)
The port is reaching functional parity and needs a clean path from "it works locally" to "users can install it reliably". The TypeScript version shipped via npm/Bun; this Rust port should ship as:
- `cargo install --path .` for local/dev installs, and later `cargo install pi_agent_rust` (crates.io) once published
- downloadable binaries (GitHub Releases) with checksums

This workstream intentionally separates **feature parity** from **release engineering** so core development isn’t blocked, but release readiness is not left as a vague TODO.

# Non-Goals
- No auto-update mechanism inside the binary (out of scope).
- No Homebrew/AUR packaging (nice-to-have; track separately if desired).

# Deliverables
- Cross-platform CI (at least build; best-effort tests)
- GitHub Release workflow producing versioned binaries + checksums
- `CHANGELOG.md` generation policy (prefer: generated from closed beads)

title: Fix global Buffer array-like length coercion
description: Node Buffer.from(arrayLike) treats a present non-number length as an empty buffer, rejects missing or undefined length, truncates fractional numeric lengths, clamps negative/NaN numeric lengths to zero, and keeps Infinity as a RangeError. Pi's global Buffer shim currently only accepts number-typed length and delegates raw lengths directly to Uint8Array. Add Node vectors and normalize generic array-like length before allocation.

title: [IDEA-WIZARD] Swarm validation slot broker and build budget governor
description:
## Idea-Wizard Phase 1 Reality / Overlap Check
AGENTS.md and README.md were reread before planning. Live Beads show the swarm replay lab is the only open program: bd-in57w.9 is freshly in_progress under AmberOsprey, while bd-in57w.11 and bd-in57w.12 are blocked by it. Agent Mail is red/corrupt for writes, so Beads are the coordination surface.

Recent completed programs already cover swarm autopilot/runpacks, context intelligence, offline replay simulation, replay preview/runpack projection, extension evidence, and resource-budget modeling. This program must not duplicate those. The non-overlapping gap is live validation admission: deciding when agents should launch cargo/rch/UBS/format gates, how many can run, how duplicate broad gates are coalesced, and how stale build/hook slots are recovered without hiding failures.

## Phase 2: 30 Ideas Considered
1. Live validation slot broker for cargo/rch gates.
2. RCH queue and worker health forecaster.
3. Stale build and stuck pre-commit hook detector.
4. Duplicate all-target gate coalescer.
5. Per-bead validation budget planner.
6. Durable build-slot lease ledger.
7. Cargo target and TMPDIR heat map.
8. Scratch-headroom admission policy.
9. RCH fail-open/local-build detector.
10. Fairness policy by bead priority and agent activity.
11. Changed-file impact classifier for validation scope.
12. Reusable validation result cache with provenance.
13. Validation artifact checksum and freshness guard.
14. No-mock validation-broker E2E harness.
15. Operator CLI status/plan surface.
16. Doctor and runpack advisory projection.
17. Failed-gate feedback into next suggested scope.
18. Build-slot expiry and handoff protocol.
19. Reservation-to-validation correlation.
20. Redaction policy for command/output evidence.
21. Large-host NUMA/CPU/memory lane planning.
22. Target-dir warm/preflight recommendation.
23. Perf-regression validation scheduler.
24. Flaky-test quarantine hinting without suppressing failures.
25. Package/module-scoped validation routing.
26. Global backpressure on broad all-target gates.
27. Validation-debt ledger for skipped gates.
28. Offline replay of validation broker decisions.
29. Rich diagnostics/TUI projection.
30. Final closeout evidence gate for broker adoption.

## Winnowed Top 5
1. Validation slot broker and build budget governor: directly reduces compile storms and wasted broad gates on 64+ core swarm hosts.
2. Source-normalized admission policy: combines Beads, RCH, Doctor, git state, cargo_headroom, and scratch headroom into explainable decisions.
3. Duplicate gate coalescer: lets one broad cargo/clippy run satisfy multiple agents when commit, features, env, and scope match.
4. Stale build/hook recovery: detects wedged cargo/rch/UBS/pre-commit paths and emits safe next actions without destructive cleanup.
5. No-mock E2E and closeout evidence: proves the broker over real project artifact shapes, not synthetic optimism.

## Phase 3: Next Best 10 Folded Into Children
RCH forecast, target/TMP heat map, per-bead validation budgets, Doctor/runpack projection, CLI status/plan, fairness policy, artifact checksums, large-host stress budgets, operator docs, and closeout artifact are included as child beads.

## Non-Goals
- Do not replace RCH, cargo_headroom.sh, Beads, Agent Mail, Doctor, runpacks, or CI.
- Do not mutate other agents' code, reservations, build processes, or Beads unless explicitly operating through the broker command being built.
- Do not suppress required gates or convert failures into success.
- Do not make release-facing performance claims without existing claim-integrity gates.
- Do not treat logs, session history, or mailbox archives as disposable cleanup targets.

## Success Criteria
Child beads deliver a contract, lease/store model, source adapters, admission policy, CLI surface, fault corpus, advisory Doctor/runpack integration, no-mock E2E harness, large-host stress evidence, docs, and final closeout artifact. The system helps agents choose the smallest sufficient validation path, coalesce equivalent broad gates, detect stale builds, and preserve fail-closed evidence for required checks.

title: Interactive: route KeyMsg -> action -> behavior
description:
# Goal
Refactor interactive mode input handling so that **key events are interpreted as actions** via the keybinding layer, rather than hard-coded key checks.

# Background
- Legacy pi-mono has `KeybindingsManager` that maps keys to `AppAction`s.
- Many interactive behaviors depend on these actions being consistent across UI states (editor vs picker vs loader).

# Scope / Deliverables
- Introduce an action dispatch step in `src/interactive.rs` update loop:
  1) Receive `bubbletea::Message::Key` (or equivalent)
  2) Canonicalize to `KeyId`
  3) Match against keybindings
  4) Dispatch action to stateful handler

- Ensure behavior works across primary states:
  - Idle editor
  - Streaming/processing
  - Pickers/overlays (session picker, model selector, tree selector, settings)

- Ensure that existing behavior remains correct:
  - Ctrl+C: clear editor; Ctrl+C twice: quit
  - Escape: cancel/abort
  - History navigation remains available (either via default bindings or re-assigned keys)

# Notes / Design Constraints
- Avoid duplicating key logic between components.
- Resolve conflicts deterministically (e.g., if an action is bound to Enter, it must not break text input editing).
- Some actions are *text-editing* operations (cursorLeft, deleteWordBackward). Decide whether to:
  - implement them in our own editor layer, or
  - delegate to bubbles TextArea where possible and only use action router for global actions.

# Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Hard-coded key checks in interactive mode are minimized; keybinding layer is the source of truth.
- [ ] The same action works consistently across modes (e.g., interrupt/cancel).

title: [IDEA-WIZARD] Swarm autopilot and evidence-driven launch control
description:
## Background
Pi now has strong individual swarm diagnostics: doctor swarm preflight, RCH headroom/admission, Agent Mail degraded-mode guidance, Beads ownership, runpacks, flight recorder, memory-pressure replay, and adaptive policy diffs. Operators still have to manually combine those signals into a safe next action under pressure.

## Goal
Build a dry-run, evidence-driven swarm autopilot layer that converts existing diagnostics into a concrete operator plan: claim this bead, wait for RCH, split work by file surface, reopen clearly stale work, switch to docs/source-inspection mode, or produce a handoff bundle.

## Non-Goals
- No autonomous destructive actions.
- No automatic git reset/clean/stash/revert.
- No release-facing performance claims without existing claim-integrity gates.
- No replacement for Beads, Agent Mail, RCH, or doctor as sources of truth.

## Success Criteria
- The plan is machine-readable and human-readable.
- Every recommendation cites exact source evidence and command provenance.
- Degraded Agent Mail and RCH states produce productive fallback actions instead of optimistic green statuses.
- Unit, fixture, and no-mock E2E coverage prove safe behavior for healthy, degraded, and saturated swarm states.

title: [IDEA-WIZARD] Define swarm autopilot input pack and source-status contract
description:

It should normalize existing source artifacts from `pi doctor --only swarm --format json`, `scripts/cargo_headroom.sh --admit-only`, Beads JSON, Agent Mail read/reservation status, git porcelain, optional runpack, and optional activity digest.

## Why
The planner must not scrape prose or infer green states from partial data. It needs deterministic source statuses, freshness, checksums where files are provided, command provenance, and explicit missing/degraded states.

## How
Reuse the source-status style from `scripts/build_swarm_operator_runpack.py`; add a Rust or script-side contract only where it fits existing architecture. Missing required inputs should produce `status=degraded` with actionable blockers, not synthetic defaults.

- JSON schema/example validation.

title: [IDEA-WIZARD] Implement dry-run swarm next-action planner
description:
## What
Implement the core planner that maps an autopilot input pack to ordered recommendations such as `claim_ready_bead`, `wait_for_rch`, `split_by_surface`, `use_beads_soft_lock`, `reopen_stale_bead_candidate`, `run_docs_only_work`, `capture_handoff`, or `stop_and_surface_blocker`.

## Why
Operators should not manually reconcile Beads, RCH, Agent Mail, git, and runpack evidence every time the swarm gets noisy. The planner should reduce hesitation while remaining strictly dry-run and evidence-cited.

## How
Prefer a library-first planner with stable schema `pi.swarm.autopilot_plan.v1`. Each action needs severity, confidence, required preconditions, evidence paths, exact commands to run, and explicit commands that are forbidden or intentionally omitted.

## Tests
- Unit tests for healthy queue, empty queue, degraded Agent Mail, saturated RCH, dirty unrelated files, stale in-progress bead, and missing evidence.
- Golden JSON tests for deterministic action ordering.
- Regression that the planner never emits destructive git/filesystem commands.

## Success Criteria
Given the same input pack, the planner emits a deterministic, non-destructive, evidence-linked plan that a new agent can follow without prior chat context.

title: [IDEA-WIZARD] Add bead-to-file work partition recommendations
description:

## Why
The existing conflict predictor surfaces risk, but agents still need a concrete partitioning hint at claim time. This reduces duplicate work and makes large swarms more fungible.

## How
Use Beads labels/title/body, recent git paths, optional Agent Mail reservations, and existing swarm conflict-predictor data when available. Keep the output diagnostic-only; do not reserve files automatically.

## Tests

- No-mock smoke scenario over a temp Beads workspace with multiple ready tasks.

## Success Criteria
A swarm operator can choose the next non-overlapping bead/file lane from the planner output without opening the full repo history first.

title: [IDEA-WIZARD] Add RCH and Agent Mail failure-action knowledge base
description:
## What
Add a small, versioned failure-action catalog used by the autopilot planner to classify common RCH, cargo, Agent Mail, and Beads failure signatures into exact next actions.

## Why
Many swarm stalls are operational, not code regressions: RCH artifact retrieval disk pressure, remote compile failure, local TMPDIR pressure, Agent Mail missing schema tables, stale build slots, and Beads JSON drift each need different responses.

## How
Start with signatures already represented in doctor/runbook code and recent operator docs. Emit stable IDs, match confidence, user-visible explanation, safe commands, and escalation text. Avoid broad regex rewrites; keep classification bounded and testable.

## Tests
- Fixture tests for known RCH retrieval, local target disk pressure, remote compile failure, unknown RCH failure, Agent Mail schema missing, Agent Mail read-only/degraded, and Beads stale DB warnings.
- Regression that unknown signatures fail closed and preserve raw excerpts.
- Redaction tests for token-like substrings.

## Success Criteria
The autopilot can explain operational blockers with specific safe next commands instead of generic failure prose.

title: [IDEA-WIZARD] Add live swarm budget drift watcher
description:
## What
Extend static swarm preflight into a live budget drift watcher that compares current cgroup, TMPDIR, CARGO_TARGET_DIR, RCH queue, and active-agent counts against the last accepted budget profile.

## Why
A preflight can be green at launch but stale after hours of remote builds, artifact retrieval, or new agents. Operators need a cheap drift signal before raising fanout or starting another heavy validation run.

## How
Use existing resource-governor and doctor data structures where possible. The watcher should emit schema `pi.swarm.budget_drift.v1` with `stable`, `degraded`, or `deny_new_work`, plus exact evidence and recommended fanout adjustments.

## Tests
- Unit tests for CPU quota reduction, memory headroom loss, TMPDIR target drift, RCH queue saturation, and recovered state.
- Fixture replay over multiple samples proving hysteresis/no flapping.
- Docs explaining this is operator admission evidence, not a release speed claim.

## Success Criteria
Autopilot plans can distinguish a still-valid startup budget from a drifted environment and recommend backoff before failures cascade.
