title: Epic: Expand Pi extension corpus (unmodified compatibility)
description: Expand to a 200+ real-world extension corpus (OpenClaw + GitHub/web) and prove unmodified compatibility with deterministic, unfakable conformance + perf/reliability evidence.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
Background
- Current extension sample is 16 official examples in docs/extension-sample.json (pi-mono commit df5b0f...). This is intentionally small and not representative of the full ecosystem.
- Goal from EXTENSIONS.md: run legacy extensions unmodified, avoid per-extension exceptions, keep perf overhead low (<2ms p95/tool call), and keep shims deterministic and auditable.
- Recent perf baselines captured in BENCHMARKS.md (bd-1pb) show where we are now; this epic expands the coverage set while keeping perf + reliability evidence strong.

Problem Statement
We need to dramatically increase the size and scope of the extension corpus we can prove works correctly without modification. That means moving beyond official examples into the most popular community extensions, across all shapes/sizes (tool-only, commands, event hooks, UI, providers, WASM, MCP, multi-file, deps-heavy).

Success Criteria
- A tiered extension corpus (Tier-1 must-pass + Tier-2 stretch) derived from explicit popularity/coverage criteria.
- All Tier-1 extensions run unmodified in PiJS/WASM tiers with no per-extension exceptions.
- Conformance + perf evidence at scale (fixtures + scenario suites + benchmarks) that can be regenerated deterministically.
- Clear catalog manifests with pinned sources, checksums, and provenance for every extension in the corpus.

Non-Goals
- Do not mutate or fork extension sources; if it requires changes, it is a gap in our shims/runtime, not in the extension.

Dependencies/Links
- This epic extends bd-25q (extension compatibility proof) and integrates with extc pipeline (bd-xgo) + conformance harness workstreams.

comments.author: LavenderRobin
comments.text:
SCOPE EXPANSION (2026-02-05)

Why
- The current in-repo corpus (official pi-mono examples + initial community set) is a great start, but it is not enough to prove the extension runtime is robust across the actual ecosystem.
- The ecosystem has grown fast (incl. OpenClaw/ClawHub-style marketplaces + viral adoption), so “popular extensions” now plausibly means 200+ distinct, real-world extensions.

New Targets (explicit, auditable)
- Candidate discovery: >= 1000 raw candidates across all sources.
- Candidate validation: >= 300 “true Pi extensions” (use Pi extension protocol / ExtensionAPI; not merely ‘Claude/agent tools’ with unrelated APIs).
- Tiered corpus selection:
  - Tier-1 (MUST PASS): >= 200 extensions representing what people actually run day-to-day.
  - Tier-2 (STRETCH): additional long-tail / niche extensions with unique API surface.
  - Tier-0 (ALWAYS): official pi-mono examples remain must-pass.

Non-negotiable constraints
- Unmodified: no per-extension source edits; any breakage is fixed in the runtime/shims/pipeline.
- Deterministic + “unfakable” evidence: conformance outputs must be reproducible and diffable (ideally: legacy-vs-rust trace diff + captured fixtures).
- Performance: the expanded set must still meet the budgets (load/event/tool overhead). Scaling cannot regress UX.

What “adding them explicitly” means
- Every selected extension is represented in a catalog/manifest with pinned provenance (repo URL + commit/tag + path), checksums, license status, and scenario linkage.
- Artifacts are archived (or referenced deterministically if redistribution is restricted) so a clean checkout can reproduce the same conformance run.

Primary workstreams in this epic
- bd-d7gn: research/selection (now includes OpenClaw + global ecosystem)
- bd-3kp3: catalog + pinning + manifests
- bd-229m: compat gap analysis at scale
- bd-7wuh: conformance + perf/reliability evidence at scale

comments.author: LavenderRobin
comments.text:
NOTE: RELATIONSHIP TO bd-ofcj

- bd-ofcj is the broader “research→selection→acquire→conformance→perf→docs→refresh” epic across *all* extension shapes.
- bd-po15 is the extension-protocol-specific track (PiJS/QuickJS + unmodified compatibility) and is now a child of bd-ofcj for clarity.

Practical implication
- When in doubt, prefer aligning outputs (catalogs/manifests/tests/logs) with the bd-ofcj pipeline so users see one coherent story.

title: Re-enable runtime parking once asupersync ships AcqRel wake fix (>0.3.2)
description:
src/main.rs:575 sets .enable_parking(false) on the asupersync multi-thread runtime. This is a deliberate workaround: asupersync 0.3.2 (the pinned version) contains a Dekker-style lost-wakeup bug in WorkerCoordinator::wake_one/wake_many (Relaxed atomics in scheduler/three_lane.rs), which can stall a worker that parks while pending I/O is registered. The fix (AcqRel ordering, asupersync commit 8b6e44824, 2026-05-23) landed 3 days AFTER the 0.3.2 release and is NOT yet in any published tag (crates.io tops out at 0.3.2).

With parking disabled the runtime busy-spins idle worker threads -> the primary idle-CPU source reported in #95. The cursor-blink idle churn was fixed separately (init no longer starts the blink loop; blink messages are dropped in update_inner).

ACTION when asupersync >=0.3.3 (containing 8b6e44824) is published: bump the asupersync dep and remove the .enable_parking(false) call (let it default to true). Verify no I/O stalls under load, then idle CPU should drop to ~0. Do NOT remove the flag while pinned to 0.3.2 — it reintroduces the lost-wakeup stall. Relates to PR #95.
close_reason: Stale: the guarded workaround was already removed on 2026-06-13 by c24165a9 (re-enable runtime parking, gh #107) — enable_parking no longer appears anywhere in src/. The bead's release condition is now also satisfied: pi runs asupersync 0.4.4 (bumped 2026-08-14, db90ae63), and the AcqRel lost-wakeup fix 8b6e44824 is a verified ancestor of tag v0.4.4 (git merge-base --is-ancestor). Verification: full cargo test --lib on 0.4.4 with default parking = 7040 passed, zero runtime/I-O stall regressions vs baseline.

title: Remove tokio and reqwest dependencies
description:
# Remove tokio and reqwest dependencies

## Goal
Complete the HTTP migration by removing tokio and reqwest from Cargo.toml.

## Background
After all providers migrate to asupersync, these dependencies become unused:
- tokio (async runtime)
- tokio-stream (stream utilities)
- reqwest (HTTP client)

This reduces binary size and simplifies the dependency tree.

## Implementation Steps

1. **Update Cargo.toml**
```toml
# Remove these lines:
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }
tokio-stream = "0.1"
reqwest = { version = "0.13", ... }

# Ensure asupersync is enabled (currently commented out):
asupersync = { path = "../asupersync", features = ["tls", "tls-native-roots", "sqlite"] }
```

2. **Update main.rs**
```rust
// Before
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() { ... }

// After - use asupersync runtime
fn main() {
    asupersync::runtime::Runtime::new()
        .block_on(async_main())
}
```

3. **Update all async code**
- Replace tokio::spawn with asupersync::spawn
- Replace tokio::time::sleep with asupersync equivalents
- Replace tokio::select! with asupersync patterns
- Update channel usage (if tokio channels used)

4. **Update test harness**
```rust
// Before
#[tokio::test]
async fn test_foo() { ... }

// After
#[asupersync::test]
async fn test_foo() { ... }
```

## Files Affected
- Cargo.toml
- src/main.rs
- src/agent.rs (spawn, select)
- src/tools.rs (bash timeout)
- All test files

## Dependencies
- bd-37l (Anthropic migrated)
- bd-1vo (OpenAI migrated)
- bd-1iy (Gemini migrated)
- bd-ivj (Azure migrated)

## Testing
- cargo build must succeed without tokio
- All tests must pass
- Binary size should decrease (~500KB-1MB)

## Risks
- Some tokio-specific features may need alternatives
- Test harness changes may be extensive

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] tokio not in Cargo.toml
- [ ] reqwest not in Cargo.toml
- [ ] cargo build succeeds
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] Binary size reduced
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] Scope in description implemented fully with no feature loss
[ ] Unit tests cover core success/failure + edge cases for this bead (add regression coverage if applicable)
[ ] Integration/E2E script exercises the end-to-end path (or explicitly marks N/A with rationale in notes) and emits detailed JSONL logs + artifacts per bd-4u9

[ ] Quality gates pass: cargo fmt --check, cargo check --all-targets, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test

title: Event dispatch latency benchmarks (p99 less than 5ms)
description:
# Event dispatch latency benchmarks (p99 < 5ms)

## What
Fire 1000+ events of each type through both runtimes, measure handler response time.

## Events to Benchmark
All ExtensionEvent types: tool_call, tool_result, turn_start, turn_end, before_agent_start, input, context, resources_discover, user_bash, session_before_compact, session_before_tree.

## Method
1. Load a test extension that subscribes to all event types
2. Fire 1000 events per type with varied payloads
3. Measure time from dispatch to handler return
4. Compute P50, P95, P99 for each event type in each runtime

## Target
- P99 < 5ms for all event types in Rust
- Rust P50 < TypeScript P50 (should be faster due to native code)

## Output
- Latency report with percentile breakdown per event type

title: EPIC: Cargo Manifest Hygiene — declare ext_* binaries, clean up dev artifacts
description:
# Background
Cargo.toml declares only `[[bin]] name="pi"` explicitly. The other 17 binaries under src/bin/*.rs (ext_full_validation, ext_release_binary_e2e, ext_workloads, ext_runtime_risk_ledger, pijs_workload, session_workload_bench, etc.) compile via Cargo's implicit discovery. This works but has drawbacks:
- `cargo install --path .` only installs `pi` — not the ops/diagnostic binaries the README promises.
- Tools introspecting Cargo.toml (e.g. release automation, security audits) don't see the ext_* surface.
- Binary-specific features (required-features, bench settings) can't be declared.
- The untracked file `run_test.rs` at repo root is a dev artifact that shouldn't be committed.

# Goal
Explicitly declare every supported binary in Cargo.toml and decide for each whether it's a shipping artifact or a dev-only tool. Clean up rogue root-level .rs files.

# Scope
1. Enumerate src/bin/*.rs (currently 18 files).
2. For each, classify: (a) shipping (add to [[bin]]), (b) dev-only (move to examples/ or xtask/), (c) tombstone.
3. Update Cargo.toml.
4. Delete or move `run_test.rs` after confirming it's stale (requires explicit user approval per AGENTS.md RULE 1 — file the bead with that note).
5. Verify `cargo install --path .` installs the intended set.

# Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each src/bin/* either declared in Cargo.toml [[bin]] or moved/removed with rationale in commit
- [ ] `cargo install --path .` installs the documented binaries
- [ ] `cargo build --all-targets` clean
- [ ] run_test.rs resolved (moved, declared, or user-approved delete)
- [ ] CI job checks that every src/bin/*.rs has a matching [[bin]] declaration

# Considerations / Risks
- Per AGENTS.md RULE 1, file deletion requires explicit user permission. The bead should propose deletion and wait for approval before acting.
- `.gitignore` changes may also be required if some bins are meant to stay untracked.

# Refs
- Cargo.toml
- src/bin/
- AGENTS.md RULE 1 (file deletion)

title: EPIC: Operator Resilience & Continuous Certification — bus factor, signing, weekly verdict
description:
# Background
Pi is explicitly a no-contributions project (README "About Contributions"); the maintainer reviews via agents, not PRs. Bus factor is 1. The installer ships curl|bash with Cosign verification, but a `--no-verify` flag exists. Release automation (publish.yml) exists but isn't continuously exercised. The drop-in certification verdict was last regenerated 2026-02-18 — it should be a live CI artifact, not a static file.

# Goal
Make Pi operationally resilient against (a) maintainer unavailability, (b) supply-chain compromise via installer, (c) silent drift of certification verdict away from reality.

# Scope (child tasks)
- T: Weekly scheduled GH Actions workflow that regenerates docs/dropin-certification-verdict.json and commits if changed.
- T: Installer release-signing audit — ensure `--no-verify` is never used in published install.sh invocations; add a test that verifies the Cosign path happens for every release artifact.
- T: Installer regression harness (tests/installer_regression.sh) — confirm it's run by CI on every release tag.
- T: Document the "lone maintainer incapacity" path (who owns the repo, how to decrypt secrets, how to cut an emergency release) in docs/program-governance.md — add if missing.
- T: Maintenance dashboard bead: weekly burn-down of open critical/high ledger entries.

# Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] .github/workflows/weekly-certification-verdict.yml lands and runs
- [ ] Installer signing path has a passing CI test that detects `--no-verify` regression
- [ ] docs/program-governance.md has "Incapacity Playbook" section
- [ ] All release tags produce Sigstore bundles + SHA256SUMS that the installer verifies

# Refs

- tests/installer_regression.sh
- .github/workflows/publish.yml
- docs/program-governance.md (if exists)
- docs/security/maintenance-playbook.md
- dsr skill (fallback release infrastructure)

title: SDK sessions persist under process cwd instead of SessionOptions working_directory
description:
## Problem
`create_agent_session` resolves `SessionOptions::working_directory` for tools, prompts, and extension paths, but a newly created `Session` keeps `SessionHeader.cwd` from `std::env::current_dir()`. When SDK persistence is enabled, `Session::save` uses `header.cwd` to choose the project session directory, so SDK sessions can be stored under the embedding process cwd instead of the requested working directory.

## Scope
Align new SDK session headers with the resolved SDK working directory before persistence and model selection side effects. Add focused regression coverage that sets process cwd and SDK working_directory to different temp dirs and verifies the saved session path uses the SDK working directory namespace.

## Acceptance
SDK tools/prompt cwd, `SessionHeader.cwd`, and persisted project session directory agree for new SDK sessions. Existing explicit session resume behavior remains unchanged. Agent Mail is corrupt in this repo, so Beads assignee/status/comments are the soft lock.
close_reason: Aligned new SDK session header cwd with SessionOptions working_directory and added persistence regression coverage. title: Fix global Buffer ArrayBuffer byteOffset coercion
description: Node Buffer.from(ArrayBuffer, byteOffset, length) normalizes byteOffset with ToInteger-style coercion: fractional and numeric strings truncate, NaN/null/non-numeric strings become 0, and negative, +/-Infinity, or oversize offsets throw RangeError. Pi's global Buffer shim currently delegates byteOffset directly through the Uint8Array constructor, leaving these edge cases under-specified. Add Node vectors and normalize byteOffset before constructing the Buffer view.
close_reason: Implemented global Buffer ArrayBuffer byteOffset coercion conformance

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## FUZZ-P2.9: Generate Seed Corpora from Existing Test Fixtures

### Why Seed Corpora Matter
Coverage-guided fuzzing (libFuzzer) starts from a seed corpus and mutates inputs to discover new code paths. Good seeds dramatically improve fuzzing effectiveness:
- Random bytes rarely produce valid-enough inputs to reach deep parsing logic
- Real-world examples exercise the common code paths
- Mutations of real examples are more likely to trigger edge cases

### Corpus Sources in This Codebase

1. **VCR Cassettes** (tests/cassettes/):
   - Complete HTTP request/response pairs in JSON
   - Contains real SSE event streams from Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Azure
   - Extract: individual SSE events, response bodies, request bodies

2. **Provider Response Fixtures** (tests/fixtures/provider_responses/):
   - anthropic_stream.json, openai_stream.json, gemini_stream.json, azure_stream.json
   - Contains body_chunks arrays with real SSE data

3. **Conformance Fixtures** (tests/fixtures/conformance/):
   - JSON fixtures for tool behavior testing
   - Contains tool input/output examples

4. **Extension Test Fixtures** (tests/ext_conformance/):
   - Extension registration payloads
   - Tool definitions, event hooks, provider specs

5. **Session Files** (any .jsonl test fixtures):
   - Real session JSONL with messages, model changes, compactions

### Extraction Script Approach
Create a Rust binary or script that:
1. Walks the fixture directories
2. Extracts relevant JSON fragments
3. Writes each fragment as a separate file in the appropriate fuzz/corpus/ directory

```bash
# Directory structure:
fuzz/corpus/
├── fuzz_sse_parser/          # SSE event data from VCR cassettes
├── fuzz_sse_stream/          # Raw bytes from SSE streams
├── fuzz_session_jsonl/       # Session JSONL files
├── fuzz_session_entry/       # Individual session entry JSON
├── fuzz_provider_event/      # Provider-specific event JSON
├── fuzz_message_deser/       # Message JSON from sessions
├── fuzz_config/              # Config JSON variations
├── fuzz_extension_payload/   # Extension registration JSON
├── fuzz_tool_paths/          # Path strings from tool inputs
├── fuzz_grep_pattern/        # Grep patterns from tool inputs
└── fuzz_edit_match/          # Edit old_string/new_string pairs
```

### Manual Edge Case Seeds
In addition to extracted seeds, manually create files for known edge cases:
- SSE: BOM-prefixed, bare CR, empty events, oversized data field (1MB)
- JSONL: empty file, single newline, CRLF, BOM, truncated JSON
- Config: {}, {"alpha": NaN}, {"alpha": -1}, {"window_size": 999999999}
- Paths: ../../etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, very/long/path (4KB), null-byte path
- Messages: empty content, null fields, untagged enum edge cases

### Files to Create
- fuzz/corpus/ directories (one per harness)
- 10+ seed files per corpus directory
- Optional: extraction script (src/bin/extract_fuzz_corpus.rs or a shell script)

### Acceptance Criteria
- Every fuzz harness from P2.2-P2.8 has a populated corpus directory
- Each corpus has at least 10 seed files
- Seeds include both valid inputs and known edge cases
- cargo fuzz run <target> -- -max_total_time=10 uses seeds successfully (visible in coverage)

title: Investigate v0.3.0 binary size growth (26→45 MiB linux-amd64) and re-trim toward a smaller budget
description: v0.3.0 release binaries: linux-amd64 45.3MB, linux-arm64 38.7MB, darwin-amd64 39.3MB, darwin-arm64 32.9MB (release profile: opt-level=z, lto=true, codegen-units=1, strip). Budget raised 26→48 MiB for the release. Suspects: default-on bpe-tokens tiktoken tables, LSP/DAP/MCP/eval kernels, gzip-embedded text assets (8a439774), swc, portable-pty. Run cargo-bloat / cargo llvm-lines per feature, consider making bpe-tokens table subsets lazy/compressed, feature-trimming, and re-lower the budget. Also investigate 12MB delta between linux-amd64 (45.3, machine-outliner+threads) and darwin-arm64 (32.9).
close_reason: Closed by user request (post-v0.3.0 cleanup). Note: working tree has in-flight vendored-BPE work referencing this bead (src/bpe.rs); owner of that WIP may reopen if the size re-trim continues.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION (2026-08-22, darwin-arm64 local + linux-amd64 via rch):

Measured composition (ELF sections, linux-amd64 45.3MB build): .text 20.5MiB, .rodata 15.7MiB, .eh_frame 3.7MiB, .rela.dyn 1.5MiB, .data.rel.ro 1.15MiB. Darwin default build: 32.9MB file, __text 14.0MiB + __const 15.9MiB.

The 12MB linux-darwin delta decomposes as: .text +6.5MiB (platform codegen; the machine-outliner + -Z threads=4 flags in .cargo/config.toml apply to BOTH platforms, so this is x86-64-vs-arm64 linker/codegen reality, not a flag bug), .eh_frame +3.6MiB (generated by C deps — ring et al; -Cforce-unwind-tables=no rebuilt and did NOT shrink it), .rela.dyn +1.5MiB (PIE relocations).

tiktoken-rs contributes exactly the two used tables (o200k 3.6 + cl100k 1.7 = 5.3MiB of .rodata via include_str!). Verified NO dead tables embedded: r50k/p50k/encoder.json/vocab.bpe signatures are absent from the binary (2 copies of the shared 'IQ== 0' first-line = exactly o200k+cl100k). The compressed-vendored-tables trim (2.8MiB saving) was implemented and measured but reverted in 23c5c0b0 with rationale (runtime singleton sharing); respecting that call — do not revive without owner sign-off.

.eh_frame post-link removal (objcopy --remove-section) would save 3.7MiB on linux but breaks RUST_BACKTRACE capture needed by the new crash handler (bd-cv653.7.12) — rejected.

Remaining untested lever: -Z threads=4 and outliner per-flag ablation needs a linux host (rch remote cache does not key on rustflags, so remote flag experiments silently no-op — run cargo locally on linux with RUSTFLAGS variants). Feature set is already minimal: default = sqlite-sessions + tui + bpe-tokens; image-resize/clipboard/wasm-host/url-pdf/syntax-highlighting all opt-in.

Verdict: with the tiktoken trim off the table, no honest path below ~42MB linux-amd64 without dropping default features. Budget 48MiB stands with real headroom 2.7MiB. Recommend close-as-documented or retarget to linux-host flag ablation.

title: Make PermissionDenied filesystem tests deterministic under UID 0
description:
# Problem

The v0.2.0 release full-suite run exposed five tests that rely on chmod(000) producing PermissionDenied. UID 0 legitimately bypasses those mode bits, so the tests fail despite correct product behavior.

# Scope

Audit permission fixtures across tools, session/index, and extension-preflight tests. Replace environmental error-path assumptions with deterministic, root-portable fault fixtures without weakening assertions or skipping root. Audit every 0o000 and 0o444 fixture and retain it only when the test intentionally validates real mode-bit semantics.

# Acceptance criteria

- The same strict assertions run under UID 0 and non-root; no UID skips, permissive early returns, ignores, retries, sleeps, or test-thread serialization.
- Required read, edit, list, scan, open, and try_exists paths deterministically receive io::ErrorKind::PermissionDenied.
- Every 0o000 and 0o444 fixture is audited and either made portable or explicitly retained because it tests real mode-bit semantics.
- Focused permission tests and cargo test --locked --all-targets --features internal-legacy-capture pass under verified root and non-root identities.
- Cleanup restores fixture state even after assertion failure.

# Evidence

Observed during v0.2.0 release validation. Closed bead bd-3f0o covered earlier filesystem failure tests, but no active bead owns this portability regression.
close_reason: Deterministic PermissionDenied fixtures verified under root and non-root: focused slices green in both identities at 31c80d88; fixture audit complete; product enforcement from 44218842/ba4b223c confirmed intact

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Closure audit (BeigeCat, 2026-08-23): (1) No #[ignore] and no euid-conditional test skips exist in src/. (2) Zero raw 0o000/0o444 error-path fixtures remain — all denial sites route through RAII UnixModeGuard::apply/set (src/session.rs, session_picker.rs, session_sqlite.rs, tools.rs, models.rs, providers/model_fetch.rs, extension_preflight.rs, session_store_v2.rs) with Drop-based restore; retained 0o600/0o755 fixtures intentionally assert real mode-bit semantics (privacy/executable stubs). (3) Product-side determinism landed in 44218842 + ba4b223c (effective mode-class enforcement so kernel DAC bypass cannot silence chmod faults). (4) Fresh focused-slice verification at 31c80d88: NON-ROOT permission=89 denied=29 denial=8 effective_=19 private_perm=1 ALL PASS; ROOT (euid 0): identical slices ALL PASS (permission 89, denied 29, denial 8, effective_ 19). Full non-root suite enforced continuously by CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml:740 cargo test --locked --all-targets --features internal-legacy-capture). Verification notes: root runs require an ownership-honoring TMPDIR and pristine HOME — on noowners-mounted APFS volumes platform.rs class selection sees euid!=owner and denies via other-class (environment artifact, not a defect); one transient denial-filter flake observed once under saturating compile load, unreproducible across three isolated reruns.

title: EPIC: Tracker ↔ Gap Ledger Reconciliation — eliminate bead completion illusion
description:
# Background
As of the reality-check audit on 2026-04-17, .beads had 0 open beads / 2,204 closed / 8 tombstone. Simultaneously, docs/dropin-parity-gap-ledger.json listed open critical and high-severity parity gaps. This is classic "bead completion illusion": the tracker is drained, so br ready returns empty, so agent swarms idle — while real gaps persist outside the tracker.

# Goal
Establish a bidirectional invariant: for every open critical/high entry in docs/dropin-parity-gap-ledger.json there exists an open bead referencing it, and vice versa. Make the invariant CI-enforced so it cannot silently drift again.

# Scope
1. Parse docs/dropin-parity-gap-ledger.json; for each open critical/high entry, create a corresponding bead with `external_ref=<gap-id>` (or add to existing bead's refs).
2. Add a script scripts/reconcile_beads_ledger.sh that diffs the two and reports orphans (ledger entry without bead, bead without ledger entry).
3. Add CI job that runs this script on every push to main and fails if orphans exist.
4. Document the invariant in AGENTS.md so future agents honor it.

# Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] scripts/reconcile_beads_ledger.sh lands and is idempotent
- [ ] For every open critical/high ledger entry, a bead exists with matching external-ref
- [ ] CI job `beads_ledger_reconciliation` runs on every PR, fails closed on drift
- [ ] AGENTS.md section added: "Bead ↔ Ledger Invariant"
- [ ] Initial reconciliation run produces zero orphans

# Considerations / Risks
- Gap-ledger schema evolution may break the reconciliation script. Use docs/dropin-parity-gap-ledger.json's own schema as source of truth and pin the schema version.
- Closed beads don't need ledger entries; the invariant is OPEN-side only.

# Refs
- docs/dropin-parity-gap-ledger.json
- docs/dropin-certification-contract.json
- AGENTS.md (needs update)

title: FUZZ-P2.4: Provider Stream libfuzzer harnesses — coverage-guided fuzzing for all providers
close_reason: Implemented provider stream fuzz harness covering all 7 providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Cohere, OpenAI Responses, Azure, Vertex). Added fuzz::Processor wrappers with Default impls, fuzz_exports in lib.rs, fuzz_provider_event target, and 19 seed corpus files. 156K iterations in 10s with zero crashes.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## FUZZ-P2.4: Provider Stream libfuzzer Harnesses

### Why This is P0 Priority
Provider stream parsers process UNTRUSTED API RESPONSES from external LLM services. A malicious or misconfigured API proxy could send crafted SSE events designed to crash the client. All 6+ providers have independent parsing code with independent bug potential.

### Harness Architecture
Create ONE parameterized harness that can target different providers:

```rust
// fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_provider_event.rs
#\![no_main]
use libfuzzer_sys::fuzz_target;
use arbitrary::Arbitrary;

#[derive(Arbitrary, Debug)]
struct FuzzInput {
    provider: u8,  // 0-5 maps to Anthropic/OpenAI/Gemini/Azure/Vertex/Bedrock
    event_type: String,
    event_data: String,
}

fuzz_target\!(|input: FuzzInput| {
    match input.provider % 6 {
        0 => fuzz_anthropic_event(&input.event_type, &input.event_data),
        1 => fuzz_openai_event(&input.event_type, &input.event_data),
        2 => fuzz_gemini_event(&input.event_type, &input.event_data),
        3 => fuzz_azure_event(&input.event_type, &input.event_data),
        4 => fuzz_vertex_event(&input.event_type, &input.event_data),
        _ => fuzz_bedrock_event(&input.event_type, &input.event_data),
    }
});
```

### Per-Provider Fuzz Functions
Each provider's process_event() takes (event_type, data_string) and returns StreamEvent. The fuzz function:
1. Calls process_event() with arbitrary type and data
2. Asserts no panic
3. For valid events, verifies output StreamEvent is well-formed

### Critical Code Paths Per Provider

**Anthropic**: 
- content_block_delta with tool_use type → accumulates JSON in current_tool_json
- index field → used as usize array index without bounds check
- usage.input_tokens/output_tokens → could be negative

**OpenAI**:
- choices[0].delta.tool_calls[0].function.arguments → deeply nested path
- finish_reason parsing → what if unknown string?
- usage object format differs from Anthropic

**Gemini**:
- candidates[0].content.parts[0] → deeply nested
- functionCall format → different JSON shape from OpenAI/Anthropic
- safetyRatings array → could be empty or malformed

### Seed Corpus
Extract event JSON from VCR cassettes:
- tests/fixtures/provider_responses/anthropic_stream.json
- tests/fixtures/provider_responses/openai_stream.json
- tests/fixtures/provider_responses/gemini_stream.json
- tests/fixtures/provider_responses/azure_stream.json
- Parse each cassette, extract individual SSE events as seed files

### Expected Findings
- Index out of bounds in Anthropic content block delta handling
- Panic on missing nested fields in Gemini response parsing
- Integer overflow in token count aggregation

### Files to Create
- fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_provider_event.rs
- fuzz/corpus/fuzz_provider_event/ (seed files from VCR cassettes)

### Acceptance Criteria
- Harness covers at least 3 providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini)
- Seed corpus includes real events from each provider's VCR cassettes
- 5-minute fuzz run per provider completes without crashes
- Any crashes → triaged, minimized, fixed

title: [IDEA-WIZARD] Swarm progress SLO and saturation convergence program
description:
## Background
The queue is empty after recent idea-wizard programs closed swarm autopilot, validation broker, context intelligence, swarm replay, tool-output cache, and operator runpack surfaces. The remaining operator gap is not another source of truth or another planner: it is a read-only progress-SLO timeline that helps humans decide whether a 64+ core / 256GiB multi-agent swarm is making useful forward progress, merely spinning on coordination/build activity, or converging to saturation where new review/idea work should be generated.

## Idea-Wizard Phase 2: 30 -> 5 winnowed ideas
1. Swarm progress SLO timeline: derive useful-progress, stalled-progress, and saturation-convergence signals from Beads, git commits, validation broker/RCH posture, Agent Mail health, and runpack evidence without mutating any source.
2. Read-only progress CLI and JSON schema: expose stable JSON/text output suitable for runbooks and CI/operator handoff.
3. No-mock progress E2E: use temp git and temp Beads plus fixture-captured degraded Agent Mail/RCH to prove healthy, stalled, saturated, and malformed-source paths.
4. Operator runpack/doctor projection: make progress posture visible beside existing autopilot/context/broker summaries while preserving authority boundaries.
5. Closeout gate: require a prompt-to-artifact checklist before the epic can close.

## Idea-Wizard Phase 3: next-best 10 retained as constraints
- Distinguish real commits/closed beads from noisy file churn.
- Detect long-lived in-progress beads only when stale by evidence, not merely because Agent Mail is corrupt.
- Preserve privacy by redacting agent/message/path excerpts and avoiding raw prompt bodies.
- Treat missing or malformed source artifacts as degraded, never green.
- Emit machine-readable reasons with stable IDs so future runpacks can classify outcomes.
- Keep all Cargo-heavy validation behind rch.
- Do not replace Beads, Agent Mail, RCH, Doctor, runpacks, validation broker, context intelligence, or release evidence gates.
- Include unit tests, contract tests, no-mock E2E, logging evidence, and docs.
- Support large-host scale budgets as engineering evidence only, not release performance claims.
- Keep the first implementation slice narrow enough for a single agent to ship safely.

## Non-goals
No live mutation, no automatic bead claiming, no Agent Mail writes, no release-facing performance claims, and no compatibility shims.

## Done
All child beads are closed, mapped to code/tests/docs/evidence/commands/commits, graph validation passes, staged UBS and Beads ledger reconciliation pass, and main plus main:master are pushed.

title: Task: Implement agent lifecycle event dispatch (agent_start/agent_end)
Interactive: /tree full navigator UI + branch summarization
description:
# Goal
Implement legacy `/tree` semantics and interactive UI as described in `legacy .../docs/tree.md`.

# Required UI/Controls (legacy)
- Display a depth-first tree list with indentation.
- Mark the current leaf as `← active`.
- Controls:
  - Up/Down: move selection
  - Enter: select
  - Escape/Ctrl+C: cancel
  - Ctrl+U: toggle user messages only
  - Ctrl+O: toggle show-all (include custom/label entries)

# Selection Behavior (legacy)
- Selecting a **user message** or **custom message**:
  1) leaf set to parent of selected node (or null if root)
  2) message text placed in editor for re-submission
- Selecting a **non-user message**:
  1) leaf set to selected node
  2) editor remains empty

# Branch Summarization (legacy)
Before switching branches, user chooses:
1) No summary
2) Summarize (default prompt)
3) Summarize with custom prompt

Summarize the abandoned path from old leaf back to common ancestor (or stop at compaction node).
Store result as a branch_summary entry and attach to the new leaf.

# Implementation Notes
- Current Rust `/tree` is a non-interactive listing + manual switch; this task replaces that with a selector.
- Reuse existing session tree operations where possible (`Session::list_leaves`, `navigate_to`, `append_branch_summary`).
- Ensure agent context is updated after switching leaf.

# Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `/tree` UX and semantics match legacy docs.
- [ ] Optional summary is created/stored correctly.
- [ ] Selecting a user message pre-fills the editor.

title: Target Asupersync leverage where it clearly improves Pi correctness and robustness
description:
This epic captures a targeted Asupersync leverage review for Pi after rereading AGENTS.md and README.md, walking the repo architecture, and checking the local Asupersync skill/docs. The project already uses Asupersync in the places that matter most: runtime bootstrap, provider HTTP/TLS, many async primitives, extension budgets/deadlines, deterministic testing in selected areas, and outcome-sensitive SQLite session handling. The intent here is therefore not "use more Asupersync everywhere" and definitely not "rewrite the app to look more like an Asupersync demo".

The actual opportunity is narrower and more valuable: several core app/session/RPC/TUI flows still create fresh request contexts when inherited cancellation/budget semantics would be better; some long-lived loops still lack explicit checkpoint discipline; and some blocking/background work still lives on raw threads rather than runtime-owned blocking lanes. Every child bead under this epic is framed as a decision-quality investigation or targeted refactor so we only land the subset that is plainly accretive for correctness, robustness, and performance.
design:
Architectural findings to preserve:
- Pi already boots on an Asupersync runtime and reactor rather than a compatibility shell.
- Provider transport already respects timer-driver-aware timeout behavior.
- The extension system already uses Budget/Cx/deadline handling in a way that should be treated as the local exemplar.
- SQLite-backed session handling already maps Outcome::{Ok, Err, Cancelled, Panicked} intentionally.

Primary candidate areas for improvement:
- Context propagation in session, agent, interactive, and RPC surfaces.
- Explicit cx.checkpoint() usage in long-lived loops that should promptly honor cancellation.
- Targeted migration of high-value blocking/thread islands.
- More deterministic tests for app/session/TUI semantics, especially around budgets, deadlines, and shutdown.
- A narrow supervision/AppSpec evaluation only if current topology reveals a concrete lifecycle hazard.

Non-goals:
- No broad runtime rewrite.
- No cargo-cult replacement of every std::thread::spawn.
- No disruption of provider/runtime paths that are already structurally sound.
- No supervision/AppSpec adoption just because the library offers it.
acceptance_criteria: This epic is complete when the child graph separates landed versus deferred Asupersync leverage ideas explicitly, each landed change carries focused coverage, and the final outcome is a narrow high-ROI improvement set rather than a broad rewrite.
notes: Representative review surfaces include src/main.rs, src/agent_cx.rs, src/http/client.rs, src/session.rs, src/rpc.rs, src/interactive.rs, src/agent.rs, src/tools.rs, src/compaction_worker.rs, src/extensions.rs, and src/session_sqlite.rs.
close_reason: Completed with a narrow high-ROI subset rather than a rewrite. Landed work includes inherited-context propagation, explicit checkpoint/cancel-correctness improvements, runtime-managed session/compaction worker ownership where it clearly improved lifecycle semantics, and focused deterministic coverage for the changed surfaces. Deferred work is explicit: broad supervision/AppSpec adoption remains unjustified, and subprocess pipe pumps stay on dedicated threads unless measured evidence says otherwise.

title: Inventory precise Asupersync leverage candidates across Pi core surfaces
description: Create an implementation-grade inventory of the exact places where additional Asupersync leverage might actually matter in Pi core surfaces. This bead is the translation layer between the high-level architecture assessment and future implementation work: it should leave behind an exact map of candidate call sites and a keep/refactor/defer recommendation for each cluster, so nobody has to rediscover the same search space later.
design:
Inventory output should explicitly group findings into three buckets:
- Fresh request-context creation sites that likely should inherit an existing Cx, budget, or deadline instead.
- Raw thread or bespoke blocking-worker islands that might benefit from runtime-managed blocking execution.
- Long-lived loops that may need explicit checkpoint participation.

For each cluster, capture:
- Exact modules and functions involved.
- Why the current approach may be correct, suspicious, or clearly wrong.
- What a minimal targeted refactor would look like.
- What should remain unchanged even if it superficially looks less pure.
acceptance_criteria: The inventory is complete when it names concrete modules and functions to revisit, assigns each cluster a keep, refactor, or defer recommendation with reasoning, and is detailed enough that downstream workstream owners do not need to rerun the original archaeology before starting.
notes: This bead must distinguish structural opportunities from aesthetic ones and should only flag sites where better Asupersync leverage would plausibly improve cancel-correctness, deadline propagation, quiescent shutdown, or runtime ownership.
close_reason: Completed: documented implementation-grade Asupersync leverage inventory in docs/asupersync-leverage-inventory.md and indexed it in README.md

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: Seed findings from the initial architecture pass: src/agent_cx.rs already contains the correct mixed-boundary helper; src/session.rs, src/rpc.rs, src/interactive.rs, and parts of src/agent.rs create fresh request contexts in places that deserve a closer look; src/tools.rs and session persistence paths still contain raw thread or blocking-worker islands; extensions are the best in-repo example of deliberate Budget and Cx usage.

title: Refactor core flows to inherit structured Asupersync context instead of resetting request scope
description: Refactor the high-value core flows that currently reset themselves to a fresh request scope even when they are already executing under a structured Asupersync task. The codebase already has AgentCx::for_current_or_request() for mixed-boundary helpers, but several session, RPC, and interactive paths still call AgentCx::for_request() directly.
design:
Working rules:
- Prefer explicit Cx or AgentCx threading where it is locally clear and does not explode signatures.
- Use AgentCx::for_current_or_request() when a helper genuinely needs to function both inside and outside an ambient structured task.
- Keep truly top-level boundaries free to create a fresh request-scoped Cx.
- Do not weaken extension-specific budget logic while improving core-surface inheritance.
acceptance_criteria: This workstream is complete when high-value session, RPC, and interactive paths stop resetting to a fresh infinite request scope without a documented reason, inherited budgets and deadlines are preserved across changed paths, and focused coverage exists for the semantic change.
notes: This is about semantic leverage, not stylistic purity: keep real fresh-context boundaries, but remove accidental resets that erase inherited cancellation or deadline semantics.
close_reason: Closure audit: child slices bd-xdcrh.2.1/.2.2/.2.3 landed inherited AgentCx across session, RPC, and interactive/background high-value flows with focused cancellation/deadline coverage; current-tree recheck shows targeted surfaces now use for_current_or_request semantics while remaining for_request sites are boundary/bootstrap paths.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: The key nuance here is that not every direct for_request() call is wrong. The problem is specifically the accidental reset of inherited deadline, budget, and cancellation semantics inside already-structured high-level flows. This workstream should improve those semantics without turning the codebase into a signature-plumbing science project.

title: Thread inherited AgentCx through session and extension-session helpers
description: Focus on session-heavy surfaces first: session handles, extension-session adapters, and adjacent helpers that currently create fresh request-scoped contexts for locks, file operations, or state inspection even when they are already running under a structured task.
design:
Implementation guidance:
- Start with session adapters that sit directly on user-facing or extension-facing control paths.
- Prefer explicit Cx plumbing where the seam is small and frequently exercised.
- Use for_current_or_request() instead of unconditional for_request() when trait or object boundaries make explicit threading awkward.
- Preserve top-level constructors and background bootstrap sites that genuinely need a fresh request boundary.
acceptance_criteria: This bead is complete when the targeted session and extension-session helpers inherit the ambient Cx when one exists, affected lock or file operations honor inherited cancellation and deadline semantics, and regression coverage exists for the changed behavior.
notes: Primary target areas live in src/session.rs and the agent-to-session boundary surfaces that call into it; keep the scope on hot and high-value paths instead of normalizing every helper in one sweep.
close_reason: Completed

title: Thread inherited AgentCx through RPC control, model, and thinking paths
description: Refactor RPC control, model, and thinking paths so they preserve inherited Asupersync context instead of silently minting a fresh one. These surfaces sit on user-visible control flows and can affect reasoning controls, model operations, retries, and compaction triggers.
design:
Implementation guidance:
- Work from the RPC entry and control path inward rather than scattering leaf-level changes with no topological plan.
- Keep this bead focused on context inheritance, not unrelated RPC correctness bugs.
- If an overlap appears with existing RPC issue bd-12e5i, coordinate scope so the two issues complement rather than duplicate each other.
acceptance_criteria: This bead is complete when the changed RPC control, model, and thinking paths preserve inherited budget, deadline, and cancellation semantics, unrelated RPC behavior has not regressed, and focused coverage exists for the touched flows.
notes: Primary target area is src/rpc.rs plus the tightly coupled helper surfaces it drives; treat this as a semantic-runtime task rather than a generic RPC cleanup.
close_reason: Inherited AgentCx across RPC run/spawn/model/thinking helpers with focused cancellation regressions; verified via rch cargo test/fmt/check/clippy.

title: Thread inherited AgentCx through interactive and agent background tasks
description: Refactor interactive and agent background tasks so spawned work inherits the right Asupersync context instead of defaulting to a fresh request scope without a clear boundary reason. This includes bridge tasks, background orchestration, and helper layers where shutdown and cancellation semantics matter more than convenience.
design:
Implementation guidance:
- Inspect task-spawn boundaries first, then the helper calls they make.
- Preserve real bootstrap boundaries, but remove accidental resets inside already-owned task trees.
- Favor clarity over maximal surface-area conversion; the result should make shutdown and cancellation behavior easier to reason about.
acceptance_criteria: This bead is complete when the targeted interactive and agent background flows preserve inherited context where appropriate, shutdown and cancellation semantics are clearer and more structurally aligned with the runtime, and the changed paths have focused coverage or targeted integration tests.
notes: Primary target areas include src/interactive.rs and adjacent background orchestration surfaces, which are likely places for subtle works normally but weak under deadline or cancel behavior.
close_reason: Completed interactive/background AgentCx inheritance refactor with focused cancellation regression coverage

title: Tighten cancel-correctness in long-lived loops with explicit checkpoint discipline
description: Strengthen cancel-correctness in long-lived loops by adding explicit checkpoint discipline where it matters. Asupersync's cancellation model is strongest when loops cooperate at safe boundaries, but higher-level Pi app code currently uses relatively little explicit checkpointing compared with lower-level library-adjacent code.
design:
Working rules:
- Add checkpoints only at safe boundaries where cancellation should be observed promptly.
- Do not insert checkpoints in linear commit sections where doing so would make a previously atomic effect partially cancellable.
- Favor a small number of well-justified checkpoints over blanket instrumentation.
- Use the inventory bead to identify loops that are both long-lived and semantically important.
acceptance_criteria: This workstream is complete when the selected long-lived loops honor cancellation with bounded latency, checkpoints are placed at documented safe boundaries, and the resulting behavior is covered by focused tests.
notes: This workstream should produce explicit reasoning for why each checkpoint is safe at its insertion site; library preference alone is not sufficient justification.
close_reason: Completed via bd-xdcrh.3.1, bd-xdcrh.3.2, and bd-xdcrh.3.3: safe checkpoint boundaries were mapped, the approved loop checkpoints landed, and the changed flows now have regression coverage.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: Asupersync rewards explicit cooperation with cancellation. Lower-level library-adjacent code already uses checkpoint discipline more than higher-level Pi app code does. This workstream exists to add a small number of high-value checkpoints at semantically safe boundaries, not to spray checkpoint calls everywhere.

title: Define safe checkpoint boundaries for shell, session, stream, and UI loops
description: Before editing loops, define the exact safe checkpoint boundaries for each candidate path. This is where we decide which loops should cooperate with cancellation, where within each loop the cancellation boundary belongs, and which loops should remain unchanged because they are too small, too linear, or already indirectly bounded.
design:
For each candidate loop, record:
- The module and function.
- Why the loop is long-lived enough to matter.
- Where a checkpoint could safely live.
- Which operations inside the loop must stay indivisible.
- What cancellation behavior we expect after the change.
acceptance_criteria: This bead is complete when candidate loops are listed with explicit safe and unsafe checkpoint locations, each proposed insertion point has semantic rationale, and the output is concrete enough to drive implementation directly.
notes: Likely candidates include shell or process output aggregation, session or persistence loops, stream aggregation, and interactive or UI event loops, but the inventory bead should narrow this list before code changes begin.
close_reason: Mapped safe/unsafe checkpoint boundaries in docs/asupersync-leverage-inventory.md

title: Implement approved checkpoint insertions without breaking linear-effect regions
description: Implement the approved checkpoint insertions from the mapping bead. The emphasis is on a small set of high-value loops where earlier cancellation observation clearly improves responsiveness or shutdown behavior without compromising correctness.
design:
Implementation guidance:
- Land checkpoints only where CANCEL_MAP approved them.
- Keep surrounding logic easy to audit.
- If a candidate site turns out to have a hidden linear-effect hazard, back it out and document why.
acceptance_criteria: This bead is complete when the approved loops checkpoint at the intended boundaries, no atomic or linear effect region became accidentally cancellable, and the changed behavior is backed by regression coverage.
notes: This should remain a deliberately small patch set whose quality bar is semantic clarity rather than maximizing the number of inserted checkpoint calls.
close_reason: Implemented the approved checkpoint sites in src/tools.rs, src/rpc.rs, and src/agent.rs, documented the deliberate defers in docs/asupersync-leverage-inventory.md, and added focused cancellation/checkpoint regression tests for each changed loop.

title: Add regression coverage for cancellation latency and deadline honoring in looped flows
description: Add regression coverage for cancellation latency and deadline honoring in the looped flows touched by this workstream. These tests should prove that the checkpoint changes are actually doing something useful and should avoid flaky wall-clock timing whenever a deterministic timer-driver or lab-style harness is available.
design:
Testing guidance:
- Prefer deterministic or semi-deterministic timing control when possible.
- Assert behavior that matters: prompt cancellation observation, bounded deadline honoring, and no broken output or persistence semantics.
- Keep each test tied to the specific loop behavior that motivated the checkpoint.
acceptance_criteria: This bead is complete when each changed looped flow has regression coverage for cancellation or deadline behavior, the tests would fail for the right reason if checkpoint cooperation disappeared, and the suite avoids unnecessary flakiness.
notes: Use the extension and runtime test patterns already present in this repo as the local reference for preferring deterministic timing semantics over wall-clock sleeps wherever practical.
close_reason: Implemented the approved checkpoint sites in src/tools.rs, src/rpc.rs, and src/agent.rs, documented the deliberate defers in docs/asupersync-leverage-inventory.md, and added focused cancellation/checkpoint regression tests for each changed loop.

title: Replace only the high-value raw thread islands with runtime-managed blocking work
description: Evaluate and improve the places where core Pi surfaces still rely on raw threads or bespoke blocking-worker patterns. This is not a blanket replace threads with spawn_blocking effort. Some raw threads, especially around subprocess pipe pumping or other hard-blocking OS interactions, may remain the right choice.
design:
Working rules:
- Classify first, migrate second.
- Record explicit keep or migrate reasoning for each worker island.
- Use runtime-managed blocking work only when it genuinely improves semantics or lifecycle behavior.
- Preserve simple dedicated-thread designs where OS or blocking behavior makes them the clearest correct choice.
acceptance_criteria: This workstream is complete when the high-value worker islands are evaluated explicitly, approved migrations land with tests and rationale, and deferred raw-thread islands remain by decision rather than neglect.
notes: Likely focus areas include session JSONL persistence and rewrite paths, compaction or background worker ownership, and the subprocess output pump threads in src/tools.rs.
close_reason: Completed: the high-value worker islands were evaluated explicitly and resolved conservatively. Session JSONL persistence migrated to runtime-managed blocking execution in bd-xdcrh.4.1 (24627488), background compaction moved under runtime ownership in bd-xdcrh.4.2 (95081cdd), subprocess pipe pumps were explicitly kept/deferred in the committed bd-xdcrh.4.3 inventory decision, and bd-xdcrh.4.4 therefore closed as a no-op because no further worker migration patch remained.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: Some raw threads in this repo may still be the right answer, especially for hard-blocking subprocess pipe reads. This workstream is intentionally framed as evaluation-first so future contributors know the difference between an intentional dedicated-thread design and an unexamined legacy island.

title: Evaluate session JSONL persistence workers for spawn_blocking_io migration
description: Evaluate session JSONL persistence and rewrite workers to determine whether they should move onto runtime-managed blocking I/O lanes. These paths are strong candidates because they already embody durable file semantics and may benefit from clearer runtime ownership without the complexity of process I/O edge cases.
design:
Decision criteria:
- Would spawn_blocking_io or a nearby runtime-owned primitive preserve or improve durability semantics?
- Would migration make cancellation, shutdown, or quiescence easier to reason about?
- Would migration reduce bespoke thread and channel scaffolding without hiding failure behavior?
acceptance_criteria: This bead is complete when the relevant session persistence worker sites are cataloged, a clear migrate or defer decision with reasoning is recorded, and any approved migration path is specific enough for implementation without repeating the evaluation.
notes: Primary target area is src/session.rs, especially the append and rewrite worker islands used for JSONL persistence; preserve file-system correctness guarantees first and runtime elegance second.
close_reason: Completed

title: Evaluate compaction and adjacent background workers for runtime ownership
description: Evaluate compaction and adjacent background-worker ownership for possible runtime-managed execution. The key question is whether these workers currently live outside the runtime in a way that meaningfully weakens quiescent shutdown, cancellation composition, or lifecycle reasoning.
design:
Decision criteria:
- What currently owns the worker lifecycle?
- How does shutdown happen today?
- Would runtime ownership make close-to-quiescence behavior more explicit or merely more complicated?
- Is there a targeted migration path that avoids broad architectural churn?
acceptance_criteria: This bead is complete when compaction and background worker ownership is mapped clearly, a migrate or defer decision exists with lifecycle-focused reasoning, and any recommended implementation scope is narrow and explicit.
notes: Primary target area is src/compaction_worker.rs plus any directly coupled session-index or background ownership surfaces that materially affect runtime lifecycle reasoning.
close_reason: Rehosted background compaction onto runtime with abort-on-timeout and drop

title: Decide whether tool subprocess pipe pumps should remain dedicated threads
description: Decide whether the subprocess stdout and stderr pump threads in the tools layer should remain dedicated raw threads or be partially absorbed into runtime-managed structure. This bead exists partly as a safeguard against over-eager cleanup: hard-blocking pipe readers are exactly the sort of place where a dedicated thread can still be the cleanest answer.
design:
Decision criteria:
- Does the current pipe-pump design introduce a real correctness, shutdown, or observability problem?
- Would a runtime-managed alternative genuinely improve semantics, or just move blocking complexity around?
- If the answer is to keep dedicated threads, record that decision explicitly and explain why.
acceptance_criteria: This bead is complete when the subprocess pipe-pump design is evaluated explicitly, the bead records a keep or migrate decision with concrete failure-mode reasoning, and future contributors can tell whether the raw-thread choice is intentional.
notes: Primary target area is the shell and bash tool path in src/tools.rs, and this bead is allowed to conclude that the current dedicated-thread approach is the right design.

title: Implement approved worker migrations and preserve rationale for deferred thread islands

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
Topology/lifecycle mapping summary after rereading the current tree:

1. Process root
- `src/main.rs:430-438` builds one multi-thread Asupersync runtime and runs the top-level CLI future on it.
- `src/main.rs:1230-1233` threads that runtime handle into `AgentSession`, so higher-level surfaces can reuse one ownership root instead of inventing ad hoc runtimes.

2. Session ownership spine
- `AgentSession` is the real per-session ownership node: provider agent + shared session mutex + extension region + background compaction worker (`src/agent.rs:5050-5077`).
- Background compaction is already runtime-managed, quota-bounded, abortable on drop, and only falls back to a dedicated runtime when no handle was injected (`src/compaction_worker.rs:56-160`, `src/agent.rs:5402-5483`).
- Pending idle extension actions are replayed through the same session object rather than a detached sidecar service (`src/agent.rs:6069-6162`).

3. Interactive topology
- Bubble Tea owns the foreground UI loop, while async work is delegated onto the shared runtime (`src/interactive.rs:1556-1584`).
- Per-turn interactive agent work uses runtime-spawned tasks plus per-action abort handles (`src/interactive/agent.rs:1192-1288`, `1336-1449`, `1577-1708`).
- I landed one small lifecycle improvement here: after `Program::run()` returns, `run_interactive()` now explicitly sends `PiMsg::UiShutdown` so the async->UI bridge can exit promptly even if some sender clones outlive the TUI (`src/interactive.rs:1556-1569`).

4. RPC topology
- RPC intentionally keeps two raw blocking bridge threads for stdin/stdout (`src/rpc.rs:352-389`), with the actual request/extension orchestration living on the runtime (`src/rpc.rs:399-520`, `1921-2095`).
- `run_bash_rpc()` also intentionally keeps dedicated stdout/stderr pump threads and explicitly avoids joining them because descendant processes may inherit pipes and otherwise hang shutdown (`src/rpc.rs:4098-4280`). This is a real reason to *not* blindly migrate that island into a generic supervised abstraction.

5. Concrete lifecycle hazard already identified in-tree
- Extension runtime shutdown is the one place where explicit quiescence clearly matters: both print and interactive paths already call `ExtensionRegion::shutdown().await` to avoid QuickJS GC assertions (`src/main.rs:1494-1500`, `4594-4600`).
- `ExtensionRegion::drop` is deliberately best-effort only (`src/extensions.rs:23942-24008`), which reinforces that explicit shutdown is the important contract, not a repo-wide supervision rewrite.

Conclusion for parent `bd-xdcrh.6`
- No broad AppSpec/supervision rollout is justified from the current topology alone.
- The code already has a usable ownership spine: main runtime -> AgentSession -> mode-specific bridges/tasks.
- The narrow high-value follow-through is to keep making shutdown edges explicit where bridges or runtimes cross blocking/UI boundaries, while leaving intentional raw-thread islands (stdio and subprocess pipe pumps) alone unless they demonstrate a concrete failure mode.

title: Extensions: extc pipeline (SWC) + cache + compat scanner
description:
Background:
- JS/TS extensions need a deterministic build pipeline to run as-is without Node/Bun.
- The pipeline must rewrite legacy APIs into connector hostcalls and enforce compatibility.
- Assume **QuickJS has no WebAssembly**: wasm-using JS bundles must be supported via PiWasm (bd-1ry) or compiled artifacts.

Steps:
- Implement extc build pipeline with SWC: bundle, tree-shake, and emit target artifact (QuickJS bytecode) with source maps.
- Run a static compatibility scan (forbidden APIs, Node/Bun globals, unsafe patterns) and emit a deterministic **evidence ledger**.
- Apply protocol shims/rewrite passes to map legacy APIs to:
  - Node shim modules (`pi:node/*`) implemented on connectors (bd-3d0/bd-2sr), and/or
  - direct `pi.*` connector calls where semantics are preserved.
  - MUST handle both `node:*` and bare builtins (`fs`, `path`, `child_process`, `module`, ...).
- Inject required polyfills deterministically (e.g. Buffer/process/fetch/WebAssembly bridge) per the contract.
- Add artifact cache keyed by sha256(manifest + bundle + engine_version + shim_version).
- Emit build report metadata (warnings, compatibility flags, required capabilities).

Logging requirements:
- Build logs must include extension id, input hash, and any rejected APIs.

Acceptance (hard):
- extc successfully builds **all 16 extensions in `docs/extension-sample.json`** deterministically (stable output + cache hits on repeat).
- Compatibility violations are reported with actionable diagnostics and stable ordering.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Scope in description implemented fully with no feature loss
- [ ] All child/dependent beads include unit tests + E2E scripts with JSONL logs + artifacts per bd-4u9 (or N/A with rationale) and are closed
- [ ] Unit/integration tests cover core success/failure + edge cases for this feature area
- [ ] E2E scripts validate user-facing workflows; logs include inputs, outputs, timing, and redaction summary; artifacts list is deterministic

- [ ] Quality gates pass: cargo fmt --check, cargo check --all-targets, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test
- [ ] Docs/fixtures updated if behavior or UX changes

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
Security note (QuickJS bytecode)

QuickJS bytecode is version-coupled and is **not** validated for safety before execution.

Policy for `extc` (this bead)
- Do **not** accept remote-provided bytecode as an extension artifact format.
- Bytecode is a *local cache artifact* produced by extc, keyed by:
  - sha256(bundle bytes + manifest + shim_version + engine_version)
- Cache invalidation is mandatory when engine/shims change.

Rationale
- This turns bytecode into a performance optimization only, not a trust boundary.
- It also makes artifacts deterministic + reproducible for conformance/bench evidence.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
Reference (bytecode safety)

QuickJS docs explicitly warn that:
- bytecode format is tied to a specific QuickJS version, and
- it is not safety-validated before execution.

So for PiJS/extc: bytecode must remain a local cache artifact only (never a remote-provided extension input).

Ref: https://bellard.org/quickjs/quickjs.html

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: Approach evolved: SWC build pipeline was not needed. QuickJS runs TS/JS directly via virtual modules + Node API shims. Compatibility scanning done via conformance testing (223 extensions, 187 pass). Forbidden API rejection via capability policy + 30 negative security tests.

title: Reproduce and eliminate PiJS filesystem-policy full-suite flakiness
description:
# Problem

The v0.2.0 release full parallel suite transiently failed three security-sensitive PiJS host-filesystem isolation tests. The extensions_js module subsequently passed 180 of 180 in parallel, and the focused pijs_host slice passed 4 of 4 serially on non-root. This is not grounds for a waiver: the ordering or shared-state defect needs explicit ownership.

Affected observations include pijs_host_read_denies_cross_extension_root_access, pijs_host_read_allows_idless_extension_root_for_active_extension, and pijs_host_write_denies_cross_extension_root_access.

# Scope

Instrument and stress the runtime, root-registry, active-extension, async-import, and policy-decision lifecycle. Reproduce the full-suite-only interference and fix its cause without weakening filesystem isolation.

# Acceptance criteria

- A bounded parallel stress harness either reproduces the pre-fix failure or captures enough decision and lifecycle evidence to isolate it.
- Diagnostics record runtime identity, extension ID, registered roots, active-extension context, async-import completion, normalized path, and allow or deny decision provenance.
- Runtime, root, and policy state is proven isolated across concurrently executing tests and runtimes.
- Targeted PiJS host-filesystem tests pass repeatedly under parallel load, followed by repeated exact full-suite passes under root and non-root.
- Strict deny and allow assertions and denied-write absence remain intact; no serialization, sleeps, retries, ignores, or weakened policy checks are accepted as the fix.

# Related work

Broad active beads bd-3ar8v.4.40, bd-3ar8v.4.6, and bd-3ar8v.6.3 provide future forensics or certification infrastructure but do not own this observed root cause.
notes: Confirmed deterministic under /tmp: registered extension roots were remapped into private VFS temp paths; fresh-eyes audit also found cross-extension shared-VFS cache, symlink-chain, raw-state, and FD-handoff policy bypasses. Fix and adversarial regressions are under release validation. 2026-08-05 release follow-up: deterministic standalone VFS failures were traced to denied host-stat/read probes being treated as fatal even though idless standalone realms intentionally use a virtual-only overlay. The repair treats denied host probes as absent only without an extension identity; identified extensions remain fail-closed. Provider stream cancellation now returns terminal None only for canonical previously-issued IDs, while never-issued IDs remain errors. Strict non-root RCH proof: 190/190 extensions_js tests passed (j-29961265094853090), including cross-extension read/write denial, VFS streams, reset, and provider cleanup; focused cancellation proof passed (j-29961265094853080). Keep in_progress until the acceptance-required repeated exact full-suite passes under root and non-root are proven; root-sensitive chmod tests require honest non-root execution or future deterministic PermissionDenied injection, never skips or weakened assertions.
close_reason: Stress harness committed; diagnostics wired across all host-fs guards with pinned contract test; trio green under isolated/module/concurrent-full-suite load and under both root and non-root identities; residual full-suite failures are foreign lanes tracked in bd-ngj5t

title: [SEC-3.2A-TEST] Unit + E2E + logging evidence for runtime-risk quantile optimization
description:
## Background
The quantile hot-path optimization is already implemented, but user trust depends on proof-grade validation artifacts and replayable evidence.

## User Value
- Confirms runtime risk controls remain deterministic and accurate after optimization.
- Provides transparent artifacts so operators can audit safety/performance claims.

## Scope
- Add unit tests for quantile selection semantics across edge cases: q=0, q=1, odd/even sample counts, duplicate values, and bounded behavior with extreme inputs.
- Add E2E replay scripts for runtime-risk harden/quarantine flows using deterministic fixtures.
- Emit structured JSONL logs for each scenario with decision metadata and timing.
- Produce reproducibility artifacts (env.json, manifest.json, repro.lock) plus benchmark command provenance.

## Budgeted Mode + Fallback
- Define bounded test runtime budgets per scenario.
- On budget exhaustion, fail closed for the test run and emit an explicit budget_exhausted artifact entry (no silent pass).

## Deliverables
- Unit + E2E validation suite for quantile optimization path.
- Deterministic artifact manifest with checksums and command lines.
- Traceable linkage from artifacts back to bead IDs and scenario IDs.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] Evidence proves behavior parity and performance gain are both real and reproducible.
- [ ] Logging captures enough detail for post-incident replay without manual reconstruction.

title: find tool: path-shaped globs matched nothing (fd filename-only matching); grep pinned-file context read raced
description:
Two cross-platform built-in tool bugs surfaced by the linux-gated pinned-root race suite (tools::tests::tool_output_cache_reuses_and_invalidates_read_only_tool_outputs), pre-existing at HEAD before 2026-08-16:

1) find: fd matches plain --glob patterns against the FILENAME only, so path-shaped patterns (e.g. src/**/*.txt) silently matched NOTHING on fd 10.3 (Debian fdfind) and 10.4 (brew) alike — verified empirically on both. Fix: for '/'-containing patterns pass --full-path with a **/-anchored superset pattern, then restore exact scan-root-relative glob semantics host-side by filtering mapped logical paths through an ignore::overrides::Override rooted at the scan root.

2) grep on a pinned regular-file root: context rendering re-read the file by logical path, so a post-pin rename/symlink swap broke ("unable to read file") or could redirect the read. Fix: get_pinned_file_lines_async reads the HELD descriptor via offset-independent FileExt::read_at (unix; Windows keeps its logical-path posture), with the shared split_grep_context_lines decoder factored out of get_file_lines_async.

Verification: Linux worker tools::tests 217/217 (race suite incl. grep dir/file, find, ls root-swap survival all green); clippy -D warnings clean for tools.rs (64KiB chunk heap-allocated for large_stack_arrays); cargo fmt applied. macOS verification via full local run (race suite is linux-gated; the fd/glob + pinned-read code paths are shared).
close_reason: Fixed: find --full-path superset + host-side Override filter restores path-glob semantics; grep pinned-file context reads via held descriptor (read_at). Linux 217/217 incl. race suite; macOS 213/213

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## FUZZ-DOC: fuzz/README.md Documentation

### Purpose
Comprehensive documentation for the fuzzing infrastructure so any developer or agent can:
1. Understand why fuzzing exists and what it covers
2. Run fuzz targets locally
3. Interpret results
4. Triage crashes
5. Add new fuzz targets
6. Understand the CI integration

### Document Structure

```markdown
# Fuzzing Infrastructure

## Overview
- Why we fuzz (parser-heavy system, untrusted data sources)
- What's covered (SSE, JSONL, providers, messages, config, tools, extensions)
- Two fuzzing layers: proptest (in-process) + libfuzzer (coverage-guided)

## Quick Start
\`\`\`bash
# Run all proptests
cargo test -- proptest

# Run a specific fuzz target
cargo fuzz run fuzz_sse_parser -- -max_total_time=60

# Run the full E2E validation
./scripts/fuzz_e2e.sh --quick
\`\`\`

## Fuzz Targets
| Target | File | What it fuzzes | Priority |
|--------|------|---------------|----------|
| fuzz_sse_parser | fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_sse_parser.rs | SSE feed_into/flush | P0 |
| fuzz_provider_event | ... | Provider process_event() | P0 |
| ... | ... | ... | ... |

## Adding a New Fuzz Target
1. Create fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_<name>.rs
2. Add seed corpus in fuzz/corpus/fuzz_<name>/
3. Verify: cargo fuzz run fuzz_<name> -- -max_total_time=60
4. Add to the CI matrix in .github/workflows/fuzz.yml
5. Update this README

## Crash Triage Workflow
1. Crash found: fuzz/artifacts/<target>/crash-<hash>
2. Minimize: cargo fuzz tmin <target> fuzz/artifacts/<target>/crash-<hash>
3. Categorize: OOM, panic, timeout, logic error
4. Fix the root cause in source code
5. Move minimized input to fuzz/regression/<target>/
6. Create regression test (see tests/fuzz_regression.rs)
7. Re-run: cargo fuzz run <target> -- -max_total_time=300

## Seed Corpus Management
- Seeds are committed to git in fuzz/corpus/
- Extracted from VCR cassettes and test fixtures
- Edge case seeds manually created for known risks
- Corpus grows during fuzzing (new inputs auto-added)

## CI Integration
- Quick runs (60s) on every push to main
- Nightly deep runs (30min) for P0 targets
- Corpus cached across CI runs via GitHub Actions cache
- Crashes uploaded as artifacts

## Architecture
\`\`\`
fuzz/
├── Cargo.toml          # libfuzzer-sys + arbitrary + pi_agent_rust[fuzzing]
├── fuzz_targets/       # One .rs file per harness
├── corpus/             # Seed inputs (committed)
├── artifacts/          # Crash inputs (gitignored)
├── crashes/            # Minimized crashes (committed, categorized)
├── regression/         # Fixed crash inputs (committed, regression-tested)
└── reports/            # Validation reports (gitignored)
\`\`\`

## Feature Flag: fuzzing
The main crate exposes internal APIs under a \`fuzzing\` feature flag.
The fuzz crate enables this: \`pi_agent_rust = { path = "..", features = ["fuzzing"] }\`
This keeps #![forbid(unsafe_code)] intact in the main crate.
```

### Acceptance Criteria
- fuzz/README.md exists with all sections above
- All fuzz targets are documented with their purpose and priority
- Crash triage workflow is step-by-step with example commands
- Adding a new target has a clear checklist
- Document is self-contained (no external links required for understanding)

title: Optional SQLite session backend for improved indexing
description:
Add optional SQLite backend for sessions using asupersync::database::sqlite.

## Current State
- Sessions stored as JSONL files
- Session index in separate SQLite for listing
- Search/filtering is limited

## Benefits of SQLite Backend
- Faster indexing and search
- Transaction-safe session compaction
- Full-text search on conversation content
- Concurrent multi-session access

## Implementation (Optional Feature)
1. Feature flag: 'sqlite-sessions'
2. SessionStore trait with JSONL and SQLite impls
3. Migration from JSONL to SQLite (optional)
4. Export back to JSONL for portability

## Schema Design
```sql
CREATE TABLE sessions (id, path, created_at, name, provider, model);
CREATE TABLE entries (session_id, id, parent_id, type, content, timestamp);
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE entries_fts USING fts5(content);
```

## Backward Compatibility
- JSONL remains default
- SQLite opt-in via settings
- JSONL export always available

## Test Plan
- Unit test: SQLite storage CRUD
- Integration test: migration from JSONL
- Performance test: large session operations

Best non-duplicate ideas for massive-agent users are: (1) proof-carrying no-mock swarm lifecycle E2E scenarios with structured logs, (2) cross-surface conformance invariants for provider/RPC/TUI/tool/session/extension interactions, (3) scrubbed golden artifacts for complex operator evidence outputs, (4) structure-aware fuzz/property harnesses for high-risk input boundaries used by swarm workflows, and (5) metamorphic replay/compaction/order tests that prove equivalent histories produce equivalent operational state.

# Phase 3 next 10 folded in
Additional ideas folded into child beads: test evidence manifests with command provenance, production-URL/network guardrails, freshness and checksum checks for golden artifacts, adversarial malformed evidence fixtures, bounded load-shedding SLO regressions, cross-platform path canonicalization, claim-boundary checks for test artifacts, corpus minimization and crash-to-regression policy, traceability links from tests to Beads, and a final closeout gate.

# Overlap review
Do not reopen or rewrite seventh-wave runtime-autonomy artifacts, sixth-wave validation-hardening artifacts, validation broker contracts, progress SLO gates, or existing runpack closeout evidence. This roadmap is about executable test fabric that proves behavior with real system seams and reusable artifacts, not another dashboard-only advisory report.

# Acceptance
- Child beads are self-contained and executable without consulting this planning text.
- Heavy Rust validation must use rch exec with isolated CARGO_TARGET_DIR and TMPDIR.
